6::COMO;;# Script for uploading files to a Google Code project.
7::COMO;;#
8::COMO;;# This is intended to be both a useful script for people who want to
9::COMO;;# streamline project uploads and a reference implementation for
10::COMO;;# uploading files to Google Code projects.
11::COMO;;#
12::COMO;;# To upload a file to Google Code, you need to provide a path to the
13::COMO;;# file on your local machine, a small summary of what the file is, a
14::COMO;;# project name, and a valid account that is a member or owner of that
15::COMO;;# project. You can optionally provide a list of labels that apply to
16::COMO;;# the file. The file will be uploaded under the same name that it has
17::COMO;;# in your local filesystem (that is, the "basename" or last path
18::COMO;;# component). Run the script with '--help' to get the exact syntax
19::COMO;;# and available options.
20::COMO;;#
21::COMO;;# Note that the upload script requests that you enter your
22::COMO;;# googlecode.com password. This is NOT your Gmail account password!
23::COMO;;# This is the password you use on googlecode.com for committing to
24::COMO;;# Subversion and uploading files. You can find your password by going
25::COMO;;# to http://code.google.com/hosting/settings when logged in with your
26::COMO;;# Gmail account. If you have already committed to your project's
27::COMO;;# Subversion repository, the script will automatically retrieve your
28::COMO;;# credentials from there (unless disabled, see the output of '--help'
29::COMO;;# for details).
30::COMO;;#
31::COMO;;# If you are looking at this script as a reference for implementing
32::COMO;;# your own Google Code file uploader, then you should take a look at
33::COMO;;# the upload() function, which is the meat of the uploader. You
34::COMO;;# basically need to build a multipart/form-data POST request with the
35::COMO;;# right fields and send it to https://PROJECT.googlecode.com/files .
36::COMO;;# Authenticate the request using HTTP Basic authentication, as is
37::COMO;;# shown below.
38::COMO;;#
39::COMO;;# Licensed under the terms of the Apache Software License 2.0:
40::COMO;;# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
41::COMO;;#
42::COMO;;# Questions, comments, feature requests and patches are most welcome.
43::COMO;;# Please direct all of these to the Google Code users group:
44::COMO;;# http://groups.google.com/group/google-code-hosting

114::COMM;;the settings panel. For instance, the default panel has a sidebar for
115::COMM;;switching between json panels whose width defaults to 200dp. If you'd
116::COMM;;prefer this to be narrower, you could add::

143::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
144::COMM;;Profiling with on_start and on_stop
145::COMM;;-----------------------------------
146::COMM;;It is often useful to profile python code in order to discover locations to
147::COMM;;optimise. The standard library profilers
148::COMM;;(http://docs.python.org/2/library/profile.html) provides multiple options for
149::COMM;;profiling code. For profiling the entire program, the natural
150::COMM;;approaches of using profile as a module or profile's run method does not work
151::COMM;;with Kivy. It is however, possible to use :meth:`App.on_start` and
152::COMM;;:meth:`App.on_stop` methods::
153::COMM;;import cProfile
154::COMM;;class MyApp(App):
155::COMM;;def on_start(self):
156::COMM;;self.profile = cProfile.Profile()
157::COMM;;self.profile.enable()
158::COMM;;def on_stop(self):
159::COMM;;self.profile.disable()
160::COMM;;self.profile.dump_stats('myapp.profile')
161::COMM;;This will create a file called `myapp.profile` when you exit your app.
162::COMM;;Customising layout
163::COMM;;------------------
164::COMM;;You can choose different settings widget layouts by setting
165::COMM;;:attr:`App.settings_cls`. By default, this is a
166::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.settings.Settings` class which provides the pictured
167::COMM;;sidebar layout, but you could set it to any of the other layouts
168::COMM;;provided in :mod:`kivy.uix.settings` or create your own. See the
169::COMM;;module documentation for :mod:`kivy.uix.settings` for more
170::COMM;;information.
171::COMM;;You can customise how the settings panel is displayed by
172::COMM;;overriding :meth:`App.display_settings` which is called before
173::COMM;;displaying the settings panel on the screen. By default, it
174::COMM;;simply draws the panel on top of the window, but you could modify it
175::COMM;;to (for instance) show the settings in a
176::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.popup.Popup` or add it to your app's
177::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.screenmanager.ScreenManager` if you are using
178::COMM;;one. If you do so, you should also modify :meth:`App.close_settings`
179::COMM;;to exit the panel appropriately. For instance, to have the settings
180::COMM;;panel appear in a popup you can do::
181::COMM;;def display_settings(self, settings):
182::COMM;;try:
183::COMM;;p = self.settings_popup
184::COMM;;except AttributeError:
185::COMM;;self.settings_popup = Popup(content=settings,
186::COMM;;title='Settings',
187::COMM;;size_hint=(0.8, 0.8))
188::COMM;;p = self.settings_popup
189::COMM;;if p.content is not settings:
190::COMM;;p.content = settings
191::COMM;;p.open()
192::COMM;;def close_settings(self, *args):
193::COMM;;try:
194::COMM;;p = self.settings_popup
195::COMM;;p.dismiss()
196::COMM;;except AttributeError:
197::COMM;;pass # Settings popup doesn't exist
198::COMM;;Finally, if you want to replace the current settings panel widget, you
199::COMM;;can remove the internal references to it using
200::COMM;;:meth:`App.destroy_settings`. If you have modified
201::COMM;;:meth:`App.display_settings`, you should be careful to detect if the
202::COMM;;settings panel has been replaced.
203::COMM;;Pause mode
204::COMM;;----------
205::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.0
206::COMM;;On tablets and phones, the user can switch at any moment to another
207::COMM;;application. By default, your application will close and the
208::COMM;;:meth:`App.on_stop` event will be fired.
209::COMM;;If you support Pause mode, when switching to another application, your
210::COMM;;application will wait indefinitely until the user
211::COMM;;switches back to your application. There is an issue with OpenGL on Android
212::COMM;;devices: it is not guaranteed that the OpenGL ES Context will be restored when
213::COMM;;your app resumes. The mechanism for restoring all the OpenGL data is not yet
214::COMM;;implemented in Kivy.
215::COMM;;The currently implemented Pause mechanism is:
216::COMM;;#. Kivy checks every frame if Pause mode is activated by the Operating
217::COMM;;System due to the user switching to another application, a phone
218::COMM;;shutdown or any other reason.
219::COMM;;#. :meth:`App.on_pause` is called:
220::COMM;;#. If False is returned or :meth:`App.on_pause` has no return statement,
221::COMM;;then :meth:`App.on_stop` is called.
222::COMM;;#. If True is returned or :meth:`App.on_pause` is not defined, the
223::COMM;;application will sleep until the OS resumes our App.
224::COMM;;#. When the app is resumed, :meth:`App.on_resume` is called.
225::COMM;;#. If our app memory has been reclaimed by the OS, then nothing will be
226::COMM;;called.
227::COMM;;Here is a simple example of how on_pause() should be used::
228::COMM;;class TestApp(App):
229::COMM;;def on_pause(self):
230::COMM;;# Here you can save data if needed
231::COMM;;return True
232::COMM;;def on_resume(self):
233::COMM;;# Here you can check if any data needs replacing (usually nothing)
234::COMM;;pass
235::COMM;;.. warning::
236::COMM;;Both `on_pause` and `on_stop` must save important data because after
237::COMM;;`on_pause` is called, `on_resume` may not be called at all.
238::COMM;;Asynchronous app
239::COMM;;----------------
240::COMM;;In addition to running an app normally,
241::COMM;;Kivy can be run within an async event loop such as provided by the standard
242::COMM;;library asyncio package or the trio package (highly recommended).
243::COMM;;Background
244::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~
245::COMM;;Normally, when a Kivy app is run, it blocks the thread that runs it until the
246::COMM;;app exits. Internally, at each clock iteration it executes all the app
247::COMM;;callbacks, handles graphics and input, and idles by sleeping for any remaining
248::COMM;;time.
249::COMM;;To be able to run asynchronously, the Kivy app may not sleep, but instead must
250::COMM;;release control of the running context to the asynchronous event loop running
251::COMM;;the Kivy app. We do this when idling by calling the appropriate functions of
252::COMM;;the async package being used instead of sleeping.
253::COMM;;Async configuration
254::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
255::COMM;;To run a Kivy app asynchronously, either the :func:`async_runTouchApp` or
256::COMM;;:meth:`App.async_run` coroutine must be scheduled to run in the event loop of
257::COMM;;the async library being used.
258::COMM;;The environmental variable ``KIVY_EVENTLOOP`` or the ``async_lib`` parameter in
259::COMM;;:func:`async_runTouchApp` and :meth:`App.async_run` set the async
260::COMM;;library that Kivy uses internally when the app is run with
261::COMM;;:func:`async_runTouchApp` and :meth:`App.async_run`. It can be set to one of
262::COMM;;`"asyncio"` when the standard library `asyncio` is used, or `"trio"` if the
263::COMM;;trio library is used. If the environment variable is not set and ``async_lib``
264::COMM;;is not provided, the stdlib ``asyncio`` is used.
265::COMM;;:meth:`~kivy.clock.ClockBaseBehavior.init_async_lib` can also be directly
266::COMM;;called to set the async library to use, but it may only be called before the
267::COMM;;app has begun running with :func:`async_runTouchApp` or :meth:`App.async_run`.
268::COMM;;To run the app asynchronously, one schedules :func:`async_runTouchApp`
269::COMM;;or :meth:`App.async_run` to run within the given library's async event loop as
270::COMM;;in the examples shown below. Kivy is then treated as just another coroutine
271::COMM;;that the given library runs in its event loop. Internally, Kivy will use the
272::COMM;;specified async library's API, so ``KIVY_EVENTLOOP`` or ``async_lib`` must
273::COMM;;match the async library that is running Kivy.
274::COMM;;For a fuller basic and more advanced examples, see the demo apps in
275::COMM;;``examples/async``.
276::COMM;;Asyncio example
277::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~--
278::COMM;;.. code-block:: python
279::COMM;;import asyncio
280::COMM;;from kivy.app import async_runTouchApp
281::COMM;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
282::COMM;;loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
283::COMM;;loop.run_until_complete(
284::COMM;;async_runTouchApp(Label(text='Hello, World!'), async_lib='asyncio'))
285::COMM;;loop.close()
286::COMM;;Trio example
287::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~--
288::COMM;;.. code-block:: python
289::COMM;;import trio
290::COMM;;from kivy.app import async_runTouchApp
291::COMM;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
292::COMM;;from functools import partial
293::COMM;;# use functools.partial() to pass keyword arguments:
294::COMM;;async_runTouchApp_func = partial(async_runTouchApp, async_lib='trio')
295::COMM;;trio.run(async_runTouchApp_func, Label(text='Hello, World!'))
296::COMM;;Interacting with Kivy app from other coroutines
297::COMM;;-----------------------------------------------
298::COMM;;It is fully safe to interact with any kivy object from other coroutines
299::COMM;;running within the same async event loop. This is because they are all running
300::COMM;;from the same thread and the other coroutines are only executed when Kivy
301::COMM;;is idling.
302::COMM;;Similarly, the kivy callbacks may safely interact with objects from other
303::COMM;;coroutines running in the same event loop. Normal single threaded rules apply
304::COMM;;to both case.
305::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 2.0.0
306::COMM;;'''
307::COMM;;__all__ = ('App', 'runTouchApp', 'async_runTouchApp', 'stopTouchApp')

327::COMM;;:func:`~kivy.base.runTouchApp` call.

331::COMM;;and indicates the UI is ready for user interaction.
332::COMM;;`on_stop`:

389::COMM;;settings_cls = ObjectProperty(None)

399::COMM;;own Settings subclass. See the documentation
400::COMM;;of :mod:`~kivy.uix.settings.Settings` for more information.
401::COMM;;:attr:`~App.settings_cls` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.ObjectProperty`

448::COMM;;widget and added to the window.
449::COMM;;:return:
450::COMM;;None or a root :class:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget` instance
451::COMM;;if no self.root exists.'''
452::COMM;;if not self.root:
453::COMM;;return Widget()
454::COMM;;def build_config(self, config):
455::COMM;;'''.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
456::COMM;;This method is called before the application is initialized to
457::COMM;;construct your :class:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser` object. This
458::COMM;;is where you can put any default section / key / value for your
459::COMM;;config. If anything is set, the configuration will be
460::COMM;;automatically saved in the file returned by
461::COMM;;:meth:`get_application_config`.
462::COMM;;:Parameters:
463::COMM;;`config`: :class:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser`
464::COMM;;Use this to add default section / key / value items
465::COMM;;'''
466::COMM;;def build_settings(self, settings):
467::COMM;;'''.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
468::COMM;;This method is called when the user (or you) want to show the
469::COMM;;application settings. It is called once when the settings panel
470::COMM;;is first opened, after which the panel is cached. It may be
471::COMM;;called again if the cached settings panel is removed by
472::COMM;;:meth:`destroy_settings`.
473::COMM;;You can use this method to add settings panels and to
474::COMM;;customise the settings widget e.g. by changing the sidebar
475::COMM;;width. See the module documentation for full details.
476::COMM;;:Parameters:
477::COMM;;`settings`: :class:`~kivy.uix.settings.Settings`
478::COMM;;Settings instance for adding panels
479::COMM;;'''
480::COMM;;def load_kv(self, filename=None):
481::COMM;;'''This method is invoked the first time the app is being run if no
482::COMM;;widget tree has been constructed before for this app.
483::COMM;;This method then looks for a matching kv file in the same directory as
484::COMM;;the file that contains the application class.
485::COMM;;For example, say you have a file named main.py that contains::
486::COMM;;class ShowcaseApp(App):
487::COMM;;pass
488::COMM;;This method will search for a file named `showcase.kv` in
489::COMM;;the directory that contains main.py. The name of the kv file has to be
490::COMM;;the lowercase name of the class, without the 'App' postfix at the end
491::COMM;;if it exists.
492::COMM;;You can define rules and a root widget in your kv file::
493::COMM;;<ClassName>: # this is a rule
494::COMM;;...
495::COMM;;ClassName: # this is a root widget
496::COMM;;...
497::COMM;;There must be only one root widget. See the :doc:`api-kivy.lang`
498::COMM;;documentation for more information on how to create kv files. If your
499::COMM;;kv file contains a root widget, it will be used as self.root, the root
500::COMM;;widget for the application.
501::COMM;;.. note::
502::COMM;;This function is called from :meth:`run`, therefore, any widget
503::COMM;;whose styling is defined in this kv file and is created before
504::COMM;;:meth:`run` is called (e.g. in `__init__`), won't have its styling
505::COMM;;applied. Note that :meth:`build` is called after :attr:`load_kv`
506::COMM;;has been called.
507::COMM;;'''
508::COMM;;# Detect filename automatically if it was not specified.
509::COMM;;if filename:
510::COMM;;filename = resource_find(filename)
511::COMM;;else:
512::COMM;;try:
513::COMM;;default_kv_directory = dirname(getfile(self.__class__))
514::COMM;;if default_kv_directory == '':
515::COMM;;default_kv_directory = '.'
516::COMM;;except TypeError:
517::COMM;;# if it's a builtin module.. use the current dir.
518::COMM;;default_kv_directory = '.'
519::COMM;;kv_directory = self.kv_directory or default_kv_directory
520::COMM;;clsname = self.__class__.__name__.lower()
521::COMM;;if (clsname.endswith('app') and
522::COMM;;not isfile(join(kv_directory, '%s.kv' % clsname))):
523::COMM;;clsname = clsname[:-3]
524::COMM;;filename = join(kv_directory, '%s.kv' % clsname)
525::COMM;;# Load KV file
526::COMM;;Logger.debug('App: Loading kv <{0}>'.format(filename))
527::COMM;;rfilename = resource_find(filename)
528::COMM;;if rfilename is None or not exists(rfilename):
529::COMM;;Logger.debug('App: kv <%s> not found' % filename)
530::COMM;;return False
531::COMM;;root = Builder.load_file(rfilename)
532::COMM;;if root:
533::COMM;;self.root = root
534::COMM;;return True
535::COMM;;def get_application_name(self):
536::COMM;;'''Return the name of the application.
537::COMM;;'''
538::COMM;;if self.title is not None:
539::COMM;;return self.title
540::COMM;;clsname = self.__class__.__name__
541::COMM;;if clsname.endswith('App'):
542::COMM;;clsname = clsname[:-3]
543::COMM;;return clsname
544::COMM;;def get_application_icon(self):
545::COMM;;'''Return the icon of the application.
546::COMM;;'''
547::COMM;;if not resource_find(self.icon):
548::COMM;;return ''
549::COMM;;else:
550::COMM;;return resource_find(self.icon)
551::COMM;;def get_application_config(self, defaultpath='%(appdir)s/%(appname)s.ini'):
552::COMM;;'''
553::COMM;;Return the filename of your application configuration. Depending
554::COMM;;on the platform, the application file will be stored in
555::COMM;;different locations:
556::COMM;;- on iOS: <appdir>/Documents/.<appname>.ini
557::COMM;;- on Android: <user_data_dir>/.<appname>.ini
558::COMM;;- otherwise: <appdir>/<appname>.ini
559::COMM;;When you are distributing your application on Desktops, please
560::COMM;;note that if the application is meant to be installed
561::COMM;;system-wide, the user might not have write-access to the
562::COMM;;application directory. If you want to store user settings, you
563::COMM;;should overload this method and change the default behavior to
564::COMM;;save the configuration file in the user directory. ::
565::COMM;;class TestApp(App):
566::COMM;;def get_application_config(self):
567::COMM;;return super(TestApp, self).get_application_config(
568::COMM;;'~/.%(appname)s.ini')
569::COMM;;Some notes:
570::COMM;;- The tilda '~' will be expanded to the user directory.
571::COMM;;- %(appdir)s will be replaced with the application :attr:`directory`
572::COMM;;- %(appname)s will be replaced with the application :attr:`name`
573::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
574::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4.0
575::COMM;;Customized the defaultpath for iOS and Android platforms. Added a
576::COMM;;defaultpath parameter for desktop OS's (not applicable to iOS
577::COMM;;and Android.)
578::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
579::COMM;;Changed the Android version to make use of the
580::COMM;;:attr:`~App.user_data_dir` and added a missing dot to the iOS
581::COMM;;config file name.
582::COMM;;'''
583::COMM;;if platform == 'android':
584::COMM;;return join(self.user_data_dir, '.{0}.ini'.format(self.name))
585::COMM;;elif platform == 'ios':
586::COMM;;defaultpath = '~/Documents/.%(appname)s.ini'
587::COMM;;elif platform == 'win':
588::COMM;;defaultpath = defaultpath.replace('/', sep)
589::COMM;;return expanduser(defaultpath) % {
590::COMM;;'appname': self.name, 'appdir': self.directory}
591::COMM;;@property
592::COMM;;def root_window(self):
593::COMM;;'''.. versionadded:: 1.9.0
594::COMM;;Returns the root window instance used by :meth:`run`.
595::COMM;;'''
596::COMM;;return self._app_window
597::COMM;;def load_config(self):
598::COMM;;'''(internal) This function is used for returning a ConfigParser with
599::COMM;;the application configuration. It's doing 3 things:
600::COMM;;#. Creating an instance of a ConfigParser
601::COMM;;#. Loading the default configuration by calling
602::COMM;;:meth:`build_config`, then
603::COMM;;#. If it exists, it loads the application configuration file,
604::COMM;;otherwise it creates one.
605::COMM;;:return:
606::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.config.ConfigParser` instance
607::COMM;;'''
608::COMM;;try:
609::COMM;;config = ConfigParser.get_configparser('app')
610::COMM;;except KeyError:
611::COMM;;config = None
612::COMM;;if config is None:
613::COMM;;config = ConfigParser(name='app')
614::COMM;;self.config = config
615::COMM;;self.build_config(config)
616::COMM;;# if no sections are created, that's mean the user don't have
617::COMM;;# configuration.
618::COMM;;if len(config.sections()) == 0:
619::COMM;;return
620::COMM;;# ok, the user have some sections, read the default file if exist
621::COMM;;# or write it !
622::COMM;;filename = self.get_application_config()
623::COMM;;if filename is None:
624::COMM;;return config
625::COMM;;Logger.debug('App: Loading configuration <{0}>'.format(filename))
626::COMM;;if exists(filename):
627::COMM;;try:
628::COMM;;config.read(filename)
629::COMM;;except:
630::COMM;;Logger.error('App: Corrupted config file, ignored.')
631::COMM;;config.name = ''
632::COMM;;try:
633::COMM;;config = ConfigParser.get_configparser('app')
634::COMM;;except KeyError:
635::COMM;;config = None
636::COMM;;if config is None:
637::COMM;;config = ConfigParser(name='app')
638::COMM;;self.config = config
639::COMM;;self.build_config(config)
640::COMM;;pass
641::COMM;;else:
642::COMM;;Logger.debug('App: First configuration, create <{0}>'.format(
643::COMM;;filename))
644::COMM;;config.filename = filename
645::COMM;;config.write()
646::COMM;;return config
647::COMM;;@property
648::COMM;;def directory(self):
649::COMM;;'''.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
650::COMM;;Return the directory where the application lives.
651::COMM;;'''
652::COMM;;if self._app_directory is None:
653::COMM;;try:
654::COMM;;self._app_directory = dirname(getfile(self.__class__))
655::COMM;;if self._app_directory == '':
656::COMM;;self._app_directory = '.'
657::COMM;;except TypeError:
658::COMM;;# if it's a builtin module.. use the current dir.
659::COMM;;self._app_directory = '.'
660::COMM;;return self._app_directory
661::COMM;;def _get_user_data_dir(self):
662::COMM;;# Determine and return the user_data_dir.
663::COMM;;data_dir = ""
664::COMM;;if platform == 'ios':
665::COMM;;data_dir = expanduser(join('~/Documents', self.name))
666::COMM;;elif platform == 'android':
667::COMM;;from jnius import autoclass, cast
668::COMM;;PythonActivity = autoclass('org.kivy.android.PythonActivity')
669::COMM;;context = cast('android.content.Context', PythonActivity.mActivity)
670::COMM;;file_p = cast('java.io.File', context.getFilesDir())
671::COMM;;data_dir = file_p.getAbsolutePath()
672::COMM;;elif platform == 'win':
673::COMM;;data_dir = os.path.join(os.environ['APPDATA'], self.name)
674::COMM;;elif platform == 'macosx':
675::COMM;;data_dir = '~/Library/Application Support/{}'.format(self.name)
676::COMM;;data_dir = expanduser(data_dir)
677::COMM;;else: # _platform == 'linux' or anything else...:
678::COMM;;data_dir = os.environ.get('XDG_CONFIG_HOME', '~/.config')
679::COMM;;data_dir = expanduser(join(data_dir, self.name))
680::COMM;;if not exists(data_dir):
681::COMM;;os.mkdir(data_dir)
682::COMM;;return data_dir
683::COMM;;@property
684::COMM;;def user_data_dir(self):
685::COMM;;'''
686::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
687::COMM;;Returns the path to the directory in the users file system which the
688::COMM;;application can use to store additional data.
689::COMM;;Different platforms have different conventions with regards to where
690::COMM;;the user can store data such as preferences, saved games and settings.
691::COMM;;This function implements these conventions. The <app_name> directory
692::COMM;;is created when the property is called, unless it already exists.
693::COMM;;On iOS, `~/Documents/<app_name>` is returned (which is inside the
694::COMM;;app's sandbox).
695::COMM;;On Windows, `%APPDATA%/<app_name>` is returned.
696::COMM;;On OS X, `~/Library/Application Support/<app_name>` is returned.
697::COMM;;On Linux, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app_name>` is returned.
698::COMM;;On Android, `Context.GetFilesDir
699::COMM;;<https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/\
700::COMM;;Context.html#getFilesDir()>`_ is returned.
701::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
702::COMM;;On Android, this function previously returned
703::COMM;;`/sdcard/<app_name>`. This folder became read-only by default
704::COMM;;in Android API 26 and the user_data_dir has therefore been moved
705::COMM;;to a writeable location.
706::COMM;;'''
707::COMM;;if self._user_data_dir == "":
708::COMM;;self._user_data_dir = self._get_user_data_dir()
709::COMM;;return self._user_data_dir
710::COMM;;@property
711::COMM;;def name(self):
712::COMM;;'''.. versionadded:: 1.0.7
713::COMM;;Return the name of the application based on the class name.
714::COMM;;'''
715::COMM;;if self._app_name is None:
716::COMM;;clsname = self.__class__.__name__
717::COMM;;if clsname.endswith('App'):
718::COMM;;clsname = clsname[:-3]
719::COMM;;self._app_name = clsname.lower()
720::COMM;;return self._app_name
721::COMM;;def _run_prepare(self):
722::COMM;;if not self.built:
723::COMM;;self.load_config()
724::COMM;;self.load_kv(filename=self.kv_file)
725::COMM;;root = self.build()
726::COMM;;if root:
727::COMM;;self.root = root
728::COMM;;if self.root:
729::COMM;;if not isinstance(self.root, Widget):
730::COMM;;Logger.critical('App.root must be an _instance_ of Widget')
731::COMM;;raise Exception('Invalid instance in App.root')
732::COMM;;from kivy.core.window import Window
733::COMM;;Window.add_widget(self.root)
734::COMM;;# Check if the window is already created
735::COMM;;from kivy.base import EventLoop
736::COMM;;window = EventLoop.window
737::COMM;;if window:
738::COMM;;self._app_window = window
739::COMM;;window.set_title(self.get_application_name())
740::COMM;;icon = self.get_application_icon()
741::COMM;;if icon:
742::COMM;;window.set_icon(icon)
743::COMM;;self._install_settings_keys(window)
744::COMM;;else:
745::COMM;;Logger.critical("Application: No window is created."
746::COMM;;" Terminating application run.")

2::COMM;;Kivy Logging
3::COMM;;============
4::COMM;;By default, Kivy provides a logging system based on the standard Python
5::COMM;;`logging <https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html>`_ module with
6::COMM;;several additional features designed to be more convenient. These features
7::COMM;;include:
8::COMM;;* simplied usage (single instance, simple configuration, works by default)
9::COMM;;* color-coded output on supported terminals
10::COMM;;* output to ``stderr`` by default
11::COMM;;* message categorization via colon separation
12::COMM;;* access to log history even if logging is disabled
13::COMM;;* built-in handling of various cross-platform considerations
14::COMM;;* any stray output written to ``sys.stderr`` is captured, and stored in the log
15::COMM;;file as a warning.
16::COMM;;These features are configurable via the Config file or environment variables -
17::COMM;;including falling back to only using the standard Python system.
18::COMM;;Logger object
19::COMM;;=============
20::COMM;;The Kivy ``Logger`` class provides a singleton logging.logger instance.
21::COMM;;As well as the standard logging levels (``debug``, ``info``,
22::COMM;;``warning``, ``error`` and ``critical``), an additional ``trace`` level is
23::COMM;;available.
24::COMM;;Example Usage
25::COMM;;-------------
26::COMM;;Use the ``Logger`` as you would a standard Python logger. ::
27::COMM;;from kivy.logger import Logger
28::COMM;;Logger.info('title: This is a info message.')
29::COMM;;Logger.debug('title: This is a debug message.')
30::COMM;;try:
31::COMM;;raise Exception('bleh')
32::COMM;;except Exception:
33::COMM;;Logger.exception('Something happened!')
34::COMM;;The message passed to the logger is split into two parts separated by a colon
35::COMM;;(:). The first part is used as a title and the second part is used as the
36::COMM;;message. This way, you can "categorize" your messages easily. ::
37::COMM;;Logger.info('Application: This is a test')
38::COMM;;# will appear as
39::COMM;;[INFO ] [Application ] This is a test
40::COMM;;You can change the logging level at any time using the ``setLevel`` method. ::
41::COMM;;from kivy.logger import Logger, LOG_LEVELS
42::COMM;;Logger.setLevel(LOG_LEVELS["debug"])
43::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 2.2.0
44::COMM;;Interaction with other logging
45::COMM;;------------------------------
46::COMM;;The Kivy logging system will, by default, present all log messages sent from
47::COMM;;any logger - e.g. from third-party libraries.
48::COMM;;Additional handlers may be added.
49::COMM;;.. warning:: Handlers that output to ``sys.stderr`` may cause loops, as stderr
50::COMM;;output is reported as a warning log message.
51::COMM;;Logger Configuration
52::COMM;;====================
53::COMM;;Kivy Log Mode
54::COMM;;-------------
55::COMM;;At the highest level, Kivy's logging system is controlled by an environment
56::COMM;;variable ``KIVY_LOG_MODE``. It may be given any of three values:
57::COMM;;``KIVY``, ``PYTHON``, ``MIXED``
58::COMM;;.. versionadded: 2.2.0
59::COMM;;KIVY Mode (default)
60::COMM;;^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
61::COMM;;In ``KIVY`` mode, all Kivy handlers are attached to the root logger, so all log
62::COMM;;messages in the system are output to the Kivy log files and to the console. Any
63::COMM;;stray output to ``sys.stderr`` is logged as a warning.
64::COMM;;If you are writing an entire Kivy app from scratch, this is the most convenient
65::COMM;;mode.
66::COMM;;PYTHON Mode
67::COMM;;^^^^^^^^^^^
68::COMM;;In ``PYTHON`` mode, no handlers are added, and ``sys.stderr`` output is not
69::COMM;;captured. It is left to the client to add appropriate handlers. (If none are
70::COMM;;added, the ``logging`` module will output them to ``stderr``.)
71::COMM;;Messages logged with ``Logger`` will be propagated to the root logger, from a
72::COMM;;logger named ``kivy``.
73::COMM;;If the Kivy app is part of a much larger project which has its own logging
74::COMM;;regimen, this is the mode that gives most control.
75::COMM;;The ``kivy.logger`` file contains a number of ``logging.handler``,
76::COMM;;``logging.formatter``, and other helper classes to allow
77::COMM;;users to adopt the features of Kivy logging that they like, including the
78::COMM;;stderr redirection.
79::COMM;;MIXED Mode
80::COMM;;^^^^^^^^^^
81::COMM;;In ``MIXED`` mode, handlers are added to the Kivy's ``Logger`` object directly,
82::COMM;;and propagation is turned off. ``sys.stderr`` is not redirected.
83::COMM;;Messages logged with Kivy's ``Logger`` will appear in the Kivy log file and
84::COMM;;output to the Console.
85::COMM;;However, messages logged with other Python loggers will not be handled by Kivy
86::COMM;;handlers. The client will need to add their own.
87::COMM;;If you like the features of Kivy ``Logger``, but are writing a Kivy app that
88::COMM;;relies on third-party libraries that don't use colon-separation of categorise
89::COMM;;or depend on the display of the logger name, this mode provides a compromise.
90::COMM;;Again, the ``kivy.logger`` file contains re-usable logging features that can be
91::COMM;;used to get the best of both systems.
92::COMM;;Config Files
93::COMM;;------------
94::COMM;;In ``KIVY`` and ``MIXED`` modes, the logger handlers can be controlled via the
95::COMM;;Kivy configuration file::
96::COMM;;[kivy]
97::COMM;;log_level = info
98::COMM;;log_enable = 1
99::COMM;;log_dir = logs
100::COMM;;log_name = kivy_%y-%m-%d_%_.txt
101::COMM;;log_maxfiles = 100
102::COMM;;More information about the allowed values are described in the
103::COMM;;:mod:`kivy.config` module.
104::COMM;;In addition, the environment variables ``KIVY_NO_FILELOG`` and
105::COMM;;``KIVY_NO_CONSOLELOG`` can be used to turn off the installation of the
106::COMM;;corresponding handlers.
107::COMM;;Logger History
108::COMM;;--------------
109::COMM;;Even if the logger is not enabled, you still have access to the last 100
110::COMM;;LogRecords::
111::COMM;;from kivy.logger import LoggerHistory
112::COMM;;print(LoggerHistory.history)

1::COMO;;# coding=utf-8
3::COMM;;Console
4::COMM;;=======
5::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.9.1
6::COMM;;Reboot of the old inspector, designed to be modular and keep concerns
7::COMM;;separated. It also has an addons architecture that allow you to add a button,
8::COMM;;panel, or more in the Console itself.
9::COMM;;.. warning::
10::COMM;;This module works, but might fail in some cases. Please contribute!
11::COMM;;Usage
12::COMM;;-----
13::COMM;;For normal module usage, please see the :mod:`~kivy.modules` documentation::
14::COMM;;python main.py -m console
15::COMM;;Mouse navigation
16::COMM;;----------------
17::COMM;;When the "Select" button is activated, you can:
18::COMM;;- tap once on a widget to select it without leaving inspect mode
19::COMM;;- double tap on a widget to select and leave inspect mode (then you can
20::COMM;;manipulate the widget again)
21::COMM;;Keyboard navigation
22::COMM;;-------------------
23::COMM;;- "Ctrl + e": toggle console
24::COMM;;- "Escape": cancel widget lookup, then hide inspector view
25::COMM;;- "Up": select the parent widget
26::COMM;;- "Down": select the first child of the currently selected widget
27::COMM;;- "Left": select the previous sibling
28::COMM;;- "Right": select the next sibling
29::COMM;;Additional information
30::COMM;;----------------------
31::COMM;;Some properties can be edited live. However, due to the delayed usage of
32::COMM;;some properties, it might crash if you don't handle the required cases.
33::COMM;;Addons
34::COMM;;------
35::COMM;;Addons must be added to `Console.addons` before the first Clock tick of the
36::COMM;;application, or before :attr:`create_console` is called. You currently cannot
37::COMM;;add addons on the fly. Addons are quite cheap until the Console is activated.
38::COMM;;Panels are even cheaper as nothing is done until the user selects them.
39::COMM;;We provide multiple addons activated by default:
40::COMM;;- ConsoleAddonFps: display the FPS at the top-right
41::COMM;;- ConsoleAddonSelect: activate the selection mode
42::COMM;;- ConsoleAddonBreadcrumb: display the hierarchy of the current widget at the
43::COMM;;bottom
44::COMM;;- ConsoleAddonWidgetTree: panel to display the widget tree of the application
45::COMM;;- ConsoleAddonWidgetPanel: panel to display the properties of the selected
46::COMM;;widget
47::COMM;;If you need to add custom widgets in the Console, please use either
48::COMM;;:class:`ConsoleButton`, :class:`ConsoleToggleButton` or :class:`ConsoleLabel`.
49::COMM;;An addon must inherit from the :class:`ConsoleAddon` class.
50::COMM;;For example, here is a simple addon for displaying the FPS at the top/right
51::COMM;;of the Console::
52::COMM;;from kivy.modules.console import Console, ConsoleAddon
53::COMM;;class ConsoleAddonFps(ConsoleAddon):
54::COMM;;def init(self):
55::COMM;;self.lbl = ConsoleLabel(text="0 Fps")
56::COMM;;self.console.add_toolbar_widget(self.lbl, right=True)
57::COMM;;def activate(self):
58::COMM;;self.event = Clock.schedule_interval(self.update_fps, 1 / 2.)
59::COMM;;def deactivated(self):
60::COMM;;self.event.cancel()
61::COMM;;def update_fps(self, *args):
62::COMM;;fps = Clock.get_fps()
63::COMM;;self.lbl.text = "{} Fps".format(int(fps))
64::COMM;;Console.register_addon(ConsoleAddonFps)
65::COMM;;You can create addons that add panels. Panel activation/deactivation is not
66::COMM;;tied to the addon activation/deactivation, but in some cases, you can use the
67::COMM;;same callback for deactivating the addon and the panel. Here is a simple
68::COMM;;"About" panel addon::
69::COMM;;from kivy.modules.console import Console, ConsoleAddon, ConsoleLabel
70::COMM;;class ConsoleAddonAbout(ConsoleAddon):
71::COMM;;def init(self):
72::COMM;;self.console.add_panel("About", self.panel_activate,
73::COMM;;self.panel_deactivate)
74::COMM;;def panel_activate(self):
75::COMM;;self.console.bind(widget=self.update_content)
76::COMM;;self.update_content()
77::COMM;;def panel_deactivate(self):
78::COMM;;self.console.unbind(widget=self.update_content)
79::COMM;;def deactivate(self):
80::COMM;;self.panel_deactivate()
81::COMM;;def update_content(self, *args):
82::COMM;;widget = self.console.widget
83::COMM;;if not widget:
84::COMM;;return
85::COMM;;text = "Selected widget is: {!r}".format(widget)
86::COMM;;lbl = ConsoleLabel(text=text)
87::COMM;;self.console.set_content(lbl)
88::COMM;;Console.register_addon(ConsoleAddonAbout)

2::COMM;;Changelog parser
3::COMM;;================
4::COMM;;This generates a changelog from a json file of the PRs of a given milestone,
5::COMM;;dumped to json, using the [GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli).
6::COMM;;First, in the command line, create the following alias::
7::COMM;;gh alias set --shell viewMilestone "gh api graphql -F owner='kivy' \
8::COMM;;-F name='kivy' -F number=\\$1 -f query='
9::COMM;;query GetMilestones(\\$name: String!, \\$owner: String!, \\$number: \
10::COMM;;Int!) {
11::COMM;;repository(owner: \\$owner, name: \\$name) {
12::COMM;;milestone(number: \\$number) {
13::COMM;;pullRequests(states: MERGED, first: 1000) {
14::COMM;;nodes {
15::COMM;;number
16::COMM;;title
17::COMM;;labels (first: 25) {
18::COMM;;nodes {
19::COMM;;name
20::COMM;;}
21::COMM;;}
22::COMM;;}
23::COMM;;}
24::COMM;;}
25::COMM;;}
26::COMM;;}
27::COMM;;'"
28::COMM;;Then, log in using ``gh`` and run::
29::COMM;;gh viewMilestone 26 > prs.json
30::COMM;;This will generate ``prs.json``. Then, to generate the changelog, run::
31::COMM;;python -m kivy.tools.changelog_parser prs.json changelog.md
32::COMM;;to generate a markdown changelog at ``changelog.md``. Then, edit as desired
33::COMM;;and paste into the
34::COMM;;[changelog here](https://github.com/kivy/kivy/blob/master/doc/sources\
35::COMM;;/changelog.rst).

2::COMM;;Behaviors
3::COMM;;=========
4::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
5::COMM;;Behavior mixin classes
6::COMM;;----------------------
7::COMM;;This module implements behaviors that can be
8::COMM;;`mixed in <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_
9::COMM;;with existing base widgets. The idea behind these classes is to encapsulate
10::COMM;;properties and events associated with certain types of widgets.
11::COMM;;Isolating these properties and events in a mixin class allows you to define
12::COMM;;your own implementation for standard kivy widgets that can act as drop-in
13::COMM;;replacements. This means you can re-style and re-define widgets as desired
14::COMM;;without breaking compatibility: as long as they implement the behaviors
15::COMM;;correctly, they can simply replace the standard widgets.
16::COMM;;Adding behaviors
17::COMM;;----------------
18::COMM;;Say you want to add :class:`~kivy.uix.button.Button` capabilities to an
19::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.image.Image`, you could do::
20::COMM;;class IconButton(ButtonBehavior, Image):
21::COMM;;pass
22::COMM;;This would give you an :class:`~kivy.uix.image.Image` with the events and
23::COMM;;properties inherited from :class:`ButtonBehavior`. For example, the *on_press*
24::COMM;;and *on_release* events would be fired when appropriate::
25::COMM;;class IconButton(ButtonBehavior, Image):
26::COMM;;def on_press(self):
27::COMM;;print("on_press")
28::COMM;;Or in kv:
29::COMM;;.. code-block:: kv
30::COMM;;IconButton:
31::COMM;;on_press: print('on_press')
32::COMM;;Naturally, you could also bind to any property changes the behavior class
33::COMM;;offers:
34::COMM;;.. code-block:: python
35::COMM;;def state_changed(*args):
36::COMM;;print('state changed')
37::COMM;;button = IconButton()
38::COMM;;button.bind(state=state_changed)
39::COMM;;.. note::
40::COMM;;The behavior class must always be _before_ the widget class. If you don't
41::COMM;;specify the inheritance in this order, the behavior will not work because
42::COMM;;the behavior methods are overwritten by the class method listed first.
43::COMM;;Similarly, if you combine a behavior class with a class which
44::COMM;;requires the use of the methods also defined by the behavior class, the
45::COMM;;resulting class may not function properly. For example, when combining the
46::COMM;;:class:`ButtonBehavior` with a :class:`~kivy.uix.slider.Slider`, both of
47::COMM;;which use the :meth:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.on_touch_up` method,
48::COMM;;the resulting class may not work properly.
49::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.9.1
50::COMM;;The individual behavior classes, previously in one big `behaviors.py`
51::COMM;;file, has been split into a single file for each class under the
52::COMM;;:mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors` module. All the behaviors are still imported
53::COMM;;in the :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors` module so they are accessible as before
54::COMM;;(e.g. both `from kivy.uix.behaviors import ButtonBehavior` and
55::COMM;;`from kivy.uix.behaviors.button import ButtonBehavior` work).
2::COMM;;Button Behavior
3::COMM;;===============
4::COMM;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.button.ButtonBehavior`
5::COMM;;`mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ class provides button behavior
6::COMM;;for Kivy widgets. You can combine this class with other widgets to add
7::COMM;;specialized press/release/cancel events and reactive pressed state tracking.
8::COMM;;For an overview of behaviors, please refer to the :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors`
9::COMM;;documentation.
10::COMM;;Examples
11::COMM;;--------
12::COMM;;Basic button with visual feedback::

21::COMM;;# Visual feedback: red when pressed, white otherwise
22::COMM;;self.color = [1, 0, 0, 1] if is_pressed else [1, 1, 1, 1]

50::COMM;;See :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.ButtonBehavior` for details.
56::COMM;;This mixin enables widgets to respond to press/release interactions with
57::COMM;;automatic multi-touch support. It provides three specialized events:
58::COMM;;:meth:`on_press`, :meth:`on_release`, and :meth:`on_cancel`, along with
59::COMM;;a reactive :attr:`pressed` property.
60::COMM;;Button State Management
61::COMM;;-----------------------
62::COMM;;Tracks active touches internally using a set-based approach. Each touch
63::COMM;;gets a unique ID (supports multi-touch). When first touch enters widget
64::COMM;;bounds, button becomes pressed. When ALL touches are released or cancelled,
65::COMM;;button returns to unpressed state. The :attr:`pressed` property is True
66::COMM;;when any touches are active.
67::COMM;;Multi-Touch Behavior
68::COMM;;--------------------
69::COMM;;The button automatically handles multiple simultaneous touches:
70::COMM;;- **First touch down**: Triggers :meth:`on_press`, sets :attr:`pressed` to True
71::COMM;;- **Additional touches**: Tracked but don't trigger :meth:`on_press` again
72::COMM;;- **Touch release**: Only triggers :meth:`on_release` after ALL touches released
73::COMM;;- **Touch cancel**: Removes touch from tracking, updates :attr:`pressed` state
74::COMM;;Release Modes
75::COMM;;-------------
76::COMM;;Controlled by :attr:`always_release` property:
77::COMM;;- **False (default)**: Standard button behavior. :meth:`on_release` only fires
78::COMM;;if touch ends within button bounds. :meth:`on_cancel` fires when touch
79::COMM;;moves outside bounds during drag (touch move).
80::COMM;;- **True**: Always fires :meth:`on_release` regardless of touch position.
81::COMM;;:meth:`on_cancel` never fires. Useful for drag-and-drop or gesture-based
82::COMM;;interfaces.
83::COMM;;Events
84::COMM;;------
85::COMM;;:meth:`on_press`
86::COMM;;First touch down on button
87::COMM;;:meth:`on_release`
88::COMM;;All touches released (respects :attr:`always_release` mode)
89::COMM;;:meth:`on_cancel`
90::COMM;;Touch moved outside bounds during drag (only when :attr:`always_release`
91::COMM;;is False)

93::COMM;;- Replaced ``state`` OptionProperty with ``pressed`` BooleanProperty
94::COMM;;- Made ``pressed`` read-only via AliasProperty
95::COMM;;- Added :meth:`on_cancel` event
96::COMM;;- Improved multi-touch handling with explicit touch sets
100::COMM;;outside widget bounds.
101::COMM;;When False (default):
102::COMM;;- :meth:`on_release` only fires if touch ends within button bounds
103::COMM;;- :meth:`on_cancel` fires when touch moves outside bounds during drag
104::COMM;;- Provides standard button behavior with cancellation feedback
105::COMM;;When True:
106::COMM;;- :meth:`on_release` always fires regardless of final touch position
107::COMM;;- :meth:`on_cancel` never fires
108::COMM;;- Useful for drag-and-drop or gesture-based interfaces where release
109::COMM;;position is irrelevant
110::COMM;;:attr:`always_release` is a :class:`~kivy.properties.BooleanProperty` and
111::COMM;;defaults to False.

123::COMM;;The button is pressed only when currently touched/clicked. This property
124::COMM;;automatically handles multi-touch scenarios, remaining True as long as at

128::COMM;;to False.

147::COMO;;# public events. They allow subclasses to implement internal state changes
148::COMO;;# (e.g., ToggleButtonBehavior updating its state) separately from
149::COMO;;# user-facing event handlers, maintaining a clean separation between

2::COMM;;Hover Behavior
3::COMM;;==============
4::COMM;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.hover.HoverBehavior`
5::COMM;;`mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ class provides hover detection
6::COMM;;and event handling for Kivy widgets. You can combine this class with other
7::COMM;;widgets to add specialized hover events (on_hover_enter, on_hover_update,
8::COMM;;on_hover_leave) and reactive hover state tracking.
9::COMM;;For an overview of behaviors, please refer to the :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors`
10::COMM;;documentation.
11::COMM;;Related Behaviors
12::COMM;;-----------------
13::COMM;;For most hover use cases, you'll want to combine
14::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.hover.HoverBehavior` with generic motion event
15::COMM;;filters from :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion`:
16::COMM;;- :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion.MotionCollideBehavior`: Filters motion
17::COMM;;events to only process those within widget bounds. Essential for
18::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.recycleview.RecycleView` and
19::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scrollview.ScrollView` to prevent hover conflicts outside
20::COMM;;visible area.
21::COMM;;- :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion.MotionBlockBehavior`: Blocks unregistered
22::COMM;;motion events from passing through. Makes widgets "opaque" to motion events,
23::COMM;;preventing leak-through.
24::COMM;;Examples
25::COMM;;--------
26::COMM;;Basic hover with visual feedback::
27::COMM;;from kivy.app import App
28::COMM;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
29::COMM;;from kivy.uix.behaviors import ButtonBehavior
30::COMM;;from kivy.uix.behaviors.hover import HoverBehavior
31::COMM;;class HoverButton(HoverBehavior, ButtonBehavior, Label):
32::COMM;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
33::COMM;;super().__init__(**kwargs)
34::COMM;;self.text = 'Hover me!'
35::COMM;;def on_hovered(self, instance, is_hovered):
36::COMM;;# Visual feedback: red when hovered, white otherwise
37::COMM;;self.color = [1, 0, 0, 1] if is_hovered else [1, 1, 1, 1]
38::COMM;;def on_hover_enter(self, motion_event):
39::COMM;;print(f"Mouse entered at {motion_event.pos}")
40::COMM;;def on_hover_leave(self, motion_event):
41::COMM;;print(f"Mouse left at {motion_event.pos}")
42::COMM;;class SampleApp(App):
43::COMM;;def build(self):
44::COMM;;return HoverButton()
45::COMM;;SampleApp().run()

96::COMM;;Tracks the lifecycle of a hover event from start to finish:
97::COMM;;- BEGIN: Initial hover detection
98::COMM;;- UPDATE: Continuous hover movement

106::COMM;;Controls how hover events are distributed through the widget hierarchy:
107::COMM;;- DEFAULT: Dispatch to children first, then self if not accepted
108::COMM;;- ALL: Dispatch to both children AND self

116::COMM;;tree.
117::COMM;;This is an internal implementation. Users should not interact with
118::COMM;;this class directly. It is automatically registered by
119::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.hover.HoverBehavior` on first use.
120::COMM;;Responsibilities:
121::COMM;;- Receives hover events from :class:`~kivy.core.window.Window`
122::COMM;;- Transforms coordinates to window space
123::COMM;;- Dispatches through widget tree via on_motion protocol
124::COMM;;- Tracks grabbed widgets between frames
125::COMM;;- Synthesizes hover leave events when widgets lose hover
126::COMM;;Static Hover Re-dispatching:
127::COMM;;Re-dispatches hover events once when the mouse position hasn't changed
128::COMM;;AND the time since last dispatch exceeds ``hover_update_interval``. This
129::COMM;;ensures widgets receive proper hover events (enter/update/leave) when:
130::COMM;;- Mouse is stationary but content scrolls (RecycleView/ScrollView)
131::COMM;;- Widget moves/resizes under cursor
132::COMM;;- Disabled widgets become enabled under cursor
133::COMM;;The interval is controlled via
134::COMM;;:meth:`HoverBehavior.set_hover_update_interval`.
135::COMM;;Set interval to negative value to disable this feature entirely.
136::COMM;;Event Flow:
137::COMM;;1. Window generates hover event (mouse movement without buttons)
138::COMM;;2. Manager transforms event coordinates
139::COMM;;3. Event propagates through widget tree
140::COMM;;4. HoverBehavior widgets handle and update state
141::COMM;;5. Manager tracks grabbed widgets
142::COMM;;6. On next frame, sends leave events to ungrabbed widgets
143::COMM;;Grab List Management:
144::COMM;;Maintains history of grabbed widgets between frames to properly
145::COMM;;synthesize leave events. When mouse moves from widget A to B,
146::COMM;;Kivy doesn't send automatic end events - we detect this by
147::COMM;;comparing grab lists.

303::COMM;;Re-dispatches existing hover events once when the time since the last
304::COMM;;event exceeds hover_update_interval. This enables hover events
305::COMM;;(enter/update/leave) to fire when content changes under a static cursor.
325::COMM;;This mixin enables widgets to respond to mouse hover events with three
326::COMM;;specialized events: :meth:`on_hover_enter`, :meth:`on_hover_update`, and
327::COMM;;:meth:`on_hover_leave`. It also provides a reactive :attr:`hovered` property.
328::COMM;;Hover State Management
329::COMM;;----------------------
330::COMM;;Tracks active hover events internally. Each hover event gets a unique
331::COMM;;ID (supports multi-touch hover). When a hover enters widget bounds,
332::COMM;;it's tracked. When it leaves, it's removed. The :attr:`hovered` property
333::COMM;;is True when any hover events are active.
334::COMM;;Event Propagation Modes
335::COMM;;------------------------
336::COMM;;- **"default"**: Standard behavior. Events go to children first. If no child
337::COMM;;accepts, the event is offered to this widget.
338::COMM;;- **"all"**: Forces dispatch to both children AND this widget, regardless
339::COMM;;of whether children accept. Use when parent needs to track hovers even
340::COMM;;while children handle them (e.g., container with hover effects).
341::COMM;;- **"self"**: Skips children entirely. This widget captures all hover events
342::COMM;;within its bounds. Use for widgets that should be "opaque" to hover
343::COMM;;(e.g., popup overlays).
344::COMM;;Static Hover Re-dispatching
345::COMM;;----------------------------
346::COMM;;By default, hover events are re-dispatched once when the mouse is
347::COMM;;stationary AND the time since the last dispatch exceeds 1/30s. This
348::COMM;;enables proper hover state tracking when content moves under a
349::COMM;;stationary cursor (e.g., scrolling with mousewheel).
350::COMM;;All three hover events (enter/update/leave) are affected:
351::COMM;;- :meth:`on_hover_enter`: Fires when widget scrolls under static cursor
352::COMM;;- :meth:`on_hover_update`: Fires once after interval
353::COMM;;- :meth:`on_hover_leave`: Fires when widget scrolls away from cursor
354::COMM;;Configure globally before creating widgets::
355::COMM;;# Disable re-dispatching entirely
356::COMM;;HoverBehavior.set_hover_update_interval(-1)
357::COMM;;# Re-dispatch once after 0.1s (max 10 updates per second)
358::COMM;;HoverBehavior.set_hover_update_interval(0.1)
359::COMM;;# Default: re-dispatch once after 1/30s (max 30 updates per second)
360::COMM;;HoverBehavior.set_hover_update_interval(1/30)
361::COMM;;Combining with Motion Filters
362::COMM;;------------------------------
363::COMM;;For most use cases, combine :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.hover.HoverBehavior`
364::COMM;;with motion event filters from :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion`:
365::COMM;;Example - ScrollView with Collision Filter::
366::COMM;;from kivy.uix.behaviors.motion import MotionCollideBehavior
367::COMM;;class HoverScrollView(MotionCollideBehavior, ScrollView):
368::COMM;;# Filters hover outside stencil bounds
369::COMM;;pass
370::COMM;;class HoverItem(HoverBehavior, MotionCollideBehavior, Label):
371::COMM;;# Only receives hover when visible
372::COMM;;pass
373::COMM;;Example - Blocking Hover Leak-Through::
374::COMM;;from kivy.uix.behaviors.motion import MotionBlockBehavior
375::COMM;;class OpaqueButton(MotionBlockBehavior, Button):
376::COMM;;# Blocks all unregistered motion events
377::COMM;;pass

410::COMM;;Modes:
411::COMM;;- **"default"**: Standard propagation. Children first, then self if not
412::COMM;;accepted. Use this for most widgets.

485::COMM;;1. Test collision with widget bounds

488::COMM;;4. Ungrab event when hover ends

490::COMM;;When hover enters bounds, we grab it with motion_event.grab(self).
491::COMM;;This marks the widget as owner. Grab persists across frames until
492::COMM;;explicit ungrab, maintaining hover state as mouse moves.
493::COMM;;:param event_type: Motion event type ("begin", "update", "end")
494::COMM;;:param motion_event: :class:`~kivy.input.motionevent.MotionEvent` instance
495::COMM;;:return: True if event was handled (collided with widget)

521::COMO;;# We own this hover - clean up and dispatch leave
527::COMO;;# Disabled widget blocking
534::COMM;;Controls the minimum time between hover re-dispatches when the mouse
535::COMM;;is stationary. Re-dispatches once when:
536::COMM;;1. Mouse hasn't moved, AND
537::COMM;;2. Time since last dispatch exceeds interval
538::COMM;;This affects all three hover events (enter/update/leave) and is
539::COMM;;essential for scenarios where content moves under a static cursor
540::COMM;;(e.g., scrolling with mousewheel).
541::COMM;;When enabled, the system re-checks which widgets should receive hover
542::COMM;;events, allowing proper enter/leave events as widgets scroll in/out
543::COMM;;of view.
544::COMM;;This configuration applies to all
545::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.hover.HoverBehavior` widgets and can be
546::COMM;;called before any widgets are instantiated.

548::COMM;;disable re-dispatching entirely
549::COMM;;Example::
550::COMM;;# Disable re-dispatching (no scroll hover updates)
551::COMM;;HoverBehavior.set_hover_update_interval(-1)
552::COMM;;# Re-dispatch once after 0.1s (max 10 updates per second)
553::COMM;;HoverBehavior.set_hover_update_interval(0.1)
554::COMM;;# Default: re-dispatch once after 1/30s (max 30 updates per second)
555::COMM;;HoverBehavior.set_hover_update_interval(1/30)
556::COMM;;.. note::
557::COMM;;When disabled (negative interval), hover events only fire when the
558::COMM;;mouse actually moves. Content scrolling under a static cursor will
559::COMM;;not trigger enter/update/leave events.

571::COMM;;Example::

2::COMM;;Motion Event Behaviors
3::COMM;;======================
4::COMM;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion.MotionCollideBehavior` and
5::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion.MotionBlockBehavior`
6::COMM;;`mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ classes provide generic
7::COMM;;motion event filtering for any motion event type (hover, drag, custom events).
8::COMM;;These behaviors are commonly used with :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.hover.HoverBehavior`
9::COMM;;but are designed to be generic and reusable with any motion event system.
10::COMM;;For an overview of behaviors, please refer to the :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors`
11::COMM;;documentation.
12::COMM;;Components
13::COMM;;----------
14::COMM;;**MotionCollideBehavior**:
15::COMM;;Filters motion events to only process those within widget bounds or grabbed.
16::COMM;;Essential for :class:`~kivy.uix.recycleview.RecycleView` and
17::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scrollview.ScrollView` to prevent conflicts outside
18::COMM;;visible area.
19::COMM;;**MotionBlockBehavior**:
20::COMM;;Blocks unregistered motion events from passing through widget bounds.
21::COMM;;Makes widgets "opaque" to motion events, preventing leak-through to
22::COMM;;background widgets.
23::COMM;;Examples
24::COMM;;--------
25::COMM;;Using MotionCollideBehavior with HoverBehavior::
26::COMM;;from kivy.uix.scrollview import ScrollView
27::COMM;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
28::COMM;;from kivy.uix.behaviors.hover import HoverBehavior
29::COMM;;from kivy.uix.behaviors.motion import MotionCollideBehavior
30::COMM;;class HoverScrollView(MotionCollideBehavior, ScrollView):
31::COMM;;# Filters hover events outside stencil bounds
32::COMM;;pass
33::COMM;;class HoverItem(HoverBehavior, MotionCollideBehavior, Label):
34::COMM;;def on_enter(self):
35::COMM;;self.color = [1, 0, 0, 1] # Red on hover
36::COMM;;def on_leave(self):
37::COMM;;self.color = [1, 1, 1, 1] # White normally
38::COMM;;Using MotionBlockBehavior to prevent event leak-through::
39::COMM;;from kivy.uix.button import Button
40::COMM;;from kivy.uix.floatlayout import FloatLayout
41::COMM;;from motion_behaviors import MotionBlockBehavior
42::COMM;;class OpaqueButton(MotionBlockBehavior, Button):
43::COMM;;# Blocks unregistered motion events from passing through
44::COMM;;pass
45::COMM;;layout = FloatLayout()
46::COMM;;layout.add_widget(HoverScrollView()) # Background
47::COMM;;layout.add_widget(OpaqueButton()) # Foreground
48::COMM;;# Hovering over button won't trigger ScrollView hover
49::COMM;;Important Notes
50::COMM;;---------------
51::COMM;;**DO NOT** use :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion.MotionCollideBehavior` and
52::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion.MotionBlockBehavior` together on the same
53::COMM;;widget. They serve different purposes:
54::COMM;;- **MotionCollideBehavior**: Filters events outside widget bounds
55::COMM;;* Use for: Items in RecycleView/ScrollView
56::COMM;;* Purpose: Ignore events when widget is outside visible area
57::COMM;;- **MotionBlockBehavior**: Blocks unregistered event types from passing through
58::COMM;;* Use for: Overlay widgets, modal dialogs, foreground elements
59::COMM;;* Purpose: Prevent events from leaking to widgets behind
60::COMM;;Combining them creates redundant or conflicting logic.
61::COMM;;See :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion.MotionCollideBehavior` and
62::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.motion.MotionBlockBehavior` for details.
67::COMM;;This mixin overrides :meth:`on_motion` to only process events that either:
68::COMM;;1. Collide with the widget's bounds, OR
69::COMM;;2. Are grabbed events (motion_event.grab_current is self)
70::COMM;;Generic Design
71::COMM;;--------------
72::COMM;;Works with ANY motion event type (hover, drag, custom events).
73::COMM;;Commonly used with :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.hover.HoverBehavior` but
74::COMM;;not limited to hover events.
75::COMM;;Primary Use Case - StencilView
76::COMM;;-------------------------------
77::COMM;;Essential for widgets that use stencil clipping
78::COMM;;(:class:`~kivy.uix.recycleview.RecycleView`,
79::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.scrollview.ScrollView`). Without this mixin, widgets
80::COMM;;outside the stencil bounds can still receive motion events, leading to
81::COMM;;confusing behavior where invisible items respond.
82::COMM;;Technical Note
83::COMM;;--------------
84::COMM;;The collision check uses :meth:`widget.collide_point(*motion_event.pos)`,
85::COMM;;which tests against the widget's bounding box. For complex shapes, override
86::COMM;;:meth:`collide_point()` in your widget class for custom collision logic.
87::COMM;;Grabbed Events
88::COMM;;--------------
89::COMM;;Grabbed events always pass through, even if they don't collide. This ensures
90::COMM;;proper event completion - if a widget grabbed an event (e.g., on hover
91::COMM;;enter), it must receive the end event even if the cursor moved outside
92::COMM;;bounds.
96::COMM;;Only processes events that:
97::COMM;;- Are currently grabbed by this widget, OR
98::COMM;;- Have position data and collide with widget bounds
99::COMM;;:param event_type: Motion event type ("begin", "update", "end")
100::COMM;;:param motion_event: MotionEvent to potentially filter
101::COMM;;:return: Result of super().on_motion() if passed filter, False otherwise
106::COMO;;# Process only grabbed events or events within bounds
109::COMO;;# Filter out non-qualifying events
113::COMM;;Makes widgets "opaque" to motion events they haven't registered to handle.
114::COMM;;When a motion event collides with the widget but the widget hasn't
115::COMM;;registered for that event type, the event is blocked from propagating to
116::COMM;;widgets behind it.
117::COMM;;Generic Design
118::COMM;;--------------
119::COMM;;Works with ANY motion event type (hover, drag, custom events). Prevents
120::COMM;;motion events from "leaking through" foreground widgets to background
121::COMM;;widgets.
122::COMM;;Comparison with HoverBehavior
123::COMM;;------------------------------
124::COMM;;- **MotionBlockBehavior**: Blocks ALL unregistered motion event types
125::COMM;;- **HoverBehavior** (hover_mode='self'): Only blocks hover events with
126::COMM;;more fine-grained control
127::COMM;;For hover-specific blocking with more control, consider using
128::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.hover.HoverBehavior` with hover_mode='self'
129::COMM;;instead.
130::COMM;;Technical Note
131::COMM;;--------------
132::COMM;;The collision check uses :meth:`widget.collide_point(*motion_event.pos)`.
133::COMM;;For custom collision shapes, override :meth:`collide_point()` in your
134::COMM;;widget.
135::COMM;;Grabbed Events
136::COMM;;--------------
137::COMM;;Grabbed events always pass through, even if not registered. This ensures
138::COMM;;proper event lifecycle - if a widget grabs an event, it must receive all
139::COMM;;subsequent updates and the end event.
143::COMM;;Processing logic:
144::COMM;;1. If grabbed by this widget -> pass to super() (process)
145::COMM;;2. If collides but NOT registered -> return True (block)
146::COMM;;3. Otherwise -> pass to super() (continue propagation)
147::COMM;;:param event_type: Motion event type ("begin", "update", "end")
148::COMM;;:param motion_event: MotionEvent to potentially block
149::COMM;;:return: True if event was blocked or handled, False otherwise
151::COMO;;# Grabbed events always pass through
154::COMO;;# Check collision and registration
158::COMO;;# Block if collides but not registered
161::COMO;;# Pass through to normal processing
2::COMM;;ToggleButton Behavior
3::COMM;;=====================
4::COMM;;The :class:`~kivy.uix.behaviors.togglebutton.ToggleButtonBehavior`
5::COMM;;`mixin <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixin>`_ class provides toggle button
6::COMM;;behavior for Kivy widgets. You can combine this class with other widgets to add
7::COMM;;specialized on/off state management with optional radio button grouping.
8::COMM;;For an overview of behaviors, please refer to the :mod:`~kivy.uix.behaviors`
9::COMM;;documentation.
10::COMM;;Examples
11::COMM;;--------
12::COMM;;Basic toggle with visual feedback::
13::COMM;;from kivy.app import App
14::COMM;;from kivy.lang import Builder
15::COMM;;from kivy.uix.label import Label
16::COMM;;from kivy.uix.behaviors import ToggleButtonBehavior
17::COMM;;class MyToggle(ToggleButtonBehavior, Label):
18::COMM;;Builder.load_string('''
19::COMM;;<MyToggle>:
20::COMM;;canvas.before:
21::COMM;;Color:
22::COMM;;rgb: self.color
23::COMM;;a: 0.25
24::COMM;;Rectangle:
25::COMM;;size: self.size
26::COMM;;pos: self.pos
27::COMM;;''')
28::COMM;;def on_active(self, instance, value):
29::COMM;;self.color = [0, 1, 0, 1] if value else [1, 1, 1, 1]
30::COMM;;class SampleApp(App):
31::COMM;;def build(self):
32::COMM;;return MyToggle()
33::COMM;;SampleApp().run()

261::COMM;;def _get_active(self):
266::COMM;;Used as the setter for :attr:`active`. Delegates all logic to
267::COMM;;:meth:`_change_active_state` to keep programmatic and interactive
268::COMM;;changes consistent.
269::COMM;;:param value: Desired active state.
270::COMM;;:type value: bool
277::COMM;;- **True**: Button is in "on" state
278::COMM;;- **False**: Button is in "off" state
279::COMM;;Unlike :attr:`pressed` (which is True only during touch), :attr:`active`
280::COMM;;maintains state after release. Can be set programmatically or toggled by
281::COMM;;user interaction.
282::COMM;;When button is in a group, setting active=True automatically deactivates
283::COMM;;other buttons in that group.
284::COMM;;When :attr:`allow_no_selection` is False, attempts to set active=False
285::COMM;;on the last active button in a group are silently rejected.
286::COMM;;:attr:`active` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.AliasProperty` and defaults
287::COMM;;to False.
288::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 3.0.0
292::COMM;;change.
293::COMM;;- **"release" (default)** — The state toggles when the button is released.
294::COMM;;- **"press"** — The state toggles immediately when the button is pressed.
295::COMM;;This property allows adjusting when the toggle action occurs, depending on
296::COMM;;the desired interaction style. It can be changed dynamically at runtime,
297::COMM;;and the new behavior takes effect immediately.
298::COMM;;:attr:`toggle_on` is an :class:`~kivy.properties.OptionProperty` and
299::COMM;;accepts either ``"press"`` or ``"release"``. Defaults to ``"release"``.
301::COMC;;_active = BooleanProperty(False) # Internal storage for active state
304::COMM;;This descriptor works as both an instance method and a class method,
305::COMM;;providing a unified API for accessing group widgets.
306::COMM;;**As instance method** (no arguments):
307::COMM;;Returns all widgets in the same group as this instance, including
308::COMM;;this instance itself.
309::COMM;;Example::
310::COMM;;# Get all widgets in my_button's group
311::COMM;;widgets = my_button.get_group()
312::COMM;;for w in widgets:
313::COMM;;print(w.text)
314::COMM;;del widgets # Release immediately
315::COMM;;**As class method** (pass group identifier):
316::COMM;;Returns all widgets in the specified group. Useful when you don't
317::COMM;;have a widget instance but know the group identifier.
318::COMM;;Example::
319::COMM;;# Get widgets by global group name
320::COMM;;widgets = ToggleButtonBehavior.get_group("options")
321::COMM;;# Get widgets by scoped group
322::COMM;;widgets = ToggleButtonBehavior.get_group((panel, "filters"))
323::COMM;;# Useful after removing a widget
324::COMM;;my_group = widget.group
325::COMM;;widget.parent.remove_widget(widget)
326::COMM;;remaining = ToggleButtonBehavior.get_group(my_group)
327::COMM;;.. warning::
328::COMM;;Always release the result immediately! Holding references prevents
329::COMM;;garbage collection::
330::COMM;;widgets = button.get_group()
331::COMM;;# use widgets
332::COMM;;del widgets
333::COMM;;.. note::
334::COMM;;List may contain recently deleted widgets that haven't been
335::COMM;;garbage collected yet.
336::COMM;;:return: List of widget instances in the group (empty list if group
337::COMM;;doesn't exist or has no members)

2::COMM;;CheckBox
3::COMM;;========
4::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
5::COMM;;.. image:: images/checkbox.png
6::COMM;;:align: right
7::COMM;;:class:`CheckBox` is a specific two-state button that can be either checked or
8::COMM;;unchecked. If the CheckBox is in a Group, it becomes a Radio button.
9::COMM;;As with the :class:`~kivy.uix.togglebutton.ToggleButton`, only one Radio button
10::COMM;;at a time can be selected when the :attr:`CheckBox.group` is set.
11::COMM;;An example usage::
12::COMM;;from kivy.uix.checkbox import CheckBox
13::COMM;;# ...
14::COMM;;def on_checkbox_active(checkbox, value):
15::COMM;;if value:
16::COMM;;print('The checkbox', checkbox, 'is active')
17::COMM;;else:
18::COMM;;print('The checkbox', checkbox, 'is inactive')
19::COMM;;checkbox = CheckBox()
20::COMM;;checkbox.bind(active=on_checkbox_active)

2::COMM;;ModalView
3::COMM;;=========
4::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4.0
5::COMM;;The :class:`ModalView` widget is used to create modal views. By default, the
6::COMM;;view will cover the whole "main" window.
7::COMM;;Remember that the default size of a Widget is size_hint=(1, 1). If you don't
8::COMM;;want your view to be fullscreen, either use size hints with values lower than
9::COMM;;1 (for instance size_hint=(.8, .8)) or deactivate the size_hint and use fixed
10::COMM;;size attributes.
11::COMM;;Examples
12::COMM;;--------
13::COMM;;Example of a simple 400x400 Hello world view::
14::COMM;;view = ModalView(size_hint=(None, None), size=(400, 400))
15::COMM;;view.add_widget(Label(text='Hello world'))
16::COMM;;By default, any click outside the view will dismiss it. If you don't
17::COMM;;want that, you can set :attr:`ModalView.auto_dismiss` to False::
18::COMM;;view = ModalView(auto_dismiss=False)
19::COMM;;view.add_widget(Label(text='Hello world'))
20::COMM;;view.open()
21::COMM;;To manually dismiss/close the view, use the :meth:`ModalView.dismiss` method of
22::COMM;;the ModalView instance::
23::COMM;;view.dismiss()
24::COMM;;Both :meth:`ModalView.open` and :meth:`ModalView.dismiss` are bind-able. That
25::COMM;;means you can directly bind the function to an action, e.g. to a button's
26::COMM;;on_press ::
27::COMM;;# create content and add it to the view
28::COMM;;content = Button(text='Close me!')
29::COMM;;view = ModalView(auto_dismiss=False)
30::COMM;;view.add_widget(content)
31::COMM;;# bind the on_press event of the button to the dismiss function
32::COMM;;content.bind(on_press=view.dismiss)
33::COMM;;# open the view
34::COMM;;view.open()
35::COMM;;ModalView Events
36::COMM;;----------------
37::COMM;;There are four events available: `on_pre_open` and `on_open` which are raised
38::COMM;;when the view is opening; `on_pre_dismiss` and `on_dismiss` which are raised
39::COMM;;when the view is closed.
40::COMM;;For `on_dismiss`, you can prevent the view from closing by explicitly
41::COMM;;returning `True` from your callback::
42::COMM;;def my_callback(instance):
43::COMM;;print('ModalView', instance, 'is being dismissed, but is prevented!')
44::COMM;;return True
45::COMM;;view = ModalView()
46::COMM;;view.add_widget(Label(text='Hello world'))
47::COMM;;view.bind(on_dismiss=my_callback)
48::COMM;;view.open()
49::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.5.0
50::COMM;;The ModalView can be closed by hitting the escape key on the
51::COMM;;keyboard if the :attr:`ModalView.auto_dismiss` property is True (the
52::COMM;;default).
62::COMM;;:Events:
63::COMM;;`on_pre_open`:
64::COMM;;Fired before the ModalView is opened. When this event is fired
65::COMM;;ModalView is not yet added to window.
66::COMM;;`on_open`:
67::COMM;;Fired when the ModalView is opened.
68::COMM;;`on_pre_dismiss`:
69::COMM;;Fired before the ModalView is closed.
70::COMM;;`on_dismiss`:
71::COMM;;Fired when the ModalView is closed. If the callback returns True,
72::COMM;;the dismiss will be canceled.
73::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.11.0
74::COMM;;Added events `on_pre_open` and `on_pre_dismiss`.
75::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 2.0.0
76::COMM;;Added property 'overlay_color'.
77::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 2.1.0
78::COMM;;Marked `attach_to` property as deprecated.

144::COMM;;don't want the animation, use::
145::COMM;;view.open(animation=False)

171::COMM;;view = ModalView()

2::COMM;;PageLayout
3::COMM;;==========
4::COMM;;.. image:: images/pagelayout.gif
5::COMM;;:align: right
6::COMM;;The :class:`PageLayout` class is used to create a simple multi-page
7::COMM;;layout, in a way that allows easy flipping from one page to another using
8::COMM;;borders.
9::COMM;;:class:`PageLayout` does not currently honor the
10::COMM;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.size_hint`,
11::COMM;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.size_hint_min`,
12::COMM;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.size_hint_max`, or
13::COMM;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.pos_hint` properties.
14::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.8.0
15::COMM;;Example:
16::COMM;;.. code-block:: kv
17::COMM;;PageLayout:
18::COMM;;Button:
19::COMM;;text: 'page1'
20::COMM;;Button:
21::COMM;;text: 'page2'
22::COMM;;Button:
23::COMM;;text: 'page3'
24::COMM;;Transitions from one page to the next are made by swiping in from the border
25::COMM;;areas on the right or left hand side. If you wish to display multiple widgets
26::COMM;;in a page, we suggest you use a containing layout. Ideally, each page should
27::COMM;;consist of a single :mod:`~kivy.uix.layout` widget that contains the remaining
28::COMM;;widgets on that page.

87::COMC;;else: # not first and there are no post pages
90::COMC;;if not p: # second page - no left margin
92::COMC;;else: # there's already a left margin

132::COMO;;# move current page until edge hits the right border

2::COMM;;RecycleView
3::COMM;;===========
4::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.10.0
5::COMM;;The RecycleView provides a flexible model for viewing selected sections of
6::COMM;;large data sets. It aims to prevent the performance degradation that can occur
7::COMM;;when generating large numbers of widgets in order to display many data items.
8::COMM;;.. warning::
9::COMM;;Because :class:`RecycleView` reuses widgets, any state change to a single
10::COMM;;widget will stay with that widget as it's reused, even if the
11::COMM;;:attr:`~RecycleView.data` assigned to it by the :class:`RecycleView`
12::COMM;;changes, unless the complete state is tracked in :attr:`~RecycleView.data`
13::COMM;;(see below).
14::COMM;;The view is generated by processing the :attr:`~RecycleView.data`, essentially
15::COMM;;a list of dicts, and uses these dicts to generate instances of the
16::COMM;;:attr:`~RecycleView.viewclass` as required. Its design is based on the
17::COMM;;MVC (`Model-View-Controller
18::COMM;;<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model%E2%80%93view%E2%80%93controller>`_)
19::COMM;;pattern.
20::COMM;;* Model: The model is formed by :attr:`~RecycleView.data` you pass in via a
21::COMM;;list of dicts.
22::COMM;;* View: The View is split across layout and views and implemented using
23::COMM;;adapters.
24::COMM;;* Controller: The controller determines the logical interaction and is
25::COMM;;implemented by :class:`RecycleViewBehavior`.
26::COMM;;These are abstract classes and cannot be used directly. The default concrete
27::COMM;;implementations are the
28::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.recycleview.datamodel.RecycleDataModel` for the model, the
29::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.recyclelayout.RecycleLayout` for the view, and the
30::COMM;;:class:`RecycleView` for the controller.
31::COMM;;When a RecycleView is instantiated, it automatically creates the views and data
32::COMM;;classes. However, one must manually create the layout classes and add them to
33::COMM;;the RecycleView.
34::COMM;;A layout manager is automatically created as a
35::COMM;;:attr:`~RecycleViewBehavior.layout_manager` when added as the child of the
36::COMM;;RecycleView. Similarly when removed. A requirement is that the layout manager
37::COMM;;must be contained as a child somewhere within the RecycleView's widget tree so
38::COMM;;the view port can be found.
39::COMM;;A minimal example might look something like this::
40::COMM;;from kivy.app import App
41::COMM;;from kivy.lang import Builder
42::COMM;;from kivy.uix.recycleview import RecycleView
43::COMM;;Builder.load_string('''
44::COMM;;<RV>:
45::COMM;;viewclass: 'Label'
46::COMM;;RecycleBoxLayout:
47::COMM;;default_size: None, dp(56)
48::COMM;;default_size_hint: 1, None
49::COMM;;size_hint_y: None
50::COMM;;height: self.minimum_height
51::COMM;;orientation: 'vertical'
52::COMM;;''')
53::COMM;;class RV(RecycleView):
54::COMM;;def __init__(self, **kwargs):
55::COMM;;super(RV, self).__init__(**kwargs)
56::COMM;;self.data = [{'text': str(x)} for x in range(100)]
57::COMM;;class TestApp(App):
58::COMM;;def build(self):
59::COMM;;return RV()
60::COMM;;if __name__ == '__main__':
61::COMM;;TestApp().run()
