130::COMM;;Viewclass State
131::COMM;;^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
132::COMM;;Because the viewclass widgets are reused or instantiated as needed by the
133::COMM;;:class:`RecycleView`, the order and content of the widgets are mutable. So any
134::COMM;;state change to a single widget will stay with that widget, even when the data
135::COMM;;assigned to it from the :attr:`~RecycleView.data` dict changes, unless
136::COMM;;:attr:`~RecycleView.data` tracks those changes or they are manually refreshed
137::COMM;;when re-used.
138::COMM;;There are two methods for managing state changes in viewclass widgets:
139::COMM;;1. Store state in the RecycleView.data Model
140::COMM;;2. Generate state changes on-the-fly by catching :attr:`~RecycleView.data`
141::COMM;;updates and manually refreshing.
142::COMM;;An example::
143::COMM;;from kivy.app import App
144::COMM;;from kivy.lang import Builder
145::COMM;;from kivy.uix.boxlayout import BoxLayout
146::COMM;;from kivy.uix.recycleview import RecycleView
147::COMM;;from kivy.uix.recycleview.views import RecycleDataViewBehavior
148::COMM;;from kivy.properties import BooleanProperty, StringProperty
149::COMM;;Builder.load_string('''
150::COMM;;<StatefulLabel>:
151::COMM;;active: stored_state.active
152::COMM;;CheckBox:
153::COMM;;id: stored_state
154::COMM;;active: root.active
155::COMM;;on_release: root.store_checkbox_state()
156::COMM;;Label:
157::COMM;;text: root.text
158::COMM;;Label:
159::COMM;;id: generate_state
160::COMM;;text: root.generated_state_text
161::COMM;;<RV>:
162::COMM;;viewclass: 'StatefulLabel'
163::COMM;;RecycleBoxLayout:
164::COMM;;size_hint_y: None
165::COMM;;height: self.minimum_height
166::COMM;;orientation: 'vertical'
167::COMM;;''')
168::COMM;;class StatefulLabel(RecycleDataViewBehavior, BoxLayout):
169::COMM;;text = StringProperty()
170::COMM;;generated_state_text = StringProperty()
171::COMM;;active = BooleanProperty()
172::COMM;;index = 0
173::COMM;;'''
174::COMM;;To change a viewclass' state as the data assigned to it changes,
175::COMM;;overload the refresh_view_attrs function (inherited from
176::COMM;;RecycleDataViewBehavior)
177::COMM;;'''
178::COMM;;def refresh_view_attrs(self, rv, index, data):
179::COMM;;self.index = index
180::COMM;;if data['text'] == '0':
181::COMM;;self.generated_state_text = "is zero"
182::COMM;;elif int(data['text']) % 2 == 1:
183::COMM;;self.generated_state_text = "is odd"
184::COMM;;else:
185::COMM;;self.generated_state_text = "is even"
186::COMM;;super(StatefulLabel, self).refresh_view_attrs(rv, index, data)

2::COMM;;ScrollView
3::COMM;;==========
4::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0.4
5::COMM;;The :class:`ScrollView` widget provides a scrollable/pannable viewport that is
6::COMM;;clipped at the scrollview's bounding box.
7::COMM;;.. note::
8::COMM;;Use :class:`~kivy.uix.recycleview.RecycleView` for generating large
9::COMM;;numbers of widgets in order to display many data items.
10::COMM;;Scrolling Behavior
11::COMM;;------------------
12::COMM;;The ScrollView accepts only one child and applies a viewport/window to
13::COMM;;it according to the :attr:`~ScrollView.scroll_x` and
14::COMM;;:attr:`~ScrollView.scroll_y` properties. Touches are analyzed to
15::COMM;;determine if the user wants to scroll or control the child in some
16::COMM;;other manner: you cannot do both at the same time. To determine if
17::COMM;;interaction is a scrolling gesture, these properties are used:
18::COMM;;- :attr:`~ScrollView.scroll_distance`: the minimum distance to travel,
19::COMM;;defaults to 20 pixels.
20::COMM;;- :attr:`~ScrollView.scroll_timeout`: the maximum time period, defaults
21::COMM;;to 55 milliseconds.
22::COMM;;If a touch travels :attr:`~ScrollView.scroll_distance` pixels within the
23::COMM;;:attr:`~ScrollView.scroll_timeout` period, it is recognized as a scrolling
24::COMM;;gesture and translation (scroll/pan) will begin. If the timeout occurs, the
25::COMM;;touch down event is dispatched to the child instead (no translation).
26::COMM;;The default value for those settings can be changed in the configuration file::
27::COMM;;[widgets]
28::COMM;;scroll_timeout = 250
29::COMM;;scroll_distance = 20
30::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.1.1
31::COMM;;ScrollView now animates scrolling in Y when a mousewheel is used.
32::COMM;;Limiting to the X or Y Axis
33::COMM;;---------------------------
34::COMM;;By default, the ScrollView allows scrolling along both the X and Y axes. You
35::COMM;;can explicitly disable scrolling on an axis by setting the
36::COMM;;:attr:`~ScrollView.do_scroll_x` or :attr:`~ScrollView.do_scroll_y` properties
37::COMM;;to False.
38::COMM;;Managing the Content Size and Position
39::COMM;;--------------------------------------
40::COMM;;The ScrollView manages the position of its children similarly to a
41::COMM;;:class:`~kivy.uix.relativelayout.RelativeLayout` but does not use the
42::COMM;;:attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.size_hint`. You must
43::COMM;;carefully specify the :attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.size` of your content to
44::COMM;;get the desired scroll/pan effect.
45::COMM;;By default, the :attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.size_hint` is (1, 1), so the
46::COMM;;content size will fit your ScrollView
47::COMM;;exactly (you will have nothing to scroll). You must deactivate at least one of
48::COMM;;the size_hint instructions (x or y) of the child to enable scrolling.
49::COMM;;Setting :attr:`~kivy.uix.widget.Widget.size_hint_min` to not be None will
50::COMM;;also enable scrolling for that dimension when the :class:`ScrollView` is
51::COMM;;smaller than the minimum size.
52::COMM;;To scroll a :class:`~kivy.uix.gridlayout.GridLayout` on it's Y-axis/vertically,
53::COMM;;set the child's width to that of the ScrollView (size_hint_x=1), and set
54::COMM;;the size_hint_y property to None::
55::COMM;;from kivy.uix.gridlayout import GridLayout
56::COMM;;from kivy.uix.button import Button
57::COMM;;from kivy.uix.scrollview import ScrollView
58::COMM;;from kivy.core.window import Window
59::COMM;;from kivy.app import runTouchApp
60::COMM;;layout = GridLayout(cols=1, spacing=10, size_hint_y=None)
61::COMM;;# Make sure the height is such that there is something to scroll.
62::COMM;;layout.bind(minimum_height=layout.setter('height'))
63::COMM;;for i in range(100):
64::COMM;;btn = Button(text=str(i), size_hint_y=None, height=40)
65::COMM;;layout.add_widget(btn)
66::COMM;;root = ScrollView(size_hint=(1, None), size=(Window.width, Window.height))
67::COMM;;root.add_widget(layout)
68::COMM;;runTouchApp(root)
69::COMM;;Kv Example::
70::COMM;;ScrollView:
71::COMM;;do_scroll_x: False
72::COMM;;do_scroll_y: True
73::COMM;;Label:
74::COMM;;size_hint_y: None
75::COMM;;height: self.texture_size[1]
76::COMM;;text_size: self.width, None
77::COMM;;padding: 10, 10
78::COMM;;text:
79::COMM;;'really some amazing text\\n' * 100
80::COMM;;Overscroll Effects
81::COMM;;------------------
82::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.7.0
83::COMM;;When scrolling would exceed the bounds of the :class:`ScrollView`, it
84::COMM;;uses a :class:`~kivy.effects.scroll.ScrollEffect` to handle the
85::COMM;;overscroll. These effects can perform actions like bouncing back,
86::COMM;;changing opacity, or simply preventing scrolling beyond the normal
87::COMM;;boundaries. Note that complex effects may perform many computations,
88::COMM;;which can be slow on weaker hardware.
89::COMM;;You can change what effect is being used by setting
90::COMM;;:attr:`~ScrollView.effect_cls` to any effect class. Current options
91::COMM;;include:
92::COMM;;- :class:`~kivy.effects.scroll.ScrollEffect`: Does not allow
93::COMM;;scrolling beyond the :class:`ScrollView` boundaries.
94::COMM;;- :class:`~kivy.effects.dampedscroll.DampedScrollEffect`: The
95::COMM;;current default. Allows the user to scroll beyond the normal
96::COMM;;boundaries, but has the content spring back once the
97::COMM;;touch/click is released.
98::COMM;;- :class:`~kivy.effects.opacityscroll.OpacityScrollEffect`: Similar
99::COMM;;to the :class:`~kivy.effect.dampedscroll.DampedScrollEffect`, but
100::COMM;;also reduces opacity during overscroll.
101::COMM;;You can also create your own scroll effect by subclassing one of these,
102::COMM;;then pass it as the :attr:`~ScrollView.effect_cls` in the same way.
103::COMM;;Alternatively, you can set :attr:`~ScrollView.effect_x` and/or
104::COMM;;:attr:`~ScrollView.effect_y` to an *instance* of the effect you want to
105::COMM;;use. This will override the default effect set in
106::COMM;;:attr:`~ScrollView.effect_cls`.
107::COMM;;All the effects are located in the :mod:`kivy.effects`.
108::COMM;;Nested ScrollViews
109::COMM;;------------------
110::COMM;;An application can have multiple levels of nested ScrollViews. The
111::COMM;;ScrollView class manages the hierarchy of nested ScrollViews.
112::COMM;;It is important to set the :attr:`do_scroll_x` and :attr:`do_scroll_y`
113::COMM;;properties to the correct values for the nested ScrollViews.
114::COMM;;The nested scrolling behavior, described below, is only applied if the
115::COMM;;:attr:`do_scroll_x` and :attr:`do_scroll_y` properties are set to the
116::COMM;;appropriate values.
117::COMM;;To achieve orthogonal scrolling, for example, the outer
118::COMM;;ScrollView should have :attr:`do_scroll_x` set to False and the inner
119::COMM;;ScrollView should have :attr:`do_scroll_y` set to True, or vice versa.
120::COMM;;For Parallel scrolling, both ScrollViews should have the same value for
121::COMM;;:attr:`do_scroll_x` and :attr:`do_scroll_y`. This can allow vertical in
122::COMM;;vertical, horizontal in horizontal, or XY in XY scrolling.
123::COMM;;For mixed scrolling, the outer ScrollView should have :attr:`do_scroll_x`
124::COMM;;and :attr:`do_scroll_y` set to True, and the inner ScrollView should have
125::COMM;;either :attr:`do_scroll_x` or :attr:`do_scroll_y` set to False.
126::COMM;;**Orthogonal Scrolling** (outer and inner scroll in different directions):
127::COMM;;- Touch: Each ScrollView scrolls only in its direction
128::COMM;;- Wheel: Innermost ScrollView scrolls if it supports that axis
129::COMM;;- Example: Vertical outer + Horizontal inner
130::COMM;;**Parallel Scrolling** (outer and inner scroll in the same direction):
131::COMM;;- Touch: Web-style boundary delegation (see below)
132::COMM;;- Wheel: Innermost ScrollView scrolls, no delegation to outer
133::COMM;;- Scrollbar: Scroll does not affect other ScrollView
134::COMM;;- Example: Vertical outer + Vertical inner
135::COMM;;**Mixed Scrolling** (outer scrolls XY, inner one axis, or vice versa):
136::COMM;;- Shared axis: Web-style boundary delegation
137::COMM;;- Exclusive axes: Immediate delegation or inner-only scrolling
138::COMM;;- Wheel: Innermost ScrollView scrolls if it supports the axis
139::COMM;;- Example: XY outer + Horizontal inner
140::COMM;;Web-Style Boundary Delegation
141::COMM;;----------------------------
142::COMM;;For parallel and shared-axis scrolling, ScrollView uses web-style
143::COMM;;delegation:
144::COMM;;- If a touch starts at the inner boundary and moves out, it delegates
145::COMM;;scrolling to the outer ScrollView right away.
146::COMM;;- If a touch starts at the inner boundary and moves in, only the inner
147::COMM;;ScrollView scrolls.
148::COMM;;- If a touch starts not at a boundary, only the inner ScrollView
149::COMM;;scrolls, even if the gesture later reaches a boundary. Delegation to
150::COMM;;the outer never occurs mid-gesture in this case.
151::COMM;;- A new touch starting at the boundary is required to delegate to the
152::COMM;;outer.
153::COMM;;Disable this behavior by setting :attr:`parallel_delegation` to False.
154::COMM;;Wheel Behavior in Nested ScrollViews
155::COMM;;------------------------------------
156::COMM;;When the mouse scroll wheel or a trackpad is used, ScrollView always
157::COMM;;applies web-style delegation:
158::COMM;;- Only the innermost ScrollView under the pointer/cursor will handle
159::COMM;;the wheel event.
160::COMM;;- If that ScrollView cannot scroll further along the wheel axis, the
161::COMM;;event is not propagated to outer ScrollViews. This matches standard
162::COMM;;browser and OS behavior.
163::COMM;;- Outer ScrollViews never respond to wheel events unless the pointer is
164::COMM;;over their scrollbars or unless there are no deeper nested
165::COMM;;ScrollViews.
166::COMM;;This prevents "scroll hijacking" and provides an intuitive nested scroll
167::COMM;;experience.
168::COMM;;**Examples:**
169::COMM;;- In a vertical ScrollView containing a horizontal ScrollView, using the
170::COMM;;wheel over the horizontal ScrollView means only the vertical (outer)
171::COMM;;ScrollView scrolls, if its direction matches the wheel.
172::COMM;;- For two nested vertical ScrollViews, the innermost one under the
173::COMM;;pointer will scroll with the wheel until it cannot scroll further;
174::COMM;;wheel events are not delegated to the parent.
175::COMM;;Wheel behavior is always active and is NOT affected by the
176::COMM;;:attr:`parallel_delegation` or :attr:`delegate_to_outer` properties.
177::COMM;;Those only control touch and touchpad gesture behavior.
178::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: VERSION_NEXT
179::COMM;;The ScrollView widgetnow supports nesting to arbitrary levels
180::COMM;;and configurations.
205::COMO;;# =============================================================================
206::COMO;;# STATE MACHINE ENUMS
207::COMO;;# =============================================================================
209::COMO;;# Touch intent detection state machine.
210::COMO;;# Tracks whether a touch gesture is a tap/click or a scroll gesture
211::COMO;;# based on movement distance and timeout thresholds.
212::COMO;;# State Transition Diagram:
213::COMO;;#
214::COMO;;# movement > scroll_distance
215::COMO;;# ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
216::COMO;;# │ │
217::COMO;;# │ v
218::COMO;;# ┌─────────┐ ┌────────┐
219::COMO;;# │ UNKNOWN │ │ SCROLL │
220::COMO;;# └─────────┘ └────────┘
221::COMO;;# │ ^
222::COMO;;# │ timeout expires │
223::COMO;;# v │
224::COMO;;# try _simulate_touch_down() │
225::COMO;;# │ │
226::COMO;;# ┌──────────┴──────────┐ │
227::COMO;;# │ │ │
228::COMO;;# child grabbed no child grabbed │
229::COMO;;# │ │ │
230::COMO;;# v └──────────────────────┘
231::COMO;;# hand off to child transition to SCROLL mode
232::COMO;;# (button, etc.) (label, empty space, etc.)
233::COMO;;#
234::COMO;;# State Descriptions:
235::COMO;;# - UNKNOWN: Initial state, accumulating movement to detect intent
236::COMO;;# - SCROLL: Scroll gesture confirmed - either movement exceeded threshold
237::COMO;;# OR timeout expired without child widget consuming the touch
238::COMC;;UNKNOWN = "unknown" # Detecting intent - accumulating movement
239::COMC;;SCROLL = "scroll" # Confirmed scroll gesture - movement exceeded threshold
242::COMM;;# Controls when an inner ScrollView delegates scrolling to its outer
243::COMM;;# ScrollView in parallel nested configurations (both scrolling same axis).
244::COMM;;# State Descriptions:
245::COMM;;# - UNLOCKED: Normal scrolling, no delegation. Inner scrolls freely.
246::COMM;;# - START_AT_BOUNDARY: Touch began at inner's boundary.
247::COMM;;# Watching movement direction.
248::COMM;;# - LOCKED: Touch trying to scroll beyond boundary.
249::COMM;;# Outer takes over, inner blocked.
250::COMM;;# State Transition Diagram:
251::COMM;;# Touch starts NOT at boundary:
252::COMM;;# ┌──────────┐
253::COMM;;# │ UNLOCKED │ (stays UNLOCKED entire gesture, inner scrolls freely)
254::COMM;;# └──────────┘
255::COMM;;# Touch starts AT boundary:
256::COMM;;# ┌──────────────────┐
257::COMM;;# │ START_AT_BOUNDARY│─────┐
258::COMM;;# └──────────────────┘ │
259::COMM;;# │ │
260::COMM;;# │ │
261::COMM;;# move into content scroll beyond boundary
262::COMM;;# │ │
263::COMM;;# v v
264::COMM;;# ┌──────────┐ ┌────────┐
265::COMM;;# │ UNLOCKED │ │ LOCKED │ (stays LOCKED entire gesture)
266::COMM;;# └──────────┘ └────────┘
267::COMM;;# Key: Once LOCKED, stays LOCKED until touch release (no transitions out)
268::COMM;;# Example (Vertical Parallel):
269::COMM;;# 1. User touches inner ScrollView at bottom (scroll_y = 1.0)
270::COMM;;# -> START_AT_BOUNDARY
271::COMM;;# 2a. User drags down (into content) -> UNLOCKED (inner scrolls normally)
272::COMM;;# 2b. User drags up (beyond bottom edge) -> LOCKED (outer takes over)
273::COMM;;# 3. If LOCKED: stays LOCKED, outer handles all further movement
274::COMM;;UNLOCKED = "unlocked" # Normal scrolling, no delegation active
275::COMM;;START_AT_BOUNDARY = "start_at_boundary" # Touch began at scroll boundary
276::COMM;;LOCKED = "locked" # At boundary trying to scroll beyond - delegate to outer
277::COMM;;# =============================================================================
278::COMM;;# HIERARCHY MANAGEMENT CLASS
279::COMM;;# =============================================================================
280::COMM;;class ScrollViewHierarchy:
281::COMM;;# INTERNAL CLASS - Manages the hierarchy of nested ScrollViews for a
282::COMM;;# touch gesture.
283::COMM;;#
284::COMM;;# Stores ScrollViews from outermost (index 0) to innermost (index n).
285::COMM;;# Each ScrollView can use its index to find its parent and navigate
286::COMM;;# the chain.
287::COMM;;#
288::COMM;;# Design Philosophy:
289::COMM;;# - ScrollViews are stored in a list
290::COMM;;# (scrollviews[0] = outer, scrollviews[-1] = inner)
291::COMM;;# - Relationship data (classification, axis_config) stored separately
292::COMM;;# - Classifications describe relationships BETWEEN levels,
293::COMM;;# not properties OF levels
294::COMM;;# - Index arithmetic is encapsulated in methods for safety
295::COMM;;#
296::COMM;;# Example for 3-level hierarchy (outer → middle → inner):
297::COMM;;# scrollviews = [outer, middle, inner]
298::COMM;;# _parent_child_data = [
299::COMM;;# {classification: 'parallel', axis_config: None}, # outer→middle
300::COMM;;# {classification: 'orthogonal', axis_config: None} # middle→inner
301::COMM;;# ]
302::COMM;;def __init__(self, outer_sv):
303::COMM;;# Initialize hierarchy with the outermost ScrollView.
304::COMM;;# Args:
305::COMM;;# outer_sv: The outermost ScrollView in the hierarchy
306::COMM;;self.scrollviews = [outer_sv] # List from outer to inner
307::COMM;;self._parent_child_data = (
308::COMM;;[]
309::COMM;;) # Relationship data between adjacent levels
310::COMM;;self.touched_index = 0 # Index of ScrollView where touch started
311::COMM;;def add_child(self, child_sv, classification, axis_config=None):
312::COMM;;# Add a child ScrollView to the hierarchy.
313::COMM;;# Args:
314::COMM;;# child_sv: The child ScrollView to add
315::COMM;;# classification: 'orthogonal', 'parallel', or 'mixed'
316::COMM;;# axis_config: Dict with axis configuration (only for mixed)
317::COMM;;self.scrollviews.append(child_sv)
318::COMM;;self._parent_child_data.append(
319::COMM;;{"classification": classification, "axis_config": axis_config}
320::COMM;;)
321::COMM;;self.touched_index = len(self.scrollviews) - 1
322::COMM;;def get_parent(self, current_index):
323::COMM;;# Get parent ScrollView for given index.
324::COMM;;# Args:
325::COMM;;# current_index: Index of the child ScrollView
326::COMM;;# Returns:
327::COMM;;# Parent ScrollView, or None if at root (index 0)
328::COMM;;if current_index > 0:
329::COMM;;return self.scrollviews[current_index - 1]
330::COMM;;return None
331::COMM;;def get_relationship(self, child_index):
332::COMM;;# Get relationship data between child at child_index and its parent.
333::COMM;;# Encapsulates the index arithmetic for accessing relationship data.
334::COMM;;# Args:
335::COMM;;# child_index: Index of the child ScrollView
336::COMM;;# Returns:
337::COMM;;# Dict with 'classification' and 'axis_config', or None if no parent
338::COMM;;if 0 < child_index < len(self.scrollviews):
339::COMM;;return self._parent_child_data[child_index - 1]
340::COMM;;return None
341::COMM;;def get_classification(self, child_index):
342::COMM;;# Get classification between child and its parent.
343::COMM;;# Args:
344::COMM;;# child_index: Index of the child ScrollView
345::COMM;;# Returns:
346::COMM;;# Classification string ('orthogonal', 'parallel', 'mixed'),
347::COMM;;# or None if child_index is 0 (no parent)
348::COMM;;rel = self.get_relationship(child_index)
349::COMM;;return rel["classification"] if rel else None
350::COMM;;def get_axis_config(self, child_index):
351::COMM;;# Get axis configuration for mixed classification.
352::COMM;;# Args:
353::COMM;;# child_index: Index of the child ScrollView
354::COMM;;# Returns:
355::COMM;;# Axis config dict for mixed cases, or None
356::COMM;;rel = self.get_relationship(child_index)
357::COMM;;return rel["axis_config"] if rel else None
358::COMM;;@property
359::COMM;;def depth(self):
360::COMM;;# Total depth of hierarchy (number of levels).
361::COMM;;return len(self.scrollviews)
362::COMM;;@property
363::COMM;;def outer(self):
364::COMM;;# Outermost ScrollView (index 0).
365::COMM;;return self.scrollviews[0]
366::COMM;;@property
367::COMM;;def inner(self):
368::COMM;;# Innermost ScrollView (last in list).
369::COMM;;return self.scrollviews[-1]
370::COMM;;# =============================================================================
371::COMM;;# CONFIGURATION CONSTANTS
372::COMM;;# =============================================================================
373::COMM;;# Boundary threshold for web-style delegation
374::COMM;;# (normalized scroll position 0.0 to 1.0)
375::COMM;;# A ScrollView is considered "at boundary" if scroll position is
376::COMM;;# within this threshold of the minimum (0.0) or maximum (1.0) position.
377::COMM;;# Used for parallel nested scrolling to determine when to delegate
378::COMM;;# to outer ScrollView.
379::COMM;;# Note: Set to 15% to account for elastic overscroll bounce-back
380::COMM;;_BOUNDARY_THRESHOLD = 0.15 # 15% from edge
381::COMM;;# When we are generating documentation, Config doesn't exist

858::COMM;;def _simulate_touch_down(self, touch):

885::COMM;;def _delegate_to_children(self, touch, method_name, check_collision=True):
886::COMM;;# Generic helper function to safely delegate touch events to child
887::COMM;;# widgets.
888::COMM;;# Handles coordinate transformation and returns the result.

909::COMM;;def _find_child_scrollview_at_touch(self, touch):
910::COMM;;# Find the child ScrollView that collides with the touch position.
911::COMM;;#
912::COMM;;# Strategy: When we encounter a Layout,
913::COMM;;# we first identify which specific child collides with the touch,
914::COMM;;# then only explore that child's subtree. This naturally handles
915::COMM;;# arbitrary depth and prevents finding ScrollViews from unrelated
916::COMM;;# sibling branches.
917::COMM;;#
918::COMM;;# Returns:
919::COMM;;# ScrollView: The first child ScrollView that collides with touch,
920::COMM;;# or None
921::COMM;;viewport = self._viewport
922::COMM;;# Safety checks: viewport must exist and have children
923::COMM;;if not viewport:
924::COMM;;return None
925::COMM;;if not hasattr(viewport, "children"):
926::COMM;;return None
927::COMM;;if not viewport.children:
928::COMM;;return None
929::COMM;;# Transform touch to viewport space
930::COMM;;touch.push()
931::COMM;;touch.apply_transform_2d(viewport.to_widget)
932::COMM;;result = self._find_scrollview_in_widget(viewport, touch)
933::COMM;;touch.pop()
934::COMM;;return result
935::COMM;;def _find_scrollview_in_widget(self, widget, touch):
936::COMM;;# Recursively find ScrollView under touch, narrowing by Layout children.
937::COMM;;#
938::COMM;;# When we encounter a widget with children (a Layout), we first
939::COMM;;# identify which specific child collides with the touch point, then
940::COMM;;# only explore that child's subtree. This prevents finding ScrollViews
941::COMM;;# from unrelated sibling branches.
942::COMM;;#
943::COMM;;# Args:
944::COMM;;# widget: The widget to search within
945::COMM;;# touch: The touch event (already transformed to appropriate space)
946::COMM;;#
947::COMM;;# Returns:
948::COMM;;# ScrollView or None: The first ScrollView found under touch
949::COMM;;# If this widget has children,
950::COMM;;# narrow down which child contains the touch
951::COMM;;if hasattr(widget, "children") and widget.children:
952::COMM;;for child in widget.children:
953::COMM;;# Skip children that don't collide with touch
954::COMM;;if not child.collide_point(*touch.pos):
955::COMM;;continue
956::COMM;;# Found a colliding child - is it a ScrollView?
957::COMM;;if isinstance(child, ScrollView):
958::COMM;;return child
959::COMM;;# Not a ScrollView, but it collides -
960::COMM;;# recursively search its subtree
961::COMM;;result = self._find_scrollview_in_widget(child, touch)
962::COMM;;if result:
963::COMM;;return result
964::COMM;;# No children or no colliding children with ScrollViews
965::COMM;;return None
966::COMM;;def _build_hierarchy_recursive(self, touch):
967::COMM;;# Build complete ScrollView hierarchy from this (outer) to innermost.
968::COMM;;#
969::COMM;;# Recursively finds all nested ScrollViews under the touch point and
970::COMM;;# builds a ScrollViewHierarchy object with classifications for each
971::COMM;;# parent-child relationship.
972::COMM;;#
973::COMM;;# Args:
974::COMM;;# touch: The touch event
975::COMM;;#
976::COMM;;# Returns:
977::COMM;;# ScrollViewHierarchy or None: Complete hierarchy from this (outer)
978::COMM;;# to innermost, or None if no children
979::COMM;;# Find immediate child
980::COMM;;child_sv = self._find_child_scrollview_at_touch(touch)
981::COMM;;if not child_sv:
982::COMM;;return None
983::COMM;;# Start building hierarchy with self as outer
984::COMM;;hierarchy = ScrollViewHierarchy(self)
985::COMM;;# Recursively build the chain
986::COMM;;current_sv = child_sv
987::COMM;;parent_sv = self
988::COMM;;while current_sv:
989::COMM;;# Classify this parent-child relationship
990::COMM;;config_type, axis_config = (
991::COMM;;parent_sv._classify_nested_configuration(current_sv))
992::COMM;;# Add to hierarchy
993::COMM;;hierarchy.add_child(current_sv, config_type, axis_config)
994::COMM;;# Look for next level down
995::COMM;;parent_sv = current_sv
996::COMM;;current_sv = current_sv._find_child_scrollview_at_touch(touch)
997::COMM;;return hierarchy
998::COMM;;def _get_nested_data(self, touch):
999::COMM;;# Extract nested coordination data for this ScrollView from touch.
1000::COMM;;#
1001::COMM;;# Provides convenient access to hierarchy, current index, and parent
1002::COMM;;# for arbitrary depth nesting. This method makes it easy for any
1003::COMM;;# ScrollView in the hierarchy to find its place and navigate.
1004::COMM;;#
1005::COMM;;# NOTE: This method is for FUTURE arbitrary nesting support (Phase 3+).
1006::COMM;;# Currently NOT USED by 2-level delegation logic. Will be integrated
1007::COMM;;# when chain delegation is implemented.
1008::COMM;;#
1009::COMM;;# Args:
1010::COMM;;# touch: The touch event
1011::COMM;;#
1012::COMM;;# Returns:
1013::COMM;;# tuple: (hierarchy, my_index, parent_sv) where:
1014::COMM;;# - hierarchy: ScrollViewHierarchy object
1015::COMM;;# - my_index: Index of this ScrollView in the hierarchy
1016::COMM;;# - parent_sv: Parent ScrollView, or None if this is outermost
1017::COMM;;#
1018::COMM;;# Returns (None, None, None) if not in a nested configuration
1019::COMM;;# or if this ScrollView is not found in the hierarchy.
1020::COMM;;if "nested" not in touch.ud:
1021::COMM;;return None, None, None
1022::COMM;;if "hierarchy" not in touch.ud["nested"]:
1023::COMM;;return None, None, None
1024::COMM;;hierarchy = touch.ud["nested"]["hierarchy"]
1025::COMM;;# Find our index in the hierarchy
1026::COMM;;my_index = None
1027::COMM;;for i, sv in enumerate(hierarchy.scrollviews):
1028::COMM;;if sv is self:
1029::COMM;;my_index = i
1030::COMM;;break
1031::COMM;;if my_index is None:
1032::COMM;;return None, None, None
1033::COMM;;parent_sv = hierarchy.get_parent(my_index)
1034::COMM;;return hierarchy, my_index, parent_sv
1035::COMM;;def _get_primary_scroll_axis(self, touch):
1036::COMM;;# Determine which axis has dominant touch movement.
1037::COMM;;#
1038::COMM;;# Compares absolute X and Y deltas to determine the primary direction
1039::COMM;;# of the current touch movement. Used for axis-specific scroll logic.
1040::COMM;;#
1041::COMM;;# Args:
1042::COMM;;# touch: Touch event with dx and dy attributes
1043::COMM;;#
1044::COMM;;# Returns:
1045::COMM;;# str: 'x' if horizontal movement dominates,
1046::COMM;;# 'y' if vertical movement dominates,
1047::COMM;;# None if no clear dominance
1048::COMM;;abs_dx = abs(touch.dx)
1049::COMM;;abs_dy = abs(touch.dy)
1050::COMM;;if abs_dx > abs_dy:
1051::COMM;;return "x"
1052::COMM;;elif abs_dy > abs_dx:
1053::COMM;;return "y"
1054::COMM;;return None
1055::COMM;;def _classify_nested_configuration(self, child_sv):
1056::COMM;;# Classify the nested ScrollView configuration type.
1057::COMM;;#
1058::COMM;;# Determines if the outer/inner relationship is:
1059::COMM;;# - Orthogonal: Different axes (e.g., outer=vertical, inner=horizontal)
1060::COMM;;# - Parallel: Same axes (e.g., both vertical)
1061::COMM;;# - Mixed: Combination (e.g., outer=xy, inner=vertical)
1062::COMM;;#
1063::COMM;;# Args:
1064::COMM;;# child_sv: The inner ScrollView
1065::COMM;;#
1066::COMM;;# Returns:
1067::COMM;;# tuple: (config_type, axis_config)
1068::COMM;;# config_type: 'orthogonal', 'parallel', or 'mixed'
1069::COMM;;# axis_config: dict with 'shared', 'outer_exclusive',
1070::COMM;;# 'inner_exclusive'
1071::COMM;;# (only for mixed configurations, None otherwise)
1072::COMM;;outer_axes = (self.do_scroll_x, self.do_scroll_y)
1073::COMM;;inner_axes = (child_sv.do_scroll_x, child_sv.do_scroll_y)
1074::COMM;;# Determine configuration type
1075::COMM;;is_orthogonal = (
1076::COMM;;outer_axes[0] != inner_axes[0]
1077::COMM;;and outer_axes[1] != inner_axes[1]
1078::COMM;;and (outer_axes[0] or outer_axes[1])
1079::COMM;;and (inner_axes[0] or inner_axes[1])
1080::COMM;;)
1081::COMM;;if is_orthogonal:
1082::COMM;;return ("orthogonal", None)
1083::COMM;;is_parallel = outer_axes == inner_axes
1084::COMM;;if is_parallel:
1085::COMM;;return ("parallel", None)
1086::COMM;;# Mixed configuration - determine axis capabilities
1087::COMM;;shared = []
1088::COMM;;outer_exclusive = []
1089::COMM;;inner_exclusive = []
1090::COMM;;# Check X axis
1091::COMM;;if outer_axes[0] and inner_axes[0]:
1092::COMM;;shared.append("x")
1093::COMM;;elif outer_axes[0] and not inner_axes[0]:
1094::COMM;;outer_exclusive.append("x")
1095::COMM;;elif not outer_axes[0] and inner_axes[0]:
1096::COMM;;inner_exclusive.append("x")
1097::COMM;;# Check Y axis
1098::COMM;;if outer_axes[1] and inner_axes[1]:
1099::COMM;;shared.append("y")
1100::COMM;;elif outer_axes[1] and not inner_axes[1]:
1101::COMM;;outer_exclusive.append("y")
1102::COMM;;elif not outer_axes[1] and inner_axes[1]:
1103::COMM;;inner_exclusive.append("y")
1104::COMM;;axis_config = {
1105::COMM;;"shared": shared,
1106::COMM;;"outer_exclusive": outer_exclusive,
1107::COMM;;"inner_exclusive": inner_exclusive,
1108::COMM;;}
1109::COMM;;return ("mixed", axis_config)
1110::COMM;;def _initialize_nested_inner(self, touch, child_sv):
1111::COMM;;# Initialize scrolling on the inner ScrollView with proper coordinate
1112::COMM;;# transformation.
1113::COMM;;#
1114::COMM;;#
1115::COMM;;# Args:
1116::COMM;;# touch: The touch/mouse event
1117::COMM;;# child_sv: The inner ScrollView to initialize
1118::COMM;;#
1119::COMM;;# Returns:
1120::COMM;;# bool: True if scrolling was successfully initialized,
1121::COMM;;# False if both rejected the touch

1269::COMM;;def _detect_scroll_intent(self, touch, ud):
1270::COMM;;# Detect if touch movement indicates scroll intent vs click.
1271::COMM;;#
1272::COMM;;# Tracks cumulative movement while in 'unknown' mode. Once movement
1273::COMM;;# exceeds scroll_distance threshold, transitions to 'scroll' mode.
1274::COMM;;#
1275::COMM;;# Args:
1276::COMM;;# touch: The touch event
1277::COMM;;# ud: The touch's user data dict for this ScrollView
1278::COMM;;#
1279::COMM;;# Returns:
1280::COMM;;# bool: True if processing should continue, False if rejected
1281::COMM;;if not (self.do_scroll_x or self.do_scroll_y):
1282::COMM;;# No scrolling enabled - trigger mode change to delegate to children
1283::COMM;;# Touch is in parent coords, but _change_touch_mode expects
1284::COMM;;# window coords
1285::COMM;;touch.push()
1286::COMM;;touch.apply_transform_2d(self.to_local)
1287::COMM;;touch.apply_transform_2d(self.to_window)
1288::COMM;;self._change_touch_mode()
1289::COMM;;touch.pop()

1291::COMM;;# Accumulate absolute movement on both axes
1292::COMM;;ud["dx"] += abs(touch.dx)
1293::COMM;;ud["dy"] += abs(touch.dy)
1294::COMM;;# Transition to scroll mode if movement exceeds threshold
1295::COMM;;if ud["dx"] > self.scroll_distance or ud["dy"] > self.scroll_distance:
1296::COMM;;ud["mode"] = ScrollMode.SCROLL
1297::COMM;;# Only dispatch on_scroll_start if we weren't already scrolling
1298::COMM;;# (e.g. from scrollbar)
1299::COMM;;if not ud["scroll_action"]:
1300::COMM;;self.dispatch("on_scroll_start")
1301::COMM;;return True
1302::COMM;;def _check_nested_delegation(self, touch, not_in_bar):
1303::COMM;;# Check if this ScrollView should delegate to its parent in hierarchy.
1304::COMM;;#
1305::COMM;;# Uses the hierarchy to find this ScrollView's relationship with
1306::COMM;;# its parent and calls the appropriate delegation method.
1307::COMM;;# Supports arbitrary depth.
1308::COMM;;#
1309::COMM;;# Only applies to ScrollViews scrolling content (not scrollbars).
1310::COMM;;#
1311::COMM;;# Args:
1312::COMM;;# touch: The touch event
1313::COMM;;# not_in_bar: Whether touch is NOT in a scrollbar
1314::COMM;;#
1315::COMM;;# Returns:
1316::COMM;;# bool: True if should delegate to parent
1317::COMM;;# False if should continue handling
1318::COMM;;# Only check delegation for nested ScrollViews scrolling content
1319::COMM;;if "nested" not in touch.ud:
1320::COMM;;return False
1321::COMM;;if not not_in_bar:
1322::COMM;;return False

1324::COMM;;hierarchy, my_index, parent_sv = self._get_nested_data(touch)
1325::COMM;;# Check if delegation to outer is enabled
1326::COMM;;if not self.delegate_to_outer:
1327::COMM;;return False # Delegation disabled - don't cascade to parent
1328::COMM;;if not hierarchy or parent_sv is None:
1329::COMM;;return False # Not nested or we're the outer - no delegation
1330::COMM;;# Only check delegation if we're the CURRENT handler in the hierarchy
1331::COMM;;# For arbitrary depth: check current_index
1332::COMM;;# Check if we're the current handler (hierarchy-based routing)
1333::COMM;;if "current_index" not in touch.ud["nested"]:
1334::COMM;;# No routing info - shouldn't happen but be safe
1335::COMM;;return False
1336::COMM;;if my_index != touch.ud["nested"]["current_index"]:
1337::COMM;;return False # Not our turn to handle, don't delegate
1338::COMM;;# CROSS-AXIS DELEGATION: Check FIRST if gesture is on an axis we can't
1339::COMM;;# handle. This applies regardless of our relationship type with our
1340::COMM;;# immediate child
1341::COMM;;# Example: V outer (can't scroll X) in V→H should delegate X gestures
1342::COMM;;# to outer XY above
1343::COMM;;primary_axis = self._get_primary_scroll_axis(touch)
1344::COMM;;if primary_axis == "x" and not self.do_scroll_x:
1345::COMM;;# Horizontal gesture but we only scroll vertically - delegate upward
1346::COMM;;return True
1347::COMM;;if primary_axis == "y" and not self.do_scroll_y:
1348::COMM;;# Vertical gesture but we only scroll horizontally - delegate upward
1349::COMM;;return True
1350::COMM;;# Get our relationship with immediate parent
1351::COMM;;classification = hierarchy.get_classification(my_index)
1352::COMM;;axis_config = hierarchy.get_axis_config(my_index)
1353::COMM;;# Dispatch to appropriate delegation method based on classification
1354::COMM;;if classification == "orthogonal":
1355::COMM;;# Check immediate parent first (standard orthogonal delegation)
1356::COMM;;if self._should_delegate_orthogonal(touch, parent_sv):
1357::COMM;;return True
1358::COMM;;# PHASE 8: Non-adjacent parallel delegation
1359::COMM;;# If orthogonal with immediate parent but we're at boundary AND
1360::COMM;;# trying to scroll beyond,look for a parallel ancestor further up
1361::COMM;;# the hierarchy
1362::COMM;;# Example: V->H->V, inner V at boundary should delegate to outer V
1363::COMM;;primary_axis = self._get_primary_scroll_axis(touch)
1364::COMM;;if primary_axis and self._is_scrolling_beyond_boundary(
1365::COMM;;primary_axis, touch
1366::COMM;;):

1368::COMM;;# search for parallel ancestor
1369::COMM;;parallel_ancestor, ancestor_idx = self._find_parallel_ancestor(
1370::COMM;;touch, primary_axis
1371::COMM;;)
1372::COMM;;if parallel_ancestor and parallel_ancestor.parallel_delegation:
1373::COMM;;# Found ancestor that can handle this axis with
1374::COMM;;# parallel_delegation enabled
1375::COMM;;# Delegate to it
1376::COMM;;# (cascade will update current_index to ancestor_idx)
1377::COMM;;touch.ud["nested"]["parallel_ancestor_index"] = ancestor_idx
1378::COMM;;return True
1379::COMM;;return False
1380::COMM;;elif classification == "mixed":
1381::COMM;;return self._should_delegate_mixed(touch, parent_sv, axis_config)
1382::COMM;;elif classification == "parallel":
1383::COMM;;return self._should_delegate_parallel(touch, parent_sv)
1384::COMM;;return False
1385::COMM;;def _is_at_scroll_boundary(self, axis):
1386::COMM;;# Check if this ScrollView is at a scroll boundary on the given axis.
1387::COMM;;#
1388::COMM;;# Args:
1389::COMM;;# axis: 'x' or 'y' - the axis to check
1390::COMM;;#
1391::COMM;;# Returns:
1392::COMM;;# bool: True if at boundary (near 0.0 or 1.0), False otherwise
1393::COMM;;if axis == "x":
1394::COMM;;if not self.do_scroll_x:
1395::COMM;;return False
1396::COMM;;scroll_pos = self.scroll_x
1397::COMM;;elif axis == "y":
1398::COMM;;if not self.do_scroll_y:
1399::COMM;;return False
1400::COMM;;scroll_pos = self.scroll_y
1401::COMM;;else:
1402::COMM;;return False
1403::COMM;;# At boundary if within threshold of min or max
1404::COMM;;return scroll_pos <= _BOUNDARY_THRESHOLD or scroll_pos >= (
1405::COMM;;1.0 - _BOUNDARY_THRESHOLD
1406::COMM;;)
1407::COMM;;def _is_scrolling_beyond_boundary(self, axis, touch):
1408::COMM;;# Check if scroll gesture is trying to move beyond the current boundary.
1409::COMM;;#
1410::COMM;;# Args:
1411::COMM;;# axis: 'x' or 'y' - the axis to check
1412::COMM;;# touch: The touch event
1413::COMM;;#
1414::COMM;;# Returns:
1415::COMM;;# bool: True if at boundary AND trying to scroll beyond it
1416::COMM;;if axis == "x":
1417::COMM;;if not self.do_scroll_x:
1418::COMM;;return False
1419::COMM;;scroll_pos = self.scroll_x
1420::COMM;;# Check scroll direction from touch movement
1421::COMM;;dx = touch.dx if hasattr(touch, "dx") else (touch.x - touch.px)
1422::COMM;;# At left boundary (scroll_x ~= 0.0) trying to scroll further left
1423::COMM;;if scroll_pos <= _BOUNDARY_THRESHOLD and dx > 0:
1424::COMM;;return True
1425::COMM;;# At right boundary (scroll_x ~= 1.0) trying to scroll further right
1426::COMM;;if scroll_pos >= (1.0 - _BOUNDARY_THRESHOLD) and dx < 0:
1427::COMM;;return True
1428::COMM;;elif axis == "y":
1429::COMM;;if not self.do_scroll_y:
1430::COMM;;return False
1431::COMM;;scroll_pos = self.scroll_y
1432::COMM;;# Check scroll direction from touch movement
1433::COMM;;dy = touch.dy if hasattr(touch, "dy") else (touch.y - touch.py)
1434::COMM;;# At top boundary (scroll_y ~= 0.0) trying to scroll further up
1435::COMM;;if scroll_pos <= _BOUNDARY_THRESHOLD and dy > 0:
1436::COMM;;return True
1437::COMM;;# At bottom boundary (scroll_y ~= 1.0) trying to scroll further down
1438::COMM;;if scroll_pos >= (1.0 - _BOUNDARY_THRESHOLD) and dy < 0:
1439::COMM;;return True
1440::COMM;;return False
1441::COMM;;def _find_parallel_ancestor(self, touch, axis):
1442::COMM;;# Find nearest ancestor in hierarchy that can scroll on the given axis.
1443::COMM;;#
1444::COMM;;# Skips orthogonal intermediates to enable non-adjacent parallel
1445::COMM;;# delegation. Used: V->H->V boundary delegation.
1446::COMM;;#
1447::COMM;;# CRITICAL: Respects delegate_to_outer property. If an intermediate
1448::COMM;;# ScrollView has delegate_to_outer=False, we stop searching there
1449::COMM;;# (acting as a delegation barrier).
1450::COMM;;#
1451::COMM;;# Args:
1452::COMM;;# touch: The touch event
1453::COMM;;# axis: 'x' or 'y' - the axis to search for
1454::COMM;;#
1455::COMM;;# Returns:
1456::COMM;;# tuple: (ancestor_sv, ancestor_index) if found,
1457::COMM;;# (None, None) if not found
1458::COMM;;#
1459::COMM;;# Example:
1460::COMM;;# V->H->V hierarchy: Inner V at boundary, searching for 'y'
1461::COMM;;# - Skips Middle H (can't scroll Y)
1462::COMM;;# - Returns Outer V (can scroll Y)
1463::COMM;;#
1464::COMM;;# BUT if Outer V has delegate_to_outer=False:
1465::COMM;;# - Returns (None, None) - can't delegate past the barrier
1466::COMM;;hierarchy, my_index, _ = self._get_nested_data(touch)
1467::COMM;;if not hierarchy:
1468::COMM;;return None, None
1469::COMM;;# Walk up hierarchy looking for ancestor that can scroll on this axis
1470::COMM;;for i in range(my_index - 1, -1, -1):
1471::COMM;;ancestor = hierarchy.scrollviews[i]
1472::COMM;;# CRITICAL: Check if this ancestor allows delegation through it
1473::COMM;;# If delegate_to_outer=False, it acts as a barrier
1474::COMM;;# - stop searching here
1475::COMM;;if not ancestor.delegate_to_outer:
1476::COMM;;return None, None
1477::COMM;;# Check if this ancestor can handle the axis we need
1478::COMM;;if axis == "x" and ancestor.do_scroll_x:
1479::COMM;;return ancestor, i
1480::COMM;;if axis == "y" and ancestor.do_scroll_y:
1481::COMM;;return ancestor, i
1482::COMM;;return None, None

1913::COMM;;# TOUCH USER DATA (touch.ud) KEY DOCUMENTATION
1914::COMM;;# ============================================
1915::COMM;;# This section documents all touch.ud keys used across ScrollView.
1916::COMM;;#
1917::COMM;;# KEY NAMING CONVENTIONS:
1918::COMM;;# ----------------------
1919::COMM;;#
1920::COMM;;# PER-INSTANCE 'sv.' NAMESPACE:
1921::COMM;;# -----------------------------
1922::COMM;;# ScrollView uses 'sv.' prefixed keys via _get_uid() to create
1923::COMM;;# instance-specific keys like 'sv.123', where 123 is the widget's
1924::COMM;;# unique ID. Each ScrollView only checks its own keys - they do NOT
1925::COMM;;# share or coordinate via these keys.
1926::COMM;;#
1927::COMM;;# Per-ScrollView Instance Keys:
1928::COMM;;# - sv.<uid>: Primary state dict for this ScrollView instance
1929::COMM;;# Contains:
1930::COMM;;# {
1931::COMM;;# 'mode': ScrollMode, # State: UNKNOWN (detecting intent)
1932::COMM;;# # -> SCROLL (confirmed)
1933::COMM;;# 'dx': float, # accumulated absolute X movement
1934::COMM;;# # for detection
1935::COMM;;# 'dy': float, # accumulated absolute Y movement
1936::COMM;;# # for detection
1937::COMM;;# 'scroll_action': bool, # True if touch started in scrollbar
1938::COMM;;# # (skips on_scroll_start dispatch)
1939::COMM;;# 'frames': int, # Clock.frames at touch start (timing)
1940::COMM;;# 'can_defocus': bool, # Whether this touch can defocus
1941::COMM;;# # focused widgets
1942::COMM;;# }
1943::COMM;;#
1944::COMM;;# - svavoid.<uid>: Flag indicating this ScrollView should avoid
1945::COMM;;# handling this touch
1946::COMM;;# Set when: Mouse wheel events are handled, or touch doesn't
1947::COMM;;# collide
1948::COMM;;# Purpose: Prevents double-processing of already-handled touches
1949::COMM;;#
1950::COMM;;# Note: Each widget (ScrollView, DragBehavior) has its own
1951::COMM;;# UID-namespaced svavoid key. Widgets do NOT coordinate via svavoid
1952::COMM;;# - each checks only its own key.
1953::COMM;;#
1954::COMM;;# Cross-ScrollView Shared Keys:
1955::COMM;;# - sv.handled: dict {'x': bool, 'y': bool}
1956::COMM;;# Purpose: Tracks which axes have been processed by a ScrollView
1957::COMM;;# Lifecycle: Set at start of on_touch_move, updated during scroll
1958::COMM;;# processing
1959::COMM;;#
1960::COMM;;# - sv.claimed_by_child: bool
1961::COMM;;# Set when: _change_touch_mode delegates touch to children and
1962::COMM;;# child grabs (timeout expired)
1963::COMM;;# Purpose: Signals a child widget (button, etc.) has claimed this
1964::COMM;;# touch. Prevents ANY ScrollView from processing scroll gestures.
1965::COMM;;# ScrollView becomes transparent, calling super() to propagate
1966::COMM;;# touch properly.
1967::COMM;;# Used in: _scroll_initialize, on_touch_move, on_touch_up
1968::COMM;;# Lifecycle: Set in _change_touch_mode when child grabs, cleared
1969::COMM;;# in on_touch_up
1970::COMM;;#
1971::COMM;;# - sv.can_defocus: bool
1972::COMM;;# Purpose: Controls whether FocusBehavior should defocus on this
1973::COMM;;# touch
1974::COMM;;# Set to False when: Touch results in actual scrolling
1975::COMM;;# Used in: on_touch_up to prevent defocus after scroll gestures
1976::COMM;;#
1977::COMM;;# NESTED SCROLLVIEW NAMESPACE
1978::COMM;;# (Arbitrary Depth Support):
1979::COMM;;# -------------------------------------------------------
1980::COMM;;# - nested: dict - Nested ScrollView coordination state for
1981::COMM;;# arbitrary depth hierarchies
1982::COMM;;# Contains:
1983::COMM;;# {
1984::COMM;;# 'hierarchy': ScrollViewHierarchy, # Chain of nested
1985::COMM;;# # ScrollViews (2+ levels)
1986::COMM;;# 'current_index': int, # Index of ScrollView currently
1987::COMM;;# # handling touch
1988::COMM;;# 'parallel_ancestor_index': int (optional), # For
1989::COMM;;# # non-adjacent delegation
1990::COMM;;# }
1991::COMM;;# Purpose: Coordinates touches across multiple levels of nested
1992::COMM;;# ScrollViews
1993::COMM;;# Lifecycle: Built in outer's on_touch_down, updated during
1994::COMM;;# cascade in on_touch_move
1995::COMM;;#
1996::COMM;;# - sv_hierarchy_handled: bool
1997::COMM;;# Global flag indicating hierarchy coordination is complete
1998::COMM;;# Set when: Outer ScrollView completes on_touch_up coordination
1999::COMM;;# (line 2623)
2000::COMM;;# Purpose: Prevents multiple hierarchies from interfering with
2001::COMM;;# each other. This occurs in non-adjacent delegation when
2002::COMM;;# skip-level cascade creates a shallower hierarchy (e.g.,
2003::COMM;;# 3-level becomes 2-level)
2004::COMM;;# Used in: on_touch_up to make all ScrollViews transparent after
2005::COMM;;# coordination done
2006::COMM;;# Lifecycle: Set once by first hierarchy to complete, checked by
2007::COMM;;# all ScrollViews
2008::COMM;;#
2009::COMM;;# GLOBAL SCROLLBAR FLAGS
2010::COMM;;# (No Namespacing Required):
2011::COMM;;# --------------------------------------------------
2012::COMM;;# - in_bar_x: bool - Touch started on horizontal scroll bar
2013::COMM;;# - in_bar_y: bool - Touch started on vertical scroll bar
2014::COMM;;# Purpose: Differentiates bar dragging from content scrolling
2015::COMM;;# Affects: Touch routing, effect handling, movement calculations,
2016::COMM;;# delegation
2017::COMM;;# Rationale: Scroll bars are positioned at widget edges and cannot
2018::COMM;;# overlap, so multiple ScrollViews can safely share these global
2019::COMM;;# flags
2020::COMM;;# =========================================================================
2021::COMM;;# MAIN TOUCH HANDLING METHODS (in lifecycle order)
2022::COMM;;# =========================================================================
2023::COMM;;def on_touch_down(self, touch):
2024::COMM;;# SCROLLVIEW TOUCH HANDLING WITH AUTO-NESTED DETECTION
2025::COMM;;# =====================================================
2026::COMM;;# This method automatically detects nested ScrollView configurations and
2027::COMM;;# sets up coordination.
2028::COMM;;if not self.collide_point(*touch.pos):
2029::COMM;;return False
2030::COMM;;# Check if we already have an active nested ScrollView touch
2031::COMM;;# This prevents multiple ScrollViews from scrolling simultaneously
2032::COMM;;if self._nested_sv_active_touch is not None:
2033::COMM;;touch.ud[self._get_uid("svavoid")] = True
2034::COMM;;return False
2035::COMM;;# NESTED DETECTION via touch event flow:
2036::COMM;;# Parent widgets receive touches BEFORE children in Kivy.
2037::COMM;;# - If 'nested' NOT in touch.ud: We're the FIRST ScrollView to see
2038::COMM;;# this touch (either outer or standalone - check for children below)
2039::COMM;;# - If 'nested' IN touch.ud: We're an INNER ScrollView
2040::COMM;;# (parent already set up coordination - process as inner)
2041::COMM;;# Check if touch is on OUR scrollbar -
2042::COMM;;# if so, handle it directly (don't look for children)
2043::COMM;;# This ensures outer scrollbar works even when there are inner SVs
2044::COMM;;in_bar_x, in_bar_y = self._check_scroll_bounds(touch)
2045::COMM;;if in_bar_x or in_bar_y:
2046::COMM;;# Touch is on our scrollbar - handle it directly
2047::COMM;;if self._scroll_initialize(touch):
2048::COMM;;touch.grab(self)
2049::COMM;;return True
2050::COMM;;return False
2051::COMM;;# We might be the outer ScrollView - check for child at touch position
2052::COMM;;# Build full hierarchy (supports arbitrary depth nesting)
2053::COMM;;hierarchy = self._build_hierarchy_recursive(touch)
2054::COMM;;is_wheel = "button" in touch.profile and touch.button.startswith(
2055::COMM;;"scroll"
2056::COMM;;)
2057::COMM;;if hierarchy:
2058::COMM;;# We're the OUTER ScrollView with nested children
2059::COMM;;# hierarchy.depth >= 2 (self + at least one child)
2060::COMM;;# For backward compatibility with 2-level code, extract outer/inner
2061::COMM;;outer_sv = hierarchy.outer
2062::COMM;;inner_sv = hierarchy.inner # Innermost (deepest) ScrollView
2063::COMM;;# Get config for the LAST relationship
2064::COMM;;# (inner with its immediate parent)
2065::COMM;;config_type = hierarchy.get_classification(hierarchy.depth - 1)

2069::COMM;;"hierarchy": hierarchy,
2070::COMM;;"current_index": hierarchy.touched_index, # Start at innermost
2071::COMM;;"config_type": config_type,
2072::COMM;;# Classification of inner with its parent
2073::COMM;;"delegation_mode": DelegationMode.UNLOCKED,
2074::COMM;;# Will be set in _scroll_initialize
2075::COMM;;}
2076::COMM;;# Store axis_config for mixed configurations
2077::COMM;;if axis_config:
2078::COMM;;touch.ud["nested"]["axis_config"] = axis_config
2079::COMM;;# WEB-STYLE WHEEL BEHAVIOR: Wheel scrolls ONLY innermost ScrollView
2080::COMM;;# under cursor
2081::COMM;;# No delegation through hierarchy - matches standard web browser UX
2082::COMM;;if is_wheel:
2083::COMM;;# Try only the innermost ScrollView
2084::COMM;;if inner_sv._scroll_initialize(touch):
2085::COMM;;return True
2086::COMM;;# Innermost couldn't handle it - don't try outer levels
2087::COMM;;# This prevents scroll hijacking when inner reaches boundary
2088::COMM;;return False
2089::COMM;;# Non-wheel touch: Initialize scrolling on the innermost child
2090::COMM;;# (handles coordinate transformation)
2091::COMM;;result = self._initialize_nested_inner(touch, inner_sv)
2092::COMM;;# After initialization, setup delegation modes for ALL ScrollViews
2093::COMM;;# in hierarchy
2094::COMM;;# (The innermost already had its mode set by
2095::COMM;;# _setup_boundary_delegation in _scroll_initialize)

2732::COMM;;# on_scroll_stop event.
2733::COMM;;current_pos = (self.scroll_x, self.scroll_y)

2806::COMM;;def _change_touch_mode(self, *largs):
2807::COMM;;# SCROLL TIMEOUT HANDLER - GESTURE DETECTION TIMEOUT
2808::COMM;;# ==================================================
2809::COMM;;# This method is called when the scroll_timeout expires without the
2810::COMM;;# touch traveling the minimum scroll_distance. It transitions from
2811::COMM;;# scroll detection mode to normal widget interaction mode by handing-off
2812::COMM;;# the touch to child widgets.
2813::COMM;;if not self._touch:
2814::COMM;;return
2815::COMM;;uid = self._get_uid()
2816::COMM;;touch = self._touch
2817::COMM;;if uid not in touch.ud:
2818::COMM;;self._touch = False
2819::COMM;;return
2820::COMM;;ud = touch.ud[uid]
2821::COMM;;# Only proceed if we're still in gesture detection mode
2822::COMM;;if ud["mode"] != ScrollMode.UNKNOWN or ud["scroll_action"]:
2823::COMM;;return
2824::COMM;;# SLOW DEVICE PROTECTION:
2825::COMM;;# On very slow devices, we need at least 3 frames to accumulate
2826::COMM;;# velocity data. Otherwise, scroll effects might not work properly.
2827::COMM;;# This addresses issues #1464 and #1499 for low-performance devices.
2828::COMM;;if self.slow_device_support:
2829::COMM;;diff_frames = Clock.frames - ud["frames"]
2830::COMM;;if diff_frames < 3:
2831::COMM;;Clock.schedule_once(self._change_touch_mode, 0)
2832::COMM;;return
2833::COMM;;# CLEANUP AND HANDOFF:
2834::COMM;;# Cancel any scroll effects that may have started
2835::COMM;;if self.do_scroll_x and self.effect_x:
2836::COMM;;self.effect_x.cancel()
2837::COMM;;if self.do_scroll_y and self.effect_y:
2838::COMM;;self.effect_y.cancel()
2839::COMM;;# Store hierarchy info
2840::COMM;;has_hierarchy = (
2841::COMM;;"nested" in touch.ud and "hierarchy" in touch.ud["nested"]
2842::COMM;;)
2843::COMM;;if has_hierarchy:
2844::COMM;;hierarchy = touch.ud["nested"]["hierarchy"]
2845::COMM;;# Cancel any scroll effects that may have started
2846::COMM;;if self.do_scroll_x and self.effect_x:
2847::COMM;;self.effect_x.cancel()
2848::COMM;;if self.do_scroll_y and self.effect_y:
2849::COMM;;self.effect_y.cancel()
2850::COMM;;touch.ungrab(self)
2851::COMM;;self._touch = None
2852::COMM;;# CONTROLLED HANDOFF TO CHILD WIDGETS:
2853::COMM;;# Transform touch coordinates and re-dispatch to children
2854::COMM;;# This allows buttons, sliders, etc. to handle the touch normally
2855::COMM;;# NOTE: Do NOT schedule _do_touch_up here, this is a live touch handoff,
2856::COMM;;# not a synthetic click. The user is still holding their finger down.
2857::COMM;;touch.push()

2859::COMM;;touch.apply_transform_2d(self.to_parent)
2860::COMM;;child_grabbed = self._simulate_touch_down(touch)
2861::COMM;;touch.pop()
2862::COMM;;if child_grabbed:
2863::COMM;;# A child widget grabbed the touch - hand it off completely
2864::COMM;;uid = self._get_uid()
2865::COMM;;if uid in touch.ud:
2866::COMM;;del touch.ud[uid]
2867::COMM;;# Set flag to prevent re-initialization, this touch belongs to child
2868::COMM;;touch.ud["sv.claimed_by_child"] = True
2869::COMM;;# Clear the nested ScrollView active touch since we're handing off
2870::COMM;;if has_hierarchy:
2871::COMM;;if hierarchy.scrollviews[0]._nested_sv_active_touch is touch:
2872::COMM;;hierarchy.scrollviews[0]._nested_sv_active_touch = None
2873::COMM;;else:

2876::COMM;;self._nested_sv_active_touch = None
2877::COMM;;else:
2878::COMM;;# No child grabbed it (e.g., user is on empty space) -
2879::COMM;;# transition to SCROLL mode so the user can begin scrolling without
2880::COMM;;# restarting the gesture
2881::COMM;;uid = self._get_uid()
2882::COMM;;if uid in touch.ud:

6::COMM;;Requests HTTP Library
7::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
8::COMM;;Requests is an HTTP library, written in Python, for human beings.
9::COMM;;Basic GET usage:
10::COMM;;>>> import requests
11::COMM;;>>> r = requests.get('https://www.python.org')
12::COMM;;>>> r.status_code
13::COMM;;200
14::COMM;;>>> b'Python is a programming language' in r.content
15::COMM;;True
16::COMM;;... or POST:
17::COMM;;>>> payload = dict(key1='value1', key2='value2')
18::COMM;;>>> r = requests.post('https://httpbin.org/post', data=payload)
19::COMM;;>>> print(r.text)
20::COMM;;{
21::COMM;;...
22::COMM;;"form": {
23::COMM;;"key1": "value1",
24::COMM;;"key2": "value2"
25::COMM;;},
26::COMM;;...
27::COMM;;}
28::COMM;;The other HTTP methods are supported - see `requests.api`. Full documentation
29::COMM;;is at <https://requests.readthedocs.io>.

124::COMM;;Provides a general-case interface for Requests sessions to contact HTTP and
125::COMM;;HTTPS urls by implementing the Transport Adapter interface. This class will
126::COMM;;usually be created by the :class:`Session <Session>` class under the
127::COMM;;covers.
128::COMM;;:param pool_connections: The number of urllib3 connection pools to cache.
129::COMM;;:param pool_maxsize: The maximum number of connections to save in the pool.
130::COMM;;:param max_retries: The maximum number of retries each connection
131::COMM;;should attempt. Note, this applies only to failed DNS lookups, socket
132::COMM;;connections and connection timeouts, never to requests where data has
133::COMM;;made it to the server. By default, Requests does not retry failed
134::COMM;;connections. If you need granular control over the conditions under
135::COMM;;which we retry a request, import urllib3's ``Retry`` class and pass
136::COMM;;that instead.
137::COMM;;:param pool_block: Whether the connection pool should block for connections.
138::COMM;;Usage::
139::COMM;;>>> import requests

141::COMM;;>>> a = requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter(max_retries=3)
142::COMM;;>>> s.mount('http://', a)

315::COMM;;This looks at the PreparedRequest, the user-specified verify value,

319::COMM;;this writing, use the following to determine what keys may be in that
320::COMM;;dictionary:
321::COMM;;* If ``verify`` is ``True``, ``"ssl_context"`` will be set and will be the
322::COMM;;default Requests SSL Context
323::COMM;;* If ``verify`` is ``False``, ``"ssl_context"`` will not be set but
324::COMM;;``"cert_reqs"`` will be set
325::COMM;;* If ``verify`` is a string, (i.e., it is a user-specified trust bundle)
326::COMM;;``"ca_certs"`` will be set if the string is not a directory recognized
327::COMM;;by :py:func:`os.path.isdir`, otherwise ``"ca_cert_dir"`` will be
328::COMM;;set.
329::COMM;;* If ``"cert"`` is specified, ``"cert_file"`` will always be set. If
330::COMM;;``"cert"`` is a tuple with a second item, ``"key_file"`` will also
331::COMM;;be present
332::COMM;;To override these settings, one may subclass this class, call this
333::COMM;;method and use the above logic to change parameters as desired. For
334::COMM;;example, if one wishes to use a custom :py:class:`ssl.SSLContext` one

2::COMM;;requests.api
3::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~~~
4::COMM;;This module implements the Requests API.
5::COMM;;:copyright: (c) 2012 by Kenneth Reitz.
6::COMM;;:license: Apache2, see LICENSE for more details.
11::COMM;;:param method: method for the new :class:`Request` object: ``GET``, ``OPTIONS``, ``HEAD``, ``POST``, ``PUT``, ``PATCH``, or ``DELETE``.
12::COMM;;:param url: URL for the new :class:`Request` object.
13::COMM;;:param params: (optional) Dictionary, list of tuples or bytes to send
14::COMM;;in the query string for the :class:`Request`.
15::COMM;;:param data: (optional) Dictionary, list of tuples, bytes, or file-like
16::COMM;;object to send in the body of the :class:`Request`.
17::COMM;;:param json: (optional) A JSON serializable Python object to send in the body of the :class:`Request`.

4::COMM;;Data structures that power Requests.
10::COMM;;Implements all methods and operations of
11::COMM;;``MutableMapping`` as well as dict's ``copy``. Also
12::COMM;;provides ``lower_items``.
13::COMM;;All keys are expected to be strings. The structure remembers the
14::COMM;;case of the last key to be set, and ``iter(instance)``,
15::COMM;;``keys()``, ``items()``, ``iterkeys()``, and ``iteritems()``
16::COMM;;will contain case-sensitive keys. However, querying and contains
17::COMM;;testing is case insensitive::
18::COMM;;cid = CaseInsensitiveDict()
19::COMM;;cid['Accept'] = 'application/json'
20::COMM;;cid['aCCEPT'] == 'application/json' # True
21::COMM;;list(cid) == ['Accept'] # True
22::COMM;;For example, ``headers['content-encoding']`` will return the
23::COMM;;value of a ``'Content-Encoding'`` response header, regardless
24::COMM;;of how the header name was originally stored.
25::COMM;;If the constructor, ``.update``, or equality comparison
26::COMM;;operations are given keys that have equal ``.lower()``s, the
27::COMM;;behavior is undefined.
35::COMO;;# Use the lowercased key for lookups, but store the actual
36::COMO;;# key alongside the value.
48::COMM;;return ((lowerkey, keyval[1]) for (lowerkey, keyval) in self._store.items())

20::COMM;;def __init__(
21::COMM;;self,
22::COMM;;handler=None,
23::COMM;;host="localhost",
24::COMM;;port=0,
25::COMM;;requests_to_handle=1,
26::COMM;;wait_to_close_event=None,
27::COMM;;):

32::COMM;;self.port = port
33::COMM;;self.requests_to_handle = requests_to_handle

37::COMM;;@classmethod
38::COMM;;def text_response_server(cls, text, request_timeout=0.5, **kwargs):
39::COMM;;def text_response_handler(sock):
40::COMM;;request_content = consume_socket_content(sock, timeout=request_timeout)
41::COMM;;sock.send(text.encode("utf-8"))
42::COMM;;return request_content

44::COMM;;@classmethod

47::COMM;;"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n" + "Content-Length: 0\r\n\r\n", **kwargs
48::COMM;;)
49::COMM;;def run(self):
50::COMM;;try:
51::COMM;;self.server_sock = self._create_socket_and_bind()
52::COMM;;# in case self.port = 0
53::COMM;;self.port = self.server_sock.getsockname()[1]
54::COMM;;self.ready_event.set()
55::COMM;;self._handle_requests()
56::COMM;;if self.wait_to_close_event:
57::COMM;;self.wait_to_close_event.wait(self.WAIT_EVENT_TIMEOUT)
58::COMM;;finally:
59::COMM;;self.ready_event.set() # just in case of exception
60::COMM;;self._close_server_sock_ignore_errors()
61::COMM;;self.stop_event.set()
62::COMM;;def _create_socket_and_bind(self):
63::COMM;;sock = socket.socket()
64::COMM;;sock.bind((self.host, self.port))
65::COMM;;sock.listen()
66::COMM;;return sock
67::COMM;;def _close_server_sock_ignore_errors(self):
68::COMM;;try:
69::COMM;;self.server_sock.close()
70::COMM;;except OSError:
71::COMM;;pass
72::COMM;;def _handle_requests(self):
73::COMM;;for _ in range(self.requests_to_handle):
74::COMM;;sock = self._accept_connection()
75::COMM;;if not sock:
76::COMM;;break
77::COMM;;handler_result = self.handler(sock)
78::COMM;;self.handler_results.append(handler_result)
79::COMM;;sock.close()
80::COMM;;def _accept_connection(self):
81::COMM;;try:
82::COMM;;ready, _, _ = select.select(
83::COMM;;[self.server_sock], [], [], self.WAIT_EVENT_TIMEOUT
84::COMM;;)
85::COMM;;if not ready:
86::COMM;;return None
87::COMM;;return self.server_sock.accept()[0]
88::COMM;;except OSError:
89::COMM;;return None
90::COMM;;def __enter__(self):
91::COMM;;self.start()
92::COMM;;if not self.ready_event.wait(self.WAIT_EVENT_TIMEOUT):
93::COMM;;raise RuntimeError("Timeout waiting for server to be ready.")
94::COMM;;return self.host, self.port
95::COMM;;def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback):
96::COMM;;if exc_type is None:
97::COMM;;self.stop_event.wait(self.WAIT_EVENT_TIMEOUT)
98::COMM;;else:
99::COMM;;if self.wait_to_close_event:
100::COMM;;# avoid server from waiting for event timeouts
101::COMM;;# if an exception is found in the main thread
102::COMM;;self.wait_to_close_event.set()
103::COMM;;# ensure server thread doesn't get stuck waiting for connections
104::COMM;;self._close_server_sock_ignore_errors()
105::COMM;;self.join()
106::COMM;;return False # allow exceptions to propagate

126::COMM;;wait_to_close_event=wait_to_close_event,
127::COMM;;)
128::COMM;;self.cert_chain = cert_chain

2::COMM;;================================
3::COMM;;Time-related feature engineering
4::COMM;;================================
5::COMM;;This notebook introduces different strategies to leverage time-related features
6::COMM;;for a bike sharing demand regression task that is highly dependent on business
7::COMM;;cycles (days, weeks, months) and yearly season cycles.
8::COMM;;In the process, we introduce how to perform periodic feature engineering using
9::COMM;;the :class:`sklearn.preprocessing.SplineTransformer` class and its
10::COMM;;`extrapolation="periodic"` option.
12::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
13::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
14::COMO;;# %%
15::COMO;;# Data exploration on the Bike Sharing Demand dataset
16::COMO;;# ---------------------------------------------------
17::COMO;;#
18::COMO;;# We start by loading the data from the OpenML repository.
22::COMO;;# %%
23::COMO;;# To get a quick understanding of the periodic patterns of the data, let us
24::COMO;;# have a look at the average demand per hour during a week.
25::COMO;;#
26::COMO;;# Note that the week starts on a Sunday, during the weekend. We can clearly
27::COMO;;# distinguish the commute patterns in the morning and evenings of the work days
28::COMO;;# and the leisure use of the bikes on the weekends with a more spread peak
29::COMO;;# demand around the middle of the days:
41::COMO;;# %%
42::COMO;;#
43::COMO;;# The target of the prediction problem is the absolute count of bike rentals on
44::COMO;;# an hourly basis:
46::COMO;;# %%
47::COMO;;#
48::COMO;;# Let us rescale the target variable (number of hourly bike rentals) to predict
49::COMO;;# a relative demand so that the mean absolute error is more easily interpreted
50::COMO;;# as a fraction of the maximum demand.
51::COMO;;#
52::COMO;;# .. note::
53::COMO;;#
54::COMO;;# The fit method of the models used in this notebook all minimizes the
55::COMO;;# mean squared error to estimate the conditional mean.
56::COMO;;# The absolute error, however, would estimate the conditional median.
57::COMO;;#
58::COMO;;# Nevertheless, when reporting performance measures on the test set in
59::COMO;;# the discussion, we choose to focus on the mean absolute error instead
60::COMO;;# of the (root) mean squared error because it is more intuitive to
61::COMO;;# interpret. Note, however, that in this study the best models for one
62::COMO;;# metric are also the best ones in terms of the other metric.
64::COMO;;# %%
71::COMO;;# %%
72::COMO;;# The input feature data frame is a time annotated hourly log of variables
73::COMO;;# describing the weather conditions. It includes both numerical and categorical
74::COMO;;# variables. Note that the time information has already been expanded into
75::COMO;;# several complementary columns.
76::COMO;;#
79::COMO;;# %%
80::COMO;;# .. note::

83::COMO;;# could have expanded it into hour-in-the-day, day-in-the-week,
84::COMO;;# day-in-the-month, month-in-the-year using pandas:
85::COMO;;# https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/user_guide/timeseries.html#time-date-components

88::COMO;;# with `"weather"`:

93::COMO;;# train machine learning models with cross validation. Instead, we simplify the
94::COMO;;# representation by collapsing those into the `"rain"` category.

109::COMO;;# Time-based cross-validation
110::COMO;;# ---------------------------
111::COMO;;#
112::COMO;;# Since the dataset is a time-ordered event log (hourly demand), we will use a
113::COMO;;# time-sensitive cross-validation splitter to evaluate our demand forecasting
114::COMO;;# model as realistically as possible. We use a gap of 2 days between the train
115::COMO;;# and test side of the splits. We also limit the training set size to make the
116::COMO;;# performance of the CV folds more stable.
117::COMO;;#
118::COMO;;# 1000 test datapoints should be enough to quantify the performance of the
119::COMO;;# model. This represents a bit less than a month and a half of contiguous test
120::COMO;;# data:

130::COMO;;# `TimeSeriesSplit` works as we expect, starting with the first split:
