260::COMM;;``mode='distance'``, then using ``metric='precomputed'`` here.
261::COMM;;Another way to reduce memory and computation time is to remove
262::COMM;;(near-)duplicate points and use ``sample_weight`` instead.
263::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.cluster.OPTICS` provides a similar clustering with lower memory
264::COMM;;usage.

312::COMM;;Takes an internal single_linkage_tree structure and adds back in a set of points
313::COMM;;that were initially detected as non-finite and returns that new tree.

363::COMM;;HDBSCAN - Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications
364::COMM;;with Noise. Performs :class:`~sklearn.cluster.DBSCAN` over varying epsilon
365::COMM;;values and integrates the result to find a clustering that gives the best
366::COMM;;stability over epsilon.
367::COMM;;This allows HDBSCAN to find clusters of varying densities (unlike
368::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.cluster.DBSCAN`), and be more robust to parameter selection.
369::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <hdbscan>`.
370::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.3
371::COMM;;Parameters
372::COMM;;----------
373::COMM;;min_cluster_size : int, default=5
374::COMM;;The minimum number of samples in a group for that group to be
375::COMM;;considered a cluster; groupings smaller than this size will be left
376::COMM;;as noise.
377::COMM;;min_samples : int, default=None
378::COMM;;The parameter `k` used to calculate the distance between a point
379::COMM;;`x_p` and its k-th nearest neighbor.
380::COMM;;When `None`, defaults to `min_cluster_size`.
381::COMM;;cluster_selection_epsilon : float, default=0.0
382::COMM;;A distance threshold. Clusters below this value will be merged.
383::COMM;;See [5]_ for more information.
384::COMM;;max_cluster_size : int, default=None
385::COMM;;A limit to the size of clusters returned by the `"eom"` cluster
386::COMM;;selection algorithm. There is no limit when `max_cluster_size=None`.
387::COMM;;Has no effect if `cluster_selection_method="leaf"`.
388::COMM;;metric : str or callable, default='euclidean'
389::COMM;;The metric to use when calculating distance between instances in a
390::COMM;;feature array.
391::COMM;;- If metric is a string or callable, it must be one of
392::COMM;;the options allowed by :func:`~sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances`
393::COMM;;for its metric parameter.
394::COMM;;- If metric is "precomputed", X is assumed to be a distance matrix and
395::COMM;;must be square.
396::COMM;;metric_params : dict, default=None
397::COMM;;Arguments passed to the distance metric.
398::COMM;;alpha : float, default=1.0
399::COMM;;A distance scaling parameter as used in robust single linkage.
400::COMM;;See [3]_ for more information.
401::COMM;;algorithm : {"auto", "brute", "kd_tree", "ball_tree"}, default="auto"
402::COMM;;Exactly which algorithm to use for computing core distances; By default
403::COMM;;this is set to `"auto"` which attempts to use a
404::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.neighbors.KDTree` tree if possible, otherwise it uses
405::COMM;;a :class:`~sklearn.neighbors.BallTree` tree. Both `"kd_tree"` and
406::COMM;;`"ball_tree"` algorithms use the
407::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.neighbors.NearestNeighbors` estimator.
408::COMM;;If the `X` passed during `fit` is sparse or `metric` is invalid for
409::COMM;;both :class:`~sklearn.neighbors.KDTree` and
410::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.neighbors.BallTree`, then it resolves to use the
411::COMM;;`"brute"` algorithm.
412::COMM;;leaf_size : int, default=40
413::COMM;;Leaf size for trees responsible for fast nearest neighbour queries when
414::COMM;;a KDTree or a BallTree are used as core-distance algorithms. A large
415::COMM;;dataset size and small `leaf_size` may induce excessive memory usage.
416::COMM;;If you are running out of memory consider increasing the `leaf_size`
417::COMM;;parameter. Ignored for `algorithm="brute"`.
418::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
419::COMM;;Number of jobs to run in parallel to calculate distances.
420::COMM;;`None` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
421::COMM;;`-1` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
422::COMM;;for more details.
423::COMM;;cluster_selection_method : {"eom", "leaf"}, default="eom"
424::COMM;;The method used to select clusters from the condensed tree. The
425::COMM;;standard approach for HDBSCAN* is to use an Excess of Mass (`"eom"`)
426::COMM;;algorithm to find the most persistent clusters. Alternatively you can
427::COMM;;instead select the clusters at the leaves of the tree -- this provides
428::COMM;;the most fine grained and homogeneous clusters.
429::COMM;;allow_single_cluster : bool, default=False
430::COMM;;By default HDBSCAN* will not produce a single cluster, setting this
431::COMM;;to True will override this and allow single cluster results in
432::COMM;;the case that you feel this is a valid result for your dataset.
433::COMM;;store_centers : str, default=None
434::COMM;;Which, if any, cluster centers to compute and store. The options are:
435::COMM;;- `None` which does not compute nor store any centers.
436::COMM;;- `"centroid"` which calculates the center by taking the weighted
437::COMM;;average of their positions. Note that the algorithm uses the
438::COMM;;euclidean metric and does not guarantee that the output will be
439::COMM;;an observed data point.
440::COMM;;- `"medoid"` which calculates the center by taking the point in the
441::COMM;;fitted data which minimizes the distance to all other points in
442::COMM;;the cluster. This is slower than "centroid" since it requires
443::COMM;;computing additional pairwise distances between points of the
444::COMM;;same cluster but guarantees the output is an observed data point.
445::COMM;;The medoid is also well-defined for arbitrary metrics, and does not
446::COMM;;depend on a euclidean metric.
447::COMM;;- `"both"` which computes and stores both forms of centers.
448::COMM;;copy : bool, default=False
449::COMM;;If `copy=True` then any time an in-place modifications would be made
450::COMM;;that would overwrite data passed to :term:`fit`, a copy will first be
451::COMM;;made, guaranteeing that the original data will be unchanged.
452::COMM;;Currently, it only applies when `metric="precomputed"`, when passing
453::COMM;;a dense array or a CSR sparse matrix and when `algorithm="brute"`.
454::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10
455::COMM;;The default value for `copy` will change from `False` to `True`
456::COMM;;in version 1.10.
457::COMM;;Attributes
458::COMM;;----------
459::COMM;;labels_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
460::COMM;;Cluster labels for each point in the dataset given to :term:`fit`.
461::COMM;;Outliers are labeled as follows:
462::COMM;;- Noisy samples are given the label -1.
463::COMM;;- Samples with infinite elements (+/- np.inf) are given the label -2.
464::COMM;;- Samples with missing data are given the label -3, even if they
465::COMM;;also have infinite elements.
466::COMM;;probabilities_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
467::COMM;;The strength with which each sample is a member of its assigned
468::COMM;;cluster.
469::COMM;;- Clustered samples have probabilities proportional to the degree that
470::COMM;;they persist as part of the cluster.
471::COMM;;- Noisy samples have probability zero.
472::COMM;;- Samples with infinite elements (+/- np.inf) have probability 0.
473::COMM;;- Samples with missing data have probability `np.nan`.
474::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
475::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
476::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
477::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
478::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
479::COMM;;centroids_ : ndarray of shape (n_clusters, n_features)
480::COMM;;A collection containing the centroid of each cluster calculated under
481::COMM;;the standard euclidean metric. The centroids may fall "outside" their
482::COMM;;respective clusters if the clusters themselves are non-convex.
483::COMM;;Note that `n_clusters` only counts non-outlier clusters. That is to
484::COMM;;say, the `-1, -2, -3` labels for the outlier clusters are excluded.
485::COMM;;medoids_ : ndarray of shape (n_clusters, n_features)
486::COMM;;A collection containing the medoid of each cluster calculated under
487::COMM;;the whichever metric was passed to the `metric` parameter. The
488::COMM;;medoids are points in the original cluster which minimize the average
489::COMM;;distance to all other points in that cluster under the chosen metric.
490::COMM;;These can be thought of as the result of projecting the `metric`-based
491::COMM;;centroid back onto the cluster.
492::COMM;;Note that `n_clusters` only counts non-outlier clusters. That is to
493::COMM;;say, the `-1, -2, -3` labels for the outlier clusters are excluded.
494::COMM;;See Also
495::COMM;;--------
496::COMM;;DBSCAN : Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications
497::COMM;;with Noise.
498::COMM;;OPTICS : Ordering Points To Identify the Clustering Structure.
499::COMM;;Birch : Memory-efficient, online-learning algorithm.
500::COMM;;Notes
501::COMM;;-----
502::COMM;;The `min_samples` parameter includes the point itself, whereas the implementation in
503::COMM;;`scikit-learn-contrib/hdbscan <https://github.com/scikit-learn-contrib/hdbscan>`_
504::COMM;;does not. To get the same results in both versions, the value of `min_samples` here
505::COMM;;must be 1 greater than the value used in `scikit-learn-contrib/hdbscan
506::COMM;;<https://github.com/scikit-learn-contrib/hdbscan>`_.

55::COMM;;# Initialization heuristic
56::COMM;;@validate_params(
57::COMM;;{

59::COMM;;"n_clusters": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],

67::COMM;;def kmeans_plusplus(
68::COMM;;X,
69::COMM;;n_clusters,
70::COMM;;*,
71::COMM;;sample_weight=None,
72::COMM;;x_squared_norms=None,
73::COMM;;random_state=None,
74::COMM;;n_local_trials=None,

129::COMM;;# Check data
130::COMM;;check_array(X, accept_sparse="csr", dtype=[np.float64, np.float32])
131::COMM;;sample_weight = _check_sample_weight(sample_weight, X, dtype=X.dtype)
132::COMM;;if X.shape[0] < n_clusters:
133::COMM;;raise ValueError(
134::COMM;;f"n_samples={X.shape[0]} should be >= n_clusters={n_clusters}."
135::COMM;;)
136::COMM;;# Check parameters
137::COMM;;if x_squared_norms is None:
138::COMM;;x_squared_norms = row_norms(X, squared=True)
139::COMM;;else:
140::COMM;;x_squared_norms = check_array(x_squared_norms, dtype=X.dtype, ensure_2d=False)
141::COMM;;if x_squared_norms.shape[0] != X.shape[0]:
142::COMM;;raise ValueError(
143::COMM;;f"The length of x_squared_norms {x_squared_norms.shape[0]} should "
144::COMM;;f"be equal to the length of n_samples {X.shape[0]}."
145::COMM;;)
146::COMM;;random_state = check_random_state(random_state)
147::COMM;;# Call private k-means++
148::COMM;;centers, indices = _kmeans_plusplus(
149::COMM;;X, n_clusters, x_squared_norms, sample_weight, random_state, n_local_trials
150::COMM;;)
151::COMM;;return centers, indices
152::COMM;;def _kmeans_plusplus(
153::COMM;;X, n_clusters, x_squared_norms, sample_weight, random_state, n_local_trials=None
154::COMM;;):
183::COMM;;n_samples, n_features = X.shape
184::COMM;;centers = np.empty((n_clusters, n_features), dtype=X.dtype)
185::COMM;;# Set the number of local seeding trials if none is given
186::COMM;;if n_local_trials is None:
187::COMM;;# This is what Arthur/Vassilvitskii tried, but did not report
188::COMM;;# specific results for other than mentioning in the conclusion
189::COMM;;# that it helped.
190::COMM;;n_local_trials = 2 + int(np.log(n_clusters))
191::COMM;;# Pick first center randomly and track index of point
192::COMM;;center_id = random_state.choice(n_samples, p=sample_weight / sample_weight.sum())
193::COMM;;indices = np.full(n_clusters, -1, dtype=int)
194::COMM;;if sp.issparse(X):
195::COMM;;centers[0] = X[[center_id]].toarray()
196::COMM;;else:
197::COMM;;centers[0] = X[center_id]
198::COMM;;indices[0] = center_id
199::COMM;;# Initialize list of closest distances and calculate current potential
200::COMM;;closest_dist_sq = _euclidean_distances(
201::COMM;;centers[0, np.newaxis], X, Y_norm_squared=x_squared_norms, squared=True
202::COMM;;)
203::COMM;;current_pot = closest_dist_sq @ sample_weight
204::COMM;;# Pick the remaining n_clusters-1 points
205::COMM;;for c in range(1, n_clusters):
206::COMM;;# Choose center candidates by sampling with probability proportional
207::COMM;;# to the squared distance to the closest existing center
208::COMM;;rand_vals = random_state.uniform(size=n_local_trials) * current_pot
209::COMM;;candidate_ids = np.searchsorted(
210::COMM;;np.cumsum(sample_weight * closest_dist_sq), rand_vals
211::COMM;;)
212::COMM;;# XXX: numerical imprecision can result in a candidate_id out of range
213::COMM;;np.clip(candidate_ids, None, closest_dist_sq.size - 1, out=candidate_ids)
214::COMM;;# Compute distances to center candidates
215::COMM;;distance_to_candidates = _euclidean_distances(
216::COMM;;X[candidate_ids], X, Y_norm_squared=x_squared_norms, squared=True
217::COMM;;)
218::COMM;;# update closest distances squared and potential for each candidate
219::COMM;;np.minimum(closest_dist_sq, distance_to_candidates, out=distance_to_candidates)
220::COMM;;candidates_pot = distance_to_candidates @ sample_weight.reshape(-1, 1)
221::COMM;;# Decide which candidate is the best
222::COMM;;best_candidate = np.argmin(candidates_pot)
223::COMM;;current_pot = candidates_pot[best_candidate]
224::COMM;;closest_dist_sq = distance_to_candidates[best_candidate]
225::COMM;;best_candidate = candidate_ids[best_candidate]
226::COMM;;# Permanently add best center candidate found in local tries
227::COMM;;if sp.issparse(X):
228::COMM;;centers[c] = X[[best_candidate]].toarray()
229::COMM;;else:
230::COMM;;centers[c] = X[best_candidate]
231::COMM;;indices[c] = best_candidate
232::COMM;;return centers, indices
233::COMM;;###############################################################################
234::COMM;;# K-means batch estimation by EM (expectation maximization)
235::COMM;;def _tolerance(X, tol):
268::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <k_means>`.
269::COMM;;Parameters
270::COMM;;----------
271::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
272::COMM;;The observations to cluster. It must be noted that the data
273::COMM;;will be converted to C ordering, which will cause a memory copy
274::COMM;;if the given data is not C-contiguous.
275::COMM;;n_clusters : int
276::COMM;;The number of clusters to form as well as the number of
277::COMM;;centroids to generate.
278::COMM;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
279::COMM;;The weights for each observation in `X`. If `None`, all observations
280::COMM;;are assigned equal weight. `sample_weight` is not used during
281::COMM;;initialization if `init` is a callable or a user provided array.
282::COMM;;init : {'k-means++', 'random'}, callable or array-like of shape \
283::COMM;;(n_clusters, n_features), default='k-means++'
284::COMM;;Method for initialization:
285::COMM;;- `'k-means++'` : selects initial cluster centers for k-mean
286::COMM;;clustering in a smart way to speed up convergence. See section
287::COMM;;Notes in k_init for more details.
288::COMM;;- `'random'`: choose `n_clusters` observations (rows) at random from data
289::COMM;;for the initial centroids.
290::COMM;;- If an array is passed, it should be of shape `(n_clusters, n_features)`
291::COMM;;and gives the initial centers.
292::COMM;;- If a callable is passed, it should take arguments `X`, `n_clusters` and a
293::COMM;;random state and return an initialization.
294::COMM;;n_init : 'auto' or int, default="auto"
295::COMM;;Number of time the k-means algorithm will be run with different
296::COMM;;centroid seeds. The final results will be the best output of
297::COMM;;n_init consecutive runs in terms of inertia.
298::COMM;;When `n_init='auto'`, the number of runs depends on the value of init:
299::COMM;;10 if using `init='random'` or `init` is a callable;
300::COMM;;1 if using `init='k-means++'` or `init` is an array-like.
301::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
302::COMM;;Added 'auto' option for `n_init`.
303::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4
304::COMM;;Default value for `n_init` changed to `'auto'`.
305::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=300
306::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations of the k-means algorithm to run.
307::COMM;;verbose : bool, default=False
308::COMM;;Verbosity mode.
309::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-4
310::COMM;;Relative tolerance with regards to Frobenius norm of the difference
311::COMM;;in the cluster centers of two consecutive iterations to declare
312::COMM;;convergence.
313::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
314::COMM;;Determines random number generation for centroid initialization. Use
315::COMM;;an int to make the randomness deterministic.
316::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
317::COMM;;copy_x : bool, default=True
318::COMM;;When pre-computing distances it is more numerically accurate to center
319::COMM;;the data first. If `copy_x` is True (default), then the original data is
320::COMM;;not modified. If False, the original data is modified, and put back
321::COMM;;before the function returns, but small numerical differences may be
322::COMM;;introduced by subtracting and then adding the data mean. Note that if
323::COMM;;the original data is not C-contiguous, a copy will be made even if
324::COMM;;`copy_x` is False. If the original data is sparse, but not in CSR format,
325::COMM;;a copy will be made even if `copy_x` is False.
326::COMM;;algorithm : {"lloyd", "elkan"}, default="lloyd"
327::COMM;;K-means algorithm to use. The classical EM-style algorithm is `"lloyd"`.
328::COMM;;The `"elkan"` variation can be more efficient on some datasets with
329::COMM;;well-defined clusters, by using the triangle inequality. However it's
330::COMM;;more memory intensive due to the allocation of an extra array of shape
331::COMM;;`(n_samples, n_clusters)`.
332::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
333::COMM;;Added Elkan algorithm
334::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
335::COMM;;Renamed "full" to "lloyd", and deprecated "auto" and "full".
336::COMM;;Changed "auto" to use "lloyd" instead of "elkan".
337::COMM;;return_n_iter : bool, default=False
338::COMM;;Whether or not to return the number of iterations.
339::COMM;;Returns
340::COMM;;-------
341::COMM;;centroid : ndarray of shape (n_clusters, n_features)
342::COMM;;Centroids found at the last iteration of k-means.
343::COMM;;label : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
344::COMM;;The `label[i]` is the code or index of the centroid the
345::COMM;;i'th observation is closest to.
346::COMM;;inertia : float
347::COMM;;The final value of the inertia criterion (sum of squared distances to
348::COMM;;the closest centroid for all observations in the training set).
349::COMM;;best_n_iter : int
350::COMM;;Number of iterations corresponding to the best results.
351::COMM;;Returned only if `return_n_iter` is set to True.
352::COMM;;Examples
353::COMM;;--------
354::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
355::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.cluster import k_means
356::COMM;;>>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 0],
357::COMM;;... [10, 2], [10, 4], [10, 0]])
358::COMM;;>>> centroid, label, inertia = k_means(
359::COMM;;... X, n_clusters=2, n_init="auto", random_state=0
360::COMM;;... )
361::COMM;;>>> centroid

363::COMM;;[ 1., 2.]])
364::COMM;;>>> label
365::COMM;;array([1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0], dtype=int32)
366::COMM;;>>> inertia

961::COMM;;----------
962::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
963::COMM;;New data.
964::COMM;;y : Ignored
965::COMM;;Not used, present here for API consistency by convention.
966::COMM;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
967::COMM;;The weights for each observation in X. If None, all observations
968::COMM;;are assigned equal weight.
969::COMM;;Returns
970::COMM;;-------
971::COMM;;score : float
972::COMM;;Opposite of the value of X on the K-means objective.
987::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <k_means>`.
988::COMM;;Parameters
989::COMM;;----------
990::COMM;;n_clusters : int, default=8
991::COMM;;The number of clusters to form as well as the number of
992::COMM;;centroids to generate.
993::COMM;;For an example of how to choose an optimal value for `n_clusters` refer to
994::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_cluster_plot_kmeans_silhouette_analysis.py`.
995::COMM;;init : {'k-means++', 'random'}, callable or array-like of shape \
996::COMM;;(n_clusters, n_features), default='k-means++'
997::COMM;;Method for initialization:
998::COMM;;* 'k-means++' : selects initial cluster centroids using sampling \
999::COMM;;based on an empirical probability distribution of the points' \
1000::COMM;;contribution to the overall inertia. This technique speeds up \
1001::COMM;;convergence. The algorithm implemented is "greedy k-means++". It \
1002::COMM;;differs from the vanilla k-means++ by making several trials at \
1003::COMM;;each sampling step and choosing the best centroid among them.
1004::COMM;;* 'random': choose `n_clusters` observations (rows) at random from \
1005::COMM;;data for the initial centroids.
1006::COMM;;* If an array is passed, it should be of shape (n_clusters, n_features)\
1007::COMM;;and gives the initial centers.
1008::COMM;;* If a callable is passed, it should take arguments X, n_clusters and a\
1009::COMM;;random state and return an initialization.
1010::COMM;;For an example of how to use the different `init` strategies, see
1011::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_cluster_plot_kmeans_digits.py`.
1012::COMM;;For an evaluation of the impact of initialization, see the example
1013::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_cluster_plot_kmeans_stability_low_dim_dense.py`.
1014::COMM;;n_init : 'auto' or int, default='auto'
1015::COMM;;Number of times the k-means algorithm is run with different centroid
1016::COMM;;seeds. The final results is the best output of `n_init` consecutive runs
1017::COMM;;in terms of inertia. Several runs are recommended for sparse
1018::COMM;;high-dimensional problems (see :ref:`kmeans_sparse_high_dim`).
1019::COMM;;When `n_init='auto'`, the number of runs depends on the value of init:
1020::COMM;;10 if using `init='random'` or `init` is a callable;
1021::COMM;;1 if using `init='k-means++'` or `init` is an array-like.
1022::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
1023::COMM;;Added 'auto' option for `n_init`.
1024::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4
1025::COMM;;Default value for `n_init` changed to `'auto'`.
1026::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=300
1027::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations of the k-means algorithm for a
1028::COMM;;single run.
1029::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-4
1030::COMM;;Relative tolerance with regards to Frobenius norm of the difference
1031::COMM;;in the cluster centers of two consecutive iterations to declare
1032::COMM;;convergence.
1033::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
1034::COMM;;Verbosity mode.
1035::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1036::COMM;;Determines random number generation for centroid initialization. Use
1037::COMM;;an int to make the randomness deterministic.
1038::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
1039::COMM;;copy_x : bool, default=True
1040::COMM;;When pre-computing distances it is more numerically accurate to center
1041::COMM;;the data first. If copy_x is True (default), then the original data is
1042::COMM;;not modified. If False, the original data is modified, and put back
1043::COMM;;before the function returns, but small numerical differences may be
1044::COMM;;introduced by subtracting and then adding the data mean. Note that if
1045::COMM;;the original data is not C-contiguous, a copy will be made even if
1046::COMM;;copy_x is False. If the original data is sparse, but not in CSR format,
1047::COMM;;a copy will be made even if copy_x is False.
1048::COMM;;algorithm : {"lloyd", "elkan"}, default="lloyd"
1049::COMM;;K-means algorithm to use. The classical EM-style algorithm is `"lloyd"`.
1050::COMM;;The `"elkan"` variation can be more efficient on some datasets with
1051::COMM;;well-defined clusters, by using the triangle inequality. However it's
1052::COMM;;more memory intensive due to the allocation of an extra array of shape
1053::COMM;;`(n_samples, n_clusters)`.
1054::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1055::COMM;;Added Elkan algorithm
1056::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
1057::COMM;;Renamed "full" to "lloyd", and deprecated "auto" and "full".
1058::COMM;;Changed "auto" to use "lloyd" instead of "elkan".
1059::COMM;;Attributes
1060::COMM;;----------
1061::COMM;;cluster_centers_ : ndarray of shape (n_clusters, n_features)
1062::COMM;;Coordinates of cluster centers. If the algorithm stops before fully
1063::COMM;;converging (see ``tol`` and ``max_iter``), these will not be
1064::COMM;;consistent with ``labels_``.
1065::COMM;;labels_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
1066::COMM;;Labels of each point
1067::COMM;;inertia_ : float
1068::COMM;;Sum of squared distances of samples to their closest cluster center,
1069::COMM;;weighted by the sample weights if provided.
1070::COMM;;n_iter_ : int
1071::COMM;;Number of iterations run.
1072::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
1073::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1074::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1075::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1076::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1077::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
1078::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1079::COMM;;See Also
1080::COMM;;--------
1081::COMM;;MiniBatchKMeans : Alternative online implementation that does incremental
1082::COMM;;updates of the centers positions using mini-batches.
1083::COMM;;For large scale learning (say n_samples > 10k) MiniBatchKMeans is
1084::COMM;;probably much faster than the default batch implementation.
1085::COMM;;Notes
1086::COMM;;-----
1087::COMM;;The k-means problem is solved using either Lloyd's or Elkan's algorithm.
1088::COMM;;The average complexity is given by O(k n T), where n is the number of
1089::COMM;;samples and T is the number of iteration.
1090::COMM;;The worst case complexity is given by O(n^(k+2/p)) with
1091::COMM;;n = n_samples, p = n_features.
1092::COMM;;Refer to :doi:`"How slow is the k-means method?" D. Arthur and S. Vassilvitskii -
1093::COMM;;SoCG2006.<10.1145/1137856.1137880>` for more details.
1094::COMM;;In practice, the k-means algorithm is very fast (one of the fastest
1095::COMM;;clustering algorithms available), but it falls in local minima. That's why
1096::COMM;;it can be useful to restart it several times.
1097::COMM;;If the algorithm stops before fully converging (because of ``tol`` or
1098::COMM;;``max_iter``), ``labels_`` and ``cluster_centers_`` will not be consistent,
1099::COMM;;i.e. the ``cluster_centers_`` will not be the means of the points in each
1100::COMM;;cluster. Also, the estimator will reassign ``labels_`` after the last
1101::COMM;;iteration to make ``labels_`` consistent with ``predict`` on the training
1102::COMM;;set.
1103::COMM;;Examples
1104::COMM;;--------
1105::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
1106::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
1107::COMM;;>>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 0],
1108::COMM;;... [10, 2], [10, 4], [10, 0]])
1109::COMM;;>>> kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=0, n_init="auto").fit(X)
1110::COMM;;>>> kmeans.labels_
1111::COMM;;array([1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0], dtype=int32)
1112::COMM;;>>> kmeans.predict([[0, 0], [12, 3]])
1113::COMM;;array([1, 0], dtype=int32)
1114::COMM;;>>> kmeans.cluster_centers_
1115::COMM;;array([[10., 2.],
1116::COMM;;[ 1., 2.]])
1117::COMM;;For examples of common problems with K-Means and how to address them see
1118::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_cluster_plot_kmeans_assumptions.py`.
1119::COMM;;For a demonstration of how K-Means can be used to cluster text documents see
1120::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_text_plot_document_clustering.py`.
1121::COMM;;For a comparison between K-Means and MiniBatchKMeans refer to example
1122::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_cluster_plot_mini_batch_kmeans.py`.
1123::COMM;;For a comparison between K-Means and BisectingKMeans refer to example
1124::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_cluster_plot_bisect_kmeans.py`.
1169::COMM;;warnings.warn(
1170::COMM;;"KMeans is known to have a memory leak on Windows "
1171::COMM;;"with MKL, when there are less chunks than available "
1172::COMM;;"threads. You can avoid it by setting the environment"
1173::COMM;;f" variable OMP_NUM_THREADS={n_active_threads}."
1174::COMM;;)

1235::COMM;;X,

1237::COMM;;init=init,
1238::COMM;;random_state=random_state,
1239::COMM;;sample_weight=sample_weight,
1240::COMM;;)

1242::COMM;;print("Initialization complete")
1243::COMM;;# run a k-means once
1244::COMM;;labels, inertia, centers, n_iter_ = kmeans_single(
1245::COMM;;X,
1246::COMM;;sample_weight,
1247::COMM;;centers_init,
1248::COMM;;max_iter=self.max_iter,
1249::COMM;;verbose=self.verbose,
1250::COMM;;tol=self._tol,
1251::COMM;;n_threads=self._n_threads,
1252::COMM;;)
1253::COMM;;# determine if these results are the best so far
1254::COMM;;# we chose a new run if it has a better inertia and the clustering is
1255::COMM;;# different from the best so far (it's possible that the inertia is
1256::COMM;;# slightly better even if the clustering is the same with potentially
1257::COMM;;# permuted labels, due to rounding errors)
1258::COMM;;if best_inertia is None or (
1259::COMM;;inertia < best_inertia

1261::COMM;;):

1264::COMM;;best_inertia = inertia

1266::COMM;;if not sp.issparse(X):
1267::COMM;;if not self.copy_x:
1268::COMM;;X += X_mean
1269::COMM;;best_centers += X_mean
1270::COMM;;distinct_clusters = len(set(best_labels))
1271::COMM;;if distinct_clusters < self.n_clusters:
1272::COMM;;warnings.warn(

1274::COMM;;"n_clusters ({}). Possibly due to duplicate points "

1276::COMM;;ConvergenceWarning,
1277::COMM;;stacklevel=2,
1278::COMM;;)
1279::COMM;;self.cluster_centers_ = best_centers
1280::COMM;;self._n_features_out = self.cluster_centers_.shape[0]
1281::COMM;;self.labels_ = best_labels
1282::COMM;;self.inertia_ = best_inertia
1283::COMM;;self.n_iter_ = best_n_iter

1285::COMM;;def _mini_batch_step(
1286::COMM;;X,
1287::COMM;;sample_weight,
1288::COMM;;centers,
1289::COMM;;centers_new,
1290::COMM;;weight_sums,
1291::COMM;;random_state,
1292::COMM;;random_reassign=False,
1293::COMM;;reassignment_ratio=0.01,
1294::COMM;;verbose=False,
1295::COMM;;n_threads=1,
1296::COMM;;):
1336::COMM;;# Perform label assignment to nearest centers
1337::COMM;;# For better efficiency, it's better to run _mini_batch_step in a
1338::COMM;;# threadpool_limit context than using _labels_inertia_threadpool_limit here
1339::COMM;;labels, inertia = _labels_inertia(X, sample_weight, centers, n_threads=n_threads)
1340::COMM;;# Update centers according to the labels
1341::COMM;;if sp.issparse(X):
1342::COMM;;_minibatch_update_sparse(
1343::COMM;;X, sample_weight, centers, centers_new, weight_sums, labels, n_threads
1344::COMM;;)
1345::COMM;;else:
1346::COMM;;_minibatch_update_dense(
1347::COMM;;X,
1348::COMM;;sample_weight,
1349::COMM;;centers,
1350::COMM;;centers_new,
1351::COMM;;weight_sums,
1352::COMM;;labels,
1353::COMM;;n_threads,
1354::COMM;;)
1355::COMM;;# Reassign clusters that have very low weight
1356::COMM;;if random_reassign and reassignment_ratio > 0:
1357::COMM;;to_reassign = weight_sums < reassignment_ratio * weight_sums.max()
1358::COMM;;# pick at most .5 * batch_size samples as new centers
1359::COMM;;if to_reassign.sum() > 0.5 * X.shape[0]:
1360::COMM;;indices_dont_reassign = np.argsort(weight_sums)[int(0.5 * X.shape[0]) :]
1361::COMM;;to_reassign[indices_dont_reassign] = False
1362::COMM;;n_reassigns = to_reassign.sum()
1363::COMM;;if n_reassigns:
1364::COMM;;# Pick new clusters amongst observations with uniform probability
1365::COMM;;new_centers = random_state.choice(
1366::COMM;;X.shape[0], replace=False, size=n_reassigns
1367::COMM;;)
1368::COMM;;if verbose:
1369::COMM;;print(f"[MiniBatchKMeans] Reassigning {n_reassigns} cluster centers.")
1370::COMM;;if sp.issparse(X):
1371::COMM;;assign_rows_csr(
1372::COMM;;X,
1373::COMM;;new_centers.astype(np.intp, copy=False),
1374::COMM;;np.where(to_reassign)[0].astype(np.intp, copy=False),
1375::COMM;;centers_new,
1376::COMM;;)
1377::COMM;;else:
1378::COMM;;centers_new[to_reassign] = X[new_centers]
1379::COMM;;# reset counts of reassigned centers, but don't reset them too small
1380::COMM;;# to avoid instant reassignment. This is a pretty dirty hack as it
1381::COMM;;# also modifies the learning rates.
1382::COMM;;weight_sums[to_reassign] = np.min(weight_sums[~to_reassign])
1383::COMM;;return inertia

1609::COMM;;def _warn_mkl_vcomp(self, n_active_threads):
1623::COMM;;# Normalize inertia to be able to compare values when
1624::COMM;;# batch_size changes
1625::COMM;;batch_inertia /= self._batch_size
1626::COMM;;# count steps starting from 1 for user friendly verbose mode.
1627::COMM;;step = step + 1
1628::COMM;;# Ignore first iteration because it's inertia from initialization.
1629::COMM;;if step == 1:
1630::COMM;;if self.verbose:
1631::COMM;;print(
1632::COMM;;f"Minibatch step {step}/{n_steps}: mean batch "
1633::COMM;;f"inertia: {batch_inertia}"
1634::COMM;;)
1635::COMM;;return False
1636::COMM;;# Compute an Exponentially Weighted Average of the inertia to
1637::COMM;;# monitor the convergence while discarding minibatch-local stochastic
1638::COMM;;# variability: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moving_average
1639::COMM;;if self._ewa_inertia is None:
1640::COMM;;self._ewa_inertia = batch_inertia
1641::COMM;;else:
1642::COMM;;alpha = self._batch_size * 2.0 / (n_samples + 1)
1643::COMM;;alpha = min(alpha, 1)
1644::COMM;;self._ewa_inertia = self._ewa_inertia * (1 - alpha) + batch_inertia * alpha
1645::COMM;;# Log progress to be able to monitor convergence
1646::COMM;;if self.verbose:
1647::COMM;;print(
1648::COMM;;f"Minibatch step {step}/{n_steps}: mean batch inertia: "
1649::COMM;;f"{batch_inertia}, ewa inertia: {self._ewa_inertia}"
1650::COMM;;)
1651::COMM;;# Early stopping based on absolute tolerance on squared change of
1652::COMM;;# centers position
1653::COMM;;if self._tol > 0.0 and centers_squared_diff <= self._tol:
1654::COMM;;if self.verbose:
1655::COMM;;print(f"Converged (small centers change) at step {step}/{n_steps}")
1656::COMM;;return True
1657::COMM;;# Early stopping heuristic due to lack of improvement on smoothed
1658::COMM;;# inertia
1659::COMM;;if self._ewa_inertia_min is None or self._ewa_inertia < self._ewa_inertia_min:
1660::COMM;;self._no_improvement = 0
1661::COMM;;self._ewa_inertia_min = self._ewa_inertia
1662::COMM;;else:
1663::COMM;;self._no_improvement += 1
1664::COMM;;if (
1665::COMM;;self.max_no_improvement is not None
1666::COMM;;and self._no_improvement >= self.max_no_improvement
1667::COMM;;):
1668::COMM;;if self.verbose:
1669::COMM;;print(
1670::COMM;;"Converged (lack of improvement in inertia) at step "
1671::COMM;;f"{step}/{n_steps}"
1672::COMM;;)
1673::COMM;;return True
1674::COMM;;return False

2::COMM;;Mean shift clustering aims to discover *blobs* in a smooth density of
3::COMM;;samples. It is a centroid based algorithm, which works by updating candidates
4::COMM;;for centroids to be the mean of the points within a given region. These
5::COMM;;candidates are then filtered in a post-processing stage to eliminate
6::COMM;;near-duplicates to form the final set of centroids.
7::COMM;;Seeding is performed using a binning technique for scalability.
9::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
10::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
35::COMM;;This function takes time at least quadratic in `n_samples`. For large
36::COMM;;datasets, it is wise to subsample by setting `n_samples`. Alternatively,
37::COMM;;the parameter `bandwidth` can be set to a small value without estimating
38::COMM;;it.

53::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None

55::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
56::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
57::COMM;;for more details.

247::COMM;;Mean shift clustering aims to discover "blobs" in a smooth density of
248::COMM;;samples. It is a centroid-based algorithm, which works by updating
249::COMM;;candidates for centroids to be the mean of the points within a given
250::COMM;;region. These candidates are then filtered in a post-processing stage to
251::COMM;;eliminate near-duplicates to form the final set of centroids.
252::COMM;;Seeding is performed using a binning technique for scalability.
253::COMM;;For an example of how to use MeanShift clustering, refer to:
254::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_cluster_plot_mean_shift.py`.
255::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <mean_shift>`.
256::COMM;;Parameters
257::COMM;;----------
258::COMM;;bandwidth : float, default=None
259::COMM;;Bandwidth used in the flat kernel.
260::COMM;;If not given, the bandwidth is estimated using
261::COMM;;sklearn.cluster.estimate_bandwidth; see the documentation for that
262::COMM;;function for hints on scalability (see also the Notes, below).
263::COMM;;seeds : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features), default=None
264::COMM;;Seeds used to initialize kernels. If not set,
265::COMM;;the seeds are calculated by clustering.get_bin_seeds
266::COMM;;with bandwidth as the grid size and default values for
267::COMM;;other parameters.
268::COMM;;bin_seeding : bool, default=False

270::COMM;;points, but rather the location of the discretized version of
271::COMM;;points, where points are binned onto a grid whose coarseness
272::COMM;;corresponds to the bandwidth. Setting this option to True will speed
273::COMM;;up the algorithm because fewer seeds will be initialized.
274::COMM;;The default value is False.
275::COMM;;Ignored if seeds argument is not None.
276::COMM;;min_bin_freq : int, default=1
277::COMM;;To speed up the algorithm, accept only those bins with at least
278::COMM;;min_bin_freq points as seeds.
279::COMM;;cluster_all : bool, default=True
280::COMM;;If true, then all points are clustered, even those orphans that are
281::COMM;;not within any kernel. Orphans are assigned to the nearest kernel.
282::COMM;;If false, then orphans are given cluster label -1.

285::COMM;;from the parallelization:

318::COMM;;-----
319::COMM;;Scalability:
320::COMM;;Because this implementation uses a flat kernel and
321::COMM;;a Ball Tree to look up members of each kernel, the complexity will tend
322::COMM;;towards O(T*n*log(n)) in lower dimensions, with n the number of samples
323::COMM;;and T the number of points. In higher dimensions the complexity will
324::COMM;;tend towards O(T*n^2).
325::COMM;;Scalability can be boosted by using fewer seeds, for example by using
326::COMM;;a higher value of min_bin_freq in the get_bin_seeds function.
327::COMM;;Note that the estimate_bandwidth function is much less scalable than the
328::COMM;;mean shift algorithm and will be the bottleneck if it is used.

2::COMM;;These routines execute the OPTICS algorithm, and implement various
3::COMM;;cluster extraction methods of the ordered list.
5::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
6::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
28::COMM;;OPTICS (Ordering Points To Identify the Clustering Structure), closely
29::COMM;;related to DBSCAN, finds core samples of high density and expands clusters
30::COMM;;from them [1]_. Unlike DBSCAN, it keeps cluster hierarchy for a variable
31::COMM;;neighborhood radius. Better suited for usage on large datasets than the
32::COMM;;current scikit-learn implementation of DBSCAN.
33::COMM;;Clusters are then extracted from the cluster-order using a
34::COMM;;DBSCAN-like method (cluster_method = 'dbscan') or an automatic
35::COMM;;technique proposed in [1]_ (cluster_method = 'xi').
36::COMM;;This implementation deviates from the original OPTICS by first performing
37::COMM;;k-nearest-neighborhood searches on all points to identify core sizes of
38::COMM;;all points (instead of computing neighbors while looping through points).
39::COMM;;Reachability distances to only unprocessed points are then computed, to
40::COMM;;construct the cluster order, similar to the original OPTICS.
41::COMM;;Note that we do not employ a heap to manage the expansion
42::COMM;;candidates, so the time complexity will be O(n^2).
43::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <optics>`.
44::COMM;;Parameters
45::COMM;;----------
46::COMM;;min_samples : int > 1 or float between 0 and 1, default=5
47::COMM;;The number of samples in a neighborhood for a point to be considered as
48::COMM;;a core point. Also, up and down steep regions can't have more than
49::COMM;;``min_samples`` consecutive non-steep points. Expressed as an absolute
50::COMM;;number or a fraction of the number of samples (rounded to be at least
51::COMM;;2).
52::COMM;;max_eps : float, default=np.inf
53::COMM;;The maximum distance between two samples for one to be considered as
54::COMM;;in the neighborhood of the other. Default value of ``np.inf`` will
55::COMM;;identify clusters across all scales; reducing ``max_eps`` will result
56::COMM;;in shorter run times.
57::COMM;;metric : str or callable, default='minkowski'
58::COMM;;Metric to use for distance computation. Any metric from scikit-learn
59::COMM;;or :mod:`scipy.spatial.distance` can be used.
60::COMM;;If `metric` is a callable function, it is called on each
61::COMM;;pair of instances (rows) and the resulting value recorded. The callable
62::COMM;;should take two arrays as input and return one value indicating the
63::COMM;;distance between them. This works for Scipy's metrics, but is less
64::COMM;;efficient than passing the metric name as a string. If metric is
65::COMM;;"precomputed", `X` is assumed to be a distance matrix and must be
66::COMM;;square.
67::COMM;;Valid values for metric are:
68::COMM;;- from scikit-learn: ['cityblock', 'cosine', 'euclidean', 'l1', 'l2',
69::COMM;;'manhattan']
70::COMM;;- from scipy.spatial.distance: ['braycurtis', 'canberra', 'chebyshev',
71::COMM;;'correlation', 'dice', 'hamming', 'jaccard', 'kulsinski',
72::COMM;;'mahalanobis', 'minkowski', 'rogerstanimoto', 'russellrao',
73::COMM;;'seuclidean', 'sokalmichener', 'sokalsneath', 'sqeuclidean',
74::COMM;;'yule']
75::COMM;;Sparse matrices are only supported by scikit-learn metrics.
76::COMM;;See :mod:`scipy.spatial.distance` for details on these metrics.
77::COMM;;.. note::
78::COMM;;`'kulsinski'` is deprecated from SciPy 1.9 and will be removed in SciPy 1.11.
79::COMM;;p : float, default=2
80::COMM;;Parameter for the Minkowski metric from
81::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances`. When p = 1, this is
82::COMM;;equivalent to using manhattan_distance (l1), and euclidean_distance
83::COMM;;(l2) for p = 2. For arbitrary p, minkowski_distance (l_p) is used.
84::COMM;;metric_params : dict, default=None
85::COMM;;Additional keyword arguments for the metric function.
86::COMM;;cluster_method : {'xi', 'dbscan'}, default='xi'
87::COMM;;The extraction method used to extract clusters using the calculated
88::COMM;;reachability and ordering.
89::COMM;;eps : float, default=None
90::COMM;;The maximum distance between two samples for one to be considered as
91::COMM;;in the neighborhood of the other. By default it assumes the same value
92::COMM;;as ``max_eps``.
93::COMM;;Used only when ``cluster_method='dbscan'``.
94::COMM;;xi : float between 0 and 1, default=0.05
95::COMM;;Determines the minimum steepness on the reachability plot that
96::COMM;;constitutes a cluster boundary. For example, an upwards point in the
97::COMM;;reachability plot is defined by the ratio from one point to its
98::COMM;;successor being at most 1-xi.
99::COMM;;Used only when ``cluster_method='xi'``.
100::COMM;;predecessor_correction : bool, default=True
101::COMM;;Correct clusters according to the predecessors calculated by OPTICS
102::COMM;;[2]_. This parameter has minimal effect on most datasets.
103::COMM;;Used only when ``cluster_method='xi'``.
104::COMM;;min_cluster_size : int > 1 or float between 0 and 1, default=None
105::COMM;;Minimum number of samples in an OPTICS cluster, expressed as an
106::COMM;;absolute number or a fraction of the number of samples (rounded to be
107::COMM;;at least 2). If ``None``, the value of ``min_samples`` is used instead.
108::COMM;;Used only when ``cluster_method='xi'``.
109::COMM;;algorithm : {'auto', 'ball_tree', 'kd_tree', 'brute'}, default='auto'
110::COMM;;Algorithm used to compute the nearest neighbors:
111::COMM;;- 'ball_tree' will use :class:`~sklearn.neighbors.BallTree`.
112::COMM;;- 'kd_tree' will use :class:`~sklearn.neighbors.KDTree`.
113::COMM;;- 'brute' will use a brute-force search.
114::COMM;;- 'auto' (default) will attempt to decide the most appropriate
115::COMM;;algorithm based on the values passed to :meth:`fit` method.
116::COMM;;Note: fitting on sparse input will override the setting of
117::COMM;;this parameter, using brute force.
118::COMM;;leaf_size : int, default=30
119::COMM;;Leaf size passed to :class:`~sklearn.neighbors.BallTree` or
120::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.neighbors.KDTree`. This can affect the speed of the
121::COMM;;construction and query, as well as the memory required to store the
122::COMM;;tree. The optimal value depends on the nature of the problem.
123::COMM;;memory : str or object with the joblib.Memory interface, default=None
124::COMM;;Used to cache the output of the computation of the tree.
125::COMM;;By default, no caching is done. If a string is given, it is the
126::COMM;;path to the caching directory.
127::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
128::COMM;;The number of parallel jobs to run for neighbors search.
129::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
130::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
131::COMM;;for more details.
132::COMM;;Attributes
133::COMM;;----------
134::COMM;;labels_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
135::COMM;;Cluster labels for each point in the dataset given to fit().
136::COMM;;Noisy samples and points which are not included in a leaf cluster
137::COMM;;of ``cluster_hierarchy_`` are labeled as -1.
138::COMM;;reachability_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
139::COMM;;Reachability distances per sample, indexed by object order. Use
140::COMM;;``clust.reachability_[clust.ordering_]`` to access in cluster order.
141::COMM;;ordering_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
142::COMM;;The cluster ordered list of sample indices.
143::COMM;;core_distances_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
144::COMM;;Distance at which each sample becomes a core point, indexed by object
145::COMM;;order. Points which will never be core have a distance of inf. Use
146::COMM;;``clust.core_distances_[clust.ordering_]`` to access in cluster order.
147::COMM;;predecessor_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
148::COMM;;Point that a sample was reached from, indexed by object order.
149::COMM;;Seed points have a predecessor of -1.
150::COMM;;cluster_hierarchy_ : ndarray of shape (n_clusters, 2)
151::COMM;;The list of clusters in the form of ``[start, end]`` in each row, with
152::COMM;;all indices inclusive. The clusters are ordered according to
153::COMM;;``(end, -start)`` (ascending) so that larger clusters encompassing
154::COMM;;smaller clusters come after those smaller ones. Since ``labels_`` does
155::COMM;;not reflect the hierarchy, usually
156::COMM;;``len(cluster_hierarchy_) > np.unique(optics.labels_)``. Please also
157::COMM;;note that these indices are of the ``ordering_``, i.e.
158::COMM;;``X[ordering_][start:end + 1]`` form a cluster.
159::COMM;;Only available when ``cluster_method='xi'``.
160::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
161::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
162::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
163::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
164::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
165::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
166::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0

405::COMM;;identify clusters across all scales; reducing ``max_eps`` will result

408::COMM;;Metric to use for distance computation. Any metric from scikit-learn
409::COMM;;or scipy.spatial.distance can be used.
410::COMM;;If metric is a callable function, it is called on each
411::COMM;;pair of instances (rows) and the resulting value recorded. The callable
412::COMM;;should take two arrays as input and return one value indicating the
413::COMM;;distance between them. This works for Scipy's metrics, but is less
414::COMM;;efficient than passing the metric name as a string. If metric is
415::COMM;;"precomputed", X is assumed to be a distance matrix and must be square.
416::COMM;;Valid values for metric are:
417::COMM;;- from scikit-learn: ['cityblock', 'cosine', 'euclidean', 'l1', 'l2',
418::COMM;;'manhattan']
419::COMM;;- from scipy.spatial.distance: ['braycurtis', 'canberra', 'chebyshev',
420::COMM;;'correlation', 'dice', 'hamming', 'jaccard', 'kulsinski',
421::COMM;;'mahalanobis', 'minkowski', 'rogerstanimoto', 'russellrao',
422::COMM;;'seuclidean', 'sokalmichener', 'sokalsneath', 'sqeuclidean',
423::COMM;;'yule']
424::COMM;;See the documentation for scipy.spatial.distance for details on these
425::COMM;;metrics.
426::COMM;;.. note::
427::COMM;;`'kulsinski'` is deprecated from SciPy 1.9 and will be removed in SciPy 1.11.
428::COMM;;p : float, default=2

430::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances`. When p = 1, this is
431::COMM;;equivalent to using manhattan_distance (l1), and euclidean_distance

505::COMO;;# Start all points as 'unprocessed' ##
520::COMO;;# Here we first do a kNN query for each point, this differs from
521::COMO;;# the original OPTICS that only used epsilon range queries.

526::COMO;;# OPTICS puts an upper limit on these, use inf for undefined.
533::COMO;;# Main OPTICS loop. Not parallelizable. The order that entries are
534::COMO;;# written to the 'ordering_' list is important!
535::COMO;;# Note that this implementation is O(n^2) theoretically, but
536::COMO;;# supposedly with very low constant factors.
540::COMO;;# Choose next based on smallest reachability distance
541::COMO;;# (And prefer smaller ids on ties, possibly np.inf!)
583::COMO;;# Assume that radius_neighbors is faster without distances
584::COMO;;# and we don't need all distances, nevertheless, this means
585::COMO;;# we may be doing some work twice.
587::COMO;;# Getting indices of neighbors that have not been processed
589::COMO;;# Neighbors of current point are already processed.
592::COMO;;# Only compute distances to unprocessed neighbors:
601::COMO;;# the same logic as neighbors, p is ignored if explicitly set
602::COMO;;# in the dict params

622::COMM;;``labels_`` which are close to a :class:`~sklearn.cluster.DBSCAN` with
623::COMM;;similar settings and ``eps``, only if ``eps`` is close to ``max_eps``.

793::COMM;;It's the same function for both upward and downward reagions, depending on

800::COMM;;``xward_point=downward`` are expected, and to extend a downward region,

845::COMM;;value, and the given complement of xi, i.e. ``1 - xi``.

882::COMM;;This is rouphly an implementation of Figure 19 of the OPTICS paper.

904::COMM;;clusters : ndarray of shape (n_clusters, 2)
905::COMM;;The list of clusters in the form of [start, end] in each row, with all
906::COMM;;indices inclusive. The clusters are ordered in a way that larger
907::COMM;;clusters encompassing smaller clusters come after those smaller
908::COMM;;clusters.
910::COMO;;# Our implementation adds an inf to the end of reachability plot
911::COMO;;# this helps to find potential clusters at the end of the
912::COMO;;# reachability plot even if there's no upward region at the end of it.
915::COMC;;sdas = [] # steep down areas, introduced in section 4.3.2 of the paper
918::COMC;;mib = 0.0 # maximum in between, section 4.3.2
919::COMO;;# Our implementation corrects a mistake in the original
920::COMO;;# paper, i.e., in Definition 9 steep downward point,
921::COMO;;# r(p) * (1 - x1) <= r(p + 1) should be
922::COMO;;# r(p) * (1 - x1) >= r(p + 1)
929::COMO;;# the following loop is almost exactly as Figure 19 of the paper.
930::COMO;;# it jumps over the areas which are not either steep down or up areas
932::COMO;;# just continue if steep_index has been a part of a discovered xward
933::COMO;;# area.
937::COMO;;# steep downward areas
946::COMO;;# steep upward areas
957::COMO;;# line (**), sc2*
960::COMO;;# Definition 11: criterion 4
963::COMO;;# Find the first index from the left side which is almost
964::COMO;;# at the same level as the end of the detected cluster.
971::COMO;;# Find the first index from the right side which is almost
972::COMO;;# at the same level as the beginning of the detected
973::COMO;;# cluster.
974::COMO;;# Our implementation corrects a mistake in the original
975::COMO;;# paper, i.e., in Definition 11 4c, r(x) < r(sD) should be
976::COMO;;# r(x) > r(sD).
979::COMO;;# predecessor correction
986::COMO;;# Definition 11: criterion 3.a
989::COMO;;# Definition 11: criterion 1
992::COMO;;# Definition 11: criterion 2
996::COMO;;# add smaller clusters first.
1002::COMM;;We rely on the fact that clusters are stored
1003::COMM;;with the smaller clusters coming before the larger ones.
1004::COMM;;Parameters
1005::COMM;;----------
1006::COMM;;ordering : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
1007::COMM;;The ordering of points calculated by OPTICS
1008::COMM;;clusters : array-like of shape (n_clusters, 2)
1009::COMM;;List of clusters i.e. (start, end) tuples,
1010::COMM;;as returned by `_xi_cluster`.
1011::COMM;;Returns
1012::COMM;;-------
1013::COMM;;labels : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
2::COMM;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
3::COMM;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
4::COMM;;import warnings
5::COMM;;from numbers import Integral, Real
6::COMM;;import numpy as np
7::COMM;;from scipy.linalg import LinAlgError, qr, svd
8::COMM;;from scipy.sparse import csc_matrix
9::COMM;;from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, ClusterMixin, _fit_context
10::COMM;;from sklearn.cluster._kmeans import k_means
11::COMM;;from sklearn.manifold._spectral_embedding import _spectral_embedding
12::COMM;;from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import KERNEL_PARAMS, pairwise_kernels
13::COMM;;from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors, kneighbors_graph

17::COMM;;def cluster_qr(vectors):
35::COMM;;k = vectors.shape[1]
36::COMM;;_, _, piv = qr(vectors.T, pivoting=True)
37::COMM;;ut, _, v = svd(vectors[piv[:k], :].T)
38::COMM;;vectors = abs(np.dot(vectors, np.dot(ut, v.conj())))
39::COMM;;return vectors.argmax(axis=1)
40::COMM;;def discretize(
41::COMM;;vectors, *, copy=True, max_svd_restarts=30, n_iter_max=20, random_state=None
42::COMM;;):
82::COMM;;random_state = check_random_state(random_state)
83::COMM;;vectors = as_float_array(vectors, copy=copy)
84::COMM;;eps = np.finfo(float).eps
85::COMM;;n_samples, n_components = vectors.shape
86::COMM;;# Normalize the eigenvectors to an equal length of a vector of ones.
87::COMM;;# Reorient the eigenvectors to point in the negative direction with respect
88::COMM;;# to the first element. This may have to do with constraining the
89::COMM;;# eigenvectors to lie in a specific quadrant to make the discretization
90::COMM;;# search easier.
91::COMM;;norm_ones = np.sqrt(n_samples)
92::COMM;;for i in range(vectors.shape[1]):
93::COMM;;vectors[:, i] = (vectors[:, i] / np.linalg.norm(vectors[:, i])) * norm_ones
94::COMM;;if vectors[0, i] != 0:
95::COMM;;vectors[:, i] = -1 * vectors[:, i] * np.sign(vectors[0, i])
96::COMM;;# Normalize the rows of the eigenvectors. Samples should lie on the unit
97::COMM;;# hypersphere centered at the origin. This transforms the samples in the
98::COMM;;# embedding space to the space of partition matrices.
99::COMM;;vectors = vectors / np.sqrt((vectors**2).sum(axis=1))[:, np.newaxis]
100::COMM;;svd_restarts = 0
101::COMM;;has_converged = False
102::COMM;;# If there is an exception we try to randomize and rerun SVD again
103::COMM;;# do this max_svd_restarts times.
104::COMM;;while (svd_restarts < max_svd_restarts) and not has_converged:
105::COMM;;# Initialize first column of rotation matrix with a row of the
106::COMM;;# eigenvectors
107::COMM;;rotation = np.zeros((n_components, n_components))
108::COMM;;rotation[:, 0] = vectors[random_state.randint(n_samples), :].T
109::COMM;;# To initialize the rest of the rotation matrix, find the rows
110::COMM;;# of the eigenvectors that are as orthogonal to each other as
111::COMM;;# possible
112::COMM;;c = np.zeros(n_samples)
113::COMM;;for j in range(1, n_components):
114::COMM;;# Accumulate c to ensure row is as orthogonal as possible to
115::COMM;;# previous picks as well as current one
116::COMM;;c += np.abs(np.dot(vectors, rotation[:, j - 1]))
117::COMM;;rotation[:, j] = vectors[c.argmin(), :].T
118::COMM;;last_objective_value = 0.0
119::COMM;;n_iter = 0
120::COMM;;while not has_converged:
121::COMM;;n_iter += 1
122::COMM;;t_discrete = np.dot(vectors, rotation)
123::COMM;;labels = t_discrete.argmax(axis=1)
124::COMM;;vectors_discrete = csc_matrix(
125::COMM;;(np.ones(len(labels)), (np.arange(0, n_samples), labels)),
126::COMM;;shape=(n_samples, n_components),
127::COMM;;)
128::COMM;;t_svd = vectors_discrete.T @ vectors
129::COMM;;try:
130::COMM;;U, S, Vh = np.linalg.svd(t_svd)
131::COMM;;except LinAlgError:
132::COMM;;svd_restarts += 1
133::COMM;;print("SVD did not converge, randomizing and trying again")
134::COMM;;break
135::COMM;;ncut_value = 2.0 * (n_samples - S.sum())
136::COMM;;if (abs(ncut_value - last_objective_value) < eps) or (n_iter > n_iter_max):
137::COMM;;has_converged = True
138::COMM;;else:
139::COMM;;# otherwise calculate rotation and continue
140::COMM;;last_objective_value = ncut_value
141::COMM;;rotation = np.dot(Vh.T, U.T)
142::COMM;;if not has_converged:
143::COMM;;raise LinAlgError("SVD did not converge")
144::COMM;;return labels
145::COMM;;@validate_params(
146::COMM;;{"affinity": ["array-like", "sparse matrix"]},
147::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=False,
148::COMM;;)
149::COMM;;def spectral_clustering(
150::COMM;;affinity,
151::COMM;;*,
152::COMM;;n_clusters=8,
153::COMM;;n_components=None,
154::COMM;;eigen_solver=None,
155::COMM;;random_state=None,
156::COMM;;n_init=10,
157::COMM;;eigen_tol="auto",
158::COMM;;assign_labels="kmeans",
159::COMM;;verbose=False,
160::COMM;;):
287::COMM;;clusterer = SpectralClustering(
288::COMM;;n_clusters=n_clusters,
289::COMM;;n_components=n_components,
290::COMM;;eigen_solver=eigen_solver,
291::COMM;;random_state=random_state,
292::COMM;;n_init=n_init,
293::COMM;;affinity="precomputed",
294::COMM;;eigen_tol=eigen_tol,
295::COMM;;assign_labels=assign_labels,
296::COMM;;verbose=verbose,
297::COMM;;).fit(affinity)
298::COMM;;return clusterer.labels_
299::COMM;;class SpectralClustering(ClusterMixin, BaseEstimator):
480::COMM;;_parameter_constraints: dict = {
481::COMM;;"n_clusters": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
482::COMM;;"eigen_solver": [StrOptions({"arpack", "lobpcg", "amg"}), None],
483::COMM;;"n_components": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left"), None],
484::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
485::COMM;;"n_init": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
486::COMM;;"gamma": [Interval(Real, 0, None, closed="left")],
487::COMM;;"affinity": [
488::COMM;;callable,
489::COMM;;StrOptions(
490::COMM;;set(KERNEL_PARAMS)
491::COMM;;| {"nearest_neighbors", "precomputed", "precomputed_nearest_neighbors"}
492::COMM;;),
493::COMM;;],
494::COMM;;"n_neighbors": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
495::COMM;;"eigen_tol": [
496::COMM;;Interval(Real, 0.0, None, closed="left"),
497::COMM;;StrOptions({"auto"}),
498::COMM;;],
499::COMM;;"assign_labels": [StrOptions({"kmeans", "discretize", "cluster_qr"})],
500::COMM;;"degree": [Interval(Real, 0, None, closed="left")],
501::COMM;;"coef0": [Interval(Real, None, None, closed="neither")],
502::COMM;;"kernel_params": [dict, None],
503::COMM;;"n_jobs": [Integral, None],
504::COMM;;"verbose": ["verbose"],
505::COMM;;}
506::COMM;;def __init__(
507::COMM;;self,
508::COMM;;n_clusters=8,
509::COMM;;*,
510::COMM;;eigen_solver=None,
511::COMM;;n_components=None,
512::COMM;;random_state=None,
513::COMM;;n_init=10,
514::COMM;;gamma=1.0,
515::COMM;;affinity="rbf",
516::COMM;;n_neighbors=10,
517::COMM;;eigen_tol="auto",
518::COMM;;assign_labels="kmeans",
519::COMM;;degree=3,
520::COMM;;coef0=1,
521::COMM;;kernel_params=None,
522::COMM;;n_jobs=None,
523::COMM;;verbose=False,
524::COMM;;):
525::COMM;;self.n_clusters = n_clusters
526::COMM;;self.eigen_solver = eigen_solver
527::COMM;;self.n_components = n_components
528::COMM;;self.random_state = random_state
529::COMM;;self.n_init = n_init
530::COMM;;self.gamma = gamma
531::COMM;;self.affinity = affinity
532::COMM;;self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
533::COMM;;self.eigen_tol = eigen_tol
534::COMM;;self.assign_labels = assign_labels
535::COMM;;self.degree = degree
536::COMM;;self.coef0 = coef0
537::COMM;;self.kernel_params = kernel_params
538::COMM;;self.n_jobs = n_jobs

540::COMM;;@_fit_context(prefer_skip_nested_validation=True)
541::COMM;;def fit(self, X, y=None):
560::COMM;;X = validate_data(
561::COMM;;self,
562::COMM;;X,
563::COMM;;accept_sparse=["csr", "csc", "coo"],
564::COMM;;dtype=np.float64,
565::COMM;;ensure_min_samples=2,
566::COMM;;)
567::COMM;;allow_squared = self.affinity in [
568::COMM;;"precomputed",
569::COMM;;"precomputed_nearest_neighbors",
570::COMM;;]
571::COMM;;if X.shape[0] == X.shape[1] and not allow_squared:
572::COMM;;warnings.warn(
573::COMM;;"The spectral clustering API has changed. ``fit``"
574::COMM;;"now constructs an affinity matrix from data. To use"
575::COMM;;" a custom affinity matrix, "
576::COMM;;"set ``affinity=precomputed``."
577::COMM;;)
578::COMM;;if self.affinity == "nearest_neighbors":
579::COMM;;connectivity = kneighbors_graph(
580::COMM;;X, n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors, include_self=True, n_jobs=self.n_jobs
581::COMM;;)
582::COMM;;self.affinity_matrix_ = 0.5 * (connectivity + connectivity.T)
583::COMM;;elif self.affinity == "precomputed_nearest_neighbors":
584::COMM;;estimator = NearestNeighbors(
585::COMM;;n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors, n_jobs=self.n_jobs, metric="precomputed"
586::COMM;;).fit(X)
587::COMM;;connectivity = estimator.kneighbors_graph(X=X, mode="connectivity")
588::COMM;;self.affinity_matrix_ = 0.5 * (connectivity + connectivity.T)
589::COMM;;elif self.affinity == "precomputed":
590::COMM;;self.affinity_matrix_ = X
591::COMM;;else:
592::COMM;;params = self.kernel_params
593::COMM;;if params is None:
594::COMM;;params = {}
595::COMM;;if not callable(self.affinity):
596::COMM;;params["gamma"] = self.gamma
597::COMM;;params["degree"] = self.degree
598::COMM;;params["coef0"] = self.coef0
599::COMM;;self.affinity_matrix_ = pairwise_kernels(
600::COMM;;X, metric=self.affinity, filter_params=True, **params
601::COMM;;)
602::COMM;;random_state = check_random_state(self.random_state)
603::COMM;;n_components = (
604::COMM;;self.n_clusters if self.n_components is None else self.n_components
605::COMM;;)
606::COMM;;# We now obtain the real valued solution matrix to the
607::COMM;;# relaxed Ncut problem, solving the eigenvalue problem
608::COMM;;# L_sym x = lambda x and recovering u = D^-1/2 x.
609::COMM;;# The first eigenvector is constant only for fully connected graphs
610::COMM;;# and should be kept for spectral clustering (drop_first = False)
611::COMM;;# See spectral_embedding documentation.
612::COMM;;maps = _spectral_embedding(
613::COMM;;self.affinity_matrix_,
614::COMM;;n_components=n_components,
615::COMM;;eigen_solver=self.eigen_solver,
616::COMM;;random_state=random_state,
617::COMM;;eigen_tol=self.eigen_tol,
618::COMM;;drop_first=False,
619::COMM;;)
620::COMM;;if self.verbose:
621::COMM;;print(f"Computing label assignment using {self.assign_labels}")
622::COMM;;if self.assign_labels == "kmeans":
623::COMM;;_, self.labels_, _ = k_means(
624::COMM;;maps,
625::COMM;;self.n_clusters,
626::COMM;;random_state=random_state,
627::COMM;;n_init=self.n_init,
628::COMM;;verbose=self.verbose,
629::COMM;;)
630::COMM;;elif self.assign_labels == "cluster_qr":
631::COMM;;self.labels_ = cluster_qr(maps)
632::COMM;;else:
633::COMM;;self.labels_ = discretize(maps, random_state=random_state)
634::COMM;;return self
635::COMM;;def fit_predict(self, X, y=None):
654::COMM;;return super().fit_predict(X, y)
655::COMM;;def __sklearn_tags__(self):
656::COMM;;tags = super().__sklearn_tags__()
657::COMM;;tags.input_tags.sparse = True
658::COMM;;tags.input_tags.pairwise = self.affinity in [
659::COMM;;"precomputed",
660::COMM;;"precomputed_nearest_neighbors",
661::COMM;;]
662::COMM;;return tags

2::COMM;;In addition to its current contents, this module will eventually be home to
3::COMM;;refurbished versions of :class:`~sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline` and
4::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.pipeline.FeatureUnion`.
6::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
7::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2::COMM;;The :mod:`sklearn.compose._column_transformer` module implements utilities
3::COMM;;to work with heterogeneous data and to apply different transformers to
4::COMM;;different columns.
6::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
7::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
60::COMM;;This estimator allows different columns or column subsets of the input
61::COMM;;to be transformed separately and the features generated by each transformer
62::COMM;;will be concatenated to form a single feature space.
63::COMM;;This is useful for heterogeneous or columnar data, to combine several
64::COMM;;feature extraction mechanisms or transformations into a single transformer.
65::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <column_transformer>`.
66::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
67::COMM;;Parameters
68::COMM;;----------
69::COMM;;transformers : list of tuples
70::COMM;;List of (name, transformer, columns) tuples specifying the
71::COMM;;transformer objects to be applied to subsets of the data.
72::COMM;;name : str
73::COMM;;Like in Pipeline and FeatureUnion, this allows the transformer and
74::COMM;;its parameters to be set using ``set_params`` and searched in grid
75::COMM;;search.
76::COMM;;transformer : {'drop', 'passthrough'} or estimator
77::COMM;;Estimator must support :term:`fit` and :term:`transform`.
78::COMM;;Special-cased strings 'drop' and 'passthrough' are accepted as
79::COMM;;well, to indicate to drop the columns or to pass them through
80::COMM;;untransformed, respectively.
81::COMM;;columns : str, array-like of str, int, array-like of int, \
82::COMM;;array-like of bool, slice or callable
83::COMM;;Indexes the data on its second axis. Integers are interpreted as
84::COMM;;positional columns, while strings can reference DataFrame columns
85::COMM;;by name. A scalar string or int should be used where
86::COMM;;``transformer`` expects X to be a 1d array-like (vector),
87::COMM;;otherwise a 2d array will be passed to the transformer.
88::COMM;;A callable is passed the input data `X` and can return any of the
89::COMM;;above. To select multiple columns by name or dtype, you can use
90::COMM;;:obj:`make_column_selector`.
91::COMM;;remainder : {'drop', 'passthrough'} or estimator, default='drop'
92::COMM;;By default, only the specified columns in `transformers` are
93::COMM;;transformed and combined in the output, and the non-specified
94::COMM;;columns are dropped. (default of ``'drop'``).
95::COMM;;By specifying ``remainder='passthrough'``, all remaining columns that
96::COMM;;were not specified in `transformers`, but present in the data passed
97::COMM;;to `fit` will be automatically passed through. This subset of columns
98::COMM;;is concatenated with the output of the transformers. For dataframes,
99::COMM;;extra columns not seen during `fit` will be excluded from the output
100::COMM;;of `transform`.
101::COMM;;By setting ``remainder`` to be an estimator, the remaining
102::COMM;;non-specified columns will use the ``remainder`` estimator. The
103::COMM;;estimator must support :term:`fit` and :term:`transform`.
104::COMM;;Note that using this feature requires that the DataFrame columns
105::COMM;;input at :term:`fit` and :term:`transform` have identical order.
106::COMM;;sparse_threshold : float, default=0.3
107::COMM;;If the output of the different transformers contains sparse matrices,
108::COMM;;these will be stacked as a sparse matrix if the overall density is
109::COMM;;lower than this value. Use ``sparse_threshold=0`` to always return
110::COMM;;dense. When the transformed output consists of all dense data, the
111::COMM;;stacked result will be dense, and this keyword will be ignored.
112::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
113::COMM;;Number of jobs to run in parallel.
114::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
115::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
116::COMM;;for more details.
117::COMM;;transformer_weights : dict, default=None
118::COMM;;Multiplicative weights for features per transformer. The output of the
119::COMM;;transformer is multiplied by these weights. Keys are transformer names,
120::COMM;;values the weights.
121::COMM;;verbose : bool, default=False
122::COMM;;If True, the time elapsed while fitting each transformer will be
123::COMM;;printed as it is completed.
124::COMM;;verbose_feature_names_out : bool, str or Callable[[str, str], str], default=True
125::COMM;;- If True, :meth:`ColumnTransformer.get_feature_names_out` will prefix
126::COMM;;all feature names with the name of the transformer that generated that
127::COMM;;feature. It is equivalent to setting
128::COMM;;`verbose_feature_names_out="{transformer_name}__{feature_name}"`.
129::COMM;;- If False, :meth:`ColumnTransformer.get_feature_names_out` will not
130::COMM;;prefix any feature names and will error if feature names are not
131::COMM;;unique.
132::COMM;;- If ``Callable[[str, str], str]``,
133::COMM;;:meth:`ColumnTransformer.get_feature_names_out` will rename all the features
134::COMM;;using the name of the transformer. The first argument of the callable is the
135::COMM;;transformer name and the second argument is the feature name. The returned
136::COMM;;string will be the new feature name.
137::COMM;;- If ``str``, it must be a string ready for formatting. The given string will
138::COMM;;be formatted using two field names: ``transformer_name`` and ``feature_name``.
139::COMM;;e.g. ``"{feature_name}__{transformer_name}"``. See :meth:`str.format` method
140::COMM;;from the standard library for more info.
141::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
142::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.6
143::COMM;;`verbose_feature_names_out` can be a callable or a string to be formatted.
144::COMM;;force_int_remainder_cols : bool, default=False
145::COMM;;This parameter has no effect.
146::COMM;;.. note::
147::COMM;;If you do not access the list of columns for the remainder columns
148::COMM;;in the `transformers_` fitted attribute, you do not need to set
149::COMM;;this parameter.
150::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.5
151::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7
152::COMM;;The default value for `force_int_remainder_cols` will change from
153::COMM;;`True` to `False` in version 1.7.
154::COMM;;.. deprecated:: 1.7
155::COMM;;`force_int_remainder_cols` is deprecated and will be removed in 1.9.
156::COMM;;Attributes
157::COMM;;----------
158::COMM;;transformers_ : list
159::COMM;;The collection of fitted transformers as tuples of (name,
160::COMM;;fitted_transformer, column). `fitted_transformer` can be an estimator,
161::COMM;;or `'drop'`; `'passthrough'` is replaced with an equivalent
162::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.FunctionTransformer`. In case there were
163::COMM;;no columns selected, this will be the unfitted transformer. If there
164::COMM;;are remaining columns, the final element is a tuple of the form:
165::COMM;;('remainder', transformer, remaining_columns) corresponding to the
166::COMM;;``remainder`` parameter. If there are remaining columns, then
167::COMM;;``len(transformers_)==len(transformers)+1``, otherwise
168::COMM;;``len(transformers_)==len(transformers)``.
169::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.7
170::COMM;;The format of the remaining columns now attempts to match that of the other
171::COMM;;transformers: if all columns were provided as column names (`str`), the
172::COMM;;remaining columns are stored as column names; if all columns were provided
173::COMM;;as mask arrays (`bool`), so are the remaining columns; in all other cases
174::COMM;;the remaining columns are stored as indices (`int`).
175::COMM;;named_transformers_ : :class:`~sklearn.utils.Bunch`
176::COMM;;Read-only attribute to access any transformer by given name.
177::COMM;;Keys are transformer names and values are the fitted transformer
178::COMM;;objects.
179::COMM;;sparse_output_ : bool
180::COMM;;Boolean flag indicating whether the output of ``transform`` is a
181::COMM;;sparse matrix or a dense numpy array, which depends on the output
182::COMM;;of the individual transformers and the `sparse_threshold` keyword.
183::COMM;;output_indices_ : dict
184::COMM;;A dictionary from each transformer name to a slice, where the slice
185::COMM;;corresponds to indices in the transformed output. This is useful to
186::COMM;;inspect which transformer is responsible for which transformed
187::COMM;;feature(s).
188::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
189::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
190::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if the
191::COMM;;underlying transformers expose such an attribute when fit.
192::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
193::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
194::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
195::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
196::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
197::COMM;;See Also
198::COMM;;--------
199::COMM;;make_column_transformer : Convenience function for
200::COMM;;combining the outputs of multiple transformer objects applied to
201::COMM;;column subsets of the original feature space.
202::COMM;;make_column_selector : Convenience function for selecting
203::COMM;;columns based on datatype or the columns name with a regex pattern.
204::COMM;;Notes
205::COMM;;-----
206::COMM;;The order of the columns in the transformed feature matrix follows the
207::COMM;;order of how the columns are specified in the `transformers` list.
208::COMM;;Columns of the original feature matrix that are not specified are
209::COMM;;dropped from the resulting transformed feature matrix, unless specified
210::COMM;;in the `passthrough` keyword. Those columns specified with `passthrough`
211::COMM;;are added at the right to the output of the transformers.
212::COMM;;Examples
213::COMM;;--------
214::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
215::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
216::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import Normalizer
217::COMM;;>>> ct = ColumnTransformer(
218::COMM;;... [("norm1", Normalizer(norm='l1'), [0, 1]),
219::COMM;;... ("norm2", Normalizer(norm='l1'), slice(2, 4))])
220::COMM;;>>> X = np.array([[0., 1., 2., 2.],
221::COMM;;... [1., 1., 0., 1.]])
222::COMM;;>>> # Normalizer scales each row of X to unit norm. A separate scaling
223::COMM;;>>> # is applied for the two first and two last elements of each
224::COMM;;>>> # row independently.
225::COMM;;>>> ct.fit_transform(X)
226::COMM;;array([[0. , 1. , 0.5, 0.5],
227::COMM;;[0.5, 0.5, 0. , 1. ]])
228::COMM;;:class:`ColumnTransformer` can be configured with a transformer that requires
229::COMM;;a 1d array by setting the column to a string:
230::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
231::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
232::COMM;;>>> import pandas as pd # doctest: +SKIP
233::COMM;;>>> X = pd.DataFrame({
234::COMM;;... "documents": ["First item", "second one here", "Is this the last?"],
235::COMM;;... "width": [3, 4, 5],
236::COMM;;... }) # doctest: +SKIP
237::COMM;;>>> # "documents" is a string which configures ColumnTransformer to
238::COMM;;>>> # pass the documents column as a 1d array to the CountVectorizer
239::COMM;;>>> ct = ColumnTransformer(
240::COMM;;... [("text_preprocess", CountVectorizer(), "documents"),
241::COMM;;... ("num_preprocess", MinMaxScaler(), ["width"])])
242::COMM;;>>> X_trans = ct.fit_transform(X) # doctest: +SKIP
243::COMM;;For a more detailed example of usage, see
244::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_compose_plot_column_transformer_mixed_types.py`.
283::COMM;;Internal list of transformer only containing the name and
284::COMM;;transformers, dropping the columns.
285::COMM;;DO NOT USE: This is for the implementation of get_params via
286::COMM;;BaseComposition._get_params which expects lists of tuples of len 2.
287::COMM;;To iterate through the transformers, use ``self._iter`` instead.
296::COMM;;BaseComposition._get_params which gives lists of tuples of len 2.
307::COMM;;Calling `set_output` will set the output of all estimators in `transformers`
308::COMM;;and `transformers_`.
309::COMM;;Parameters
310::COMM;;----------
311::COMM;;transform : {"default", "pandas", "polars"}, default=None
312::COMM;;Configure output of `transform` and `fit_transform`.
313::COMM;;- `"default"`: Default output format of a transformer
314::COMM;;- `"pandas"`: DataFrame output
315::COMM;;- `"polars"`: Polars output
316::COMM;;- `None`: Transform configuration is unchanged
317::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
318::COMM;;`"polars"` option was added.
319::COMM;;Returns
320::COMM;;-------
321::COMM;;self : estimator instance
322::COMM;;Estimator instance.

1::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
