22::COMM;;Useful for applying a non-linear transformation to the target `y` in
23::COMM;;regression problems. This transformation can be given as a Transformer
24::COMM;;such as the :class:`~sklearn.preprocessing.QuantileTransformer` or as a
25::COMM;;function and its inverse such as `np.log` and `np.exp`.
26::COMM;;The computation during :meth:`fit` is::
27::COMM;;regressor.fit(X, func(y))
28::COMM;;or::
29::COMM;;regressor.fit(X, transformer.transform(y))
30::COMM;;The computation during :meth:`predict` is::
31::COMM;;inverse_func(regressor.predict(X))
32::COMM;;or::
33::COMM;;transformer.inverse_transform(regressor.predict(X))
34::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <transformed_target_regressor>`.
35::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
36::COMM;;Parameters
37::COMM;;----------
38::COMM;;regressor : object, default=None
39::COMM;;Regressor object such as derived from
40::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.base.RegressorMixin`. This regressor will
41::COMM;;automatically be cloned each time prior to fitting. If `regressor is
42::COMM;;None`, :class:`~sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression` is created and used.
43::COMM;;transformer : object, default=None
44::COMM;;Estimator object such as derived from
45::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.base.TransformerMixin`. Cannot be set at the same time
46::COMM;;as `func` and `inverse_func`. If `transformer is None` as well as
47::COMM;;`func` and `inverse_func`, the transformer will be an identity
48::COMM;;transformer. Note that the transformer will be cloned during fitting.
49::COMM;;Also, the transformer is restricting `y` to be a numpy array.
50::COMM;;func : function, default=None
51::COMM;;Function to apply to `y` before passing to :meth:`fit`. Cannot be set
52::COMM;;at the same time as `transformer`. If `func is None`, the function used will be
53::COMM;;the identity function. If `func` is set, `inverse_func` also needs to be
54::COMM;;provided. The function needs to return a 2-dimensional array.
55::COMM;;inverse_func : function, default=None
56::COMM;;Function to apply to the prediction of the regressor. Cannot be set at
57::COMM;;the same time as `transformer`. The inverse function is used to return
58::COMM;;predictions to the same space of the original training labels. If
59::COMM;;`inverse_func` is set, `func` also needs to be provided. The inverse
60::COMM;;function needs to return a 2-dimensional array.
61::COMM;;check_inverse : bool, default=True
62::COMM;;Whether to check that `transform` followed by `inverse_transform`
63::COMM;;or `func` followed by `inverse_func` leads to the original targets.
64::COMM;;Attributes
65::COMM;;----------
66::COMM;;regressor_ : object
67::COMM;;Fitted regressor.
68::COMM;;transformer_ : object
69::COMM;;Transformer used in :meth:`fit` and :meth:`predict`.
70::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
71::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if the
72::COMM;;underlying regressor exposes such an attribute when fit.
73::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
74::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
75::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
76::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
77::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
78::COMM;;See Also
79::COMM;;--------
80::COMM;;sklearn.preprocessing.FunctionTransformer : Construct a transformer from an
81::COMM;;arbitrary callable.
82::COMM;;Notes
83::COMM;;-----
84::COMM;;Internally, the target `y` is always converted into a 2-dimensional array
85::COMM;;to be used by scikit-learn transformers. At the time of prediction, the
86::COMM;;output will be reshaped to a have the same number of dimensions as `y`.
87::COMM;;Examples
88::COMM;;--------
89::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
90::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
91::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.compose import TransformedTargetRegressor
92::COMM;;>>> tt = TransformedTargetRegressor(regressor=LinearRegression(),
93::COMM;;... func=np.log, inverse_func=np.exp)
94::COMM;;>>> X = np.arange(4).reshape(-1, 1)
95::COMM;;>>> y = np.exp(2 * X).ravel()
96::COMM;;>>> tt.fit(X, y)
97::COMM;;TransformedTargetRegressor(...)
98::COMM;;>>> tt.score(X, y)
99::COMM;;1.0
100::COMM;;>>> tt.regressor_.coef_
101::COMM;;array([2.])
102::COMM;;For a more detailed example use case refer to
103::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_compose_plot_transformed_target.py`.

129::COMM;;check on a subset (optional).

2::COMM;;They estimate the covariance of features at given sets of points, as well as the
3::COMM;;precision matrix defined as the inverse of the covariance. Covariance estimation is
4::COMM;;closely related to the theory of Gaussian graphical models.
6::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
7::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
1::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
2::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
12::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <outlier_detection>`.
13::COMM;;Parameters
14::COMM;;----------
15::COMM;;store_precision : bool, default=True
16::COMM;;Specify if the estimated precision is stored.
17::COMM;;assume_centered : bool, default=False
18::COMM;;If True, the support of robust location and covariance estimates
19::COMM;;is computed, and a covariance estimate is recomputed from it,
20::COMM;;without centering the data.
21::COMM;;Useful to work with data whose mean is significantly equal to
22::COMM;;zero but is not exactly zero.
23::COMM;;If False, the robust location and covariance are directly computed
24::COMM;;with the FastMCD algorithm without additional treatment.
25::COMM;;support_fraction : float, default=None
26::COMM;;The proportion of points to be included in the support of the raw
27::COMM;;MCD estimate. If None, the minimum value of support_fraction will
28::COMM;;be used within the algorithm: `(n_samples + n_features + 1) / 2 * n_samples`.
29::COMM;;Range is (0, 1).
30::COMM;;contamination : float, default=0.1
31::COMM;;The amount of contamination of the data set, i.e. the proportion
32::COMM;;of outliers in the data set. Range is (0, 0.5].
33::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
34::COMM;;Determines the pseudo random number generator for shuffling
35::COMM;;the data. Pass an int for reproducible results across multiple function
36::COMM;;calls. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
37::COMM;;Attributes
38::COMM;;----------
39::COMM;;location_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
40::COMM;;Estimated robust location.
41::COMM;;covariance_ : ndarray of shape (n_features, n_features)
42::COMM;;Estimated robust covariance matrix.
43::COMM;;precision_ : ndarray of shape (n_features, n_features)
44::COMM;;Estimated pseudo inverse matrix.
45::COMM;;(stored only if store_precision is True)
46::COMM;;support_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
47::COMM;;A mask of the observations that have been used to compute the
48::COMM;;robust estimates of location and shape.
49::COMM;;offset_ : float
50::COMM;;Offset used to define the decision function from the raw scores.
51::COMM;;We have the relation: ``decision_function = score_samples - offset_``.
52::COMM;;The offset depends on the contamination parameter and is defined in
53::COMM;;such a way we obtain the expected number of outliers (samples with
54::COMM;;decision function < 0) in training.
55::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
56::COMM;;raw_location_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
57::COMM;;The raw robust estimated location before correction and re-weighting.
58::COMM;;raw_covariance_ : ndarray of shape (n_features, n_features)
59::COMM;;The raw robust estimated covariance before correction and re-weighting.
60::COMM;;raw_support_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
61::COMM;;A mask of the observations that have been used to compute
62::COMM;;the raw robust estimates of location and shape, before correction
63::COMM;;and re-weighting.
64::COMM;;dist_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
65::COMM;;Mahalanobis distances of the training set (on which :meth:`fit` is
66::COMM;;called) observations.
67::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
68::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
69::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
70::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
71::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
72::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
73::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
74::COMM;;See Also
75::COMM;;--------
76::COMM;;EmpiricalCovariance : Maximum likelihood covariance estimator.
77::COMM;;GraphicalLasso : Sparse inverse covariance estimation
78::COMM;;with an l1-penalized estimator.
79::COMM;;LedoitWolf : LedoitWolf Estimator.
80::COMM;;MinCovDet : Minimum Covariance Determinant
81::COMM;;(robust estimator of covariance).
82::COMM;;OAS : Oracle Approximating Shrinkage Estimator.
83::COMM;;ShrunkCovariance : Covariance estimator with shrinkage.
84::COMM;;Notes
85::COMM;;-----
86::COMM;;Outlier detection from covariance estimation may break or not
87::COMM;;perform well in high-dimensional settings. In particular, one will
88::COMM;;always take care to work with ``n_samples > n_features ** 2``.
89::COMM;;References
90::COMM;;----------

36::COMO;;# Helper functions to compute the objective and dual objective functions
37::COMO;;# of the l1-penalized estimator
40::COMM;;the objective function is made of a shifted scaled version of the
41::COMM;;normalized log-likelihood (i.e. its empirical mean over the samples) and a
42::COMM;;penalisation term to promote sparsity
50::COMM;;The specific definition is given in Duchi "Projected Subgradient Methods
51::COMM;;for Learning Sparse Gaussians".
57::COMO;;# The g-lasso algorithm
72::COMO;;# Early return without regularization
82::COMO;;# As a trivial regularization (Tikhonov like), we scale down the
83::COMO;;# off-diagonal coefficients of our starting point: This is needed, as
84::COMO;;# in the cross-validation the cov_init can easily be
85::COMO;;# ill-conditioned, and the CV loop blows. Beside, this takes
86::COMO;;# conservative stand-point on the initial conditions, and it tends to
87::COMO;;# make the convergence go faster.
93::COMC;;i = 0 # initialize the counter to be robust to `max_iter=0`
95::COMO;;# The different l1 regression solver have different numerical errors
101::COMO;;# be robust to the max_iter=0 edge case, see:
102::COMO;;# https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/4134
104::COMO;;# set a sub_covariance buffer
108::COMO;;# To keep the contiguous matrix `sub_covariance` equal to
109::COMO;;# covariance_[indices != idx].T[indices != idx]
110::COMO;;# we only need to update 1 column and 1 line when idx changes
120::COMO;;# Use coordinate descent

133::COMO;;# solver (graphical lasso) is coupled with the max_iter of
134::COMO;;# the inner solver (CD). Ideally, CD has its own parameter
135::COMO;;# enet_max_iter (like enet_tol). A minimum of 20 is rather
136::COMO;;# arbitrary, but not unreasonable.
144::COMC;;else: # mode == "lars"

722::COMM;;graphical_lasso : L1-penalized covariance estimator.
723::COMM;;GraphicalLasso : Sparse inverse covariance estimation
724::COMM;;with an l1-penalized estimator.
725::COMM;;Notes
726::COMM;;-----
727::COMM;;The search for the optimal penalization parameter (`alpha`) is done on an
728::COMM;;iteratively refined grid: first the cross-validated scores on a grid are
729::COMM;;computed, then a new refined grid is centered around the maximum, and so
730::COMM;;on.
731::COMM;;One of the challenges which is faced here is that the solvers can
732::COMM;;fail to converge to a well-conditioned estimate. The corresponding
733::COMM;;values of `alpha` then come out as missing values, but the optimum may
734::COMM;;be close to these missing values.
735::COMM;;In `fit`, once the best parameter `alpha` is found through
736::COMM;;cross-validation, the model is fit again using the entire training set.
737::COMM;;Examples
738::COMM;;--------
739::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
740::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.covariance import GraphicalLassoCV
741::COMM;;>>> true_cov = np.array([[0.8, 0.0, 0.2, 0.0],
742::COMM;;... [0.0, 0.4, 0.0, 0.0],
743::COMM;;... [0.2, 0.0, 0.3, 0.1],
744::COMM;;... [0.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.7]])
745::COMM;;>>> np.random.seed(0)
746::COMM;;>>> X = np.random.multivariate_normal(mean=[0, 0, 0, 0],
747::COMM;;... cov=true_cov,
748::COMM;;... size=200)
749::COMM;;>>> cov = GraphicalLassoCV().fit(X)
750::COMM;;>>> np.around(cov.covariance_, decimals=3)
751::COMM;;array([[0.816, 0.051, 0.22 , 0.017],
752::COMM;;[0.051, 0.364, 0.018, 0.036],
753::COMM;;[0.22 , 0.018, 0.322, 0.094],
754::COMM;;[0.017, 0.036, 0.094, 0.69 ]])
755::COMM;;>>> np.around(cov.location_, decimals=3)
756::COMM;;array([0.073, 0.04 , 0.038, 0.143])
757::COMM;;For an example comparing :class:`sklearn.covariance.GraphicalLassoCV`,
758::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.covariance.ledoit_wolf` shrinkage and the empirical covariance
759::COMM;;on high-dimensional gaussian data, see
760::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_covariance_plot_sparse_cov.py`.

226::COMM;;The purpose of this function is to find the best sets of n_support
227::COMM;;observations with respect to a minimization of their covariance
228::COMM;;matrix determinant. Equivalently, it removes n_samples-n_support
229::COMM;;observations to construct what we call a pure data set (i.e. not
230::COMM;;containing outliers). The list of the observations of the pure
231::COMM;;data set is referred to as the `support`.
232::COMM;;Starting from a random support, the pure data set is found by the
233::COMM;;c_step procedure introduced by Rousseeuw and Van Driessen in
234::COMM;;[RV]_.

377::COMM;;-----
378::COMM;;The FastMCD algorithm has been introduced by Rousseuw and Van Driessen
379::COMM;;in "A Fast Algorithm for the Minimum Covariance Determinant Estimator,
380::COMM;;1999, American Statistical Association and the American Society

34::COMM;;def _oas(X, *, assume_centered=False):
42::COMM;;if len(X.shape) == 2 and X.shape[1] == 1:
43::COMM;;# for only one feature, the result is the same whatever the shrinkage
44::COMM;;if not assume_centered:
45::COMM;;X = X - X.mean()
46::COMM;;return np.atleast_2d((X**2).mean()), 0.0
47::COMM;;n_samples, n_features = X.shape
48::COMM;;emp_cov = empirical_covariance(X, assume_centered=assume_centered)
49::COMM;;# The shrinkage is defined as:
50::COMM;;# shrinkage = min(
51::COMM;;# trace(S @ S.T) + trace(S)**2) / ((n + 1) (trace(S @ S.T) - trace(S)**2 / p), 1
52::COMM;;# )
53::COMM;;# where n and p are n_samples and n_features, respectively (cf. Eq. 23 in [1]).
54::COMM;;# The factor 2 / p is omitted since it does not impact the value of the estimator
55::COMM;;# for large p.
56::COMM;;# Instead of computing trace(S)**2, we can compute the average of the squared
57::COMM;;# elements of S that is equal to trace(S)**2 / p**2.
58::COMM;;# See the definition of the Frobenius norm:
59::COMM;;# https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_norm#Frobenius_norm
60::COMM;;alpha = np.mean(emp_cov**2)
61::COMM;;mu = np.trace(emp_cov) / n_features
62::COMM;;mu_squared = mu**2
63::COMM;;# The factor 1 / p**2 will cancel out since it is in both the numerator and
64::COMM;;# denominator
65::COMM;;num = alpha + mu_squared
66::COMM;;den = (n_samples + 1) * (alpha - mu_squared / n_features)
67::COMM;;shrinkage = 1.0 if den == 0 else min(num / den, 1.0)
68::COMM;;# The shrunk covariance is defined as:
69::COMM;;# (1 - shrinkage) * S + shrinkage * F (cf. Eq. 4 in [1])
70::COMM;;# where S is the empirical covariance and F is the shrinkage target defined as
71::COMM;;# F = trace(S) / n_features * np.identity(n_features) (cf. Eq. 3 in [1])
72::COMM;;shrunk_cov = (1.0 - shrinkage) * emp_cov
73::COMM;;shrunk_cov.flat[:: n_features + 1] += shrinkage * mu
74::COMM;;return shrunk_cov, shrinkage

120::COMM;;mu = np.expand_dims(mu, axis=tuple(range(mu.ndim, emp_cov.ndim)))
121::COMM;;shrunk_cov += shrinkage * mu * np.eye(n_features)

223::COMM;;self._set_covariance(covariance)

225::COMM;;# Ledoit-Wolf estimator
226::COMM;;@validate_params(
227::COMM;;{
228::COMM;;"X": ["array-like"],
229::COMM;;"assume_centered": ["boolean"],
230::COMM;;"block_size": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
231::COMM;;},
232::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
233::COMM;;)
234::COMM;;def ledoit_wolf_shrinkage(X, assume_centered=False, block_size=1000):
269::COMM;;X = check_array(X)
270::COMM;;# for only one feature, the result is the same whatever the shrinkage
271::COMM;;if len(X.shape) == 2 and X.shape[1] == 1:
272::COMM;;return 0.0
273::COMM;;if X.ndim == 1:
274::COMM;;X = np.reshape(X, (1, -1))
275::COMM;;if X.shape[0] == 1:
276::COMM;;warnings.warn(
277::COMM;;"Only one sample available. You may want to reshape your data array"
278::COMM;;)
279::COMM;;n_samples, n_features = X.shape
280::COMM;;# optionally center data
281::COMM;;if not assume_centered:
282::COMM;;X = X - X.mean(0)
283::COMM;;# A non-blocked version of the computation is present in the tests
284::COMM;;# in tests/test_covariance.py
285::COMM;;# number of blocks to split the covariance matrix into
286::COMM;;n_splits = int(n_features / block_size)
287::COMM;;X2 = X**2
288::COMM;;emp_cov_trace = np.sum(X2, axis=0) / n_samples
289::COMM;;mu = np.sum(emp_cov_trace) / n_features
290::COMM;;beta_ = 0.0 # sum of the coefficients of <X2.T, X2>
291::COMM;;delta_ = 0.0 # sum of the *squared* coefficients of <X.T, X>
292::COMM;;# starting block computation
293::COMM;;for i in range(n_splits):
294::COMM;;for j in range(n_splits):
295::COMM;;rows = slice(block_size * i, block_size * (i + 1))
296::COMM;;cols = slice(block_size * j, block_size * (j + 1))
297::COMM;;beta_ += np.sum(np.dot(X2.T[rows], X2[:, cols]))
298::COMM;;delta_ += np.sum(np.dot(X.T[rows], X[:, cols]) ** 2)
299::COMM;;rows = slice(block_size * i, block_size * (i + 1))
300::COMM;;beta_ += np.sum(np.dot(X2.T[rows], X2[:, block_size * n_splits :]))
301::COMM;;delta_ += np.sum(np.dot(X.T[rows], X[:, block_size * n_splits :]) ** 2)
302::COMM;;for j in range(n_splits):
303::COMM;;cols = slice(block_size * j, block_size * (j + 1))
304::COMM;;beta_ += np.sum(np.dot(X2.T[block_size * n_splits :], X2[:, cols]))
305::COMM;;delta_ += np.sum(np.dot(X.T[block_size * n_splits :], X[:, cols]) ** 2)
306::COMM;;delta_ += np.sum(
307::COMM;;np.dot(X.T[block_size * n_splits :], X[:, block_size * n_splits :]) ** 2
308::COMM;;)
309::COMM;;delta_ /= n_samples**2
310::COMM;;beta_ += np.sum(
311::COMM;;np.dot(X2.T[block_size * n_splits :], X2[:, block_size * n_splits :])
312::COMM;;)
313::COMM;;# use delta_ to compute beta
314::COMM;;beta = 1.0 / (n_features * n_samples) * (beta_ / n_samples - delta_)
315::COMM;;# delta is the sum of the squared coefficients of (<X.T,X> - mu*Id) / p
316::COMM;;delta = delta_ - 2.0 * mu * emp_cov_trace.sum() + n_features * mu**2
317::COMM;;delta /= n_features
318::COMM;;# get final beta as the min between beta and delta
319::COMM;;# We do this to prevent shrinking more than "1", which would invert
320::COMM;;# the value of covariances
321::COMM;;beta = min(beta, delta)
322::COMM;;# finally get shrinkage
323::COMM;;shrinkage = 0 if beta == 0 else beta / delta
324::COMM;;return shrinkage
325::COMM;;@validate_params(
326::COMM;;{"X": ["array-like"]},
327::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=False,
328::COMM;;)
329::COMM;;def ledoit_wolf(X, *, assume_centered=False, block_size=1000):
370::COMM;;estimator = LedoitWolf(
371::COMM;;assume_centered=assume_centered,
372::COMM;;block_size=block_size,
373::COMM;;store_precision=False,
374::COMM;;).fit(X)
375::COMM;;return estimator.covariance_, estimator.shrinkage_

66::COMO;;# (i.e. n_support = n_samples)
72::COMO;;# Check that MCD completes when the covariance matrix is singular
73::COMO;;# i.e. one of the rows and columns are all zeros
75::COMO;;# Think of these as the values for X and Y -> 10 values between -5 and 5
77::COMO;;# Get the cartesian product of all possible coordinate pairs from above set
79::COMO;;# Add a third column that's all zeros to make our data a set of point
80::COMO;;# within a plane, which means that the covariance matrix will be singular
82::COMO;;# The below line of code should raise an exception if the covariance matrix
83::COMO;;# is singular. As a further test, since we have points in XYZ, the
84::COMO;;# principle components (Eigenvectors) of these directly relate to the
85::COMO;;# geometry of the points. Since it's a plane, we should be able to test
86::COMO;;# that the Eigenvector that corresponds to the smallest Eigenvalue is the
87::COMO;;# plane normal, specifically [0, 0, 1], since everything is in the XY plane
88::COMO;;# (as I've set it up above). To do this one would start by:
89::COMO;;#
90::COMO;;# evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(mcd_fit.covariance_)
91::COMO;;# normal = evecs[:, np.argmin(evals)]
92::COMO;;#
93::COMO;;# After which we need to assert that our `normal` is equal to [0, 0, 1].
94::COMO;;# Do note that there is floating point error associated with this, so it's
95::COMO;;# best to subtract the two and then compare some small tolerance (e.g.
96::COMO;;# 1e-12).
99::COMO;;# Check that MCD returns a ValueError with informative message when the
100::COMO;;# covariance of the support data is equal to 0.
113::COMO;;# Check that a warning is raised if we observe increasing determinants
114::COMO;;# during the c_step. In theory the sequence of determinants should be
115::COMO;;# decreasing. Increasing determinants are likely due to ill-conditioned
116::COMO;;# covariance matrices that result in poor precision matrices.
145::COMM;;variance on Gaussian data.

221::COMM;;norm_y_weights = self._norm_y_weights

234::COMM;;# review from Wegelin. See above for a notation mapping from code to
235::COMM;;# paper.
236::COMM;;y_eps = np.finfo(yk.dtype).eps
237::COMM;;for k in range(n_components):

261::COMM;;break

265::COMM;;# inplace sign flip for consistency across solvers and archs
266::COMM;;_svd_flip_1d(x_weights, y_weights)

274::COMM;;# Deflation: subtract rank-one approx to obtain Xk+1 and yk+1
275::COMM;;x_loadings = np.dot(x_scores, Xk) / np.dot(x_scores, x_scores)
276::COMM;;Xk -= np.outer(x_scores, x_loadings)

280::COMM;;yk -= np.outer(y_scores, y_loadings)
281::COMM;;if self.deflation_mode == "regression":
282::COMM;;# regress yk on x_score
283::COMM;;y_loadings = np.dot(x_scores, yk) / np.dot(x_scores, x_scores)
284::COMM;;yk -= np.outer(x_scores, y_loadings)
285::COMM;;self.x_weights_[:, k] = x_weights
286::COMM;;self.y_weights_[:, k] = y_weights
287::COMM;;self._x_scores[:, k] = x_scores
288::COMM;;self._y_scores[:, k] = y_scores
289::COMM;;self.x_loadings_[:, k] = x_loadings

291::COMM;;# X was approximated as Xi . Gamma.T + X_(R+1)
292::COMM;;# Xi . Gamma.T is a sum of n_components rank-1 matrices. X_(R+1) is
293::COMM;;# whatever is left to fully reconstruct X, and can be 0 if X is of rank
294::COMM;;# n_components.
295::COMM;;# Similarly, y was approximated as Omega . Delta.T + y_(R+1)
296::COMM;;# Compute transformation matrices (rotations_). See User Guide.
297::COMM;;self.x_rotations_ = np.dot(

300::COMM;;)

304::COMM;;)

306::COMM;;self.coef_ = (self.coef_ * self._y_std).T / self._x_std
307::COMM;;self.intercept_ = self._y_mean

309::COMM;;return self

219::COMM;;num_obs = max(arff_data[1]) + 1
220::COMM;;X_shape = (num_obs, len(feature_indices_to_select))
221::COMM;;X = sp.sparse.coo_matrix(
222::COMM;;(arff_data_X[0], (arff_data_X[1], arff_data_X[2])),
223::COMM;;shape=X_shape,
224::COMM;;dtype=np.float64,
225::COMM;;)
226::COMM;;X = X.tocsr()
227::COMM;;y = _sparse_data_to_array(arff_data, target_indices_to_select)
228::COMM;;else:
229::COMM;;# This should never happen
230::COMM;;raise ValueError(
231::COMM;;f"Unexpected type for data obtained from arff: {type(arff_data)}"
232::COMM;;)
233::COMM;;is_classification = {
234::COMM;;col_name in categories for col_name in target_names_to_select
235::COMM;;}
236::COMM;;if not is_classification:
237::COMM;;# No target
238::COMM;;pass
239::COMM;;elif all(is_classification):
240::COMM;;y = np.hstack(
241::COMM;;[
242::COMM;;np.take(
243::COMM;;np.asarray(categories.pop(col_name), dtype="O"),
244::COMM;;y[:, i : i + 1].astype(int, copy=False),
245::COMM;;)
246::COMM;;for i, col_name in enumerate(target_names_to_select)
247::COMM;;]
248::COMM;;)
249::COMM;;elif any(is_classification):
250::COMM;;raise ValueError(
251::COMM;;"Mix of nominal and non-nominal targets is not currently supported"
252::COMM;;)
253::COMM;;# reshape y back to 1-D array, if there is only 1 target column;
254::COMM;;# back to None if there are not target columns
255::COMM;;if y.shape[1] == 1:
256::COMM;;y = y.reshape((-1,))
257::COMM;;elif y.shape[1] == 0:
258::COMM;;y = None
259::COMM;;if output_arrays_type == "pandas":
260::COMM;;return X, y, frame, None
261::COMM;;return X, y, None, categories
262::COMM;;def _pandas_arff_parser(
263::COMM;;gzip_file,
264::COMM;;output_arrays_type,
265::COMM;;openml_columns_info,
266::COMM;;feature_names_to_select,
267::COMM;;target_names_to_select,
268::COMM;;read_csv_kwargs=None,
269::COMM;;):
306::COMM;;import pandas as pd
307::COMM;;# read the file until the data section to skip the ARFF metadata headers
308::COMM;;for line in gzip_file:
309::COMM;;if line.decode("utf-8").lower().startswith("@data"):
310::COMM;;break
311::COMM;;dtypes = {}
312::COMM;;for name in openml_columns_info:
313::COMM;;column_dtype = openml_columns_info[name]["data_type"]
314::COMM;;if column_dtype.lower() == "integer":
315::COMM;;# Use Int64 to infer missing values from data
316::COMM;;# XXX: this line is not covered by our tests. Is this really needed?
317::COMM;;dtypes[name] = "Int64"
318::COMM;;elif column_dtype.lower() == "nominal":
319::COMM;;dtypes[name] = "category"
320::COMM;;# since we will not pass `names` when reading the ARFF file, we need to translate
321::COMM;;# `dtypes` from column names to column indices to pass to `pandas.read_csv`
322::COMM;;dtypes_positional = {
323::COMM;;col_idx: dtypes[name]
324::COMM;;for col_idx, name in enumerate(openml_columns_info)
325::COMM;;if name in dtypes
326::COMM;;}
327::COMM;;default_read_csv_kwargs = {
328::COMM;;"header": None,
329::COMM;;"index_col": False, # always force pandas to not use the first column as index
330::COMM;;"na_values": ["?"], # missing values are represented by `?`
331::COMM;;"keep_default_na": False, # only `?` is a missing value given the ARFF specs
332::COMM;;"comment": "%", # skip line starting by `%` since they are comments
333::COMM;;"quotechar": '"', # delimiter to use for quoted strings
334::COMM;;"skipinitialspace": True, # skip spaces after delimiter to follow ARFF specs
335::COMM;;"escapechar": "\\",
336::COMM;;"dtype": dtypes_positional,
337::COMM;;}
338::COMM;;read_csv_kwargs = {**default_read_csv_kwargs, **(read_csv_kwargs or {})}
339::COMM;;frame = pd.read_csv(gzip_file, **read_csv_kwargs)
340::COMM;;try:
341::COMM;;# Setting the columns while reading the file will select the N first columns
342::COMM;;# and not raise a ParserError. Instead, we set the columns after reading the
343::COMM;;# file and raise a ParserError if the number of columns does not match the
344::COMM;;# number of columns in the metadata given by OpenML.
345::COMM;;frame.columns = [name for name in openml_columns_info]
346::COMM;;except ValueError as exc:
347::COMM;;raise pd.errors.ParserError(
348::COMM;;"The number of columns provided by OpenML does not match the number of "
349::COMM;;"columns inferred by pandas when reading the file."
350::COMM;;) from exc
351::COMM;;columns_to_select = feature_names_to_select + target_names_to_select
352::COMM;;columns_to_keep = [col for col in frame.columns if col in columns_to_select]
353::COMM;;frame = frame[columns_to_keep]
354::COMM;;# `pd.read_csv` automatically handles double quotes for quoting non-numeric
355::COMM;;# CSV cell values. Contrary to LIAC-ARFF, `pd.read_csv` cannot be configured to
356::COMM;;# consider either single quotes and double quotes as valid quoting chars at
357::COMM;;# the same time since this case does not occur in regular (non-ARFF) CSV files.
358::COMM;;# To mimic the behavior of LIAC-ARFF parser, we manually strip single quotes
359::COMM;;# on categories as a post-processing steps if needed.
360::COMM;;#
361::COMM;;# Note however that we intentionally do not attempt to do this kind of manual
362::COMM;;# post-processing of (non-categorical) string-typed columns because we cannot
363::COMM;;# resolve the ambiguity of the case of CSV cell with nesting quoting such as
364::COMM;;# `"'some string value'"` with pandas.
365::COMM;;single_quote_pattern = re.compile(r"^'(?P<contents>.*)'$")
366::COMM;;def strip_single_quotes(input_string):
367::COMM;;match = re.search(single_quote_pattern, input_string)
368::COMM;;if match is None:
369::COMM;;return input_string
370::COMM;;return match.group("contents")
371::COMM;;categorical_columns = [
372::COMM;;name
373::COMM;;for name, dtype in frame.dtypes.items()
374::COMM;;if isinstance(dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype)
375::COMM;;]
376::COMM;;for col in categorical_columns:
377::COMM;;frame[col] = frame[col].cat.rename_categories(strip_single_quotes)
378::COMM;;X, y = _post_process_frame(frame, feature_names_to_select, target_names_to_select)
379::COMM;;if output_arrays_type == "pandas":
380::COMM;;return X, y, frame, None
381::COMM;;else:
382::COMM;;X, y = X.to_numpy(), y.to_numpy()
383::COMM;;categories = {
384::COMM;;name: dtype.categories.tolist()
385::COMM;;for name, dtype in frame.dtypes.items()
386::COMM;;if isinstance(dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype)
387::COMM;;}
388::COMM;;return X, y, None, categories
389::COMM;;def load_arff_from_gzip_file(
390::COMM;;gzip_file,
391::COMM;;parser,
392::COMM;;output_type,
393::COMM;;openml_columns_info,
394::COMM;;feature_names_to_select,
395::COMM;;target_names_to_select,
396::COMM;;shape=None,
397::COMM;;read_csv_kwargs=None,
398::COMM;;):
436::COMM;;if parser == "liac-arff":
437::COMM;;return _liac_arff_parser(
438::COMM;;gzip_file,
439::COMM;;output_type,
440::COMM;;openml_columns_info,
441::COMM;;feature_names_to_select,
442::COMM;;target_names_to_select,
443::COMM;;shape,
444::COMM;;)
445::COMM;;elif parser == "pandas":
446::COMM;;return _pandas_arff_parser(
447::COMM;;gzip_file,
448::COMM;;output_type,
449::COMM;;openml_columns_info,
450::COMM;;feature_names_to_select,
451::COMM;;target_names_to_select,
452::COMM;;read_csv_kwargs,
453::COMM;;)
454::COMM;;else:
455::COMM;;raise ValueError(
456::COMM;;f"Unknown parser: '{parser}'. Should be 'liac-arff' or 'pandas'."
457::COMM;;)

42::COMM;;This folder is used by some large dataset loaders to avoid downloading the
43::COMM;;data several times.

45::COMM;;user home folder.

48::COMM;;symbol is expanded to the user home folder.

80::COMM;;Parameters

134::COMM;;Individual samples are assumed to be files stored a two levels folder
135::COMM;;structure such as the following:
136::COMM;;.. code-block:: text
137::COMM;;container_folder/
138::COMM;;category_1_folder/
139::COMM;;file_1.txt
140::COMM;;file_2.txt
141::COMM;;...
142::COMM;;file_42.txt
143::COMM;;category_2_folder/
144::COMM;;file_43.txt
145::COMM;;file_44.txt
146::COMM;;...
147::COMM;;The folder names are used as supervised signal label names. The individual
148::COMM;;file names are not important.
149::COMM;;This function does not try to extract features into a numpy array or scipy
150::COMM;;sparse matrix. In addition, if load_content is false it does not try to
151::COMM;;load the files in memory.
152::COMM;;To use text files in a scikit-learn classification or clustering algorithm,
153::COMM;;you will need to use the :mod:`~sklearn.feature_extraction.text` module to
154::COMM;;build a feature extraction transformer that suits your problem.
155::COMM;;If you set load_content=True, you should also specify the encoding of the
156::COMM;;text using the 'encoding' parameter. For many modern text files, 'utf-8'
157::COMM;;will be the correct encoding. If you leave encoding equal to None, then the
158::COMM;;content will be made of bytes instead of Unicode, and you will not be able
159::COMM;;to use most functions in :mod:`~sklearn.feature_extraction.text`.
160::COMM;;Similar feature extractors should be built for other kind of unstructured
161::COMM;;data input such as images, audio, video, ...
162::COMM;;If you want files with a specific file extension (e.g. `.txt`) then you
163::COMM;;can pass a list of those file extensions to `allowed_extensions`.
164::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <datasets>`.
165::COMM;;Parameters
166::COMM;;----------
167::COMM;;container_path : str
168::COMM;;Path to the main folder holding one subfolder per category.
169::COMM;;description : str, default=None
170::COMM;;A paragraph describing the characteristic of the dataset: its source,
171::COMM;;reference, etc.
172::COMM;;categories : list of str, default=None
173::COMM;;If None (default), load all the categories. If not None, list of
174::COMM;;category names to load (other categories ignored).
175::COMM;;load_content : bool, default=True
176::COMM;;Whether to load or not the content of the different files. If true a
177::COMM;;'data' attribute containing the text information is present in the data
178::COMM;;structure returned. If not, a filenames attribute gives the path to the
179::COMM;;files.
180::COMM;;shuffle : bool, default=True
181::COMM;;Whether or not to shuffle the data: might be important for models that
182::COMM;;make the assumption that the samples are independent and identically
183::COMM;;distributed (i.i.d.), such as stochastic gradient descent.
184::COMM;;encoding : str, default=None
185::COMM;;If None, do not try to decode the content of the files (e.g. for images
186::COMM;;or other non-text content). If not None, encoding to use to decode text
187::COMM;;files to Unicode if load_content is True.
188::COMM;;decode_error : {'strict', 'ignore', 'replace'}, default='strict'
189::COMM;;Instruction on what to do if a byte sequence is given to analyze that
190::COMM;;contains characters not of the given `encoding`. Passed as keyword
191::COMM;;argument 'errors' to bytes.decode.
192::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=0
193::COMM;;Determines random number generation for dataset shuffling. Pass an int
194::COMM;;for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
195::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
196::COMM;;allowed_extensions : list of str, default=None
197::COMM;;List of desired file extensions to filter the files to be loaded.
198::COMM;;Returns
199::COMM;;-------

1180::COMM;;def _fetch_remote(remote, dirname=None, n_retries=3, delay=1):
1207::COMM;;if dirname is None:
1208::COMM;;folder_path = Path(".")
1209::COMM;;else:
1210::COMM;;folder_path = Path(dirname)
1211::COMM;;file_path = folder_path / remote.filename
1212::COMM;;if file_path.exists():
1213::COMM;;if remote.checksum is None:
1214::COMM;;return file_path
1215::COMM;;checksum = _sha256(file_path)
1216::COMM;;if checksum == remote.checksum:
1217::COMM;;return file_path
1218::COMM;;else:
1219::COMM;;warnings.warn(
1220::COMM;;f"SHA256 checksum of existing local file {file_path.name} "
1221::COMM;;f"({checksum}) differs from expected ({remote.checksum}): "
1222::COMM;;f"re-downloading from {remote.url} ."
1223::COMM;;)
1224::COMM;;# We create a temporary file dedicated to this particular download to avoid
1225::COMM;;# conflicts with parallel downloads. If the download is successful, the
1226::COMM;;# temporary file is atomically renamed to the final file path (with
1227::COMM;;# `shutil.move`). We therefore pass `delete=False` to `NamedTemporaryFile`.
1228::COMM;;# Otherwise, garbage collecting temp_file would raise an error when
1229::COMM;;# attempting to delete a file that was already renamed. If the download
1230::COMM;;# fails or the result does not match the expected SHA256 digest, the
1231::COMM;;# temporary file is removed manually in the except block.
1232::COMM;;temp_file = NamedTemporaryFile(
1233::COMM;;prefix=remote.filename + ".part_", dir=folder_path, delete=False
1234::COMM;;)
1235::COMM;;# Note that Python 3.12's `delete_on_close=True` is ignored as we set
1236::COMM;;# `delete=False` explicitly. So after this line the empty temporary file still
1237::COMM;;# exists on disk to make sure that it's uniquely reserved for this specific call of
1238::COMM;;# `_fetch_remote` and therefore it protects against any corruption by parallel
1239::COMM;;# calls.
1240::COMM;;temp_file.close()
1241::COMM;;try:
1242::COMM;;temp_file_path = Path(temp_file.name)
1243::COMM;;while True:
1244::COMM;;try:
1245::COMM;;urlretrieve(remote.url, temp_file_path)
1246::COMM;;break
1247::COMM;;except (URLError, TimeoutError):
1248::COMM;;if n_retries == 0:
1249::COMM;;# If no more retries are left, re-raise the caught exception.
1250::COMM;;raise
1251::COMM;;warnings.warn(f"Retry downloading from url: {remote.url}")
1252::COMM;;n_retries -= 1
1253::COMM;;time.sleep(delay)
1254::COMM;;checksum = _sha256(temp_file_path)
1255::COMM;;if remote.checksum is not None and remote.checksum != checksum:
1256::COMM;;raise OSError(
1257::COMM;;f"The SHA256 checksum of {remote.filename} ({checksum}) "
1258::COMM;;f"differs from expected ({remote.checksum})."
1259::COMM;;)
1260::COMM;;except (Exception, KeyboardInterrupt):
1261::COMM;;os.unlink(temp_file.name)
1262::COMM;;raise
1263::COMM;;# The following renaming is atomic whenever temp_file_path and
1264::COMM;;# file_path are on the same filesystem. This should be the case most of
1265::COMM;;# the time, but we still use shutil.move instead of os.rename in case
1266::COMM;;# they are not.
1267::COMM;;shutil.move(temp_file_path, file_path)
1268::COMM;;return file_path
1269::COMM;;def _filter_filename(value, filter_dots=True):
1278::COMM;;value = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", value).lower()
1279::COMM;;if filter_dots:
1280::COMM;;value = re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]+", "_", value)
1281::COMM;;else:
1282::COMM;;value = re.sub(r"[^.\w\s-]+", "_", value)
1283::COMM;;value = re.sub(r"[\s-]+", "-", value)
1284::COMM;;return value.strip("-_.")
1285::COMM;;def _derive_folder_and_filename_from_url(url):
1286::COMM;;parsed_url = urlparse(url)
1287::COMM;;if not parsed_url.hostname:
1288::COMM;;raise ValueError(f"Invalid URL: {url}")
1289::COMM;;folder_components = [_filter_filename(parsed_url.hostname, filter_dots=False)]
1290::COMM;;path = parsed_url.path
1291::COMM;;if "/" in path:
1292::COMM;;base_folder, raw_filename = path.rsplit("/", 1)
1293::COMM;;base_folder = _filter_filename(base_folder)
1294::COMM;;if base_folder:
1295::COMM;;folder_components.append(base_folder)
1296::COMM;;else:
1297::COMM;;raw_filename = path
1298::COMM;;filename = _filter_filename(raw_filename, filter_dots=False)
1299::COMM;;if not filename:
1300::COMM;;filename = "downloaded_file"
1301::COMM;;return "/".join(folder_components), filename
1302::COMM;;def fetch_file(

1304::COMM;;):

1337::COMM;;remote_metadata = RemoteFileMetadata(
1338::COMM;;filename=local_filename, url=url, checksum=sha256
1339::COMM;;)
1340::COMM;;return _fetch_remote(
1341::COMM;;remote_metadata, dirname=folder, n_retries=n_retries, delay=delay

79::COMM;;If True, returns `(data, target)` instead of a `Bunch` object. See
80::COMM;;below for more information about the `data` and `target` object.
81::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
82::COMM;;n_retries : int, default=3
83::COMM;;Number of retries when HTTP errors are encountered.
84::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.5
85::COMM;;delay : float, default=1.0
86::COMM;;Number of seconds between retries.
87::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.5
88::COMM;;Returns
89::COMM;;-------
90::COMM;;data : :class:`~sklearn.utils.Bunch`
91::COMM;;Dictionary-like object, with the following attributes.
92::COMM;;data: ndarray, shape (400, 4096)
93::COMM;;Each row corresponds to a ravelled
94::COMM;;face image of original size 64 x 64 pixels.
95::COMM;;images : ndarray, shape (400, 64, 64)
96::COMM;;Each row is a face image
97::COMM;;corresponding to one of the 40 subjects of the dataset.
98::COMM;;target : ndarray, shape (400,)
99::COMM;;Labels associated to each face image.
100::COMM;;Those labels are ranging from 0-39 and correspond to the
101::COMM;;Subject IDs.
102::COMM;;DESCR : str
103::COMM;;Description of the modified Olivetti Faces Dataset.
104::COMM;;(data, target) : tuple if `return_X_y=True`
105::COMM;;Tuple with the `data` and `target` objects described above.
106::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
107::COMM;;Examples
108::COMM;;--------
109::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import fetch_olivetti_faces
110::COMM;;>>> olivetti_faces = fetch_olivetti_faces()

112::COMM;;(400, 4096)
113::COMM;;>>> olivetti_faces.target.shape
114::COMM;;(400,)
115::COMM;;>>> olivetti_faces.images.shape
116::COMM;;(400, 64, 64)
128::COMO;;# delete raw .mat data
135::COMO;;# We want floating point data, but float32 is enough (there is only
136::COMO;;# one byte of precision in the original uint8s anyway)
141::COMO;;# 10 images per class, 400 images total, each class is contiguous.
1::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
2::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
45::COMM;;file is removed, and the function is called again. If ``data_home`` is
46::COMM;;``None``, then the function is called once. We can provide a specific
47::COMM;;exception to not retry on using `no_retry_exception` parameter.
74::COMM;;up to ``n_retries`` times with a ``delay`` between each call. If the error
75::COMM;;has a 412 status code, don't call the function again as this is a specific
76::COMM;;OpenML error.
77::COMM;;The url parameter is used to give more information to the user about the
78::COMM;;error.
88::COMO;;# 412 is a specific OpenML error code.
96::COMO;;# Avoid a ResourceWarning on Python 3.14 and later.
107::COMM;;Returns a resource from OpenML.org. Caches it to data_home if required.
108::COMM;;Parameters
109::COMM;;----------

113::COMM;;cache folder.

145::COMO;;# concurrence safety of the dataset caching mechanism.

190::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
191::COMM;;# Count features, clusters and samples
192::COMM;;if n_informative + n_redundant + n_repeated > n_features:
193::COMM;;raise ValueError(
194::COMM;;"Number of informative, redundant and repeated "
195::COMM;;"features must sum to less than the number of total"
196::COMM;;" features"
197::COMM;;)
198::COMM;;# Use log2 to avoid overflow errors
199::COMM;;if n_informative < np.log2(n_classes * n_clusters_per_class):
200::COMM;;msg = "n_classes({}) * n_clusters_per_class({}) must be"
201::COMM;;msg += " smaller or equal 2**n_informative({})={}"
202::COMM;;raise ValueError(
203::COMM;;msg.format(n_classes, n_clusters_per_class, n_informative, 2**n_informative)
204::COMM;;)
205::COMM;;if weights is not None:
206::COMM;;# we define new variable, weight_, instead of modifying user defined parameter.
207::COMM;;if len(weights) not in [n_classes, n_classes - 1]:
208::COMM;;raise ValueError(
209::COMM;;"Weights specified but incompatible with number of classes."
210::COMM;;)
211::COMM;;if len(weights) == n_classes - 1:
212::COMM;;if isinstance(weights, list):
213::COMM;;weights_ = weights + [1.0 - sum(weights)]
214::COMM;;else:
215::COMM;;weights_ = np.resize(weights, n_classes)
216::COMM;;weights_[-1] = 1.0 - sum(weights_[:-1])
217::COMM;;else:
218::COMM;;weights_ = weights.copy()
219::COMM;;else:
220::COMM;;weights_ = [1.0 / n_classes] * n_classes
221::COMM;;n_random = n_features - n_informative - n_redundant - n_repeated
222::COMM;;n_clusters = n_classes * n_clusters_per_class
223::COMM;;# Distribute samples among clusters by weight
224::COMM;;n_samples_per_cluster = [
225::COMM;;int(n_samples * weights_[k % n_classes] / n_clusters_per_class)
226::COMM;;for k in range(n_clusters)
227::COMM;;]
228::COMM;;for i in range(n_samples - sum(n_samples_per_cluster)):
229::COMM;;n_samples_per_cluster[i % n_clusters] += 1
230::COMM;;# Initialize X and y
231::COMM;;X = np.zeros((n_samples, n_features))
232::COMM;;y = np.zeros(n_samples, dtype=int)
233::COMM;;# Build the polytope whose vertices become cluster centroids
234::COMM;;centroids = _generate_hypercube(n_clusters, n_informative, generator).astype(
235::COMM;;float, copy=False
236::COMM;;)
237::COMM;;centroids *= 2 * class_sep
238::COMM;;centroids -= class_sep
239::COMM;;if not hypercube:
240::COMM;;centroids *= generator.uniform(size=(n_clusters, 1))
241::COMM;;centroids *= generator.uniform(size=(1, n_informative))
242::COMM;;# Initially draw informative features from the standard normal
243::COMM;;X[:, :n_informative] = generator.standard_normal(size=(n_samples, n_informative))
244::COMM;;# Create each cluster; a variant of make_blobs
245::COMM;;stop = 0
246::COMM;;for k, centroid in enumerate(centroids):
247::COMM;;start, stop = stop, stop + n_samples_per_cluster[k]
248::COMM;;y[start:stop] = k % n_classes # assign labels
249::COMM;;X_k = X[start:stop, :n_informative] # slice a view of the cluster
250::COMM;;A = 2 * generator.uniform(size=(n_informative, n_informative)) - 1
251::COMM;;X_k[...] = np.dot(X_k, A) # introduce random covariance
252::COMM;;X_k += centroid # shift the cluster to a vertex

256::COMM;;X[:, n_informative : n_informative + n_redundant] = np.dot(
257::COMM;;X[:, :n_informative], B

259::COMM;;# Repeat some features

261::COMM;;if n_repeated > 0:

263::COMM;;X[:, n : n + n_repeated] = X[:, indices]
264::COMM;;# Fill useless features
265::COMM;;if n_random > 0:
266::COMM;;X[:, -n_random:] = generator.standard_normal(size=(n_samples, n_random))
267::COMM;;# Randomly replace labels

270::COMM;;y[flip_mask] = generator.randint(n_classes, size=flip_mask.sum())
271::COMM;;# Randomly shift and scale

274::COMM;;X += shift
275::COMM;;if scale is None:
276::COMM;;scale = 1 + 100 * generator.uniform(size=n_features)
277::COMM;;X *= scale

281::COMM;;X, y = util_shuffle(X, y, random_state=generator)
282::COMM;;# Randomly permute features
283::COMM;;generator.shuffle(indices)
284::COMM;;X[:, :] = X[:, indices]

292::COMM;;elif n_informative <= index < n_informative + n_redundant:

337::COMM;;def make_multilabel_classification(
338::COMM;;n_samples=100,
339::COMM;;n_features=20,
340::COMM;;*,
341::COMM;;n_classes=5,
342::COMM;;n_labels=2,
343::COMM;;length=50,
344::COMM;;allow_unlabeled=True,
345::COMM;;sparse=False,
346::COMM;;return_indicator="dense",
347::COMM;;return_distributions=False,
348::COMM;;random_state=None,
349::COMM;;):
420::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
421::COMM;;p_c = generator.uniform(size=n_classes)
422::COMM;;p_c /= p_c.sum()
423::COMM;;cumulative_p_c = np.cumsum(p_c)
424::COMM;;p_w_c = generator.uniform(size=(n_features, n_classes))
425::COMM;;p_w_c /= np.sum(p_w_c, axis=0)
426::COMM;;def sample_example():
427::COMM;;_, n_classes = p_w_c.shape
428::COMM;;# pick a nonzero number of labels per document by rejection sampling
429::COMM;;y_size = n_classes + 1
430::COMM;;while (not allow_unlabeled and y_size == 0) or y_size > n_classes:
431::COMM;;y_size = generator.poisson(n_labels)
432::COMM;;# pick n classes
433::COMM;;y = set()
434::COMM;;while len(y) != y_size:
435::COMM;;# pick a class with probability P(c)
436::COMM;;c = np.searchsorted(cumulative_p_c, generator.uniform(size=y_size - len(y)))
437::COMM;;y.update(c)
438::COMM;;y = list(y)
439::COMM;;# pick a non-zero document length by rejection sampling
440::COMM;;n_words = 0
441::COMM;;while n_words == 0:
442::COMM;;n_words = generator.poisson(length)
443::COMM;;# generate a document of length n_words
444::COMM;;if len(y) == 0:
445::COMM;;# if sample does not belong to any class, generate noise word
446::COMM;;words = generator.randint(n_features, size=n_words)
447::COMM;;return words, y
448::COMM;;# sample words with replacement from selected classes
449::COMM;;cumulative_p_w_sample = p_w_c.take(y, axis=1).sum(axis=1).cumsum()
450::COMM;;cumulative_p_w_sample /= cumulative_p_w_sample[-1]
451::COMM;;words = np.searchsorted(cumulative_p_w_sample, generator.uniform(size=n_words))
452::COMM;;return words, y
453::COMM;;X_indices = array.array("i")
454::COMM;;X_indptr = array.array("i", [0])
455::COMM;;Y = []
456::COMM;;for i in range(n_samples):
457::COMM;;words, y = sample_example()
458::COMM;;X_indices.extend(words)
459::COMM;;X_indptr.append(len(X_indices))
460::COMM;;Y.append(y)
461::COMM;;X_data = np.ones(len(X_indices), dtype=np.float64)
462::COMM;;X = sp.csr_matrix((X_data, X_indices, X_indptr), shape=(n_samples, n_features))
463::COMM;;X.sum_duplicates()
464::COMM;;if not sparse:
465::COMM;;X = X.toarray()
466::COMM;;# return_indicator can be True due to backward compatibility
467::COMM;;if return_indicator in (True, "sparse", "dense"):
468::COMM;;lb = MultiLabelBinarizer(sparse_output=(return_indicator == "sparse"))
469::COMM;;Y = lb.fit([range(n_classes)]).transform(Y)
470::COMM;;if return_distributions:
471::COMM;;return X, Y, p_c, p_w_c
472::COMM;;return X, Y

480::COMM;;def make_hastie_10_2(n_samples=12000, *, random_state=None):

520::COMM;;shape = (n_samples, 10)

523::COMM;;y[y == 0.0] = -1.0
524::COMM;;return X, y

541::COMM;;def make_regression(

544::COMM;;*,

628::COMM;;else:
629::COMM;;# Randomly generate a low rank, fat tail input set
630::COMM;;X = make_low_rank_matrix(
631::COMM;;n_samples=n_samples,
632::COMM;;n_features=n_features,
633::COMM;;effective_rank=effective_rank,
634::COMM;;tail_strength=tail_strength,
635::COMM;;random_state=generator,
636::COMM;;)
637::COMM;;# Generate a ground truth model with only n_informative features being non
638::COMM;;# zeros (the other features are not correlated to y and should be ignored
639::COMM;;# by a sparsifying regularizers such as L1 or elastic net)
640::COMM;;ground_truth = np.zeros((n_features, n_targets))
641::COMM;;ground_truth[:n_informative, :] = 100 * generator.uniform(
642::COMM;;size=(n_informative, n_targets)
643::COMM;;)
644::COMM;;y = np.dot(X, ground_truth) + bias
645::COMM;;# Add noise
646::COMM;;if noise > 0.0:
647::COMM;;y += generator.normal(scale=noise, size=y.shape)
648::COMM;;# Randomly permute samples and features
649::COMM;;if shuffle:
650::COMM;;X, y = util_shuffle(X, y, random_state=generator)
651::COMM;;indices = np.arange(n_features)
652::COMM;;generator.shuffle(indices)
653::COMM;;X[:, :] = X[:, indices]
654::COMM;;ground_truth = ground_truth[indices]
655::COMM;;y = np.squeeze(y)
656::COMM;;if coef:
657::COMM;;return X, y, np.squeeze(ground_truth)
658::COMM;;else:
659::COMM;;return X, y
660::COMM;;@validate_params(
661::COMM;;{
662::COMM;;"n_samples": [Interval(Integral, 0, None, closed="left"), tuple],
663::COMM;;"shuffle": ["boolean"],
664::COMM;;"noise": [Interval(Real, 0, None, closed="left"), None],
665::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
666::COMM;;"factor": [Interval(Real, 0, 1, closed="left")],
667::COMM;;},
668::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
669::COMM;;)
670::COMM;;def make_circles(
671::COMM;;n_samples=100, *, shuffle=True, noise=None, random_state=None, factor=0.8
672::COMM;;):
714::COMM;;if isinstance(n_samples, numbers.Integral):
715::COMM;;n_samples_out = n_samples // 2
716::COMM;;n_samples_in = n_samples - n_samples_out
717::COMM;;else: # n_samples is a tuple
718::COMM;;if len(n_samples) != 2:
719::COMM;;raise ValueError("When a tuple, n_samples must have exactly two elements.")
720::COMM;;n_samples_out, n_samples_in = n_samples
721::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
722::COMM;;# so as not to have the first point = last point, we set endpoint=False
723::COMM;;linspace_out = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n_samples_out, endpoint=False)
724::COMM;;linspace_in = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n_samples_in, endpoint=False)
725::COMM;;outer_circ_x = np.cos(linspace_out)
726::COMM;;outer_circ_y = np.sin(linspace_out)
727::COMM;;inner_circ_x = np.cos(linspace_in) * factor
728::COMM;;inner_circ_y = np.sin(linspace_in) * factor
729::COMM;;X = np.vstack(
730::COMM;;[np.append(outer_circ_x, inner_circ_x), np.append(outer_circ_y, inner_circ_y)]
731::COMM;;).T
732::COMM;;y = np.hstack(
733::COMM;;[np.zeros(n_samples_out, dtype=np.intp), np.ones(n_samples_in, dtype=np.intp)]
734::COMM;;)
735::COMM;;if shuffle:
736::COMM;;X, y = util_shuffle(X, y, random_state=generator)
737::COMM;;if noise is not None:
738::COMM;;X += generator.normal(scale=noise, size=X.shape)
739::COMM;;return X, y

745::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
746::COMM;;},

748::COMM;;)
749::COMM;;def make_moons(n_samples=100, *, shuffle=True, noise=None, random_state=None):
783::COMM;;if isinstance(n_samples, numbers.Integral):
784::COMM;;n_samples_out = n_samples // 2
785::COMM;;n_samples_in = n_samples - n_samples_out

1078::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)

1080::COMM;;X[:, 0] *= 100
1081::COMM;;X[:, 1] *= 520 * np.pi

1097::COMM;;def make_friedman3(n_samples=100, *, noise=0.0, random_state=None):
1143::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
1144::COMM;;X = generator.uniform(size=(n_samples, 4))
1145::COMM;;X[:, 0] *= 100
1146::COMM;;X[:, 1] *= 520 * np.pi
1147::COMM;;X[:, 1] += 40 * np.pi
1148::COMM;;X[:, 3] *= 10
1149::COMM;;X[:, 3] += 1

1152::COMM;;) + noise * generator.standard_normal(size=(n_samples))

1154::COMM;;@validate_params(
1155::COMM;;{
1156::COMM;;"n_samples": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1157::COMM;;"n_features": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1158::COMM;;"effective_rank": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1159::COMM;;"tail_strength": [Interval(Real, 0, 1, closed="both")],
1160::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
1161::COMM;;},
1162::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
1163::COMM;;)
1164::COMM;;def make_low_rank_matrix(
1165::COMM;;n_samples=100,
1166::COMM;;n_features=100,
1167::COMM;;*,
1168::COMM;;effective_rank=10,
1169::COMM;;tail_strength=0.5,
1170::COMM;;random_state=None,
1171::COMM;;):
1220::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
1221::COMM;;n = min(n_samples, n_features)
1222::COMM;;# Random (ortho normal) vectors
1223::COMM;;u, _ = linalg.qr(
1224::COMM;;generator.standard_normal(size=(n_samples, n)),
1225::COMM;;mode="economic",
1226::COMM;;check_finite=False,
1227::COMM;;)
1228::COMM;;v, _ = linalg.qr(
1229::COMM;;generator.standard_normal(size=(n_features, n)),
1230::COMM;;mode="economic",
1231::COMM;;check_finite=False,
1232::COMM;;)
1233::COMM;;# Index of the singular values
1234::COMM;;singular_ind = np.arange(n, dtype=np.float64)
1235::COMM;;# Build the singular profile by assembling signal and noise components
1236::COMM;;low_rank = (1 - tail_strength) * np.exp(-1.0 * (singular_ind / effective_rank) ** 2)
1237::COMM;;tail = tail_strength * np.exp(-0.1 * singular_ind / effective_rank)
1238::COMM;;s = np.identity(n) * (low_rank + tail)
1239::COMM;;return np.dot(np.dot(u, s), v.T)
1240::COMM;;@validate_params(
1241::COMM;;{
1242::COMM;;"n_samples": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1243::COMM;;"n_components": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1244::COMM;;"n_features": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1245::COMM;;"n_nonzero_coefs": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1246::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
1247::COMM;;},
1248::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
1249::COMM;;)
1250::COMM;;def make_sparse_coded_signal(
1251::COMM;;n_samples,
1252::COMM;;*,
1253::COMM;;n_components,
1254::COMM;;n_features,
1255::COMM;;n_nonzero_coefs,
1256::COMM;;random_state=None,
1257::COMM;;):
1303::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
1304::COMM;;# generate dictionary
1305::COMM;;D = generator.standard_normal(size=(n_features, n_components))
1306::COMM;;D /= np.sqrt(np.sum((D**2), axis=0))
1307::COMM;;# generate code
1308::COMM;;X = np.zeros((n_components, n_samples))
1309::COMM;;for i in range(n_samples):
1310::COMM;;idx = np.arange(n_components)
1311::COMM;;generator.shuffle(idx)
1312::COMM;;idx = idx[:n_nonzero_coefs]
1313::COMM;;X[idx, i] = generator.standard_normal(size=n_nonzero_coefs)
1314::COMM;;# encode signal
1315::COMM;;Y = np.dot(D, X)
1316::COMM;;# Transpose to have shapes consistent with the rest of the API
1317::COMM;;Y, D, X = Y.T, D.T, X.T
1318::COMM;;return map(np.squeeze, (Y, D, X))
1319::COMM;;@validate_params(
1320::COMM;;{
1321::COMM;;"n_samples": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1322::COMM;;"n_features": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1323::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
1324::COMM;;},
1325::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
1326::COMM;;)
1327::COMM;;def make_sparse_uncorrelated(n_samples=100, n_features=10, *, random_state=None):
1365::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
1366::COMM;;X = generator.normal(loc=0, scale=1, size=(n_samples, n_features))
1367::COMM;;y = generator.normal(
1368::COMM;;loc=(X[:, 0] + 2 * X[:, 1] - 2 * X[:, 2] - 1.5 * X[:, 3]),
1369::COMM;;scale=np.ones(n_samples),
1370::COMM;;)
1371::COMM;;return X, y
1372::COMM;;@validate_params(
1373::COMM;;{
1374::COMM;;"n_dim": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1375::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
1376::COMM;;},
1377::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
1378::COMM;;)
1379::COMM;;def make_spd_matrix(n_dim, *, random_state=None):
1404::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
1405::COMM;;A = generator.uniform(size=(n_dim, n_dim))
1406::COMM;;U, _, Vt = linalg.svd(np.dot(A.T, A), check_finite=False)
1407::COMM;;X = np.dot(np.dot(U, 1.0 + np.diag(generator.uniform(size=n_dim))), Vt)
1408::COMM;;return X
1409::COMM;;@validate_params(
1410::COMM;;{
1411::COMM;;"n_dim": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1412::COMM;;"alpha": [Interval(Real, 0, 1, closed="both")],
1413::COMM;;"norm_diag": ["boolean"],
1414::COMM;;"smallest_coef": [Interval(Real, 0, 1, closed="both")],
1415::COMM;;"largest_coef": [Interval(Real, 0, 1, closed="both")],
1416::COMM;;"sparse_format": [
1417::COMM;;StrOptions({"bsr", "coo", "csc", "csr", "dia", "dok", "lil"}),
1418::COMM;;None,
1419::COMM;;],
1420::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
1421::COMM;;},
1422::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
1423::COMM;;)
1424::COMM;;def make_sparse_spd_matrix(
1425::COMM;;n_dim=1,
1426::COMM;;*,
1427::COMM;;alpha=0.95,
1428::COMM;;norm_diag=False,
1429::COMM;;smallest_coef=0.1,
1430::COMM;;largest_coef=0.9,
1431::COMM;;sparse_format=None,
1432::COMM;;random_state=None,
1433::COMM;;):
1482::COMM;;random_state = check_random_state(random_state)
1483::COMM;;chol = -sp.eye(n_dim)
1484::COMM;;aux = sp.random(
1485::COMM;;m=n_dim,
1486::COMM;;n=n_dim,
1487::COMM;;density=1 - alpha,
1488::COMM;;data_rvs=lambda x: random_state.uniform(
1489::COMM;;low=smallest_coef, high=largest_coef, size=x
1490::COMM;;),
1491::COMM;;random_state=random_state,
1492::COMM;;)
1493::COMM;;# We need to avoid "coo" format because it does not support slicing
1494::COMM;;aux = sp.tril(aux, k=-1, format="csc")
1495::COMM;;# Permute the lines: we don't want to have asymmetries in the final
1496::COMM;;# SPD matrix
1497::COMM;;permutation = random_state.permutation(n_dim)
1498::COMM;;aux = aux[permutation].T[permutation]
1499::COMM;;chol += aux
1500::COMM;;prec = chol.T @ chol
1501::COMM;;if norm_diag:
1502::COMM;;# Form the diagonal vector into a row matrix
1503::COMM;;d = sp.diags(1.0 / np.sqrt(prec.diagonal()))
1504::COMM;;prec = d @ prec @ d
1505::COMM;;if sparse_format is None:
1506::COMM;;return prec.toarray()
1507::COMM;;else:
1508::COMM;;return prec.asformat(sparse_format)
1509::COMM;;@validate_params(
1510::COMM;;{
1511::COMM;;"n_samples": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1512::COMM;;"noise": [Interval(Real, 0, None, closed="left")],
1513::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
1514::COMM;;"hole": ["boolean"],
1515::COMM;;},
1516::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
1517::COMM;;)
1518::COMM;;def make_swiss_roll(n_samples=100, *, noise=0.0, random_state=None, hole=False):
1558::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
1559::COMM;;if not hole:
1560::COMM;;t = 1.5 * np.pi * (1 + 2 * generator.uniform(size=n_samples))
1561::COMM;;y = 21 * generator.uniform(size=n_samples)
1562::COMM;;else:
1563::COMM;;corners = np.array(
1564::COMM;;[[np.pi * (1.5 + i), j * 7] for i in range(3) for j in range(3)]
1565::COMM;;)
1566::COMM;;corners = np.delete(corners, 4, axis=0)
1567::COMM;;corner_index = generator.choice(8, n_samples)
1568::COMM;;parameters = generator.uniform(size=(2, n_samples)) * np.array([[np.pi], [7]])
1569::COMM;;t, y = corners[corner_index].T + parameters
1570::COMM;;x = t * np.cos(t)
1571::COMM;;z = t * np.sin(t)
1572::COMM;;X = np.vstack((x, y, z))
1573::COMM;;X += noise * generator.standard_normal(size=(3, n_samples))
1574::COMM;;X = X.T
1575::COMM;;t = np.squeeze(t)
1576::COMM;;return X, t
1577::COMM;;@validate_params(
1578::COMM;;{
1579::COMM;;"n_samples": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],
1580::COMM;;"noise": [Interval(Real, 0, None, closed="left")],
1581::COMM;;"random_state": ["random_state"],
1582::COMM;;},
1583::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
1584::COMM;;)
1585::COMM;;def make_s_curve(n_samples=100, *, noise=0.0, random_state=None):
1614::COMM;;generator = check_random_state(random_state)
1615::COMM;;t = 3 * np.pi * (generator.uniform(size=(1, n_samples)) - 0.5)
1616::COMM;;X = np.empty(shape=(n_samples, 3), dtype=np.float64)
1617::COMM;;X[:, 0] = np.sin(t)

1619::COMM;;X[:, 2] = np.sign(t) * (np.cos(t) - 1)
1620::COMM;;X += noise * generator.standard_normal(size=(3, n_samples)).T
1621::COMM;;t = np.squeeze(t)
1622::COMM;;return X, t
1623::COMM;;@validate_params(
1624::COMM;;{
1625::COMM;;"mean": ["array-like", None],
1626::COMM;;"cov": [Interval(Real, 0, None, closed="left")],
1627::COMM;;"n_samples": [Interval(Integral, 1, None, closed="left")],

58::COMM;;This format is a text-based format, with one sample per line. It does
59::COMM;;not store zero valued features hence is suitable for sparse dataset.
60::COMM;;The first element of each line can be used to store a target variable
61::COMM;;to predict.
62::COMM;;This format is used as the default format for both svmlight and the
63::COMM;;libsvm command line programs.
64::COMM;;Parsing a text based source can be expensive. When repeatedly
65::COMM;;working on the same dataset, it is recommended to wrap this
66::COMM;;loader with joblib.Memory.cache to store a memmapped backup of the
67::COMM;;CSR results of the first call and benefit from the near instantaneous
68::COMM;;loading of memmapped structures for the subsequent calls.
69::COMM;;In case the file contains a pairwise preference constraint (known
70::COMM;;as "qid" in the svmlight format) these are ignored unless the
71::COMM;;query_id parameter is set to True. These pairwise preference
72::COMM;;constraints can be used to constraint the combination of samples
73::COMM;;when using pairwise loss functions (as is the case in some
74::COMM;;learning to rank problems) so that only pairs with the same
75::COMM;;query_id value are considered.
76::COMM;;This implementation is written in Cython and is reasonably fast.
77::COMM;;However, a faster API-compatible loader is also available at:
78::COMM;;https://github.com/mblondel/svmlight-loader
79::COMM;;Parameters
80::COMM;;----------
81::COMM;;f : str, path-like, file-like or int
82::COMM;;(Path to) a file to load. If a path ends in ".gz" or ".bz2", it will
83::COMM;;be uncompressed on the fly. If an integer is passed, it is assumed to
84::COMM;;be a file descriptor. A file-like or file descriptor will not be closed
85::COMM;;by this function. A file-like object must be opened in binary mode.
86::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.2
87::COMM;;Path-like objects are now accepted.
88::COMM;;n_features : int, default=None
89::COMM;;The number of features to use. If None, it will be inferred. This
90::COMM;;argument is useful to load several files that are subsets of a
91::COMM;;bigger sliced dataset: each subset might not have examples of
92::COMM;;every feature, hence the inferred shape might vary from one
93::COMM;;slice to another.
94::COMM;;n_features is only required if ``offset`` or ``length`` are passed a
95::COMM;;non-default value.
96::COMM;;dtype : numpy data type, default=np.float64
97::COMM;;Data type of dataset to be loaded. This will be the data type of the
98::COMM;;output numpy arrays ``X`` and ``y``.
99::COMM;;multilabel : bool, default=False
100::COMM;;Samples may have several labels each (see
101::COMM;;https://www.csie.ntu.edu.tw/~cjlin/libsvmtools/datasets/multilabel.html).
102::COMM;;zero_based : bool or "auto", default="auto"
103::COMM;;Whether column indices in f are zero-based (True) or one-based
104::COMM;;(False). If column indices are one-based, they are transformed to
105::COMM;;zero-based to match Python/NumPy conventions.
106::COMM;;If set to "auto", a heuristic check is applied to determine this from
107::COMM;;the file contents. Both kinds of files occur "in the wild", but they
108::COMM;;are unfortunately not self-identifying. Using "auto" or True should
109::COMM;;always be safe when no ``offset`` or ``length`` is passed.
110::COMM;;If ``offset`` or ``length`` are passed, the "auto" mode falls back
111::COMM;;to ``zero_based=True`` to avoid having the heuristic check yield
112::COMM;;inconsistent results on different segments of the file.
113::COMM;;query_id : bool, default=False
114::COMM;;If True, will return the query_id array for each file.
115::COMM;;offset : int, default=0
116::COMM;;Ignore the offset first bytes by seeking forward, then
117::COMM;;discarding the following bytes up until the next new line
118::COMM;;character.
119::COMM;;length : int, default=-1
120::COMM;;If strictly positive, stop reading any new line of data once the
121::COMM;;position in the file has reached the (offset + length) bytes threshold.
122::COMM;;Returns

405::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
406::COMM;;Training vectors, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
407::COMM;;`n_features` is the number of features.
408::COMM;;y : {array-like, sparse matrix}, shape = (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_labels)
409::COMM;;Target values. Class labels must be an
410::COMM;;integer or float, or array-like objects of integer or float for
411::COMM;;multilabel classifications.
412::COMM;;f : str or file-like in binary mode
413::COMM;;If string, specifies the path that will contain the data.
414::COMM;;If file-like, data will be written to f. f should be opened in binary
415::COMM;;mode.
416::COMM;;zero_based : bool, default=True
417::COMM;;Whether column indices should be written zero-based (True) or one-based
418::COMM;;(False).
419::COMM;;comment : str or bytes, default=None
420::COMM;;Comment to insert at the top of the file. This should be either a
421::COMM;;Unicode string, which will be encoded as UTF-8, or an ASCII byte
422::COMM;;string.
423::COMM;;If a comment is given, then it will be preceded by one that identifies
424::COMM;;the file as having been dumped by scikit-learn. Note that not all
425::COMM;;tools grok comments in SVMlight files.
426::COMM;;query_id : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
427::COMM;;Array containing pairwise preference constraints (qid in svmlight
428::COMM;;format).
429::COMM;;multilabel : bool, default=False
430::COMM;;Samples may have several labels each (see
431::COMM;;https://www.csie.ntu.edu.tw/~cjlin/libsvmtools/datasets/multilabel.html).
432::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
433::COMM;;parameter `multilabel` to support multilabel datasets.
434::COMM;;Examples
435::COMM;;--------
436::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import dump_svmlight_file, make_classification
437::COMM;;>>> X, y = make_classification(random_state=0)
438::COMM;;>>> output_file = "my_dataset.svmlight"
439::COMM;;>>> dump_svmlight_file(X, y, output_file) # doctest: +SKIP
442::COMO;;# Convert comment string to list of lines in UTF-8.

444::COMO;;# if a user wants to get fancy, they'll have to decode themselves.
446::COMC;;comment.decode("ascii") # just for the exception

467::COMO;;# so sort them here, but first make sure we don't modify the user's X.

2::COMM;;The description of the dataset is available on the official website at:

4::COMM;;Quoting the introduction:
5::COMM;;The 20 Newsgroups data set is a collection of approximately 20,000
6::COMM;;newsgroup documents, partitioned (nearly) evenly across 20 different
7::COMM;;newsgroups. To the best of my knowledge, it was originally collected
8::COMM;;by Ken Lang, probably for his Newsweeder: Learning to filter netnews
9::COMM;;paper, though he does not explicitly mention this collection. The 20
10::COMM;;newsgroups collection has become a popular data set for experiments
11::COMM;;in text applications of machine learning techniques, such as text
12::COMM;;classification and text clustering.
13::COMM;;This dataset loader will download the recommended "by date" variant of the
14::COMM;;dataset and which features a point in time split between the train and
15::COMM;;test sets. The compressed dataset size is around 14 Mb compressed. Once
16::COMM;;uncompressed the train set is 52 MB and the test set is 34 MB.

106::COMM;;def strip_newsgroup_footer(text):

487::COMM;;code, S, dictionary = linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
488::COMM;;# flip the initial code's sign to enforce deterministic output
489::COMM;;code, dictionary = svd_flip(code, dictionary)
490::COMM;;dictionary = S[:, np.newaxis] * dictionary
491::COMM;;r = len(dictionary)
492::COMM;;if n_components <= r: # True even if n_components=None
493::COMM;;code = code[:, :n_components]
494::COMM;;dictionary = dictionary[:n_components, :]
495::COMM;;else:
496::COMM;;code = np.c_[code, np.zeros((len(code), n_components - r))]
497::COMM;;dictionary = np.r_[
498::COMM;;dictionary, np.zeros((n_components - r, dictionary.shape[1]))
499::COMM;;]
500::COMM;;# Fortran-order dict better suited for the sparse coding which is the
501::COMM;;# bottleneck of this algorithm.
502::COMM;;dictionary = np.asfortranarray(dictionary)
503::COMM;;errors = []

507::COMM;;# If max_iter is 0, number of iterations returned should be zero
508::COMM;;ii = -1
509::COMM;;for ii in range(max_iter):
510::COMM;;dt = time.time() - t0
511::COMM;;if verbose == 1:
512::COMM;;sys.stdout.write(".")
513::COMM;;sys.stdout.flush()
514::COMM;;elif verbose:

517::COMM;;% (ii, dt, dt / 60, current_cost)
518::COMM;;)
519::COMM;;# Update code

522::COMM;;dictionary,
523::COMM;;algorithm=method,
524::COMM;;alpha=alpha,
525::COMM;;init=code,

527::COMM;;positive=positive_code,
528::COMM;;max_iter=method_max_iter,
529::COMM;;verbose=verbose,
530::COMM;;)
531::COMM;;# Update dictionary in place

538::COMM;;positive=positive_dict,
539::COMM;;)
540::COMM;;# Cost function
541::COMM;;current_cost = 0.5 * np.sum((X - code @ dictionary) ** 2) + alpha * np.sum(
542::COMM;;np.abs(code)
543::COMM;;)
544::COMM;;errors.append(current_cost)
545::COMM;;if ii > 0:

547::COMM;;# assert(dE >= -tol * errors[-1])
548::COMM;;if dE < tol * errors[-1]:

978::COMM;;Transformed data.
984::COMM;;Finds a sparse representation of data against a fixed, precomputed
985::COMM;;dictionary.
986::COMM;;Each row of the result is the solution to a sparse coding problem.
987::COMM;;The goal is to find a sparse array `code` such that::
988::COMM;;X ~= code * dictionary
989::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <SparseCoder>`.
990::COMM;;Parameters
991::COMM;;----------
992::COMM;;dictionary : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features)
993::COMM;;The dictionary atoms used for sparse coding. Lines are assumed to be
994::COMM;;normalized to unit norm.
995::COMM;;transform_algorithm : {'lasso_lars', 'lasso_cd', 'lars', 'omp', \
996::COMM;;'threshold'}, default='omp'
997::COMM;;Algorithm used to transform the data:
998::COMM;;- `'lars'`: uses the least angle regression method
999::COMM;;(`linear_model.lars_path`);
1000::COMM;;- `'lasso_lars'`: uses Lars to compute the Lasso solution;
1001::COMM;;- `'lasso_cd'`: uses the coordinate descent method to compute the
1002::COMM;;Lasso solution (linear_model.Lasso). `'lasso_lars'` will be faster if
1003::COMM;;the estimated components are sparse;
1004::COMM;;- `'omp'`: uses orthogonal matching pursuit to estimate the sparse
1005::COMM;;solution;
1006::COMM;;- `'threshold'`: squashes to zero all coefficients less than alpha from
1007::COMM;;the projection ``dictionary * X'``.
1008::COMM;;transform_n_nonzero_coefs : int, default=None
1009::COMM;;Number of nonzero coefficients to target in each column of the
1010::COMM;;solution. This is only used by `algorithm='lars'` and `algorithm='omp'`
1011::COMM;;and is overridden by `alpha` in the `omp` case. If `None`, then
1012::COMM;;`transform_n_nonzero_coefs=int(n_features / 10)`.
1013::COMM;;transform_alpha : float, default=None
1014::COMM;;If `algorithm='lasso_lars'` or `algorithm='lasso_cd'`, `alpha` is the
1015::COMM;;penalty applied to the L1 norm.
1016::COMM;;If `algorithm='threshold'`, `alpha` is the absolute value of the
1017::COMM;;threshold below which coefficients will be squashed to zero.
1018::COMM;;If `algorithm='omp'`, `alpha` is the tolerance parameter: the value of
1019::COMM;;the reconstruction error targeted. In this case, it overrides
1020::COMM;;`n_nonzero_coefs`.
1021::COMM;;If `None`, default to 1.
1022::COMM;;split_sign : bool, default=False
1023::COMM;;Whether to split the sparse feature vector into the concatenation of
1024::COMM;;its negative part and its positive part. This can improve the
1025::COMM;;performance of downstream classifiers.
1026::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
1027::COMM;;Number of parallel jobs to run.
1028::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
1029::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
1030::COMM;;for more details.
1031::COMM;;positive_code : bool, default=False
1032::COMM;;Whether to enforce positivity when finding the code.
1033::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
1034::COMM;;transform_max_iter : int, default=1000
1035::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations to perform if `algorithm='lasso_cd'` or
1036::COMM;;`lasso_lars`.
1037::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1038::COMM;;Attributes
1039::COMM;;----------
1040::COMM;;n_components_ : int

1047::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
