1456::COMM;;Finds a dictionary (a set of atoms) that performs well at sparsely
1457::COMM;;encoding the fitted data.
1458::COMM;;Solves the optimization problem::
1459::COMM;;(U^*,V^*) = argmin 0.5 || X - U V ||_Fro^2 + alpha * || U ||_1,1
1460::COMM;;(U,V)
1461::COMM;;with || V_k ||_2 <= 1 for all 0 <= k < n_components
1462::COMM;;||.||_Fro stands for the Frobenius norm and ||.||_1,1 stands for
1463::COMM;;the entry-wise matrix norm which is the sum of the absolute values
1464::COMM;;of all the entries in the matrix.
1465::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <DictionaryLearning>`.
1466::COMM;;Parameters
1467::COMM;;----------
1468::COMM;;n_components : int, default=None
1469::COMM;;Number of dictionary elements to extract.
1470::COMM;;alpha : float, default=1
1471::COMM;;Sparsity controlling parameter.
1472::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=1_000
1473::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations over the complete dataset before
1474::COMM;;stopping independently of any early stopping criterion heuristics.
1475::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
1476::COMM;;fit_algorithm : {'lars', 'cd'}, default='lars'
1477::COMM;;The algorithm used:
1478::COMM;;- `'lars'`: uses the least angle regression method to solve the lasso
1479::COMM;;problem (`linear_model.lars_path`)
1480::COMM;;- `'cd'`: uses the coordinate descent method to compute the
1481::COMM;;Lasso solution (`linear_model.Lasso`). Lars will be faster if
1482::COMM;;the estimated components are sparse.
1483::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
1484::COMM;;Number of parallel jobs to run.
1485::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
1486::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
1487::COMM;;for more details.
1488::COMM;;batch_size : int, default=256
1489::COMM;;Number of samples in each mini-batch.
1490::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.3
1491::COMM;;The default value of `batch_size` changed from 3 to 256 in version 1.3.
1492::COMM;;shuffle : bool, default=True
1493::COMM;;Whether to shuffle the samples before forming batches.
1494::COMM;;dict_init : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features), default=None
1495::COMM;;Initial value of the dictionary for warm restart scenarios.
1496::COMM;;transform_algorithm : {'lasso_lars', 'lasso_cd', 'lars', 'omp', \
1497::COMM;;'threshold'}, default='omp'
1498::COMM;;Algorithm used to transform the data:
1499::COMM;;- `'lars'`: uses the least angle regression method
1500::COMM;;(`linear_model.lars_path`);
1501::COMM;;- `'lasso_lars'`: uses Lars to compute the Lasso solution.
1502::COMM;;- `'lasso_cd'`: uses the coordinate descent method to compute the
1503::COMM;;Lasso solution (`linear_model.Lasso`). `'lasso_lars'` will be faster
1504::COMM;;if the estimated components are sparse.
1505::COMM;;- `'omp'`: uses orthogonal matching pursuit to estimate the sparse
1506::COMM;;solution.
1507::COMM;;- `'threshold'`: squashes to zero all coefficients less than alpha from
1508::COMM;;the projection ``dictionary * X'``.
1509::COMM;;transform_n_nonzero_coefs : int, default=None
1510::COMM;;Number of nonzero coefficients to target in each column of the
1511::COMM;;solution. This is only used by `algorithm='lars'` and
1512::COMM;;`algorithm='omp'`. If `None`, then
1513::COMM;;`transform_n_nonzero_coefs=int(n_features / 10)`.
1514::COMM;;transform_alpha : float, default=None
1515::COMM;;If `algorithm='lasso_lars'` or `algorithm='lasso_cd'`, `alpha` is the
1516::COMM;;penalty applied to the L1 norm.
1517::COMM;;If `algorithm='threshold'`, `alpha` is the absolute value of the
1518::COMM;;threshold below which coefficients will be squashed to zero.
1519::COMM;;If `None`, defaults to `alpha`.
1520::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.2
1521::COMM;;When None, default value changed from 1.0 to `alpha`.
1522::COMM;;verbose : bool or int, default=False
1523::COMM;;To control the verbosity of the procedure.
1524::COMM;;split_sign : bool, default=False
1525::COMM;;Whether to split the sparse feature vector into the concatenation of
1526::COMM;;its negative part and its positive part. This can improve the
1527::COMM;;performance of downstream classifiers.
1528::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1529::COMM;;Used for initializing the dictionary when ``dict_init`` is not
1530::COMM;;specified, randomly shuffling the data when ``shuffle`` is set to
1531::COMM;;``True``, and updating the dictionary. Pass an int for reproducible
1532::COMM;;results across multiple function calls.
1533::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
1534::COMM;;positive_code : bool, default=False
1535::COMM;;Whether to enforce positivity when finding the code.
1536::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
1537::COMM;;positive_dict : bool, default=False
1538::COMM;;Whether to enforce positivity when finding the dictionary.
1539::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
1540::COMM;;transform_max_iter : int, default=1000
1541::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations to perform if `algorithm='lasso_cd'` or
1542::COMM;;`'lasso_lars'`.
1543::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1544::COMM;;callback : callable, default=None
1545::COMM;;A callable that gets invoked at the end of each iteration.

1547::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-3
1548::COMM;;Control early stopping based on the norm of the differences in the
1549::COMM;;dictionary between 2 steps.
1550::COMM;;To disable early stopping based on changes in the dictionary, set
1551::COMM;;`tol` to 0.0.

1556::COMM;;To disable convergence detection based on cost function, set
1557::COMM;;`max_no_improvement` to None.

1759::COMM;;def _check_convergence(
1760::COMM;;self, X, batch_cost, new_dict, old_dict, n_samples, step, n_steps
1761::COMM;;):
1770::COMM;;batch_size = X.shape[0]
1771::COMM;;# counts steps starting from 1 for user friendly verbose mode.
1772::COMM;;step = step + 1
1773::COMM;;# Ignore 100 first steps or 1 epoch to avoid initializing the ewa_cost with a
1774::COMM;;# too bad value
1775::COMM;;if step <= min(100, n_samples / batch_size):
1776::COMM;;if self.verbose:
1777::COMM;;print(f"Minibatch step {step}/{n_steps}: mean batch cost: {batch_cost}")
1778::COMM;;return False
1779::COMM;;# Compute an Exponentially Weighted Average of the cost function to
1780::COMM;;# monitor the convergence while discarding minibatch-local stochastic
1781::COMM;;# variability: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moving_average
1782::COMM;;if self._ewa_cost is None:
1783::COMM;;self._ewa_cost = batch_cost
1784::COMM;;else:
1785::COMM;;alpha = batch_size / (n_samples + 1)
1786::COMM;;alpha = min(alpha, 1)
1787::COMM;;self._ewa_cost = self._ewa_cost * (1 - alpha) + batch_cost * alpha
1788::COMM;;if self.verbose:
1789::COMM;;print(
1790::COMM;;f"Minibatch step {step}/{n_steps}: mean batch cost: "
1791::COMM;;f"{batch_cost}, ewa cost: {self._ewa_cost}"
1792::COMM;;)
1793::COMM;;# Early stopping based on change of dictionary
1794::COMM;;dict_diff = linalg.norm(new_dict - old_dict) / self._n_components
1795::COMM;;if self.tol > 0 and dict_diff <= self.tol:
1796::COMM;;if self.verbose:
1797::COMM;;print(f"Converged (small dictionary change) at step {step}/{n_steps}")
1798::COMM;;return True
1799::COMM;;# Early stopping heuristic due to lack of improvement on smoothed
1800::COMM;;# cost function
1801::COMM;;if self._ewa_cost_min is None or self._ewa_cost < self._ewa_cost_min:
1802::COMM;;self._no_improvement = 0
1803::COMM;;self._ewa_cost_min = self._ewa_cost
1804::COMM;;else:
1805::COMM;;self._no_improvement += 1
1806::COMM;;if (
1807::COMM;;self.max_no_improvement is not None
1808::COMM;;and self._no_improvement >= self.max_no_improvement
1809::COMM;;):
1810::COMM;;if self.verbose:
1811::COMM;;print(
1812::COMM;;"Converged (lack of improvement in objective function) "
1813::COMM;;f"at step {step}/{n_steps}"
1814::COMM;;)
1815::COMM;;return True
1816::COMM;;return False

2::COMM;;A latent linear variable model.
3::COMM;;FactorAnalysis is similar to probabilistic PCA implemented by PCA.score
4::COMM;;While PCA assumes Gaussian noise with the same variance for each
5::COMM;;feature, the FactorAnalysis model assumes different variances for
6::COMM;;each of them.
7::COMM;;This implementation is based on David Barber's Book,
8::COMM;;Bayesian Reasoning and Machine Learning,
9::COMM;;http://www.cs.ucl.ac.uk/staff/d.barber/brml,
10::COMM;;Algorithm 21.1
12::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
13::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
32::COMM;;A simple linear generative model with Gaussian latent variables.
33::COMM;;The observations are assumed to be caused by a linear transformation of
34::COMM;;lower dimensional latent factors and added Gaussian noise.
35::COMM;;Without loss of generality the factors are distributed according to a
36::COMM;;Gaussian with zero mean and unit covariance. The noise is also zero mean
37::COMM;;and has an arbitrary diagonal covariance matrix.
38::COMM;;If we would restrict the model further, by assuming that the Gaussian
39::COMM;;noise is even isotropic (all diagonal entries are the same) we would obtain
40::COMM;;:class:`PCA`.
41::COMM;;FactorAnalysis performs a maximum likelihood estimate of the so-called
42::COMM;;`loading` matrix, the transformation of the latent variables to the
43::COMM;;observed ones, using SVD based approach.
44::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <FA>`.
45::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.13
46::COMM;;Parameters
47::COMM;;----------
48::COMM;;n_components : int, default=None
49::COMM;;Dimensionality of latent space, the number of components
50::COMM;;of ``X`` that are obtained after ``transform``.
51::COMM;;If None, n_components is set to the number of features.
52::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-2
53::COMM;;Stopping tolerance for log-likelihood increase.
54::COMM;;copy : bool, default=True
55::COMM;;Whether to make a copy of X. If ``False``, the input X gets overwritten
56::COMM;;during fitting.
57::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=1000
58::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations.
59::COMM;;noise_variance_init : array-like of shape (n_features,), default=None
60::COMM;;The initial guess of the noise variance for each feature.
61::COMM;;If None, it defaults to np.ones(n_features).
62::COMM;;svd_method : {'lapack', 'randomized'}, default='randomized'
63::COMM;;Which SVD method to use. If 'lapack' use standard SVD from
64::COMM;;scipy.linalg, if 'randomized' use fast ``randomized_svd`` function.
65::COMM;;Defaults to 'randomized'. For most applications 'randomized' will
66::COMM;;be sufficiently precise while providing significant speed gains.
67::COMM;;Accuracy can also be improved by setting higher values for
68::COMM;;`iterated_power`. If this is not sufficient, for maximum precision
69::COMM;;you should choose 'lapack'.
70::COMM;;iterated_power : int, default=3
71::COMM;;Number of iterations for the power method. 3 by default. Only used
72::COMM;;if ``svd_method`` equals 'randomized'.
73::COMM;;rotation : {'varimax', 'quartimax'}, default=None
74::COMM;;If not None, apply the indicated rotation. Currently, varimax and
75::COMM;;quartimax are implemented. See
76::COMM;;`"The varimax criterion for analytic rotation in factor analysis"
77::COMM;;<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF02289233>`_
78::COMM;;H. F. Kaiser, 1958.
79::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
80::COMM;;random_state : int or RandomState instance, default=0
81::COMM;;Only used when ``svd_method`` equals 'randomized'. Pass an int for
82::COMM;;reproducible results across multiple function calls.
83::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
84::COMM;;Attributes
85::COMM;;----------
86::COMM;;components_ : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features)
87::COMM;;Components with maximum variance.
88::COMM;;loglike_ : list of shape (n_iterations,)
89::COMM;;The log likelihood at each iteration.
90::COMM;;noise_variance_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
91::COMM;;The estimated noise variance for each feature.
92::COMM;;n_iter_ : int
93::COMM;;Number of iterations run.
94::COMM;;mean_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
95::COMM;;Per-feature empirical mean, estimated from the training set.
96::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
97::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
98::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
99::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
100::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
101::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
102::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
103::COMM;;See Also
104::COMM;;--------
105::COMM;;PCA: Principal component analysis is also a latent linear variable model
106::COMM;;which however assumes equal noise variance for each feature.
107::COMM;;This extra assumption makes probabilistic PCA faster as it can be
108::COMM;;computed in closed form.
109::COMM;;FastICA: Independent component analysis, a latent variable model with
110::COMM;;non-Gaussian latent variables.
111::COMM;;References
112::COMM;;----------
113::COMM;;- David Barber, Bayesian Reasoning and Machine Learning,
114::COMM;;Algorithm 21.1.
115::COMM;;- Christopher M. Bishop: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning,
116::COMM;;Chapter 12.2.4.
117::COMM;;Examples

120::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.decomposition import FactorAnalysis

122::COMM;;>>> transformer = FactorAnalysis(n_components=7, random_state=0)
123::COMM;;>>> X_transformed = transformer.fit_transform(X)
124::COMM;;>>> X_transformed.shape

352::COMM;;def _ortho_rotation(components, method="varimax", tol=1e-6, max_iter=100):
2::COMM;;Python implementation of the fast ICA algorithms.
3::COMM;;Reference: Tables 8.3 and 8.4 page 196 in the book:
4::COMM;;Independent Component Analysis, by Hyvarinen et al.
6::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
7::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
30::COMM;;Orthonormalize w wrt the first j rows of W.
31::COMM;;Parameters
32::COMM;;----------
33::COMM;;w : ndarray of shape (n,)
34::COMM;;Array to be orthogonalized
35::COMM;;W : ndarray of shape (p, n)
36::COMM;;Null space definition
37::COMM;;j : int < p
38::COMM;;The no of (from the first) rows of Null space W wrt which w is
39::COMM;;orthogonalized.
40::COMM;;Notes
41::COMM;;-----
42::COMM;;Assumes that W is orthogonal
43::COMM;;w changed in place
49::COMM;;i.e. W <- (W * W.T) ^{-1/2} * W
52::COMO;;# Avoid sqrt of negative values because of rounding errors. Note that
53::COMO;;# np.sqrt(tiny) is larger than tiny and therefore this clipping also
54::COMO;;# prevents division by zero in the next step.
56::COMO;;# u (resp. s) contains the eigenvectors (resp. square roots of
57::COMO;;# the eigenvalues) of W * W.T
61::COMM;;Used internally by FastICA.
66::COMO;;# j is the index of the extracted component
84::COMM;;Used internally by FastICA --main loop
93::COMO;;# builtin max, abs are faster than numpy counter parts.
94::COMO;;# np.einsum allows having the lowest memory footprint.
95::COMO;;# It is faster than np.diag(np.dot(W1, W.T)).
109::COMO;;# Some standard non-linear functions.
110::COMO;;# XXX: these should be optimized, as they can be a bottleneck.
112::COMC;;alpha = fun_args.get("alpha", 1.0) # comment it out?
114::COMC;;gx = np.tanh(x, x) # apply the tanh inplace
116::COMO;;# XXX compute in chunks to avoid extra allocation
117::COMC;;for i, gx_i in enumerate(gx): # please don't vectorize.
154::COMM;;The implementation is based on [1]_.
155::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <ICA>`.
156::COMM;;Parameters
157::COMM;;----------
158::COMM;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
159::COMM;;Training vector, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
160::COMM;;`n_features` is the number of features.
161::COMM;;n_components : int, default=None
162::COMM;;Number of components to use. If None is passed, all are used.
163::COMM;;algorithm : {'parallel', 'deflation'}, default='parallel'
164::COMM;;Specify which algorithm to use for FastICA.
165::COMM;;whiten : str or bool, default='unit-variance'
166::COMM;;Specify the whitening strategy to use.
167::COMM;;- If 'arbitrary-variance', a whitening with variance
168::COMM;;arbitrary is used.
169::COMM;;- If 'unit-variance', the whitening matrix is rescaled to ensure that
170::COMM;;each recovered source has unit variance.
171::COMM;;- If False, the data is already considered to be whitened, and no
172::COMM;;whitening is performed.
173::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.3
174::COMM;;The default value of `whiten` changed to 'unit-variance' in 1.3.
175::COMM;;fun : {'logcosh', 'exp', 'cube'} or callable, default='logcosh'
176::COMM;;The functional form of the G function used in the
177::COMM;;approximation to neg-entropy. Could be either 'logcosh', 'exp',
178::COMM;;or 'cube'.
179::COMM;;You can also provide your own function. It should return a tuple
180::COMM;;containing the value of the function, and of its derivative, in the
181::COMM;;point. The derivative should be averaged along its last dimension.
182::COMM;;Example::
183::COMM;;def my_g(x):
184::COMM;;return x ** 3, (3 * x ** 2).mean(axis=-1)
185::COMM;;fun_args : dict, default=None
186::COMM;;Arguments to send to the functional form.
187::COMM;;If empty or None and if fun='logcosh', fun_args will take value
188::COMM;;{'alpha' : 1.0}.
189::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=200
190::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations to perform.
191::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-4
192::COMM;;A positive scalar giving the tolerance at which the
193::COMM;;un-mixing matrix is considered to have converged.
194::COMM;;w_init : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_components), default=None
195::COMM;;Initial un-mixing array. If `w_init=None`, then an array of values
196::COMM;;drawn from a normal distribution is used.
197::COMM;;whiten_solver : {"eigh", "svd"}, default="svd"
198::COMM;;The solver to use for whitening.
199::COMM;;- "svd" is more stable numerically if the problem is degenerate, and
200::COMM;;often faster when `n_samples <= n_features`.
201::COMM;;- "eigh" is generally more memory efficient when
202::COMM;;`n_samples >= n_features`, and can be faster when
203::COMM;;`n_samples >= 50 * n_features`.
204::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
205::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
206::COMM;;Used to initialize ``w_init`` when not specified, with a
207::COMM;;normal distribution. Pass an int, for reproducible results
208::COMM;;across multiple function calls.
209::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
210::COMM;;return_X_mean : bool, default=False
211::COMM;;If True, X_mean is returned too.
212::COMM;;compute_sources : bool, default=True
213::COMM;;If False, sources are not computed, but only the rotation matrix.
214::COMM;;This can save memory when working with big data. Defaults to True.
215::COMM;;return_n_iter : bool, default=False
216::COMM;;Whether or not to return the number of iterations.
217::COMM;;Returns
218::COMM;;-------
219::COMM;;K : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features) or None
220::COMM;;If whiten is 'True', K is the pre-whitening matrix that projects data
221::COMM;;onto the first n_components principal components. If whiten is 'False',
222::COMM;;K is 'None'.
223::COMM;;W : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_components)
224::COMM;;The square matrix that unmixes the data after whitening.
225::COMM;;The mixing matrix is the pseudo-inverse of matrix ``W K``
226::COMM;;if K is not None, else it is the inverse of W.
227::COMM;;S : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_components) or None
228::COMM;;Estimated source matrix.
229::COMM;;X_mean : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
230::COMM;;The mean over features. Returned only if return_X_mean is True.
231::COMM;;n_iter : int
232::COMM;;If the algorithm is "deflation", n_iter is the
233::COMM;;maximum number of iterations run across all components. Else
234::COMM;;they are just the number of iterations taken to converge. This is
235::COMM;;returned only when return_n_iter is set to `True`.
236::COMM;;Notes
237::COMM;;-----
238::COMM;;The data matrix X is considered to be a linear combination of
239::COMM;;non-Gaussian (independent) components i.e. X = AS where columns of S
240::COMM;;contain the independent components and A is a linear mixing
241::COMM;;matrix. In short ICA attempts to `un-mix' the data by estimating an
242::COMM;;un-mixing matrix W where ``S = W K X.``
243::COMM;;While FastICA was proposed to estimate as many sources
244::COMM;;as features, it is possible to estimate less by setting
245::COMM;;n_components < n_features. It this case K is not a square matrix
246::COMM;;and the estimated A is the pseudo-inverse of ``W K``.
247::COMM;;This implementation was originally made for data of shape
248::COMM;;[n_features, n_samples]. Now the input is transposed
249::COMM;;before the algorithm is applied. This makes it slightly
250::COMM;;faster for Fortran-ordered input.
251::COMM;;References
252::COMM;;----------
253::COMM;;.. [1] A. Hyvarinen and E. Oja, "Fast Independent Component Analysis",
254::COMM;;Algorithms and Applications, Neural Networks, 13(4-5), 2000,
255::COMM;;pp. 411-430.
256::COMM;;Examples
257::COMM;;--------
258::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import load_digits
259::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.decomposition import fastica
260::COMM;;>>> X, _ = load_digits(return_X_y=True)
261::COMM;;>>> K, W, S = fastica(X, n_components=7, random_state=0, whiten='unit-variance')
262::COMM;;>>> K.shape
263::COMM;;(7, 64)
264::COMM;;>>> W.shape
265::COMM;;(7, 7)
266::COMM;;>>> S.shape
267::COMM;;(1797, 7)
297::COMM;;The implementation is based on [1]_.
298::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <ICA>`.
299::COMM;;Parameters
300::COMM;;----------
301::COMM;;n_components : int, default=None
302::COMM;;Number of components to use. If None is passed, all are used.
303::COMM;;algorithm : {'parallel', 'deflation'}, default='parallel'
304::COMM;;Specify which algorithm to use for FastICA.
305::COMM;;whiten : str or bool, default='unit-variance'
306::COMM;;Specify the whitening strategy to use.
307::COMM;;- If 'arbitrary-variance', a whitening with variance
308::COMM;;arbitrary is used.
309::COMM;;- If 'unit-variance', the whitening matrix is rescaled to ensure that
310::COMM;;each recovered source has unit variance.
311::COMM;;- If False, the data is already considered to be whitened, and no
312::COMM;;whitening is performed.
313::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.3
314::COMM;;The default value of `whiten` changed to 'unit-variance' in 1.3.
315::COMM;;fun : {'logcosh', 'exp', 'cube'} or callable, default='logcosh'
316::COMM;;The functional form of the G function used in the
317::COMM;;approximation to neg-entropy. Could be either 'logcosh', 'exp',
318::COMM;;or 'cube'.
319::COMM;;You can also provide your own function. It should return a tuple
320::COMM;;containing the value of the function, and of its derivative, in the
321::COMM;;point. The derivative should be averaged along its last dimension.
322::COMM;;Example::
323::COMM;;def my_g(x):
324::COMM;;return x ** 3, (3 * x ** 2).mean(axis=-1)
325::COMM;;fun_args : dict, default=None
326::COMM;;Arguments to send to the functional form.
327::COMM;;If empty or None and if fun='logcosh', fun_args will take value
328::COMM;;{'alpha' : 1.0}.
329::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=200
330::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations during fit.
331::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-4
332::COMM;;A positive scalar giving the tolerance at which the
333::COMM;;un-mixing matrix is considered to have converged.
334::COMM;;w_init : array-like of shape (n_components, n_components), default=None
335::COMM;;Initial un-mixing array. If `w_init=None`, then an array of values
336::COMM;;drawn from a normal distribution is used.
337::COMM;;whiten_solver : {"eigh", "svd"}, default="svd"
338::COMM;;The solver to use for whitening.
339::COMM;;- "svd" is more stable numerically if the problem is degenerate, and
340::COMM;;often faster when `n_samples <= n_features`.
341::COMM;;- "eigh" is generally more memory efficient when
342::COMM;;`n_samples >= n_features`, and can be faster when
343::COMM;;`n_samples >= 50 * n_features`.
344::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
345::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
346::COMM;;Used to initialize ``w_init`` when not specified, with a
347::COMM;;normal distribution. Pass an int, for reproducible results
348::COMM;;across multiple function calls.
349::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
350::COMM;;Attributes
351::COMM;;----------
352::COMM;;components_ : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features)
353::COMM;;The linear operator to apply to the data to get the independent
354::COMM;;sources. This is equal to the unmixing matrix when ``whiten`` is
355::COMM;;False, and equal to ``np.dot(unmixing_matrix, self.whitening_)`` when
356::COMM;;``whiten`` is True.
357::COMM;;mixing_ : ndarray of shape (n_features, n_components)
358::COMM;;The pseudo-inverse of ``components_``. It is the linear operator
359::COMM;;that maps independent sources to the data.
360::COMM;;mean_ : ndarray of shape(n_features,)
361::COMM;;The mean over features. Only set if `self.whiten` is True.
362::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
363::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
364::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
365::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
366::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
367::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
368::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
369::COMM;;n_iter_ : int
370::COMM;;If the algorithm is "deflation", n_iter is the
371::COMM;;maximum number of iterations run across all components. Else
372::COMM;;they are just the number of iterations taken to converge.
373::COMM;;whitening_ : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features)
374::COMM;;Only set if whiten is 'True'. This is the pre-whitening matrix
375::COMM;;that projects data onto the first `n_components` principal components.
376::COMM;;See Also
377::COMM;;--------
378::COMM;;PCA : Principal component analysis (PCA).
379::COMM;;IncrementalPCA : Incremental principal components analysis (IPCA).
380::COMM;;KernelPCA : Kernel Principal component analysis (KPCA).
381::COMM;;MiniBatchSparsePCA : Mini-batch Sparse Principal Components Analysis.
382::COMM;;SparsePCA : Sparse Principal Components Analysis (SparsePCA).
383::COMM;;References
384::COMM;;----------
385::COMM;;.. [1] A. Hyvarinen and E. Oja, Independent Component Analysis:
386::COMM;;Algorithms and Applications, Neural Networks, 13(4-5), 2000,
387::COMM;;pp. 411-430.
388::COMM;;Examples
389::COMM;;--------

392::COMM;;>>> X, _ = load_digits(return_X_y=True)

274::COMM;;def _fit_transform_in_place(self, K):

283::COMO;;# compute eigenvectors
292::COMO;;# Note: subset_by_index specifies the indices of smallest/largest to return
309::COMO;;# make sure that the eigenvalues are ok and fix numerical issues
313::COMO;;# flip eigenvectors' sign to enforce deterministic output
315::COMO;;# sort eigenvectors in descending order
319::COMO;;# remove eigenvectors with a zero eigenvalue (null space) if required
323::COMO;;# Maintenance note on Eigenvectors normalization
324::COMO;;# ----------------------------------------------
325::COMO;;# there is a link between
326::COMO;;# the eigenvectors of K=Phi(X)'Phi(X) and the ones of Phi(X)Phi(X)'
327::COMO;;# if v is an eigenvector of K
328::COMO;;# then Phi(X)v is an eigenvector of Phi(X)Phi(X)'
329::COMO;;# if u is an eigenvector of Phi(X)Phi(X)'
330::COMO;;# then Phi(X)'u is an eigenvector of Phi(X)'Phi(X)
331::COMO;;#
332::COMO;;# At this stage our self.eigenvectors_ (the v) have norm 1, we need to scale
333::COMO;;# them so that eigenvectors in kernel feature space (the u) have norm=1
334::COMO;;# instead
335::COMO;;#
336::COMO;;# We COULD scale them here:
337::COMO;;# self.eigenvectors_ = self.eigenvectors_ / np.sqrt(self.eigenvalues_)
338::COMO;;#
339::COMO;;# But choose to perform that LATER when needed, in `fit()` and in
340::COMO;;# `transform()`.

432::COMM;;``inverse_transform`` approximates the inverse transformation using

439::COMM;;of the mean of kernel features, such information is not taken into
440::COMM;;account in reconstruction.
441::COMM;;.. note::

443::COMM;;kernel, it is recommended that they use

3::COMM;;Online Latent Dirichlet Allocation with variational inference
4::COMM;;=============================================================
5::COMM;;This implementation is modified from Matthew D. Hoffman's onlineldavb code

64::COMM;;(doc_topic_distr, suff_stats) :
65::COMM;;`doc_topic_distr` is unnormalized topic distribution for each document.
66::COMM;;In the literature, this is `gamma`. we can calculate `E[log(theta)]`

80::COMO;;# In the literature, this is `exp(E[log(theta)])`
82::COMO;;# diff on `component_` (only calculate it when `cal_diff` is True)
90::COMO;;# These cython functions are called in a nested loop on usually very small arrays
91::COMO;;# (length=n_topics). In that case, finding the appropriate signature of the
92::COMO;;# fused-typed function can be more costly than its execution, hence the dispatch
93::COMO;;# is done outside of the loop.
106::COMO;;# The next one is a copy, since the inner loop overwrites it.
109::COMO;;# Iterate between `doc_topic_d` and `norm_phi` until convergence
112::COMO;;# The optimal phi_{dwk} is proportional to
113::COMO;;# exp(E[log(theta_{dk})]) * exp(E[log(beta_{dw})]).
116::COMO;;# Note: adds doc_topic_prior to doc_topic_d, in-place.
121::COMO;;# Contribution of document d to the expected sufficient
122::COMO;;# statistics for the M step.
131::COMM;;The implementation is based on [1]_ and [2]_.
132::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
133::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <LatentDirichletAllocation>`.
134::COMM;;Parameters
135::COMM;;----------
136::COMM;;n_components : int, default=10
137::COMM;;Number of topics.
138::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.19
139::COMM;;``n_topics`` was renamed to ``n_components``
140::COMM;;doc_topic_prior : float, default=None
141::COMM;;Prior of document topic distribution `theta`. If the value is None,
142::COMM;;defaults to `1 / n_components`.
143::COMM;;In [1]_, this is called `alpha`.
144::COMM;;topic_word_prior : float, default=None
145::COMM;;Prior of topic word distribution `beta`. If the value is None, defaults
146::COMM;;to `1 / n_components`.
147::COMM;;In [1]_, this is called `eta`.
148::COMM;;learning_method : {'batch', 'online'}, default='batch'
149::COMM;;Method used to update `_component`. Only used in :meth:`fit` method.
150::COMM;;In general, if the data size is large, the online update will be much
151::COMM;;faster than the batch update.
152::COMM;;Valid options:
153::COMM;;- 'batch': Batch variational Bayes method. Use all training data in each EM
154::COMM;;update. Old `components_` will be overwritten in each iteration.
155::COMM;;- 'online': Online variational Bayes method. In each EM update, use mini-batch
156::COMM;;of training data to update the ``components_`` variable incrementally. The
157::COMM;;learning rate is controlled by the ``learning_decay`` and the
158::COMM;;``learning_offset`` parameters.
159::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.20
160::COMM;;The default learning method is now ``"batch"``.
161::COMM;;learning_decay : float, default=0.7
162::COMM;;It is a parameter that control learning rate in the online learning
163::COMM;;method. The value should be set between (0.5, 1.0] to guarantee
164::COMM;;asymptotic convergence. When the value is 0.0 and batch_size is
165::COMM;;``n_samples``, the update method is same as batch learning. In the
166::COMM;;literature, this is called kappa.
167::COMM;;learning_offset : float, default=10.0
168::COMM;;A (positive) parameter that downweights early iterations in online
169::COMM;;learning. It should be greater than 1.0. In the literature, this is
170::COMM;;called tau_0.
171::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=10
172::COMM;;The maximum number of passes over the training data (aka epochs).
173::COMM;;It only impacts the behavior in the :meth:`fit` method, and not the
174::COMM;;:meth:`partial_fit` method.
175::COMM;;batch_size : int, default=128
176::COMM;;Number of documents to use in each EM iteration. Only used in online
177::COMM;;learning.
178::COMM;;evaluate_every : int, default=-1
179::COMM;;How often to evaluate perplexity. Only used in `fit` method.
180::COMM;;set it to 0 or negative number to not evaluate perplexity in
181::COMM;;training at all. Evaluating perplexity can help you check convergence
182::COMM;;in training process, but it will also increase total training time.
183::COMM;;Evaluating perplexity in every iteration might increase training time
184::COMM;;up to two-fold.
185::COMM;;total_samples : int, default=1e6
186::COMM;;Total number of documents. Only used in the :meth:`partial_fit` method.
187::COMM;;perp_tol : float, default=1e-1
188::COMM;;Perplexity tolerance. Only used when ``evaluate_every`` is greater than 0.
189::COMM;;mean_change_tol : float, default=1e-3
190::COMM;;Stopping tolerance for updating document topic distribution in E-step.
191::COMM;;max_doc_update_iter : int, default=100
192::COMM;;Max number of iterations for updating document topic distribution in
193::COMM;;the E-step.
194::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
195::COMM;;The number of jobs to use in the E-step.
196::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
197::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
198::COMM;;for more details.
199::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
200::COMM;;Verbosity level.
201::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
202::COMM;;Pass an int for reproducible results across multiple function calls.
203::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
204::COMM;;Attributes
205::COMM;;----------
206::COMM;;components_ : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features)
207::COMM;;Variational parameters for topic word distribution. Since the complete
208::COMM;;conditional for topic word distribution is a Dirichlet,
209::COMM;;``components_[i, j]`` can be viewed as pseudocount that represents the
210::COMM;;number of times word `j` was assigned to topic `i`.
211::COMM;;It can also be viewed as distribution over the words for each topic
212::COMM;;after normalization:
213::COMM;;``model.components_ / model.components_.sum(axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]``.
214::COMM;;exp_dirichlet_component_ : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features)
215::COMM;;Exponential value of expectation of log topic word distribution.
216::COMM;;In the literature, this is `exp(E[log(beta)])`.
217::COMM;;n_batch_iter_ : int
218::COMM;;Number of iterations of the EM step.
219::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
220::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
221::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
222::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
223::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
224::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
225::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
226::COMM;;n_iter_ : int
227::COMM;;Number of passes over the dataset.
228::COMM;;bound_ : float
229::COMM;;Final perplexity score on training set.
230::COMM;;doc_topic_prior_ : float
231::COMM;;Prior of document topic distribution `theta`. If the value is None,
232::COMM;;it is `1 / n_components`.
233::COMM;;random_state_ : RandomState instance
234::COMM;;RandomState instance that is generated either from a seed, the random
235::COMM;;number generator or by `np.random`.
236::COMM;;topic_word_prior_ : float
237::COMM;;Prior of topic word distribution `beta`. If the value is None, it is
238::COMM;;`1 / n_components`.

345::COMM;;def _e_step(self, X, cal_sstats, random_init, parallel=None):
368::COMM;;# Run e-step in parallel
369::COMM;;random_state = self.random_state_ if random_init else None
370::COMM;;# TODO: make Parallel._effective_n_jobs public instead?
371::COMM;;n_jobs = effective_n_jobs(self.n_jobs)
372::COMM;;if parallel is None:
373::COMM;;parallel = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs, verbose=max(0, self.verbose - 1))
374::COMM;;results = parallel(
375::COMM;;delayed(_update_doc_distribution)(
376::COMM;;X[idx_slice, :],
377::COMM;;self.exp_dirichlet_component_,
378::COMM;;self.doc_topic_prior_,
379::COMM;;self.max_doc_update_iter,
380::COMM;;self.mean_change_tol,
381::COMM;;cal_sstats,
382::COMM;;random_state,
383::COMM;;)
384::COMM;;for idx_slice in gen_even_slices(X.shape[0], n_jobs)
385::COMM;;)
386::COMM;;# merge result
387::COMM;;doc_topics, sstats_list = zip(*results)
388::COMM;;doc_topic_distr = np.vstack(doc_topics)
389::COMM;;if cal_sstats:
390::COMM;;# This step finishes computing the sufficient statistics for the
391::COMM;;# M-step.
392::COMM;;suff_stats = np.zeros(self.components_.shape, dtype=self.components_.dtype)
393::COMM;;for sstats in sstats_list:
394::COMM;;suff_stats += sstats
395::COMM;;suff_stats *= self.exp_dirichlet_component_
396::COMM;;else:
397::COMM;;suff_stats = None
398::COMM;;return (doc_topic_distr, suff_stats)
399::COMM;;def _em_step(self, X, total_samples, batch_update, parallel=None):
419::COMM;;# E-step
420::COMM;;_, suff_stats = self._e_step(
421::COMM;;X, cal_sstats=True, random_init=True, parallel=parallel
422::COMM;;)
423::COMM;;# M-step
424::COMM;;if batch_update:
425::COMM;;self.components_ = self.topic_word_prior_ + suff_stats
426::COMM;;else:
427::COMM;;# online update
428::COMM;;# In the literature, the weight is `rho`
429::COMM;;weight = np.power(
430::COMM;;self.learning_offset + self.n_batch_iter_, -self.learning_decay
431::COMM;;)
432::COMM;;doc_ratio = float(total_samples) / X.shape[0]
433::COMM;;self.components_ *= 1 - weight
434::COMM;;self.components_ += weight * (
435::COMM;;self.topic_word_prior_ + doc_ratio * suff_stats
436::COMM;;)
437::COMM;;# update `component_` related variables
438::COMM;;self.exp_dirichlet_component_ = np.exp(
439::COMM;;_dirichlet_expectation_2d(self.components_)
440::COMM;;)
441::COMM;;self.n_batch_iter_ += 1
442::COMM;;return

631::COMM;;def _approx_bound(self, X, doc_topic_distr, sub_sampling):
650::COMM;;def _loglikelihood(prior, distr, dirichlet_distr, size):

61::COMM;;def _beta_divergence(X, W, H, beta, square_root=False):

111::COMM;;indices = X_data > EPSILON

113::COMM;;X_data = X_data[indices]

171::COMM;;def _initialize_nmf(X, n_components, init=None, eps=1e-6, random_state=None):

238::COMM;;X.dtype, copy=False

241::COMM;;X.dtype, copy=False

244::COMM;;np.abs(W, out=W)

247::COMM;;U, S, V = _randomized_svd(X, n_components, random_state=random_state)
248::COMM;;W = np.zeros_like(U)
249::COMM;;H = np.zeros_like(V)

251::COMM;;# so it can be used as is for initialization.
252::COMM;;W[:, 0] = np.sqrt(S[0]) * np.abs(U[:, 0])
253::COMM;;H[0, :] = np.sqrt(S[0]) * np.abs(V[0, :])
254::COMM;;for j in range(1, n_components):
255::COMM;;x, y = U[:, j], V[j, :]
256::COMM;;# extract positive and negative parts of column vectors
257::COMM;;x_p, y_p = np.maximum(x, 0), np.maximum(y, 0)
258::COMM;;x_n, y_n = np.abs(np.minimum(x, 0)), np.abs(np.minimum(y, 0))
259::COMM;;# and their norms
260::COMM;;x_p_nrm, y_p_nrm = norm(x_p), norm(y_p)
261::COMM;;x_n_nrm, y_n_nrm = norm(x_n), norm(y_n)
262::COMM;;m_p, m_n = x_p_nrm * y_p_nrm, x_n_nrm * y_n_nrm
263::COMM;;# choose update

273::COMM;;W[:, j] = lbd * u

276::COMM;;H[H < eps] = 0

278::COMM;;pass
279::COMM;;elif init == "nndsvda":
280::COMM;;avg = X.mean()
281::COMM;;W[W == 0] = avg

283::COMM;;elif init == "nndsvdar":

588::COMM;;def _fit_multiplicative_update(
589::COMM;;X,
590::COMM;;W,
591::COMM;;H,
592::COMM;;beta_loss="frobenius",
593::COMM;;max_iter=200,
594::COMM;;tol=1e-4,
595::COMM;;l1_reg_W=0,
596::COMM;;l1_reg_H=0,
597::COMM;;l2_reg_W=0,
598::COMM;;l2_reg_H=0,
599::COMM;;update_H=True,
600::COMM;;verbose=0,
601::COMM;;):
654::COMM;;start_time = time.time()
655::COMM;;beta_loss = _beta_loss_to_float(beta_loss)
656::COMM;;# gamma for Maximization-Minimization (MM) algorithm [Fevotte 2011]
657::COMM;;if beta_loss < 1:
658::COMM;;gamma = 1.0 / (2.0 - beta_loss)
659::COMM;;elif beta_loss > 2:
660::COMM;;gamma = 1.0 / (beta_loss - 1.0)
661::COMM;;else:
662::COMM;;gamma = 1.0
663::COMM;;# used for the convergence criterion
664::COMM;;error_at_init = _beta_divergence(X, W, H, beta_loss, square_root=True)
665::COMM;;previous_error = error_at_init
666::COMM;;H_sum, HHt, XHt = None, None, None
667::COMM;;for n_iter in range(1, max_iter + 1):
668::COMM;;# update W
669::COMM;;# H_sum, HHt and XHt are saved and reused if not update_H
670::COMM;;W, H_sum, HHt, XHt = _multiplicative_update_w(
671::COMM;;X,
672::COMM;;W,
673::COMM;;H,
674::COMM;;beta_loss=beta_loss,
675::COMM;;l1_reg_W=l1_reg_W,
676::COMM;;l2_reg_W=l2_reg_W,
677::COMM;;gamma=gamma,
678::COMM;;H_sum=H_sum,
679::COMM;;HHt=HHt,
680::COMM;;XHt=XHt,

19::COMM;;def _assess_dimension(spectrum, rank, n_samples):
44::COMM;;xp, _ = get_namespace(spectrum)
45::COMM;;n_features = spectrum.shape[0]
46::COMM;;if not 1 <= rank < n_features:
47::COMM;;raise ValueError("the tested rank should be in [1, n_features - 1]")
48::COMM;;eps = 1e-15
49::COMM;;if spectrum[rank - 1] < eps:
50::COMM;;# When the tested rank is associated with a small eigenvalue, there's
51::COMM;;# no point in computing the log-likelihood: it's going to be very
52::COMM;;# small and won't be the max anyway. Also, it can lead to numerical
53::COMM;;# issues below when computing pa, in particular in log((spectrum[i] -
54::COMM;;# spectrum[j]) because this will take the log of something very small.
55::COMM;;return -xp.inf
56::COMM;;pu = -rank * log(2.0)
57::COMM;;for i in range(1, rank + 1):
58::COMM;;pu += (
59::COMM;;lgamma((n_features - i + 1) / 2.0) - log(xp.pi) * (n_features - i + 1) / 2.0
60::COMM;;)
61::COMM;;pl = xp.sum(xp.log(spectrum[:rank]))
62::COMM;;pl = -pl * n_samples / 2.0
63::COMM;;v = max(eps, xp.sum(spectrum[rank:]) / (n_features - rank))
64::COMM;;pv = -log(v) * n_samples * (n_features - rank) / 2.0
65::COMM;;m = n_features * rank - rank * (rank + 1.0) / 2.0
66::COMM;;pp = log(2.0 * xp.pi) * (m + rank) / 2.0
67::COMM;;pa = 0.0
68::COMM;;spectrum_ = xp.asarray(spectrum, copy=True)
69::COMM;;spectrum_[rank:n_features] = v
70::COMM;;for i in range(rank):
71::COMM;;for j in range(i + 1, spectrum.shape[0]):
72::COMM;;pa += log(
73::COMM;;(spectrum[i] - spectrum[j]) * (1.0 / spectrum_[j] - 1.0 / spectrum_[i])
74::COMM;;) + log(n_samples)
75::COMM;;ll = pu + pl + pv + pp - pa / 2.0 - rank * log(n_samples) / 2.0
76::COMM;;return ll
77::COMM;;def _infer_dimension(spectrum, n_samples):
81::COMM;;xp, _ = get_namespace(spectrum)
82::COMM;;ll = xp.empty_like(spectrum)
83::COMM;;ll[0] = -xp.inf # we don't want to return n_components = 0
84::COMM;;for rank in range(1, spectrum.shape[0]):
85::COMM;;ll[rank] = _assess_dimension(spectrum, rank, n_samples)
86::COMM;;return xp.argmax(ll)

389::COMO;;# Raise an error for sparse input and unsupported svd_solver

401::COMO;;# supports sparse input data and the `covariance_eigh` solver are
402::COMO;;# written in a way to avoid the need for any inplace modification of
403::COMO;;# the input data contrary to the other solvers.
404::COMO;;# The copy will happen
405::COMO;;# later, only if needed, once the solver negotiation below is done.
426::COMO;;# Tall and skinny problems are best handled by precomputing the
427::COMO;;# covariance matrix.

435::COMO;;# This is also the case of n_components in (0, 1)
438::COMO;;# Call different fits for either full or truncated SVD

446::COMM;;if n_components == "mle":
447::COMM;;if n_samples < n_features:
448::COMM;;raise ValueError(

450::COMM;;)
451::COMM;;elif not 0 <= n_components <= min(n_samples, n_features):
452::COMM;;raise ValueError(

454::COMM;;f"min(n_samples, n_features)={min(n_samples, n_features)} with "
455::COMM;;f"svd_solver={self._fit_svd_solver!r}"

457::COMM;;self.mean_ = xp.mean(X, axis=0)
458::COMM;;# When X is a scipy sparse matrix, self.mean_ is a numpy matrix, so we need
459::COMM;;# to transform it to a 1D array. Note that this is not the case when X
460::COMM;;# is a scipy sparse array.
461::COMM;;# TODO: remove the following two lines when scikit-learn only depends
462::COMM;;# on scipy versions that no longer support scipy.sparse matrices.
463::COMM;;self.mean_ = xp.reshape(xp.asarray(self.mean_), (-1,))
464::COMM;;if self._fit_svd_solver == "full":
465::COMM;;X_centered = xp.asarray(X, copy=True) if self.copy else X
466::COMM;;X_centered -= self.mean_
467::COMM;;x_is_centered = not self.copy
468::COMM;;if not is_array_api_compliant:
469::COMM;;# Use scipy.linalg with NumPy/SciPy inputs for the sake of not
470::COMM;;# introducing unanticipated behavior changes. In the long run we
471::COMM;;# could instead decide to always use xp.linalg.svd for all inputs,
472::COMM;;# but that would make this code rely on numpy's SVD instead of
473::COMM;;# scipy's. It's not 100% clear whether they use the same LAPACK
474::COMM;;# solver by default though (assuming both are built against the
475::COMM;;# same BLAS).
476::COMM;;U, S, Vt = linalg.svd(X_centered, full_matrices=False)
477::COMM;;else:
478::COMM;;U, S, Vt = xp.linalg.svd(X_centered, full_matrices=False)
479::COMM;;explained_variance_ = (S**2) / (n_samples - 1)
480::COMM;;else:
481::COMM;;assert self._fit_svd_solver == "covariance_eigh"
482::COMM;;# In the following, we center the covariance matrix C afterwards
483::COMM;;# (without centering the data X first) to avoid an unnecessary copy
484::COMM;;# of X. Note that the mean_ attribute is still needed to center
485::COMM;;# test data in the transform method.
486::COMM;;#
487::COMM;;# Note: at the time of writing, `xp.cov` does not exist in the
488::COMM;;# Array API standard:
489::COMM;;# https://github.com/data-apis/array-api/issues/43
490::COMM;;#
491::COMM;;# Besides, using `numpy.cov`, as of numpy 1.26.0, would not be
492::COMM;;# memory efficient for our use case when `n_samples >> n_features`:
493::COMM;;# `numpy.cov` centers a copy of the data before computing the
494::COMM;;# matrix product instead of subtracting a small `(n_features,
495::COMM;;# n_features)` square matrix from the gram matrix X.T @ X, as we do
496::COMM;;# below.
497::COMM;;x_is_centered = False

499::COMM;;C -= (

502::COMM;;* xp.reshape(self.mean_, (1, -1))
503::COMM;;)

506::COMM;;# When X is a scipy sparse matrix, the following two datastructures
507::COMM;;# are returned as instances of the soft-deprecated numpy.matrix
508::COMM;;# class. Note that this problem does not occur when X is a scipy
509::COMM;;# sparse array (or another other kind of supported array).
510::COMM;;# TODO: remove the following two lines when scikit-learn only
511::COMM;;# depends on scipy versions that no longer support scipy.sparse
512::COMM;;# matrices.
513::COMM;;eigenvals = xp.reshape(xp.asarray(eigenvals), (-1,))
514::COMM;;eigenvecs = xp.asarray(eigenvecs)
515::COMM;;eigenvals = xp.flip(eigenvals, axis=0)
516::COMM;;eigenvecs = xp.flip(eigenvecs, axis=1)
517::COMM;;# The covariance matrix C is positive semi-definite by
518::COMM;;# construction. However, the eigenvalues returned by xp.linalg.eigh
519::COMM;;# can be slightly negative due to numerical errors. This would be
520::COMM;;# an issue for the subsequent sqrt, hence the manual clipping.

533::COMM;;explained_variance_ratio_ = explained_variance_ / total_var
534::COMM;;singular_values_ = xp.asarray(S, copy=True) # Store the singular values.
535::COMM;;# Postprocess the number of components required
536::COMM;;if n_components == "mle":
537::COMM;;n_components = _infer_dimension(explained_variance_, n_samples)
538::COMM;;elif 0 < n_components < 1.0:
539::COMM;;# number of components for which the cumulated explained
540::COMM;;# variance percentage is superior to the desired threshold
541::COMM;;# side='right' ensures that number of features selected
542::COMM;;# their variance is always greater than n_components float
543::COMM;;# passed. More discussion in issue: #15669
544::COMM;;ratio_cumsum = xp.cumulative_sum(explained_variance_ratio_)
545::COMM;;n_components = (
546::COMM;;xp.searchsorted(

548::COMM;;xp.asarray(n_components, device=device(ratio_cumsum)),
549::COMM;;side="right",
550::COMM;;)

552::COMM;;)

554::COMM;;# The sigma2 maximum likelihood (cf. eq. 12.46)

556::COMM;;self.noise_variance_ = xp.mean(explained_variance_[n_components:])
557::COMM;;else:

560::COMM;;self.n_components_ = n_components
561::COMM;;# Assign a copy of the result of the truncation of the components in
562::COMM;;# order to:
563::COMM;;# - release the memory used by the discarded components,
564::COMM;;# - ensure that the kept components are allocated contiguously in

566::COMM;;# locality.

268::COMO;;# flip eigenvectors' sign to enforce deterministic output
279::COMM;;Finds the set of sparse components that can optimally reconstruct
280::COMM;;the data. The amount of sparseness is controllable by the coefficient
281::COMM;;of the L1 penalty, given by the parameter alpha.
282::COMM;;For an example comparing sparse PCA to PCA, see
283::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_decomposition_plot_faces_decomposition.py`
284::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <SparsePCA>`.
285::COMM;;Parameters
286::COMM;;----------
287::COMM;;n_components : int, default=None
288::COMM;;Number of sparse atoms to extract. If None, then ``n_components``
289::COMM;;is set to ``n_features``.
290::COMM;;alpha : int, default=1
291::COMM;;Sparsity controlling parameter. Higher values lead to sparser
292::COMM;;components.
293::COMM;;ridge_alpha : float, default=0.01
294::COMM;;Amount of ridge shrinkage to apply in order to improve
295::COMM;;conditioning when calling the transform method.
296::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=1_000
297::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations over the complete dataset before
298::COMM;;stopping independently of any early stopping criterion heuristics.
299::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
300::COMM;;callback : callable, default=None
301::COMM;;Callable that gets invoked every five iterations.
302::COMM;;batch_size : int, default=3
303::COMM;;The number of features to take in each mini batch.
304::COMM;;verbose : int or bool, default=False
305::COMM;;Controls the verbosity; the higher, the more messages. Defaults to 0.
306::COMM;;shuffle : bool, default=True
307::COMM;;Whether to shuffle the data before splitting it in batches.
308::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
309::COMM;;Number of parallel jobs to run.
310::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
311::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
312::COMM;;for more details.
313::COMM;;method : {'lars', 'cd'}, default='lars'
314::COMM;;Method to be used for optimization.
315::COMM;;lars: uses the least angle regression method to solve the lasso problem
316::COMM;;(linear_model.lars_path)
317::COMM;;cd: uses the coordinate descent method to compute the
318::COMM;;Lasso solution (linear_model.Lasso). Lars will be faster if
319::COMM;;the estimated components are sparse.
320::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
321::COMM;;Used for random shuffling when ``shuffle`` is set to ``True``,
322::COMM;;during online dictionary learning. Pass an int for reproducible results
323::COMM;;across multiple function calls.
324::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
325::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-3
326::COMM;;Control early stopping based on the norm of the differences in the
327::COMM;;dictionary between 2 steps.
328::COMM;;To disable early stopping based on changes in the dictionary, set
329::COMM;;`tol` to 0.0.
330::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
331::COMM;;max_no_improvement : int or None, default=10
332::COMM;;Control early stopping based on the consecutive number of mini batches
333::COMM;;that does not yield an improvement on the smoothed cost function.
334::COMM;;To disable convergence detection based on cost function, set
335::COMM;;`max_no_improvement` to `None`.
336::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.1
337::COMM;;Attributes
338::COMM;;----------
339::COMM;;components_ : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features)
340::COMM;;Sparse components extracted from the data.
341::COMM;;n_components_ : int
342::COMM;;Estimated number of components.
343::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.23
344::COMM;;n_iter_ : int
345::COMM;;Number of iterations run.
346::COMM;;mean_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
347::COMM;;Per-feature empirical mean, estimated from the training set.
348::COMM;;Equal to ``X.mean(axis=0)``.
349::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
350::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
351::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
352::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
353::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
354::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
355::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
356::COMM;;See Also
357::COMM;;--------
358::COMM;;DictionaryLearning : Find a dictionary that sparsely encodes data.
359::COMM;;IncrementalPCA : Incremental principal components analysis.
360::COMM;;PCA : Principal component analysis.
361::COMM;;SparsePCA : Sparse Principal Components Analysis.
362::COMM;;TruncatedSVD : Dimensionality reduction using truncated SVD.
363::COMM;;Examples
364::COMM;;--------
365::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
366::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import make_friedman1
367::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.decomposition import MiniBatchSparsePCA
368::COMM;;>>> X, _ = make_friedman1(n_samples=200, n_features=30, random_state=0)

370::COMM;;... max_iter=10, random_state=0)
371::COMM;;>>> transformer.fit(X)
372::COMM;;MiniBatchSparsePCA(...)
373::COMM;;>>> X_transformed = transformer.transform(X)
374::COMM;;>>> X_transformed.shape
375::COMM;;(200, 5)

377::COMM;;>>> np.mean(transformer.components_ == 0)

140::COMM;;class DiscriminantAnalysisPredictionMixin:
144::COMM;;Parameters
145::COMM;;----------
146::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
147::COMM;;Array of samples (test vectors).
148::COMM;;Returns
149::COMM;;-------
150::COMM;;y_scores : ndarray of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_classes)
151::COMM;;Decision function values related to each class, per sample.
152::COMM;;In the two-class case, the shape is `(n_samples,)`, giving the
153::COMM;;log likelihood ratio of the positive class.
161::COMM;;Returns the class label for each sample.
162::COMM;;Parameters
163::COMM;;----------
164::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
165::COMM;;Input vectors, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
166::COMM;;`n_features` is the number of features.
167::COMM;;Returns
168::COMM;;-------
169::COMM;;y_pred : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
170::COMM;;Class label for each sample.
176::COMM;;Parameters
177::COMM;;----------
178::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
179::COMM;;Input data.
180::COMM;;Returns
181::COMM;;-------
182::COMM;;y_proba : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
183::COMM;;Probability estimate of the sample for each class in the
184::COMM;;model, where classes are ordered as they are in `self.classes_`.
189::COMM;;Parameters
190::COMM;;----------
191::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
192::COMM;;Input data.
193::COMM;;Returns
194::COMM;;-------
195::COMM;;y_log_proba : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
196::COMM;;Estimated log probabilities.
210::COMM;;A classifier with a linear decision boundary, generated by fitting class
211::COMM;;conditional densities to the data and using Bayes' rule.
212::COMM;;The model fits a Gaussian density to each class, assuming that all classes
213::COMM;;share the same covariance matrix.
214::COMM;;The fitted model can also be used to reduce the dimensionality of the input
215::COMM;;by projecting it to the most discriminative directions, using the
216::COMM;;`transform` method.
217::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
218::COMM;;For a comparison between
219::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.discriminant_analysis.LinearDiscriminantAnalysis`
220::COMM;;and :class:`~sklearn.discriminant_analysis.QuadraticDiscriminantAnalysis`, see
221::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_classification_plot_lda_qda.py`.
222::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <lda_qda>`.
223::COMM;;Parameters
224::COMM;;----------
225::COMM;;solver : {'svd', 'lsqr', 'eigen'}, default='svd'
226::COMM;;Solver to use, possible values:
227::COMM;;- 'svd': Singular value decomposition (default).
228::COMM;;Does not compute the covariance matrix, therefore this solver is
229::COMM;;recommended for data with a large number of features.
230::COMM;;- 'lsqr': Least squares solution.
231::COMM;;Can be combined with shrinkage or custom covariance estimator.
232::COMM;;- 'eigen': Eigenvalue decomposition.
233::COMM;;Can be combined with shrinkage or custom covariance estimator.
234::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.2
235::COMM;;`solver="svd"` now has experimental Array API support. See the
236::COMM;;:ref:`Array API User Guide <array_api>` for more details.
237::COMM;;shrinkage : 'auto' or float, default=None
238::COMM;;Shrinkage parameter, possible values:
239::COMM;;- None: no shrinkage (default).
240::COMM;;- 'auto': automatic shrinkage using the Ledoit-Wolf lemma.
241::COMM;;- float between 0 and 1: fixed shrinkage parameter.
242::COMM;;This should be left to None if `covariance_estimator` is used.
243::COMM;;Note that shrinkage works only with 'lsqr' and 'eigen' solvers.
244::COMM;;For a usage example, see
245::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_classification_plot_lda.py`.
246::COMM;;priors : array-like of shape (n_classes,), default=None
247::COMM;;The class prior probabilities. By default, the class proportions are
248::COMM;;inferred from the training data.
249::COMM;;n_components : int, default=None
250::COMM;;Number of components (<= min(n_classes - 1, n_features)) for
251::COMM;;dimensionality reduction. If None, will be set to
252::COMM;;min(n_classes - 1, n_features). This parameter only affects the
253::COMM;;`transform` method.
254::COMM;;For a usage example, see
255::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_decomposition_plot_pca_vs_lda.py`.
256::COMM;;store_covariance : bool, default=False
257::COMM;;If True, explicitly compute the weighted within-class covariance
258::COMM;;matrix when solver is 'svd'. The matrix is always computed
259::COMM;;and stored for the other solvers.
260::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
261::COMM;;tol : float, default=1.0e-4
262::COMM;;Absolute threshold for a singular value of X to be considered
263::COMM;;significant, used to estimate the rank of X. Dimensions whose
264::COMM;;singular values are non-significant are discarded. Only used if
265::COMM;;solver is 'svd'.
266::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
267::COMM;;covariance_estimator : covariance estimator, default=None
268::COMM;;If not None, `covariance_estimator` is used to estimate
269::COMM;;the covariance matrices instead of relying on the empirical
270::COMM;;covariance estimator (with potential shrinkage).
271::COMM;;The object should have a fit method and a ``covariance_`` attribute
272::COMM;;like the estimators in :mod:`sklearn.covariance`.
273::COMM;;if None the shrinkage parameter drives the estimate.
274::COMM;;This should be left to None if `shrinkage` is used.
275::COMM;;Note that `covariance_estimator` works only with 'lsqr' and 'eigen'
276::COMM;;solvers.
277::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
278::COMM;;Attributes
279::COMM;;----------
280::COMM;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,) or (n_classes, n_features)
281::COMM;;Weight vector(s).
282::COMM;;intercept_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)
283::COMM;;Intercept term.
284::COMM;;covariance_ : array-like of shape (n_features, n_features)
285::COMM;;Weighted within-class covariance matrix. It corresponds to
286::COMM;;`sum_k prior_k * C_k` where `C_k` is the covariance matrix of the
287::COMM;;samples in class `k`. The `C_k` are estimated using the (potentially
288::COMM;;shrunk) biased estimator of covariance. If solver is 'svd', only
289::COMM;;exists when `store_covariance` is True.
290::COMM;;explained_variance_ratio_ : ndarray of shape (n_components,)
291::COMM;;Percentage of variance explained by each of the selected components.
292::COMM;;If ``n_components`` is not set then all components are stored and the
293::COMM;;sum of explained variances is equal to 1.0. Only available when eigen
294::COMM;;or svd solver is used.
295::COMM;;means_ : array-like of shape (n_classes, n_features)
296::COMM;;Class-wise means.
297::COMM;;priors_ : array-like of shape (n_classes,)
298::COMM;;Class priors (sum to 1).
299::COMM;;scalings_ : array-like of shape (rank, n_classes - 1)
300::COMM;;Scaling of the features in the space spanned by the class centroids.
301::COMM;;Only available for 'svd' and 'eigen' solvers.
302::COMM;;xbar_ : array-like of shape (n_features,)
303::COMM;;Overall mean. Only present if solver is 'svd'.
304::COMM;;classes_ : array-like of shape (n_classes,)
305::COMM;;Unique class labels.
306::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
307::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
308::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
309::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
310::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
311::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
312::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0

351::COMC;;self.store_covariance = store_covariance # used only in svd solver
352::COMC;;self.tol = tol # used only in svd solver
356::COMM;;The least squares solver computes a straightforward solution of the
357::COMM;;optimal decision rule based directly on the discriminant functions. It
358::COMM;;can only be used for classification (with any covariance estimator),
359::COMM;;because
360::COMM;;estimation of eigenvectors is not performed. Therefore, dimensionality
361::COMM;;reduction with the transform is not supported.
362::COMM;;Parameters
363::COMM;;----------
364::COMM;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
365::COMM;;Training data.
366::COMM;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_classes)
367::COMM;;Target values.
368::COMM;;shrinkage : 'auto', float or None
369::COMM;;Shrinkage parameter, possible values:
370::COMM;;- None: no shrinkage.
371::COMM;;- 'auto': automatic shrinkage using the Ledoit-Wolf lemma.
372::COMM;;- float between 0 and 1: fixed shrinkage parameter.
373::COMM;;Shrinkage parameter is ignored if `covariance_estimator` is
374::COMM;;not None
375::COMM;;covariance_estimator : estimator, default=None
376::COMM;;If not None, `covariance_estimator` is used to estimate
377::COMM;;the covariance matrices instead of relying the empirical
378::COMM;;covariance estimator (with potential shrinkage).
379::COMM;;The object should have a fit method and a ``covariance_`` attribute
380::COMM;;like the estimators in sklearn.covariance.
381::COMM;;if None the shrinkage parameter drives the estimate.
382::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
383::COMM;;Notes
384::COMM;;-----
385::COMM;;This solver is based on [1]_, section 2.6.2, pp. 39-41.
386::COMM;;References
387::COMM;;----------
388::COMM;;.. [1] R. O. Duda, P. E. Hart, D. G. Stork. Pattern Classification
389::COMM;;(Second Edition). John Wiley & Sons, Inc., New York, 2001. ISBN
390::COMM;;0-471-05669-3.
402::COMM;;The eigenvalue solver computes the optimal solution of the Rayleigh
403::COMM;;coefficient (basically the ratio of between class scatter to within
404::COMM;;class scatter). This solver supports both classification and
405::COMM;;dimensionality reduction (with any covariance estimator).
406::COMM;;Parameters
407::COMM;;----------
408::COMM;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
409::COMM;;Training data.
410::COMM;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_targets)
411::COMM;;Target values.
412::COMM;;shrinkage : 'auto', float or None
413::COMM;;Shrinkage parameter, possible values:
414::COMM;;- None: no shrinkage.
415::COMM;;- 'auto': automatic shrinkage using the Ledoit-Wolf lemma.
416::COMM;;- float between 0 and 1: fixed shrinkage constant.
417::COMM;;Shrinkage parameter is ignored if `covariance_estimator` is
418::COMM;;not None
419::COMM;;covariance_estimator : estimator, default=None
420::COMM;;If not None, `covariance_estimator` is used to estimate
421::COMM;;the covariance matrices instead of relying the empirical
422::COMM;;covariance estimator (with potential shrinkage).
423::COMM;;The object should have a fit method and a ``covariance_`` attribute
424::COMM;;like the estimators in sklearn.covariance.
425::COMM;;if None the shrinkage parameter drives the estimate.
426::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
427::COMM;;Notes
428::COMM;;-----
429::COMM;;This solver is based on [1]_, section 3.8.3, pp. 121-124.
430::COMM;;References
431::COMM;;----------
432::COMM;;.. [1] R. O. Duda, P. E. Hart, D. G. Stork. Pattern Classification
433::COMM;;(Second Edition). John Wiley & Sons, Inc., New York, 2001. ISBN
434::COMM;;0-471-05669-3.
440::COMC;;Sw = self.covariance_ # within scatter
441::COMC;;St = _cov(X, shrinkage, covariance_estimator) # total scatter
442::COMC;;Sb = St - Sw # between scatter
447::COMC;;evecs = evecs[:, np.argsort(evals)[::-1]] # sort eigenvectors
455::COMM;;Parameters
456::COMM;;----------
457::COMM;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
458::COMM;;Training data.
459::COMM;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_targets)
460::COMM;;Target values.
478::COMO;;# 1) within (univariate) scaling by with classes std-dev
480::COMO;;# avoid division by zero in normalization
483::COMO;;# 2) Within variance scaling

648::COMM;;Estimated log probabilities.
657::COMM;;The decision function is equal (up to a constant factor) to the
658::COMM;;log-posterior of the model, i.e. `log p(y = k | x)`. In a binary
659::COMM;;classification setting this instead corresponds to the difference
660::COMM;;`log p(y = 1 | x) - log p(y = 0 | x)`. See :ref:`lda_qda_math`.

665::COMM;;Returns

668::COMM;;Decision function values related to each class, per sample.
669::COMM;;In the two-class case, the shape is `(n_samples,)`, giving the
670::COMM;;log likelihood ratio of the positive class.
672::COMO;;# Only overrides for the docstring.
682::COMM;;A classifier with a quadratic decision boundary, generated
683::COMM;;by fitting class conditional densities to the data
684::COMM;;and using Bayes' rule.
685::COMM;;The model fits a Gaussian density to each class.
686::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
687::COMM;;For a comparison between
688::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.discriminant_analysis.QuadraticDiscriminantAnalysis`
689::COMM;;and :class:`~sklearn.discriminant_analysis.LinearDiscriminantAnalysis`, see
690::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_classification_plot_lda_qda.py`.
691::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <lda_qda>`.
692::COMM;;Parameters
693::COMM;;----------
694::COMM;;solver : {'svd', 'eigen'}, default='svd'
695::COMM;;Solver to use, possible values:
696::COMM;;- 'svd': Singular value decomposition (default).
697::COMM;;Does not compute the covariance matrix, therefore this solver is
698::COMM;;recommended for data with a large number of features.
699::COMM;;- 'eigen': Eigenvalue decomposition.
700::COMM;;Can be combined with shrinkage or custom covariance estimator.
701::COMM;;shrinkage : 'auto' or float, default=None
702::COMM;;Shrinkage parameter, possible values:
703::COMM;;- None: no shrinkage (default).
704::COMM;;- 'auto': automatic shrinkage using the Ledoit-Wolf lemma.
705::COMM;;- float between 0 and 1: fixed shrinkage parameter.
706::COMM;;Enabling shrinkage is expected to improve the model when some
707::COMM;;classes have a relatively small number of training data points
708::COMM;;compared to the number of features by mitigating overfitting during
709::COMM;;the covariance estimation step.
710::COMM;;This should be left to `None` if `covariance_estimator` is used.
711::COMM;;Note that shrinkage works only with 'eigen' solver.
712::COMM;;priors : array-like of shape (n_classes,), default=None
713::COMM;;Class priors. By default, the class proportions are inferred from the
714::COMM;;training data.
715::COMM;;reg_param : float, default=0.0
716::COMM;;Regularizes the per-class covariance estimates by transforming S2 as
717::COMM;;``S2 = (1 - reg_param) * S2 + reg_param * np.eye(n_features)``,
718::COMM;;where S2 corresponds to the `scaling_` attribute of a given class.
719::COMM;;store_covariance : bool, default=False
720::COMM;;If True, the class covariance matrices are explicitly computed and
721::COMM;;stored in the `self.covariance_` attribute.
722::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
723::COMM;;tol : float, default=1.0e-4
724::COMM;;Absolute threshold for the covariance matrix to be considered rank
725::COMM;;deficient after applying some regularization (see `reg_param`) to each
726::COMM;;`Sk` where `Sk` represents covariance matrix for k-th class. This
727::COMM;;parameter does not affect the predictions. It controls when a warning
728::COMM;;is raised if the covariance matrix is not full rank.
729::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
730::COMM;;covariance_estimator : covariance estimator, default=None
731::COMM;;If not None, `covariance_estimator` is used to estimate the covariance
732::COMM;;matrices instead of relying on the empirical covariance estimator
733::COMM;;(with potential shrinkage). The object should have a fit method and
734::COMM;;a ``covariance_`` attribute like the estimators in
735::COMM;;:mod:`sklearn.covariance`. If None the shrinkage parameter drives the
736::COMM;;estimate.
737::COMM;;This should be left to `None` if `shrinkage` is used.
738::COMM;;Note that `covariance_estimator` works only with the 'eigen' solver.
739::COMM;;Attributes
740::COMM;;----------
741::COMM;;covariance_ : list of len n_classes of ndarray \
742::COMM;;of shape (n_features, n_features)
743::COMM;;For each class, gives the covariance matrix estimated using the
744::COMM;;samples of that class. The estimations are unbiased. Only present if
745::COMM;;`store_covariance` is True.
746::COMM;;means_ : array-like of shape (n_classes, n_features)
747::COMM;;Class-wise means.
748::COMM;;priors_ : array-like of shape (n_classes,)
749::COMM;;Class priors (sum to 1).
750::COMM;;rotations_ : list of len n_classes of ndarray of shape (n_features, n_k)
751::COMM;;For each class k an array of shape (n_features, n_k), where
752::COMM;;``n_k = min(n_features, number of elements in class k)``
753::COMM;;It is the rotation of the Gaussian distribution, i.e. its
754::COMM;;principal axis. It corresponds to `V`, the matrix of eigenvectors
755::COMM;;coming from the SVD of `Xk = U S Vt` where `Xk` is the centered
756::COMM;;matrix of samples from class k.
757::COMM;;scalings_ : list of len n_classes of ndarray of shape (n_k,)
758::COMM;;For each class, contains the scaling of
759::COMM;;the Gaussian distributions along its principal axes, i.e. the
760::COMM;;variance in the rotated coordinate system. It corresponds to `S^2 /
761::COMM;;(n_samples - 1)`, where `S` is the diagonal matrix of singular values
762::COMM;;from the SVD of `Xk`, where `Xk` is the centered matrix of samples
763::COMM;;from class k.
764::COMM;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)
765::COMM;;Unique class labels.
766::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
767::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
768::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
769::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
770::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
771::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
