565::COMM;;@abstractmethod
566::COMM;;def _get_estimator(self):
575::COMM;;A Bagging classifier is an ensemble meta-estimator that fits base
576::COMM;;classifiers each on random subsets of the original dataset and then
577::COMM;;aggregate their individual predictions (either by voting or by averaging)
578::COMM;;to form a final prediction. Such a meta-estimator can typically be used as
579::COMM;;a way to reduce the variance of a black-box estimator (e.g., a decision
580::COMM;;tree), by introducing randomization into its construction procedure and
581::COMM;;then making an ensemble out of it.
582::COMM;;This algorithm encompasses several works from the literature. When random
583::COMM;;subsets of the dataset are drawn as random subsets of the samples, then
584::COMM;;this algorithm is known as Pasting [1]_. If samples are drawn with
585::COMM;;replacement, then the method is known as Bagging [2]_. When random subsets
586::COMM;;of the dataset are drawn as random subsets of the features, then the method
587::COMM;;is known as Random Subspaces [3]_. Finally, when base estimators are built
588::COMM;;on subsets of both samples and features, then the method is known as
589::COMM;;Random Patches [4]_.
590::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <bagging>`.
591::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.15
592::COMM;;Parameters
593::COMM;;----------
594::COMM;;estimator : object, default=None
595::COMM;;The base estimator to fit on random subsets of the dataset.
596::COMM;;If None, then the base estimator is a
597::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeClassifier`.
598::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
599::COMM;;`base_estimator` was renamed to `estimator`.
600::COMM;;n_estimators : int, default=10
601::COMM;;The number of base estimators in the ensemble.
602::COMM;;max_samples : int or float, default=1.0
603::COMM;;The number of samples to draw from X to train each base estimator (with
604::COMM;;replacement by default, see `bootstrap` for more details).
605::COMM;;- If int, then draw `max_samples` samples.
606::COMM;;- If float, then draw `max_samples * X.shape[0]` unweighted samples
607::COMM;;or `max_samples * sample_weight.sum()` weighted samples.
608::COMM;;max_features : int or float, default=1.0
609::COMM;;The number of features to draw from X to train each base estimator (
610::COMM;;without replacement by default, see `bootstrap_features` for more
611::COMM;;details).
612::COMM;;- If int, then draw `max_features` features.
613::COMM;;- If float, then draw `max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features.
614::COMM;;bootstrap : bool, default=True
615::COMM;;Whether samples are drawn with replacement. If False, sampling without
616::COMM;;replacement is performed. If fitting with `sample_weight`, it is
617::COMM;;strongly recommended to choose True, as only drawing with replacement
618::COMM;;will ensure the expected frequency semantics of `sample_weight`.
619::COMM;;bootstrap_features : bool, default=False
620::COMM;;Whether features are drawn with replacement.
621::COMM;;oob_score : bool, default=False
622::COMM;;Whether to use out-of-bag samples to estimate
623::COMM;;the generalization error. Only available if bootstrap=True.
624::COMM;;warm_start : bool, default=False
625::COMM;;When set to True, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit
626::COMM;;and add more estimators to the ensemble, otherwise, just fit
627::COMM;;a whole new ensemble. See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
628::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
629::COMM;;*warm_start* constructor parameter.
630::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
631::COMM;;The number of jobs to run in parallel for both :meth:`fit` and
632::COMM;;:meth:`predict`. ``None`` means 1 unless in a
633::COMM;;:obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context. ``-1`` means using all
634::COMM;;processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>` for more details.
635::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
636::COMM;;Controls the random resampling of the original dataset
637::COMM;;(sample wise and feature wise).
638::COMM;;If the base estimator accepts a `random_state` attribute, a different
639::COMM;;seed is generated for each instance in the ensemble.
640::COMM;;Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple function calls.
641::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
642::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
643::COMM;;Controls the verbosity when fitting and predicting.
644::COMM;;Attributes
645::COMM;;----------
646::COMM;;estimator_ : estimator
647::COMM;;The base estimator from which the ensemble is grown.
648::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
649::COMM;;`base_estimator_` was renamed to `estimator_`.
650::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
651::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
652::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
653::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
654::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
655::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
656::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
657::COMM;;estimators_ : list of estimators
658::COMM;;The collection of fitted base estimators.
659::COMM;;estimators_samples_ : list of arrays
660::COMM;;The subset of drawn samples (i.e., the in-bag samples) for each base
661::COMM;;estimator. Each subset is defined by an array of the indices selected.
662::COMM;;estimators_features_ : list of arrays
663::COMM;;The subset of drawn features for each base estimator.
664::COMM;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)
665::COMM;;The classes labels.
666::COMM;;n_classes_ : int or list
667::COMM;;The number of classes.
668::COMM;;oob_score_ : float
669::COMM;;Score of the training dataset obtained using an out-of-bag estimate.
670::COMM;;This attribute exists only when ``oob_score`` is True.
671::COMM;;oob_decision_function_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
672::COMM;;Decision function computed with out-of-bag estimate on the training
673::COMM;;set. If n_estimators is small it might be possible that a data point
674::COMM;;was never left out during the bootstrap. In this case,
675::COMM;;`oob_decision_function_` might contain NaN. This attribute exists
676::COMM;;only when ``oob_score`` is True.
677::COMM;;See Also
678::COMM;;--------
679::COMM;;BaggingRegressor : A Bagging regressor.
680::COMM;;References
681::COMM;;----------
682::COMM;;.. [1] L. Breiman, "Pasting small votes for classification in large
683::COMM;;databases and on-line", Machine Learning, 36(1), 85-103, 1999.
684::COMM;;.. [2] L. Breiman, "Bagging predictors", Machine Learning, 24(2), 123-140,
685::COMM;;1996.
686::COMM;;.. [3] T. Ho, "The random subspace method for constructing decision
687::COMM;;forests", Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 20(8), 832-844,
688::COMM;;1998.
689::COMM;;.. [4] G. Louppe and P. Geurts, "Ensembles on Random Patches", Machine
690::COMM;;Learning and Knowledge Discovery in Databases, 346-361, 2012.
691::COMM;;Examples
692::COMM;;--------
693::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.svm import SVC
694::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.ensemble import BaggingClassifier
695::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
696::COMM;;>>> X, y = make_classification(n_samples=100, n_features=4,
697::COMM;;... n_informative=2, n_redundant=0,
698::COMM;;... random_state=0, shuffle=False)
699::COMM;;>>> clf = BaggingClassifier(estimator=SVC(),
700::COMM;;... n_estimators=10, random_state=0).fit(X, y)
701::COMM;;>>> clf.predict([[0, 0, 0, 0]])
702::COMM;;array([1])
734::COMM;;if self.estimator is None:

737::COMM;;def _set_oob_score(self, X, y):
738::COMM;;n_samples = y.shape[0]
739::COMM;;n_classes_ = self.n_classes_
740::COMM;;predictions = np.zeros((n_samples, n_classes_))
741::COMM;;for estimator, samples, features in zip(
742::COMM;;self.estimators_, self.estimators_samples_, self.estimators_features_
743::COMM;;):
744::COMM;;# Create mask for OOB samples
745::COMM;;mask = ~indices_to_mask(samples, n_samples)
746::COMM;;if hasattr(estimator, "predict_proba"):
747::COMM;;predictions[mask, :] += estimator.predict_proba(
748::COMM;;(X[mask, :])[:, features]
749::COMM;;)
750::COMM;;else:
751::COMM;;p = estimator.predict((X[mask, :])[:, features])
752::COMM;;j = 0
753::COMM;;for i in range(n_samples):
754::COMM;;if mask[i]:
755::COMM;;predictions[i, p[j]] += 1
756::COMM;;j += 1
757::COMM;;if (predictions.sum(axis=1) == 0).any():
758::COMM;;warn(
759::COMM;;"Some inputs do not have OOB scores. "
760::COMM;;"This probably means too few estimators were used "
761::COMM;;"to compute any reliable oob estimates."
762::COMM;;)
763::COMM;;oob_decision_function = predictions / predictions.sum(axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]
764::COMM;;oob_score = accuracy_score(y, np.argmax(predictions, axis=1))
765::COMM;;self.oob_decision_function_ = oob_decision_function
766::COMM;;self.oob_score_ = oob_score

2::COMM;;Forest of trees-based ensemble methods.
3::COMM;;Those methods include random forests and extremely randomized trees.
4::COMM;;The module structure is the following:
5::COMM;;- The ``BaseForest`` base class implements a common ``fit`` method for all
6::COMM;;the estimators in the module. The ``fit`` method of the base ``Forest``
7::COMM;;class calls the ``fit`` method of each sub-estimator on random samples
8::COMM;;(with replacement, a.k.a. bootstrap) of the training set.
9::COMM;;The init of the sub-estimator is further delegated to the
10::COMM;;``BaseEnsemble`` constructor.
11::COMM;;- The ``ForestClassifier`` and ``ForestRegressor`` base classes further
12::COMM;;implement the prediction logic by computing an average of the predicted
13::COMM;;outcomes of the sub-estimators.
14::COMM;;- The ``RandomForestClassifier`` and ``RandomForestRegressor`` derived
15::COMM;;classes provide the user with concrete implementations of
16::COMM;;the forest ensemble method using classical, deterministic
17::COMM;;``DecisionTreeClassifier`` and ``DecisionTreeRegressor`` as
18::COMM;;sub-estimator implementations.
19::COMM;;- The ``ExtraTreesClassifier`` and ``ExtraTreesRegressor`` derived
20::COMM;;classes provide the user with concrete implementations of the
21::COMM;;forest ensemble method using the extremely randomized trees
22::COMM;;``ExtraTreeClassifier`` and ``ExtraTreeRegressor`` as
23::COMM;;sub-estimator implementations.
24::COMM;;Single and multi-output problems are both handled.
26::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers

787::COMM;;The class probability of a single tree is the fraction of samples of
788::COMM;;the same class in a leaf.
789::COMM;;Parameters

961::COMM;;Parameters

980::COMO;;# Note: we don't sum in parallel because the GIL isn't released in
981::COMO;;# the fast method.
985::COMO;;# Average over the forest
994::COMM;;A random forest classifier.
995::COMM;;A random forest is a meta estimator that fits a number of decision tree
996::COMM;;classifiers on various sub-samples of the dataset and uses averaging to
997::COMM;;improve the predictive accuracy and control over-fitting.
998::COMM;;Trees in the forest use the best split strategy, i.e. equivalent to passing
999::COMM;;`splitter="best"` to the underlying :class:`~sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeClassifier`.
1000::COMM;;The sub-sample size is controlled with the `max_samples` parameter if
1001::COMM;;`bootstrap=True` (default), otherwise the whole dataset is used to build
1002::COMM;;each tree.
1003::COMM;;For a comparison between tree-based ensemble models see the example
1004::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_ensemble_plot_forest_hist_grad_boosting_comparison.py`.
1005::COMM;;This estimator has native support for missing values (NaNs). During training,
1006::COMM;;the tree grower learns at each split point whether samples with missing values
1007::COMM;;should go to the left or right child, based on the potential gain. When predicting,
1008::COMM;;samples with missing values are assigned to the left or right child consequently.
1009::COMM;;If no missing values were encountered for a given feature during training, then
1010::COMM;;samples with missing values are mapped to whichever child has the most samples.
1011::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <forest>`.
1012::COMM;;Parameters
1013::COMM;;----------
1014::COMM;;n_estimators : int, default=100
1015::COMM;;The number of trees in the forest.
1016::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
1017::COMM;;The default value of ``n_estimators`` changed from 10 to 100
1018::COMM;;in 0.22.
1019::COMM;;criterion : {"gini", "entropy", "log_loss"}, default="gini"
1020::COMM;;The function to measure the quality of a split. Supported criteria are
1021::COMM;;"gini" for the Gini impurity and "log_loss" and "entropy" both for the
1022::COMM;;Shannon information gain, see :ref:`tree_mathematical_formulation`.
1023::COMM;;Note: This parameter is tree-specific.
1024::COMM;;max_depth : int, default=None
1025::COMM;;The maximum depth of the tree. If None, then nodes are expanded until
1026::COMM;;all leaves are pure or until all leaves contain less than
1027::COMM;;min_samples_split samples.
1028::COMM;;min_samples_split : int or float, default=2
1029::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to split an internal node:
1030::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_split` as the minimum number.
1031::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_split` is a fraction and
1032::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_split * n_samples)` are the minimum
1033::COMM;;number of samples for each split.
1034::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1035::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1036::COMM;;min_samples_leaf : int or float, default=1
1037::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node.
1038::COMM;;A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at
1039::COMM;;least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and
1040::COMM;;right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model,
1041::COMM;;especially in regression.
1042::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_leaf` as the minimum number.
1043::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_leaf` is a fraction and
1044::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_leaf * n_samples)` are the minimum
1045::COMM;;number of samples for each node.
1046::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1047::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1048::COMM;;min_weight_fraction_leaf : float, default=0.0
1049::COMM;;The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all
1050::COMM;;the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have
1051::COMM;;equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.
1052::COMM;;max_features : {"sqrt", "log2", None}, int or float, default="sqrt"
1053::COMM;;The number of features to consider when looking for the best split:
1054::COMM;;- If int, then consider `max_features` features at each split.
1055::COMM;;- If float, then `max_features` is a fraction and
1056::COMM;;`max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features are considered at each
1057::COMM;;split.
1058::COMM;;- If "sqrt", then `max_features=sqrt(n_features)`.
1059::COMM;;- If "log2", then `max_features=log2(n_features)`.
1060::COMM;;- If None, then `max_features=n_features`.
1061::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
1062::COMM;;The default of `max_features` changed from `"auto"` to `"sqrt"`.
1063::COMM;;Note: the search for a split does not stop until at least one
1064::COMM;;valid partition of the node samples is found, even if it requires to
1065::COMM;;effectively inspect more than ``max_features`` features.
1066::COMM;;max_leaf_nodes : int, default=None
1067::COMM;;Grow trees with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion.
1068::COMM;;Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity.
1069::COMM;;If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.
1070::COMM;;min_impurity_decrease : float, default=0.0
1071::COMM;;A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity
1072::COMM;;greater than or equal to this value.
1073::COMM;;The weighted impurity decrease equation is the following::
1074::COMM;;N_t / N * (impurity - N_t_R / N_t * right_impurity
1075::COMM;;- N_t_L / N_t * left_impurity)
1076::COMM;;where ``N`` is the total number of samples, ``N_t`` is the number of
1077::COMM;;samples at the current node, ``N_t_L`` is the number of samples in the
1078::COMM;;left child, and ``N_t_R`` is the number of samples in the right child.
1079::COMM;;``N``, ``N_t``, ``N_t_R`` and ``N_t_L`` all refer to the weighted sum,
1080::COMM;;if ``sample_weight`` is passed.
1081::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1082::COMM;;bootstrap : bool, default=True
1083::COMM;;Whether bootstrap samples are used when building trees. If False, the
1084::COMM;;whole dataset is used to build each tree.
1085::COMM;;oob_score : bool or callable, default=False
1086::COMM;;Whether to use out-of-bag samples to estimate the generalization score.
1087::COMM;;By default, :func:`~sklearn.metrics.accuracy_score` is used.
1088::COMM;;Provide a callable with signature `metric(y_true, y_pred)` to use a
1089::COMM;;custom metric. Only available if `bootstrap=True`.
1090::COMM;;For an illustration of out-of-bag (OOB) error estimation, see the example
1091::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_ensemble_plot_ensemble_oob.py`.
1092::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
1093::COMM;;The number of jobs to run in parallel. :meth:`fit`, :meth:`predict`,
1094::COMM;;:meth:`decision_path` and :meth:`apply` are all parallelized over the
1095::COMM;;trees. ``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend`
1096::COMM;;context. ``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary
1097::COMM;;<n_jobs>` for more details.
1098::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1099::COMM;;Controls both the randomness of the bootstrapping of the samples used
1100::COMM;;when building trees (if ``bootstrap=True``) and the sampling of the
1101::COMM;;features to consider when looking for the best split at each node
1102::COMM;;(if ``max_features < n_features``).
1103::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
1104::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
1105::COMM;;Controls the verbosity when fitting and predicting.
1106::COMM;;warm_start : bool, default=False
1107::COMM;;When set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit
1108::COMM;;and add more estimators to the ensemble, otherwise, just fit a whole
1109::COMM;;new forest. See :term:`Glossary <warm_start>` and
1110::COMM;;:ref:`tree_ensemble_warm_start` for details.
1111::COMM;;class_weight : {"balanced", "balanced_subsample"}, dict or list of dicts, \
1112::COMM;;default=None
1113::COMM;;Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
1114::COMM;;If not given, all classes are supposed to have weight one. For
1115::COMM;;multi-output problems, a list of dicts can be provided in the same
1116::COMM;;order as the columns of y.
1117::COMM;;Note that for multioutput (including multilabel) weights should be
1118::COMM;;defined for each class of every column in its own dict. For example,
1119::COMM;;for four-class multilabel classification weights should be
1120::COMM;;[{0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1, 1: 5}, {0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1, 1: 1}] instead of
1121::COMM;;[{1:1}, {2:5}, {3:1}, {4:1}].
1122::COMM;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
1123::COMM;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
1124::COMM;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``
1125::COMM;;The "balanced_subsample" mode is the same as "balanced" except that
1126::COMM;;weights are computed based on the bootstrap sample for every tree
1127::COMM;;grown.
1128::COMM;;For multi-output, the weights of each column of y will be multiplied.
1129::COMM;;Note that these weights will be multiplied with sample_weight (passed
1130::COMM;;through the fit method) if sample_weight is specified.
1131::COMM;;ccp_alpha : non-negative float, default=0.0
1132::COMM;;Complexity parameter used for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning. The
1133::COMM;;subtree with the largest cost complexity that is smaller than
1134::COMM;;``ccp_alpha`` will be chosen. By default, no pruning is performed. See
1135::COMM;;:ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details. See
1136::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_cost_complexity_pruning.py`
1137::COMM;;for an example of such pruning.
1138::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1139::COMM;;max_samples : int or float, default=None
1140::COMM;;If bootstrap is True, the number of samples to draw from X
1141::COMM;;to train each base estimator.
1142::COMM;;- If None (default), then draw `X.shape[0]` samples.
1143::COMM;;- If int, then draw `max_samples` samples.
1144::COMM;;- If float, then draw `max(round(n_samples * max_samples), 1)` samples. Thus,
1145::COMM;;`max_samples` should be in the interval `(0.0, 1.0]`.
1146::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1147::COMM;;monotonic_cst : array-like of int of shape (n_features), default=None
1148::COMM;;Indicates the monotonicity constraint to enforce on each feature.
1149::COMM;;- 1: monotonic increase
1150::COMM;;- 0: no constraint
1151::COMM;;- -1: monotonic decrease
1152::COMM;;If monotonic_cst is None, no constraints are applied.
1153::COMM;;Monotonicity constraints are not supported for:
1154::COMM;;- multiclass classifications (i.e. when `n_classes > 2`),
1155::COMM;;- multioutput classifications (i.e. when `n_outputs_ > 1`),
1156::COMM;;- classifications trained on data with missing values.
1157::COMM;;The constraints hold over the probability of the positive class.
1158::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <monotonic_cst_gbdt>`.
1159::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
1160::COMM;;Attributes
1161::COMM;;----------
1162::COMM;;estimator_ : :class:`~sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeClassifier`
1163::COMM;;The child estimator template used to create the collection of fitted
1164::COMM;;sub-estimators.
1165::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
1166::COMM;;`base_estimator_` was renamed to `estimator_`.
1167::COMM;;estimators_ : list of DecisionTreeClassifier
1168::COMM;;The collection of fitted sub-estimators.
1169::COMM;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,) or a list of such arrays
1170::COMM;;The classes labels (single output problem), or a list of arrays of
1171::COMM;;class labels (multi-output problem).
1172::COMM;;n_classes_ : int or list
1173::COMM;;The number of classes (single output problem), or a list containing the
1174::COMM;;number of classes for each output (multi-output problem).
1175::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
1176::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1177::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1178::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1179::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1180::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
1181::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1182::COMM;;n_outputs_ : int
1183::COMM;;The number of outputs when ``fit`` is performed.
1184::COMM;;feature_importances_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
1185::COMM;;The impurity-based feature importances.
1186::COMM;;The higher, the more important the feature.
1187::COMM;;The importance of a feature is computed as the (normalized)
1188::COMM;;total reduction of the criterion brought by that feature. It is also
1189::COMM;;known as the Gini importance.
1190::COMM;;Warning: impurity-based feature importances can be misleading for
1191::COMM;;high cardinality features (many unique values). See
1192::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance` as an alternative.
1193::COMM;;oob_score_ : float
1194::COMM;;Score of the training dataset obtained using an out-of-bag estimate.
1195::COMM;;This attribute exists only when ``oob_score`` is True.
1196::COMM;;oob_decision_function_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes) or \
1197::COMM;;(n_samples, n_classes, n_outputs)
1198::COMM;;Decision function computed with out-of-bag estimate on the training
1199::COMM;;set. If n_estimators is small it might be possible that a data point
1200::COMM;;was never left out during the bootstrap. In this case,
1201::COMM;;`oob_decision_function_` might contain NaN. This attribute exists
1202::COMM;;only when ``oob_score`` is True.
1203::COMM;;estimators_samples_ : list of arrays
1204::COMM;;The subset of drawn samples (i.e., the in-bag samples) for each base
1205::COMM;;estimator. Each subset is defined by an array of the indices selected.
1206::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
1207::COMM;;See Also
1208::COMM;;--------
1209::COMM;;sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeClassifier : A decision tree classifier.
1210::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier : Ensemble of extremely randomized
1211::COMM;;tree classifiers.
1212::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.HistGradientBoostingClassifier : A Histogram-based Gradient
1213::COMM;;Boosting Classification Tree, very fast for big datasets (n_samples >=
1214::COMM;;10_000).
1215::COMM;;Notes
1216::COMM;;-----
1217::COMM;;The default values for the parameters controlling the size of the trees
1218::COMM;;(e.g. ``max_depth``, ``min_samples_leaf``, etc.) lead to fully grown and
1219::COMM;;unpruned trees which can potentially be very large on some data sets. To
1220::COMM;;reduce memory consumption, the complexity and size of the trees should be
1221::COMM;;controlled by setting those parameter values.
1222::COMM;;The features are always randomly permuted at each split. Therefore,
1223::COMM;;the best found split may vary, even with the same training data,
1224::COMM;;``max_features=n_features`` and ``bootstrap=False``, if the improvement
1225::COMM;;of the criterion is identical for several splits enumerated during the
1226::COMM;;search of the best split. To obtain a deterministic behaviour during
1227::COMM;;fitting, ``random_state`` has to be fixed.
1228::COMM;;References
1229::COMM;;----------
1230::COMM;;.. [1] :doi:`L. Breiman, "Random Forests", Machine Learning, 45(1), 5-32, 2001.
1231::COMM;;<10.1023/A:1010933404324>`
1232::COMM;;Examples
1233::COMM;;--------
1234::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
1235::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
1236::COMM;;>>> X, y = make_classification(n_samples=1000, n_features=4,
1237::COMM;;... n_informative=2, n_redundant=0,
1238::COMM;;... random_state=0, shuffle=False)
1239::COMM;;>>> clf = RandomForestClassifier(max_depth=2, random_state=0)
1240::COMM;;>>> clf.fit(X, y)
1241::COMM;;RandomForestClassifier(...)
1242::COMM;;>>> print(clf.predict([[0, 0, 0, 0]]))
1243::COMM;;[1]
1316::COMM;;A random forest regressor.
1317::COMM;;A random forest is a meta estimator that fits a number of decision tree
1318::COMM;;regressors on various sub-samples of the dataset and uses averaging to
1319::COMM;;improve the predictive accuracy and control over-fitting.
1320::COMM;;Trees in the forest use the best split strategy, i.e. equivalent to passing
1321::COMM;;`splitter="best"` to the underlying :class:`~sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeRegressor`.
1322::COMM;;The sub-sample size is controlled with the `max_samples` parameter if
1323::COMM;;`bootstrap=True` (default), otherwise the whole dataset is used to build
1324::COMM;;each tree.
1325::COMM;;This estimator has native support for missing values (NaNs). During training,
1326::COMM;;the tree grower learns at each split point whether samples with missing values
1327::COMM;;should go to the left or right child, based on the potential gain. When predicting,
1328::COMM;;samples with missing values are assigned to the left or right child consequently.
1329::COMM;;If no missing values were encountered for a given feature during training, then
1330::COMM;;samples with missing values are mapped to whichever child has the most samples.
1331::COMM;;For a comparison between tree-based ensemble models see the example
1332::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_ensemble_plot_forest_hist_grad_boosting_comparison.py`.
1333::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <forest>`.
1334::COMM;;Parameters
1335::COMM;;----------
1336::COMM;;n_estimators : int, default=100
1337::COMM;;The number of trees in the forest.
1338::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
1339::COMM;;The default value of ``n_estimators`` changed from 10 to 100
1340::COMM;;in 0.22.
1341::COMM;;criterion : {"squared_error", "absolute_error", "friedman_mse", "poisson"}, \
1342::COMM;;default="squared_error"
1343::COMM;;The function to measure the quality of a split. Supported criteria
1344::COMM;;are "squared_error" for the mean squared error, which is equal to
1345::COMM;;variance reduction as feature selection criterion and minimizes the L2
1346::COMM;;loss using the mean of each terminal node, "friedman_mse", which uses
1347::COMM;;mean squared error with Friedman's improvement score for potential
1348::COMM;;splits, "absolute_error" for the mean absolute error, which minimizes
1349::COMM;;the L1 loss using the median of each terminal node, and "poisson" which
1350::COMM;;uses reduction in Poisson deviance to find splits.
1351::COMM;;Training using "absolute_error" is significantly slower
1352::COMM;;than when using "squared_error".
1353::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.18
1354::COMM;;Mean Absolute Error (MAE) criterion.
1355::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1356::COMM;;Poisson criterion.
1357::COMM;;max_depth : int, default=None
1358::COMM;;The maximum depth of the tree. If None, then nodes are expanded until
1359::COMM;;all leaves are pure or until all leaves contain less than
1360::COMM;;min_samples_split samples.
1361::COMM;;min_samples_split : int or float, default=2
1362::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to split an internal node:
1363::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_split` as the minimum number.
1364::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_split` is a fraction and
1365::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_split * n_samples)` are the minimum
1366::COMM;;number of samples for each split.
1367::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1368::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1369::COMM;;min_samples_leaf : int or float, default=1
1370::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node.
1371::COMM;;A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at
1372::COMM;;least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and
1373::COMM;;right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model,
1374::COMM;;especially in regression.
1375::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_leaf` as the minimum number.
1376::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_leaf` is a fraction and
1377::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_leaf * n_samples)` are the minimum
1378::COMM;;number of samples for each node.
1379::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1380::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1381::COMM;;min_weight_fraction_leaf : float, default=0.0
1382::COMM;;The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all
1383::COMM;;the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have
1384::COMM;;equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.
1385::COMM;;max_features : {"sqrt", "log2", None}, int or float, default=1.0
1386::COMM;;The number of features to consider when looking for the best split:
1387::COMM;;- If int, then consider `max_features` features at each split.
1388::COMM;;- If float, then `max_features` is a fraction and
1389::COMM;;`max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features are considered at each
1390::COMM;;split.
1391::COMM;;- If "sqrt", then `max_features=sqrt(n_features)`.
1392::COMM;;- If "log2", then `max_features=log2(n_features)`.
1393::COMM;;- If None or 1.0, then `max_features=n_features`.
1394::COMM;;.. note::
1395::COMM;;The default of 1.0 is equivalent to bagged trees and more
1396::COMM;;randomness can be achieved by setting smaller values, e.g. 0.3.
1397::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
1398::COMM;;The default of `max_features` changed from `"auto"` to 1.0.
1399::COMM;;Note: the search for a split does not stop until at least one
1400::COMM;;valid partition of the node samples is found, even if it requires to
1401::COMM;;effectively inspect more than ``max_features`` features.
1402::COMM;;max_leaf_nodes : int, default=None
1403::COMM;;Grow trees with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion.
1404::COMM;;Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity.
1405::COMM;;If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.
1406::COMM;;min_impurity_decrease : float, default=0.0
1407::COMM;;A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity
1408::COMM;;greater than or equal to this value.
1409::COMM;;The weighted impurity decrease equation is the following::
1410::COMM;;N_t / N * (impurity - N_t_R / N_t * right_impurity
1411::COMM;;- N_t_L / N_t * left_impurity)
1412::COMM;;where ``N`` is the total number of samples, ``N_t`` is the number of
1413::COMM;;samples at the current node, ``N_t_L`` is the number of samples in the
1414::COMM;;left child, and ``N_t_R`` is the number of samples in the right child.
1415::COMM;;``N``, ``N_t``, ``N_t_R`` and ``N_t_L`` all refer to the weighted sum,
1416::COMM;;if ``sample_weight`` is passed.
1417::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1418::COMM;;bootstrap : bool, default=True
1419::COMM;;Whether bootstrap samples are used when building trees. If False, the
1420::COMM;;whole dataset is used to build each tree.
1421::COMM;;oob_score : bool or callable, default=False
1422::COMM;;Whether to use out-of-bag samples to estimate the generalization score.
1423::COMM;;By default, :func:`~sklearn.metrics.r2_score` is used.
1424::COMM;;Provide a callable with signature `metric(y_true, y_pred)` to use a
1425::COMM;;custom metric. Only available if `bootstrap=True`.
1426::COMM;;For an illustration of out-of-bag (OOB) error estimation, see the example
1427::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_ensemble_plot_ensemble_oob.py`.
1428::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
1429::COMM;;The number of jobs to run in parallel. :meth:`fit`, :meth:`predict`,
1430::COMM;;:meth:`decision_path` and :meth:`apply` are all parallelized over the
1431::COMM;;trees. ``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend`
1432::COMM;;context. ``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary
1433::COMM;;<n_jobs>` for more details.
1434::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1435::COMM;;Controls both the randomness of the bootstrapping of the samples used
1436::COMM;;when building trees (if ``bootstrap=True``) and the sampling of the
1437::COMM;;features to consider when looking for the best split at each node
1438::COMM;;(if ``max_features < n_features``).
1439::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
1440::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
1441::COMM;;Controls the verbosity when fitting and predicting.
1442::COMM;;warm_start : bool, default=False
1443::COMM;;When set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit
1444::COMM;;and add more estimators to the ensemble, otherwise, just fit a whole
1445::COMM;;new forest. See :term:`Glossary <warm_start>` and
1446::COMM;;:ref:`tree_ensemble_warm_start` for details.
1447::COMM;;ccp_alpha : non-negative float, default=0.0
1448::COMM;;Complexity parameter used for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning. The
1449::COMM;;subtree with the largest cost complexity that is smaller than
1450::COMM;;``ccp_alpha`` will be chosen. By default, no pruning is performed. See
1451::COMM;;:ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details. See
1452::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_cost_complexity_pruning.py`
1453::COMM;;for an example of such pruning.
1454::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1455::COMM;;max_samples : int or float, default=None
1456::COMM;;If bootstrap is True, the number of samples to draw from X
1457::COMM;;to train each base estimator.
1458::COMM;;- If None (default), then draw `X.shape[0]` samples.
1459::COMM;;- If int, then draw `max_samples` samples.
1460::COMM;;- If float, then draw `max(round(n_samples * max_samples), 1)` samples. Thus,
1461::COMM;;`max_samples` should be in the interval `(0.0, 1.0]`.
1462::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1463::COMM;;monotonic_cst : array-like of int of shape (n_features), default=None
1464::COMM;;Indicates the monotonicity constraint to enforce on each feature.
1465::COMM;;- 1: monotonically increasing
1466::COMM;;- 0: no constraint
1467::COMM;;- -1: monotonically decreasing
1468::COMM;;If monotonic_cst is None, no constraints are applied.
1469::COMM;;Monotonicity constraints are not supported for:
1470::COMM;;- multioutput regressions (i.e. when `n_outputs_ > 1`),
1471::COMM;;- regressions trained on data with missing values.
1472::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <monotonic_cst_gbdt>`.
1473::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
1474::COMM;;Attributes
1475::COMM;;----------
1476::COMM;;estimator_ : :class:`~sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeRegressor`
1477::COMM;;The child estimator template used to create the collection of fitted
1478::COMM;;sub-estimators.
1479::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
1480::COMM;;`base_estimator_` was renamed to `estimator_`.
1481::COMM;;estimators_ : list of DecisionTreeRegressor
1482::COMM;;The collection of fitted sub-estimators.
1483::COMM;;feature_importances_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
1484::COMM;;The impurity-based feature importances.
1485::COMM;;The higher, the more important the feature.
1486::COMM;;The importance of a feature is computed as the (normalized)
1487::COMM;;total reduction of the criterion brought by that feature. It is also
1488::COMM;;known as the Gini importance.
1489::COMM;;Warning: impurity-based feature importances can be misleading for
1490::COMM;;high cardinality features (many unique values). See
1491::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance` as an alternative.
1492::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
1493::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1494::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1495::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1496::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1497::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
1498::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1499::COMM;;n_outputs_ : int
1500::COMM;;The number of outputs when ``fit`` is performed.
1501::COMM;;oob_score_ : float
1502::COMM;;Score of the training dataset obtained using an out-of-bag estimate.
1503::COMM;;This attribute exists only when ``oob_score`` is True.
1504::COMM;;oob_prediction_ : ndarray of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs)
1505::COMM;;Prediction computed with out-of-bag estimate on the training set.
1506::COMM;;This attribute exists only when ``oob_score`` is True.
1507::COMM;;estimators_samples_ : list of arrays
1508::COMM;;The subset of drawn samples (i.e., the in-bag samples) for each base
1509::COMM;;estimator. Each subset is defined by an array of the indices selected.
1510::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4

1513::COMM;;sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeRegressor : A decision tree regressor.
1514::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor : Ensemble of extremely randomized
1515::COMM;;tree regressors.
1516::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.HistGradientBoostingRegressor : A Histogram-based Gradient
1517::COMM;;Boosting Regression Tree, very fast for big datasets (n_samples >=
1518::COMM;;10_000).
1519::COMM;;Notes
1520::COMM;;-----
1521::COMM;;The default values for the parameters controlling the size of the trees
1522::COMM;;(e.g. ``max_depth``, ``min_samples_leaf``, etc.) lead to fully grown and
1523::COMM;;unpruned trees which can potentially be very large on some data sets. To
1524::COMM;;reduce memory consumption, the complexity and size of the trees should be
1525::COMM;;controlled by setting those parameter values.
1526::COMM;;The features are always randomly permuted at each split. Therefore,
1527::COMM;;the best found split may vary, even with the same training data,
1528::COMM;;``max_features=n_features`` and ``bootstrap=False``, if the improvement
1529::COMM;;of the criterion is identical for several splits enumerated during the
1530::COMM;;search of the best split. To obtain a deterministic behaviour during
1531::COMM;;fitting, ``random_state`` has to be fixed.
1532::COMM;;The default value ``max_features=1.0`` uses ``n_features``
1533::COMM;;rather than ``n_features / 3``. The latter was originally suggested in
1534::COMM;;[1]_, whereas the former was more recently justified empirically in [2]_.
1535::COMM;;References
1536::COMM;;----------
1537::COMM;;.. [1] :doi:`L. Breiman, "Random Forests", Machine Learning, 45(1), 5-32, 2001.
1538::COMM;;<10.1023/A:1010933404324>`
1539::COMM;;.. [2] P. Geurts, D. Ernst., and L. Wehenkel, "Extremely randomized
1540::COMM;;trees", Machine Learning, 63(1), 3-42, 2006.
1541::COMM;;Examples
1542::COMM;;--------
1543::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
1544::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import make_regression
1545::COMM;;>>> X, y = make_regression(n_features=4, n_informative=2,
1546::COMM;;... random_state=0, shuffle=False)
1547::COMM;;>>> regr = RandomForestRegressor(max_depth=2, random_state=0)
1548::COMM;;>>> regr.fit(X, y)
1549::COMM;;RandomForestRegressor(...)
1550::COMM;;>>> print(regr.predict([[0, 0, 0, 0]]))
1551::COMM;;[-8.32987858]
1616::COMM;;An extra-trees classifier.
1617::COMM;;This class implements a meta estimator that fits a number of
1618::COMM;;randomized decision trees (a.k.a. extra-trees) on various sub-samples
1619::COMM;;of the dataset and uses averaging to improve the predictive accuracy
1620::COMM;;and control over-fitting.
1621::COMM;;This estimator has native support for missing values (NaNs) for
1622::COMM;;random splits. During training, a random threshold will be chosen
1623::COMM;;to split the non-missing values on. Then the non-missing values will be sent
1624::COMM;;to the left and right child based on the randomly selected threshold, while
1625::COMM;;the missing values will also be randomly sent to the left or right child.
1626::COMM;;This is repeated for every feature considered at each split. The best split
1627::COMM;;among these is chosen.
1628::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <forest>`.
1629::COMM;;Parameters
1630::COMM;;----------
1631::COMM;;n_estimators : int, default=100
1632::COMM;;The number of trees in the forest.
1633::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
1634::COMM;;The default value of ``n_estimators`` changed from 10 to 100
1635::COMM;;in 0.22.
1636::COMM;;criterion : {"gini", "entropy", "log_loss"}, default="gini"
1637::COMM;;The function to measure the quality of a split. Supported criteria are
1638::COMM;;"gini" for the Gini impurity and "log_loss" and "entropy" both for the
1639::COMM;;Shannon information gain, see :ref:`tree_mathematical_formulation`.
1640::COMM;;Note: This parameter is tree-specific.
1641::COMM;;max_depth : int, default=None
1642::COMM;;The maximum depth of the tree. If None, then nodes are expanded until
1643::COMM;;all leaves are pure or until all leaves contain less than
1644::COMM;;min_samples_split samples.
1645::COMM;;min_samples_split : int or float, default=2
1646::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to split an internal node:
1647::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_split` as the minimum number.
1648::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_split` is a fraction and
1649::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_split * n_samples)` are the minimum
1650::COMM;;number of samples for each split.
1651::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1652::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1653::COMM;;min_samples_leaf : int or float, default=1
1654::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node.
1655::COMM;;A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at
1656::COMM;;least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and
1657::COMM;;right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model,
1658::COMM;;especially in regression.
1659::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_leaf` as the minimum number.
1660::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_leaf` is a fraction and
1661::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_leaf * n_samples)` are the minimum
1662::COMM;;number of samples for each node.
1663::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1664::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1665::COMM;;min_weight_fraction_leaf : float, default=0.0
1666::COMM;;The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all
1667::COMM;;the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have
1668::COMM;;equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.
1669::COMM;;max_features : {"sqrt", "log2", None}, int or float, default="sqrt"
1670::COMM;;The number of features to consider when looking for the best split:
1671::COMM;;- If int, then consider `max_features` features at each split.
1672::COMM;;- If float, then `max_features` is a fraction and
1673::COMM;;`max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features are considered at each
1674::COMM;;split.
1675::COMM;;- If "sqrt", then `max_features=sqrt(n_features)`.
1676::COMM;;- If "log2", then `max_features=log2(n_features)`.
1677::COMM;;- If None, then `max_features=n_features`.
1678::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
1679::COMM;;The default of `max_features` changed from `"auto"` to `"sqrt"`.
1680::COMM;;Note: the search for a split does not stop until at least one
1681::COMM;;valid partition of the node samples is found, even if it requires to
1682::COMM;;effectively inspect more than ``max_features`` features.
1683::COMM;;max_leaf_nodes : int, default=None
1684::COMM;;Grow trees with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion.
1685::COMM;;Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity.
1686::COMM;;If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.
1687::COMM;;min_impurity_decrease : float, default=0.0
1688::COMM;;A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity
1689::COMM;;greater than or equal to this value.
1690::COMM;;The weighted impurity decrease equation is the following::
1691::COMM;;N_t / N * (impurity - N_t_R / N_t * right_impurity
1692::COMM;;- N_t_L / N_t * left_impurity)
1693::COMM;;where ``N`` is the total number of samples, ``N_t`` is the number of
1694::COMM;;samples at the current node, ``N_t_L`` is the number of samples in the
1695::COMM;;left child, and ``N_t_R`` is the number of samples in the right child.
1696::COMM;;``N``, ``N_t``, ``N_t_R`` and ``N_t_L`` all refer to the weighted sum,
1697::COMM;;if ``sample_weight`` is passed.
1698::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1699::COMM;;bootstrap : bool, default=False
1700::COMM;;Whether bootstrap samples are used when building trees. If False, the
1701::COMM;;whole dataset is used to build each tree.
1702::COMM;;oob_score : bool or callable, default=False
1703::COMM;;Whether to use out-of-bag samples to estimate the generalization score.
1704::COMM;;By default, :func:`~sklearn.metrics.accuracy_score` is used.
1705::COMM;;Provide a callable with signature `metric(y_true, y_pred)` to use a
1706::COMM;;custom metric. Only available if `bootstrap=True`.
1707::COMM;;For an illustration of out-of-bag (OOB) error estimation, see the example
1708::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_ensemble_plot_ensemble_oob.py`.
1709::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
1710::COMM;;The number of jobs to run in parallel. :meth:`fit`, :meth:`predict`,
1711::COMM;;:meth:`decision_path` and :meth:`apply` are all parallelized over the
1712::COMM;;trees. ``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend`
1713::COMM;;context. ``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary
1714::COMM;;<n_jobs>` for more details.
1715::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1716::COMM;;Controls 3 sources of randomness:
1717::COMM;;- the bootstrapping of the samples used when building trees
1718::COMM;;(if ``bootstrap=True``)
1719::COMM;;- the sampling of the features to consider when looking for the best
1720::COMM;;split at each node (if ``max_features < n_features``)
1721::COMM;;- the draw of the splits for each of the `max_features`
1722::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
1723::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
1724::COMM;;Controls the verbosity when fitting and predicting.
1725::COMM;;warm_start : bool, default=False
1726::COMM;;When set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit
1727::COMM;;and add more estimators to the ensemble, otherwise, just fit a whole
1728::COMM;;new forest. See :term:`Glossary <warm_start>` and
1729::COMM;;:ref:`tree_ensemble_warm_start` for details.
1730::COMM;;class_weight : {"balanced", "balanced_subsample"}, dict or list of dicts, \
1731::COMM;;default=None
1732::COMM;;Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
1733::COMM;;If not given, all classes are supposed to have weight one. For
1734::COMM;;multi-output problems, a list of dicts can be provided in the same
1735::COMM;;order as the columns of y.
1736::COMM;;Note that for multioutput (including multilabel) weights should be
1737::COMM;;defined for each class of every column in its own dict. For example,
1738::COMM;;for four-class multilabel classification weights should be
1739::COMM;;[{0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1, 1: 5}, {0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1, 1: 1}] instead of
1740::COMM;;[{1:1}, {2:5}, {3:1}, {4:1}].
1741::COMM;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
1742::COMM;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
1743::COMM;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``
1744::COMM;;The "balanced_subsample" mode is the same as "balanced" except that
1745::COMM;;weights are computed based on the bootstrap sample for every tree
1746::COMM;;grown.
1747::COMM;;For multi-output, the weights of each column of y will be multiplied.
1748::COMM;;Note that these weights will be multiplied with sample_weight (passed
1749::COMM;;through the fit method) if sample_weight is specified.
1750::COMM;;ccp_alpha : non-negative float, default=0.0
1751::COMM;;Complexity parameter used for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning. The
1752::COMM;;subtree with the largest cost complexity that is smaller than
1753::COMM;;``ccp_alpha`` will be chosen. By default, no pruning is performed. See
1754::COMM;;:ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details. See
1755::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_cost_complexity_pruning.py`
1756::COMM;;for an example of such pruning.
1757::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1758::COMM;;max_samples : int or float, default=None
1759::COMM;;If bootstrap is True, the number of samples to draw from X
1760::COMM;;to train each base estimator.
1761::COMM;;- If None (default), then draw `X.shape[0]` samples.
1762::COMM;;- If int, then draw `max_samples` samples.
1763::COMM;;- If float, then draw `max_samples * X.shape[0]` samples. Thus,
1764::COMM;;`max_samples` should be in the interval `(0.0, 1.0]`.
1765::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1766::COMM;;monotonic_cst : array-like of int of shape (n_features), default=None
1767::COMM;;Indicates the monotonicity constraint to enforce on each feature.
1768::COMM;;- 1: monotonically increasing
1769::COMM;;- 0: no constraint
1770::COMM;;- -1: monotonically decreasing
1771::COMM;;If monotonic_cst is None, no constraints are applied.
1772::COMM;;Monotonicity constraints are not supported for:
1773::COMM;;- multiclass classifications (i.e. when `n_classes > 2`),
1774::COMM;;- multioutput classifications (i.e. when `n_outputs_ > 1`),
1775::COMM;;- classifications trained on data with missing values.
1776::COMM;;The constraints hold over the probability of the positive class.
1777::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <monotonic_cst_gbdt>`.
1778::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4

1799::COMM;;known as the Gini importance.
1800::COMM;;Warning: impurity-based feature importances can be misleading for

1843::COMM;;--------
1844::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.ensemble import ExtraTreesClassifier
1845::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
1846::COMM;;>>> X, y = make_classification(n_features=4, random_state=0)
1847::COMM;;>>> clf = ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=0)

1851::COMM;;array([1])
1924::COMM;;An extra-trees regressor.
1925::COMM;;This class implements a meta estimator that fits a number of
1926::COMM;;randomized decision trees (a.k.a. extra-trees) on various sub-samples
1927::COMM;;of the dataset and uses averaging to improve the predictive accuracy
1928::COMM;;and control over-fitting.
1929::COMM;;This estimator has native support for missing values (NaNs) for
1930::COMM;;random splits. During training, a random threshold will be chosen
1931::COMM;;to split the non-missing values on. Then the non-missing values will be sent
1932::COMM;;to the left and right child based on the randomly selected threshold, while
1933::COMM;;the missing values will also be randomly sent to the left or right child.
1934::COMM;;This is repeated for every feature considered at each split. The best split
1935::COMM;;among these is chosen.
1936::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <forest>`.
1937::COMM;;Parameters
1938::COMM;;----------
1939::COMM;;n_estimators : int, default=100
1940::COMM;;The number of trees in the forest.
1941::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
1942::COMM;;The default value of ``n_estimators`` changed from 10 to 100
1943::COMM;;in 0.22.
1944::COMM;;criterion : {"squared_error", "absolute_error", "friedman_mse", "poisson"}, \
1945::COMM;;default="squared_error"
1946::COMM;;The function to measure the quality of a split. Supported criteria
1947::COMM;;are "squared_error" for the mean squared error, which is equal to
1948::COMM;;variance reduction as feature selection criterion and minimizes the L2
1949::COMM;;loss using the mean of each terminal node, "friedman_mse", which uses
1950::COMM;;mean squared error with Friedman's improvement score for potential
1951::COMM;;splits, "absolute_error" for the mean absolute error, which minimizes
1952::COMM;;the L1 loss using the median of each terminal node, and "poisson" which
1953::COMM;;uses reduction in Poisson deviance to find splits.
1954::COMM;;Training using "absolute_error" is significantly slower
1955::COMM;;than when using "squared_error".
1956::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.18
1957::COMM;;Mean Absolute Error (MAE) criterion.
1958::COMM;;max_depth : int, default=None
1959::COMM;;The maximum depth of the tree. If None, then nodes are expanded until
1960::COMM;;all leaves are pure or until all leaves contain less than
1961::COMM;;min_samples_split samples.
1962::COMM;;min_samples_split : int or float, default=2
1963::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to split an internal node:
1964::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_split` as the minimum number.
1965::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_split` is a fraction and
1966::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_split * n_samples)` are the minimum
1967::COMM;;number of samples for each split.
1968::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1969::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1970::COMM;;min_samples_leaf : int or float, default=1
1971::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node.
1972::COMM;;A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at
1973::COMM;;least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and
1974::COMM;;right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model,
1975::COMM;;especially in regression.
1976::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_leaf` as the minimum number.
1977::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_leaf` is a fraction and
1978::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_leaf * n_samples)` are the minimum
1979::COMM;;number of samples for each node.
1980::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1981::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1982::COMM;;min_weight_fraction_leaf : float, default=0.0
1983::COMM;;The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all
1984::COMM;;the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have
1985::COMM;;equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.
1986::COMM;;max_features : {"sqrt", "log2", None}, int or float, default=1.0
1987::COMM;;The number of features to consider when looking for the best split:
1988::COMM;;- If int, then consider `max_features` features at each split.
1989::COMM;;- If float, then `max_features` is a fraction and
1990::COMM;;`max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features are considered at each
1991::COMM;;split.
1992::COMM;;- If "sqrt", then `max_features=sqrt(n_features)`.
1993::COMM;;- If "log2", then `max_features=log2(n_features)`.
1994::COMM;;- If None or 1.0, then `max_features=n_features`.
1995::COMM;;.. note::
1996::COMM;;The default of 1.0 is equivalent to bagged trees and more
1997::COMM;;randomness can be achieved by setting smaller values, e.g. 0.3.
1998::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
1999::COMM;;The default of `max_features` changed from `"auto"` to 1.0.
2000::COMM;;Note: the search for a split does not stop until at least one
2001::COMM;;valid partition of the node samples is found, even if it requires to
2002::COMM;;effectively inspect more than ``max_features`` features.
2003::COMM;;max_leaf_nodes : int, default=None
2004::COMM;;Grow trees with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion.
2005::COMM;;Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity.
2006::COMM;;If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.
2007::COMM;;min_impurity_decrease : float, default=0.0
2008::COMM;;A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity
2009::COMM;;greater than or equal to this value.
2010::COMM;;The weighted impurity decrease equation is the following::
2011::COMM;;N_t / N * (impurity - N_t_R / N_t * right_impurity
2012::COMM;;- N_t_L / N_t * left_impurity)
2013::COMM;;where ``N`` is the total number of samples, ``N_t`` is the number of
2014::COMM;;samples at the current node, ``N_t_L`` is the number of samples in the
2015::COMM;;left child, and ``N_t_R`` is the number of samples in the right child.
2016::COMM;;``N``, ``N_t``, ``N_t_R`` and ``N_t_L`` all refer to the weighted sum,
2017::COMM;;if ``sample_weight`` is passed.
2018::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
2019::COMM;;bootstrap : bool, default=False
2020::COMM;;Whether bootstrap samples are used when building trees. If False, the
2021::COMM;;whole dataset is used to build each tree.
2022::COMM;;oob_score : bool or callable, default=False
2023::COMM;;Whether to use out-of-bag samples to estimate the generalization score.
2024::COMM;;By default, :func:`~sklearn.metrics.r2_score` is used.
2025::COMM;;Provide a callable with signature `metric(y_true, y_pred)` to use a
2026::COMM;;custom metric. Only available if `bootstrap=True`.
2027::COMM;;For an illustration of out-of-bag (OOB) error estimation, see the example
2028::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_ensemble_plot_ensemble_oob.py`.
2029::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
2030::COMM;;The number of jobs to run in parallel. :meth:`fit`, :meth:`predict`,
2031::COMM;;:meth:`decision_path` and :meth:`apply` are all parallelized over the
2032::COMM;;trees. ``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend`
2033::COMM;;context. ``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary
2034::COMM;;<n_jobs>` for more details.
2035::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
2036::COMM;;Controls 3 sources of randomness:
2037::COMM;;- the bootstrapping of the samples used when building trees
2038::COMM;;(if ``bootstrap=True``)
2039::COMM;;- the sampling of the features to consider when looking for the best
2040::COMM;;split at each node (if ``max_features < n_features``)
2041::COMM;;- the draw of the splits for each of the `max_features`
2042::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
2043::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
2044::COMM;;Controls the verbosity when fitting and predicting.
2045::COMM;;warm_start : bool, default=False
2046::COMM;;When set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit
2047::COMM;;and add more estimators to the ensemble, otherwise, just fit a whole
2048::COMM;;new forest. See :term:`Glossary <warm_start>` and
2049::COMM;;:ref:`tree_ensemble_warm_start` for details.
2050::COMM;;ccp_alpha : non-negative float, default=0.0
2051::COMM;;Complexity parameter used for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning. The
2052::COMM;;subtree with the largest cost complexity that is smaller than
2053::COMM;;``ccp_alpha`` will be chosen. By default, no pruning is performed. See
2054::COMM;;:ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details. See
2055::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_cost_complexity_pruning.py`
2056::COMM;;for an example of such pruning.
2057::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
2058::COMM;;max_samples : int or float, default=None
2059::COMM;;If bootstrap is True, the number of samples to draw from X
2060::COMM;;to train each base estimator.
2061::COMM;;- If None (default), then draw `X.shape[0]` samples.
2062::COMM;;- If int, then draw `max_samples` samples.
2063::COMM;;- If float, then draw `max_samples * X.shape[0]` samples. Thus,
2064::COMM;;`max_samples` should be in the interval `(0.0, 1.0]`.
2065::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
2066::COMM;;monotonic_cst : array-like of int of shape (n_features), default=None
2067::COMM;;Indicates the monotonicity constraint to enforce on each feature.
2068::COMM;;- 1: monotonically increasing
2069::COMM;;- 0: no constraint
2070::COMM;;- -1: monotonically decreasing
2071::COMM;;If monotonic_cst is None, no constraints are applied.
2072::COMM;;Monotonicity constraints are not supported for:
2073::COMM;;- multioutput regressions (i.e. when `n_outputs_ > 1`),
2074::COMM;;- regressions trained on data with missing values.
2075::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <monotonic_cst_gbdt>`.
2076::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4

2206::COMM;;An ensemble of totally random trees.
2207::COMM;;An unsupervised transformation of a dataset to a high-dimensional
2208::COMM;;sparse representation. A datapoint is coded according to which leaf of
2209::COMM;;each tree it is sorted into. Using a one-hot encoding of the leaves,
2210::COMM;;this leads to a binary coding with as many ones as there are trees in
2211::COMM;;the forest.
2212::COMM;;The dimensionality of the resulting representation is
2213::COMM;;``n_out <= n_estimators * max_leaf_nodes``. If ``max_leaf_nodes == None``,
2214::COMM;;the number of leaf nodes is at most ``n_estimators * 2 ** max_depth``.
2215::COMM;;For an example of applying Random Trees Embedding to non-linear
2216::COMM;;classification, see

2::COMM;;This module contains methods for fitting gradient boosted regression trees for
3::COMM;;both classification and regression.
4::COMM;;The module structure is the following:
5::COMM;;- The ``BaseGradientBoosting`` base class implements a common ``fit`` method
6::COMM;;for all the estimators in the module. Regression and classification
7::COMM;;only differ in the concrete ``LossFunction`` used.
8::COMM;;- ``GradientBoostingClassifier`` implements gradient boosting for
9::COMM;;classification problems.
10::COMM;;- ``GradientBoostingRegressor`` implements gradient boosting for
11::COMM;;regression problems.

63::COMM;;# This is used for classifiers where the denominator might become zero exactly.
64::COMM;;# For instance for log loss, HalfBinomialLoss, if proba=0 or proba=1 exactly, then
65::COMM;;# denominator = hessian = 0, and we should set the node value in the line search to
66::COMM;;# zero as there is no improvement of the loss possible.
67::COMM;;# For numerical safety, we do this already for extremely tiny values.
68::COMM;;if abs(denominator) < 1e-150:
69::COMM;;return 0.0
70::COMM;;else:
71::COMM;;# Cast to Python float to trigger Python errors, e.g. ZeroDivisionError,
72::COMM;;# without relying on `np.errstate` that is not supported by Pyodide.
73::COMM;;result = float(numerator) / float(denominator)
74::COMM;;# Cast to Python float to trigger a ZeroDivisionError without relying
75::COMM;;# on `np.errstate` that is not supported by Pyodide.
76::COMM;;result = float(numerator) / float(denominator)
77::COMM;;if math.isinf(result):
78::COMM;;warnings.warn("overflow encountered in _safe_divide", RuntimeWarning)
79::COMM;;return result
80::COMM;;def _init_raw_predictions(X, estimator, loss, use_predict_proba):
100::COMM;;# TODO: Use loss.fit_intercept_only where appropriate instead of
101::COMM;;# DummyRegressor which is the default given by the `init` parameter,
102::COMM;;# see also _init_state.
103::COMM;;if use_predict_proba:
104::COMM;;# Our parameter validation, set via _fit_context and _parameter_constraints
105::COMM;;# already guarantees that estimator has a predict_proba method.
106::COMM;;predictions = estimator.predict_proba(X)
107::COMM;;if not loss.is_multiclass:
108::COMM;;predictions = predictions[:, 1] # probability of positive class
109::COMM;;eps = np.finfo(np.float64).eps
110::COMM;;predictions = np.clip(predictions, eps, 1 - eps, dtype=np.float64)
111::COMM;;else:
112::COMM;;predictions = estimator.predict(X).astype(np.float64)
113::COMM;;if predictions.ndim == 1:
114::COMM;;return loss.link.link(predictions).reshape(-1, 1)
115::COMM;;else:
116::COMM;;return loss.link.link(predictions)
117::COMM;;def _update_terminal_regions(
118::COMM;;loss,
119::COMM;;tree,
120::COMM;;X,
121::COMM;;y,
122::COMM;;neg_gradient,
123::COMM;;raw_prediction,
124::COMM;;sample_weight,
125::COMM;;sample_mask,
126::COMM;;learning_rate=0.1,
127::COMM;;k=0,
128::COMM;;):
165::COMM;;# compute leaf for each sample in ``X``.
166::COMM;;terminal_regions = tree.apply(X)
167::COMM;;if not isinstance(loss, HalfSquaredError):
168::COMM;;# mask all which are not in sample mask.
169::COMM;;masked_terminal_regions = terminal_regions.copy()
170::COMM;;masked_terminal_regions[~sample_mask] = -1
171::COMM;;if isinstance(loss, HalfBinomialLoss):
172::COMM;;def compute_update(y_, indices, neg_gradient, raw_prediction, k):
173::COMM;;# Make a single Newton-Raphson step, see "Additive Logistic Regression:
174::COMM;;# A Statistical View of Boosting" FHT00 and note that we use a slightly
175::COMM;;# different version (factor 2) of "F" with proba=expit(raw_prediction).
176::COMM;;# Our node estimate is given by:
177::COMM;;# sum(w * (y - prob)) / sum(w * prob * (1 - prob))
178::COMM;;# we take advantage that: y - prob = neg_gradient
179::COMM;;neg_g = neg_gradient.take(indices, axis=0)
180::COMM;;prob = y_ - neg_g
181::COMM;;# numerator = negative gradient = y - prob
182::COMM;;numerator = np.average(neg_g, weights=sw)
183::COMM;;# denominator = hessian = prob * (1 - prob)
184::COMM;;denominator = np.average(prob * (1 - prob), weights=sw)
185::COMM;;return _safe_divide(numerator, denominator)
186::COMM;;elif isinstance(loss, HalfMultinomialLoss):
187::COMM;;def compute_update(y_, indices, neg_gradient, raw_prediction, k):
188::COMM;;# we take advantage that: y - prob = neg_gradient
189::COMM;;neg_g = neg_gradient.take(indices, axis=0)
190::COMM;;prob = y_ - neg_g
191::COMM;;K = loss.n_classes
192::COMM;;# numerator = negative gradient * (k - 1) / k
193::COMM;;# Note: The factor (k - 1)/k appears in the original papers "Greedy
194::COMM;;# Function Approximation" by Friedman and "Additive Logistic
195::COMM;;# Regression" by Friedman, Hastie, Tibshirani. This factor is, however,
196::COMM;;# wrong or at least arbitrary as it directly multiplies the
197::COMM;;# learning_rate. We keep it for backward compatibility.
198::COMM;;numerator = np.average(neg_g, weights=sw)
199::COMM;;numerator *= (K - 1) / K
200::COMM;;# denominator = (diagonal) hessian = prob * (1 - prob)
201::COMM;;denominator = np.average(prob * (1 - prob), weights=sw)
202::COMM;;return _safe_divide(numerator, denominator)
203::COMM;;elif isinstance(loss, ExponentialLoss):
204::COMM;;def compute_update(y_, indices, neg_gradient, raw_prediction, k):
205::COMM;;neg_g = neg_gradient.take(indices, axis=0)
206::COMM;;# numerator = negative gradient = y * exp(-raw) - (1-y) * exp(raw)
207::COMM;;numerator = np.average(neg_g, weights=sw)
208::COMM;;# denominator = hessian = y * exp(-raw) + (1-y) * exp(raw)
209::COMM;;# if y=0: hessian = exp(raw) = -neg_g
210::COMM;;# y=1: hessian = exp(-raw) = neg_g
211::COMM;;hessian = neg_g.copy()
212::COMM;;hessian[y_ == 0] *= -1
213::COMM;;denominator = np.average(hessian, weights=sw)
214::COMM;;return _safe_divide(numerator, denominator)
215::COMM;;else:
216::COMM;;def compute_update(y_, indices, neg_gradient, raw_prediction, k):
217::COMM;;return loss.fit_intercept_only(
218::COMM;;y_true=y_ - raw_prediction[indices, k],
219::COMM;;sample_weight=sw,
220::COMM;;)
221::COMM;;# update each leaf (= perform line search)
222::COMM;;for leaf in np.nonzero(tree.children_left == TREE_LEAF)[0]:
223::COMM;;indices = np.nonzero(masked_terminal_regions == leaf)[
224::COMM;;0
225::COMM;;] # of terminal regions
226::COMM;;y_ = y.take(indices, axis=0)
227::COMM;;sw = None if sample_weight is None else sample_weight[indices]
228::COMM;;update = compute_update(y_, indices, neg_gradient, raw_prediction, k)
229::COMM;;# TODO: Multiply here by learning rate instead of everywhere else.
230::COMM;;tree.value[leaf, 0, 0] = update
231::COMM;;# update predictions (both in-bag and out-of-bag)
232::COMM;;raw_prediction[:, k] += learning_rate * tree.value[:, 0, 0].take(
233::COMM;;terminal_regions, axis=0
234::COMM;;)

724::COMM;;def _fit_stages(
725::COMM;;self,
726::COMM;;X,
727::COMM;;y,
728::COMM;;raw_predictions,
729::COMM;;sample_weight,
730::COMM;;random_state,

753::COMM;;loss_history = np.full(self.n_iter_no_change, np.inf)
754::COMM;;# We create a generator to get the predictions for X_val after
755::COMM;;# the addition of each successive stage
756::COMM;;y_val_pred_iter = self._staged_raw_predict(X_val, check_input=False)
757::COMM;;# Older versions of GBT had its own loss functions. With the new common
758::COMM;;# private loss function submodule _loss, we often are a factor of 2
759::COMM;;# away from the old version. Here we keep backward compatibility for
760::COMM;;# oob_scores_ and oob_improvement_, even if the old way is quite
761::COMM;;# inconsistent (sometimes the gradient is half the gradient, sometimes
762::COMM;;# not).
763::COMM;;if isinstance(
764::COMM;;self._loss,
765::COMM;;(
766::COMM;;HalfSquaredError,
767::COMM;;HalfBinomialLoss,
768::COMM;;),
769::COMM;;):

771::COMM;;else:
772::COMM;;factor = 1
773::COMM;;# perform boosting iterations
774::COMM;;i = begin_at_stage
775::COMM;;for i in range(begin_at_stage, self.n_estimators):
776::COMM;;# subsampling

778::COMM;;sample_mask = _random_sample_mask(n_samples, n_inbag, random_state)
779::COMM;;y_oob_masked = y[~sample_mask]
780::COMM;;sample_weight_oob_masked = sample_weight[~sample_mask]
781::COMM;;if i == 0: # store the initial loss to compute the OOB score
782::COMM;;initial_loss = factor * self._loss(

785::COMM;;sample_weight=sample_weight_oob_masked,

789::COMM;;i,

795::COMM;;random_state,

797::COMM;;X_csr=X_csr,
798::COMM;;)

800::COMM;;if do_oob:
801::COMM;;self.train_score_[i] = factor * self._loss(
802::COMM;;y_true=y[sample_mask],
803::COMM;;raw_prediction=raw_predictions[sample_mask],
804::COMM;;sample_weight=sample_weight[sample_mask],
805::COMM;;)
806::COMM;;self.oob_scores_[i] = factor * self._loss(
807::COMM;;y_true=y_oob_masked,
808::COMM;;raw_prediction=raw_predictions[~sample_mask],
809::COMM;;sample_weight=sample_weight_oob_masked,
810::COMM;;)
811::COMM;;previous_loss = initial_loss if i == 0 else self.oob_scores_[i - 1]
812::COMM;;self.oob_improvement_[i] = previous_loss - self.oob_scores_[i]
813::COMM;;self.oob_score_ = self.oob_scores_[-1]
814::COMM;;else:
815::COMM;;# no need to fancy index w/ no subsampling
816::COMM;;self.train_score_[i] = factor * self._loss(
817::COMM;;y_true=y,
818::COMM;;raw_prediction=raw_predictions,
819::COMM;;sample_weight=sample_weight,
820::COMM;;)

823::COMM;;if monitor is not None:

825::COMM;;if early_stopping:
826::COMM;;break

828::COMM;;# validation set (X_val, y_val), if n_iter_no_change is set
829::COMM;;if self.n_iter_no_change is not None:
830::COMM;;# By calling next(y_val_pred_iter), we get the predictions
831::COMM;;# for X_val after the addition of the current stage
832::COMM;;validation_loss = factor * self._loss(
833::COMM;;y_val, next(y_val_pred_iter), sample_weight_val
834::COMM;;)

836::COMM;;# one of the last n_iter_no_change evaluations
837::COMM;;if np.any(validation_loss + self.tol < loss_history):
838::COMM;;loss_history[i % len(loss_history)] = validation_loss
839::COMM;;else:
840::COMM;;break
841::COMM;;return i + 1
