16::COMM;;Parameters
17::COMM;;----------
18::COMM;;w : ndarray, shape (n_features + 1,) or (n_features + 2,)
19::COMM;;Feature vector.
20::COMM;;w[:n_features] gives the coefficients
21::COMM;;w[-1] gives the scale factor and if the intercept is fit w[-2]
22::COMM;;gives the intercept factor.
23::COMM;;X : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
24::COMM;;Input data.
25::COMM;;y : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
26::COMM;;Target vector.
27::COMM;;epsilon : float
28::COMM;;Robustness of the Huber estimator.
29::COMM;;alpha : float
30::COMM;;Regularization parameter.
31::COMM;;sample_weight : ndarray of shape (n_samples,), default=None
32::COMM;;Weight assigned to each sample.
33::COMM;;Returns
34::COMM;;-------
35::COMM;;loss : float
36::COMM;;Huber loss.
37::COMM;;gradient : ndarray, shape (len(w))
38::COMM;;Returns the derivative of the Huber loss with respect to each
39::COMM;;coefficient, intercept and the scale as a vector.
48::COMO;;# Calculate the values where |y - X'w -c / sigma| > epsilon
49::COMO;;# The values above this threshold are outliers.
55::COMO;;# Calculate the linear loss due to the outliers.
56::COMO;;# This is equal to (2 * M * |y - X'w -c / sigma| - M**2) * sigma
60::COMO;;# n_sq_outliers includes the weight give to the outliers while
61::COMO;;# num_outliers is just the number of outliers.
68::COMO;;# Calculate the quadratic loss due to the non-outliers.-
69::COMO;;# This is equal to |(y - X'w - c)**2 / sigma**2| * sigma
78::COMO;;# Gradient due to the squared loss.
83::COMO;;# Gradient due to the linear loss.
90::COMO;;# Gradient due to the penalty.
92::COMO;;# Gradient due to sigma.
96::COMO;;# Gradient due to the intercept.
105::COMM;;The Huber Regressor optimizes the squared loss for the samples where
106::COMM;;``|(y - Xw - c) / sigma| < epsilon`` and the absolute loss for the samples
107::COMM;;where ``|(y - Xw - c) / sigma| > epsilon``, where the model coefficients
108::COMM;;``w``, the intercept ``c`` and the scale ``sigma`` are parameters
109::COMM;;to be optimized. The parameter `sigma` makes sure that if `y` is scaled up
110::COMM;;or down by a certain factor, one does not need to rescale `epsilon` to
111::COMM;;achieve the same robustness. Note that this does not take into account
112::COMM;;the fact that the different features of `X` may be of different scales.
113::COMM;;The Huber loss function has the advantage of not being heavily influenced
114::COMM;;by the outliers while not completely ignoring their effect.
115::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <huber_regression>`
116::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.18
117::COMM;;Parameters
118::COMM;;----------
119::COMM;;epsilon : float, default=1.35
120::COMM;;The parameter epsilon controls the number of samples that should be
121::COMM;;classified as outliers. The smaller the epsilon, the more robust it is
122::COMM;;to outliers. Epsilon must be in the range `[1, inf)`.
123::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=100
124::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations that
125::COMM;;``scipy.optimize.minimize(method="L-BFGS-B")`` should run for.
126::COMM;;alpha : float, default=0.0001
127::COMM;;Strength of the squared L2 regularization. Note that the penalty is
128::COMM;;equal to ``alpha * ||w||^2``.
129::COMM;;Must be in the range `[0, inf)`.
130::COMM;;warm_start : bool, default=False
131::COMM;;This is useful if the stored attributes of a previously used model
132::COMM;;has to be reused. If set to False, then the coefficients will
133::COMM;;be rewritten for every call to fit.
134::COMM;;See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
135::COMM;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
136::COMM;;Whether or not to fit the intercept. This can be set to False
137::COMM;;if the data is already centered around the origin.
138::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-05
139::COMM;;The iteration will stop when
140::COMM;;``max{|proj g_i | i = 1, ..., n}`` <= ``tol``
141::COMM;;where pg_i is the i-th component of the projected gradient.
142::COMM;;Attributes
143::COMM;;----------
144::COMM;;coef_ : array, shape (n_features,)
145::COMM;;Features got by optimizing the L2-regularized Huber loss.
146::COMM;;intercept_ : float
147::COMM;;Bias.
148::COMM;;scale_ : float
149::COMM;;The value by which ``|y - Xw - c|`` is scaled down.
150::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
151::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
152::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
153::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
154::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
155::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
156::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
157::COMM;;n_iter_ : int
158::COMM;;Number of iterations that
159::COMM;;``scipy.optimize.minimize(method="L-BFGS-B")`` has run for.
160::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.20
161::COMM;;In SciPy <= 1.0.0 the number of lbfgs iterations may exceed
162::COMM;;``max_iter``. ``n_iter_`` will now report at most ``max_iter``.
163::COMM;;outliers_ : array, shape (n_samples,)
164::COMM;;A boolean mask which is set to True where the samples are identified
165::COMM;;as outliers.
166::COMM;;See Also
167::COMM;;--------
168::COMM;;RANSACRegressor : RANSAC (RANdom SAmple Consensus) algorithm.
169::COMM;;TheilSenRegressor : Theil-Sen Estimator robust multivariate regression model.
170::COMM;;SGDRegressor : Fitted by minimizing a regularized empirical loss with SGD.
171::COMM;;References
172::COMM;;----------
173::COMM;;.. [1] Peter J. Huber, Elvezio M. Ronchetti, Robust Statistics
174::COMM;;Concomitant scale estimates, p. 172
175::COMM;;.. [2] Art B. Owen (2006), `A robust hybrid of lasso and ridge regression.
176::COMM;;<https://artowen.su.domains/reports/hhu.pdf>`_

184::COMM;;... n_samples=200, n_features=2, noise=4.0, coef=True, random_state=0)
185::COMM;;>>> X[:4] = rng.uniform(10, 20, (4, 2))
186::COMM;;>>> y[:4] = rng.uniform(10, 20, 4)
187::COMM;;>>> huber = HuberRegressor().fit(X, y)

231::COMM;;`n_features` is the number of features.

258::COMO;;# Make sure to initialize the scale parameter to a strictly
259::COMO;;# positive value:
261::COMO;;# Sigma or the scale factor should be non-negative.
262::COMO;;# Setting it to be zero might cause undefined bounds hence we set it
263::COMO;;# to a value close to zero.
2::COMM;;Least Angle Regression algorithm. See the documentation on the
3::COMM;;Generalized Linear Model for a complete discussion.

18::COMO;;# mypy error: Module 'sklearn.utils' has no attribute 'arrayfuncs'
73::COMM;;The optimization objective for the case method='lasso' is::
74::COMM;;(1 / (2 * n_samples)) * ||y - Xw||^2_2 + alpha * ||w||_1
75::COMM;;in the case of method='lar', the objective function is only known in
76::COMM;;the form of an implicit equation (see discussion in [1]_).
77::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <least_angle_regression>`.
78::COMM;;Parameters
79::COMM;;----------
80::COMM;;X : None or ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
81::COMM;;Input data. If X is `None`, Gram must also be `None`.
82::COMM;;If only the Gram matrix is available, use `lars_path_gram` instead.
83::COMM;;y : None or ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
84::COMM;;Input targets.
85::COMM;;Xy : array-like of shape (n_features,), default=None
86::COMM;;`Xy = X.T @ y` that can be precomputed. It is useful
87::COMM;;only when the Gram matrix is precomputed.
88::COMM;;Gram : None, 'auto', bool, ndarray of shape (n_features, n_features), \
89::COMM;;default=None
90::COMM;;Precomputed Gram matrix `X.T @ X`, if `'auto'`, the Gram
91::COMM;;matrix is precomputed from the given X, if there are more samples
92::COMM;;than features.
93::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=500
94::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations to perform, set to infinity for no limit.
95::COMM;;alpha_min : float, default=0
96::COMM;;Minimum correlation along the path. It corresponds to the
97::COMM;;regularization parameter `alpha` in the Lasso.
98::COMM;;method : {'lar', 'lasso'}, default='lar'
99::COMM;;Specifies the returned model. Select `'lar'` for Least Angle
100::COMM;;Regression, `'lasso'` for the Lasso.
101::COMM;;copy_X : bool, default=True
102::COMM;;If `False`, `X` is overwritten.
103::COMM;;eps : float, default=np.finfo(float).eps
104::COMM;;The machine-precision regularization in the computation of the
105::COMM;;Cholesky diagonal factors. Increase this for very ill-conditioned
106::COMM;;systems. Unlike the `tol` parameter in some iterative
107::COMM;;optimization-based algorithms, this parameter does not control
108::COMM;;the tolerance of the optimization.
109::COMM;;copy_Gram : bool, default=True
110::COMM;;If `False`, `Gram` is overwritten.
111::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
112::COMM;;Controls output verbosity.
113::COMM;;return_path : bool, default=True
114::COMM;;If `True`, returns the entire path, else returns only the
115::COMM;;last point of the path.
116::COMM;;return_n_iter : bool, default=False
117::COMM;;Whether to return the number of iterations.
118::COMM;;positive : bool, default=False
119::COMM;;Restrict coefficients to be >= 0.
120::COMM;;This option is only allowed with method 'lasso'. Note that the model
121::COMM;;coefficients will not converge to the ordinary-least-squares solution
122::COMM;;for small values of alpha. Only coefficients up to the smallest alpha
123::COMM;;value (`alphas_[alphas_ > 0.].min()` when fit_path=True) reached by
124::COMM;;the stepwise Lars-Lasso algorithm are typically in congruence with the
125::COMM;;solution of the coordinate descent `lasso_path` function.
126::COMM;;Returns
127::COMM;;-------
128::COMM;;alphas : ndarray of shape (n_alphas + 1,)
129::COMM;;Maximum of covariances (in absolute value) at each iteration.
130::COMM;;`n_alphas` is either `max_iter`, `n_features`, or the
131::COMM;;number of nodes in the path with `alpha >= alpha_min`, whichever
132::COMM;;is smaller.
133::COMM;;active : ndarray of shape (n_alphas,)
134::COMM;;Indices of active variables at the end of the path.
135::COMM;;coefs : ndarray of shape (n_features, n_alphas + 1)
136::COMM;;Coefficients along the path.
137::COMM;;n_iter : int
138::COMM;;Number of iterations run. Returned only if `return_n_iter` is set
139::COMM;;to True.

779::COMM;;verbose : bool or int, default=False
780::COMM;;Sets the verbosity amount.
781::COMM;;precompute : bool, 'auto' or array-like , default='auto'
782::COMM;;Whether to use a precomputed Gram matrix to speed up
783::COMM;;calculations. If set to ``'auto'`` let us decide. The Gram
784::COMM;;matrix can also be passed as argument.
785::COMM;;n_nonzero_coefs : int, default=500
786::COMM;;Target number of non-zero coefficients. Use ``np.inf`` for no limit.
787::COMM;;eps : float, default=np.finfo(float).eps
788::COMM;;The machine-precision regularization in the computation of the
789::COMM;;Cholesky diagonal factors. Increase this for very ill-conditioned
790::COMM;;systems. Unlike the ``tol`` parameter in some iterative
791::COMM;;optimization-based algorithms, this parameter does not control
792::COMM;;the tolerance of the optimization.
793::COMM;;copy_X : bool, default=True
794::COMM;;If ``True``, X will be copied; else, it may be overwritten.
795::COMM;;fit_path : bool, default=True
796::COMM;;If True the full path is stored in the ``coef_path_`` attribute.
797::COMM;;If you compute the solution for a large problem or many targets,
798::COMM;;setting ``fit_path`` to ``False`` will lead to a speedup, especially
799::COMM;;with a small alpha.
800::COMM;;jitter : float, default=None
801::COMM;;Upper bound on a uniform noise parameter to be added to the
802::COMM;;`y` values, to satisfy the model's assumption of
803::COMM;;one-at-a-time computations. Might help with stability.
804::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.23
805::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None

809::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.23

825::COMM;;of array-like, the length of the outer list is `n_targets`.

376::COMM;;----------
377::COMM;;coef : ndarray of shape (n_dof,), (n_classes, n_dof) or (n_classes * n_dof,)

398::COMM;;might be created.

401::COMM;;Raw prediction values (in link space). If provided, these are used. If
402::COMM;;None, then raw_prediction = X @ coef + intercept is calculated.
403::COMM;;Returns
404::COMM;;-------
405::COMM;;gradient : ndarray of shape coef.shape
406::COMM;;The gradient of the loss.
407::COMM;;hessian : ndarray of shape (n_dof, n_dof) or \
408::COMM;;(n_classes, n_dof, n_dof, n_classes)
409::COMM;;Hessian matrix.
410::COMM;;hessian_warning : bool
411::COMM;;True if pointwise hessian has more than 25% of its elements non-positive.
420::COMO;;# Allocate gradient.
432::COMO;;# Allocate hessian.
433::COMC;;n = coef.size # for multinomial this equals n_dof * n_classes
456::COMO;;# For non-canonical link functions and far away from the optimum, the
457::COMO;;# pointwise hessian can be negative. We take care that 75% of the hessian
458::COMO;;# entries are positive.
467::COMO;;# Exit early without computing the hessian.
471::COMO;;# The L2 penalty enters the Hessian on the diagonal only. To add those
472::COMO;;# terms, we use a flattened view of the array.
478::COMO;;# With intercept included as added column to X, the hessian becomes
479::COMO;;# hess = (X, 1)' @ diag(h) @ (X, 1)
480::COMO;;# = (X' @ diag(h) @ X, X' @ h)
481::COMO;;# ( h @ X, sum(h))
482::COMO;;# The left upper part has already been filled, it remains to compute
483::COMO;;# the last row and the last column.
489::COMO;;# Here we may safely assume HalfMultinomialLoss aka categorical
490::COMO;;# cross-entropy.
491::COMO;;# HalfMultinomialLoss computes only the diagonal part of the hessian, i.e.
492::COMO;;# diagonal in the classes. Here, we want the full hessian. Therefore, we
493::COMO;;# call gradient_proba.
507::COMO;;# The full hessian matrix, i.e. not only the diagonal part, dropping most
508::COMO;;# indices, is given by:
509::COMO;;#
510::COMO;;# hess = X' @ h @ X
511::COMO;;#
512::COMO;;# Here, h is a priori a 4-dimensional matrix of shape
513::COMO;;# (n_samples, n_samples, n_classes, n_classes). It is diagonal its first
514::COMO;;# two dimensions (the ones with n_samples), i.e. it is
515::COMO;;# effectively a 3-dimensional matrix (n_samples, n_classes, n_classes).
516::COMO;;#
517::COMO;;# h = diag(p) - p' p
518::COMO;;#
519::COMO;;# or with indices k and l for classes
520::COMO;;#
521::COMO;;# h_kl = p_k * delta_kl - p_k * p_l
522::COMO;;#
523::COMO;;# with p_k the (predicted) probability for class k. Only the dimension in
524::COMO;;# n_samples multiplies with X.
525::COMO;;# For 3 classes and n_samples = 1, this looks like ("@" is a bit misused
526::COMO;;# here):
527::COMO;;#
528::COMO;;# hess = X' @ (h00 h10 h20) @ X
529::COMO;;# (h10 h11 h12)
530::COMO;;# (h20 h12 h22)
531::COMO;;# = (X' @ diag(h00) @ X, X' @ diag(h10), X' @ diag(h20))
532::COMO;;# (X' @ diag(h10) @ X, X' @ diag(h11), X' @ diag(h12))
533::COMO;;# (X' @ diag(h20) @ X, X' @ diag(h12), X' @ diag(h22))
534::COMO;;#
535::COMO;;# Now coef of shape (n_classes * n_dof) is contiguous in n_classes.
536::COMO;;# Therefore, we want the hessian to follow this convention, too, i.e.
537::COMO;;# hess[:n_classes, :n_classes] = (x0' @ h00 @ x0, x0' @ h10 @ x0, ..)
538::COMO;;# (x0' @ h10 @ x0, x0' @ h11 @ x0, ..)
539::COMO;;# (x0' @ h20 @ x0, x0' @ h12 @ x0, ..)
540::COMO;;# is the first feature, x0, for all classes. In our implementation, we
541::COMO;;# still want to take advantage of BLAS "X.T @ X". Therefore, we have some
542::COMO;;# index/slicing battle to fight.
548::COMO;;# Diagonal terms (in classes) hess_kk.
549::COMO;;# Note that this also writes to some of the lower triangular part.
556::COMO;;# See above in the non multiclass case.
569::COMO;;# Off diagonal terms (in classes) hess_kl.
571::COMO;;# Upper triangle (in classes).
590::COMO;;# Fill lower triangle (in classes).
593::COMO;;# See above in the non multiclass case.
598::COMO;;# The pointwise hessian is always non-negative for the multinomial loss.
605::COMM;;Parameters
606::COMM;;----------
607::COMM;;coef : ndarray of shape (n_dof,), (n_classes, n_dof) or (n_classes * n_dof,)
608::COMM;;Coefficients of a linear model.
609::COMM;;If shape (n_classes * n_dof,), the classes of one feature are contiguous,
610::COMM;;i.e. one reconstructs the 2d-array via
611::COMM;;coef.reshape((n_classes, -1), order="F").
612::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
613::COMM;;Training data.
614::COMM;;y : contiguous array of shape (n_samples,)
615::COMM;;Observed, true target values.
616::COMM;;sample_weight : None or contiguous array of shape (n_samples,), default=None
617::COMM;;Sample weights.
618::COMM;;l2_reg_strength : float, default=0.0
619::COMM;;L2 regularization strength
620::COMM;;n_threads : int, default=1
621::COMM;;Number of OpenMP threads to use.
622::COMM;;Returns
623::COMM;;-------
624::COMM;;gradient : ndarray of shape coef.shape
625::COMM;;The gradient of the loss.
626::COMM;;hessp : callable
627::COMM;;Function that takes in a vector input of shape of gradient and
628::COMM;;and returns matrix-vector product with hessian.
647::COMO;;# Precompute as much as possible: hX, hX_sum and hessian_sum
657::COMO;;# Calculate the double derivative with respect to intercept.
658::COMO;;# Note: In case hX is sparse, hX.sum is a matrix object.
660::COMO;;# prevent squeezing to zero-dim array if n_features == 1
662::COMO;;# With intercept included and l2_reg_strength = 0, hessp returns
663::COMO;;# res = (X, 1)' @ diag(h) @ (X, 1) @ s
664::COMO;;# = (X, 1)' @ (hX @ s[:n_features], sum(h) * s[-1])
665::COMO;;# res[:n_features] = X' @ hX @ s[:n_features] + sum(h) * s[-1]
666::COMO;;# res[-1] = 1' @ hX @ s[:n_features] + sum(h) * s[-1]
679::COMO;;# Here we may safely assume HalfMultinomialLoss aka categorical
680::COMO;;# cross-entropy.
681::COMO;;# HalfMultinomialLoss computes only the diagonal part of the hessian, i.e.
682::COMO;;# diagonal in the classes. Here, we want the matrix-vector product of the
683::COMO;;# full hessian. Therefore, we call gradient_proba.
695::COMO;;# Full hessian-vector product, i.e. not only the diagonal part of the
696::COMO;;# hessian. Derivation with some index battle for input vector s:
697::COMO;;# - sample index i
698::COMO;;# - feature indices j, m
699::COMO;;# - class indices k, l
700::COMO;;# - 1_{k=l} is one if k=l else 0
701::COMO;;# - p_i_k is the (predicted) probability that sample i belongs to class k
702::COMO;;# for all i: sum_k p_i_k = 1
703::COMO;;# - s_l_m is input vector for class l and feature m
704::COMO;;# - X' = X transposed
705::COMO;;#
706::COMO;;# Note: Hessian with dropping most indices is just:
707::COMO;;# X' @ p_k (1(k=l) - p_l) @ X
708::COMO;;#
709::COMO;;# result_{k j} = sum_{i, l, m} Hessian_{i, k j, m l} * s_l_m
710::COMO;;# = sum_{i, l, m} (X')_{ji} * p_i_k * (1_{k=l} - p_i_l)
711::COMO;;# * X_{im} s_l_m
712::COMO;;# = sum_{i, m} (X')_{ji} * p_i_k
713::COMO;;# * (X_{im} * s_k_m - sum_l p_i_l * X_{im} * s_l_m)
714::COMO;;#
715::COMO;;# See also https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/3646#discussion_r17461411
717::COMC;;s = s.reshape((n_classes, -1), order="F") # shape = (n_classes, n_dof)
720::COMC;;s = s[:, :-1] # shape = (n_classes, n_features)
723::COMC;;tmp = X @ s.T + s_intercept # X_{im} * s_k_m
724::COMC;;tmp += (-proba * tmp).sum(axis=1)[:, np.newaxis] # - sum_l ..
725::COMC;;tmp *= proba # * p_i_k
728::COMO;;# hess_prod = empty_like(grad), but we ravel grad below and this
729::COMO;;# function is run after that.
2::COMM;;Logistic Regression
4::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
5::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
54::COMC;;"#logistic-regression"
95::COMM;;parameters.
96::COMM;;This is an implementation that uses the result of the previous model
97::COMM;;to speed up computations along the set of solutions, making it faster
98::COMM;;than sequentially calling LogisticRegression for the different parameters.
99::COMM;;Note that there will be no speedup with liblinear solver, since it does
100::COMM;;not handle warm-starting.
101::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <logistic_regression>`.
102::COMM;;Parameters
103::COMM;;----------
104::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
105::COMM;;Input data.
106::COMM;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_targets)
107::COMM;;Input data, target values.
108::COMM;;classes : ndarray
109::COMM;;A list of class labels known to the classifier.
110::COMM;;Cs : int or array-like of shape (n_cs,), default=10
111::COMM;;List of values for the regularization parameter or integer specifying
112::COMM;;the number of regularization parameters that should be used. In this
113::COMM;;case, the parameters will be chosen in a logarithmic scale between
114::COMM;;1e-4 and 1e4.
115::COMM;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
116::COMM;;Whether to fit an intercept for the model. In this case the shape of
117::COMM;;the returned array is (n_cs, n_features + 1).
118::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=100
119::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations for the solver.
120::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-4
121::COMM;;Stopping criterion. For the newton-cg and lbfgs solvers, the iteration
122::COMM;;will stop when ``max{|g_i | i = 1, ..., n} <= tol``
123::COMM;;where ``g_i`` is the i-th component of the gradient.
124::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
125::COMM;;For the liblinear and lbfgs solvers set verbose to any positive
126::COMM;;number for verbosity.
127::COMM;;solver : {'lbfgs', 'liblinear', 'newton-cg', 'newton-cholesky', 'sag', 'saga'}, \
128::COMM;;default='lbfgs'
129::COMM;;Numerical solver to use.
130::COMM;;coef : array-like of shape (n_classes, features + int(fit_intercept)) or \
131::COMM;;(1, n_features + int(fit_intercept)) or \
132::COMM;;(n_features + int(fit_intercept)), default=None
133::COMM;;Initialization value for coefficients of logistic regression.
134::COMM;;Useless for liblinear solver.
135::COMM;;class_weight : dict or 'balanced', default=None
136::COMM;;Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
137::COMM;;If not given, all classes are supposed to have weight one.
138::COMM;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
139::COMM;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
140::COMM;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``.
141::COMM;;Note that these weights will be multiplied with sample_weight (passed
142::COMM;;through the fit method) if sample_weight is specified.
143::COMM;;dual : bool, default=False
144::COMM;;Dual or primal formulation. Dual formulation is only implemented for
145::COMM;;l2 penalty with liblinear solver. Prefer dual=False when
146::COMM;;n_samples > n_features.
147::COMM;;penalty : {'l1', 'l2', 'elasticnet'}, default='l2'
148::COMM;;Used to specify the norm used in the penalization. The 'newton-cg',
149::COMM;;'sag' and 'lbfgs' solvers support only l2 penalties. 'elasticnet' is
150::COMM;;only supported by the 'saga' solver.
151::COMM;;intercept_scaling : float, default=1.
152::COMM;;Useful only when the solver `liblinear` is used
153::COMM;;and `self.fit_intercept` is set to `True`. In this case, `x` becomes
154::COMM;;`[x, self.intercept_scaling]`,
155::COMM;;i.e. a "synthetic" feature with constant value equal to
156::COMM;;`intercept_scaling` is appended to the instance vector.
157::COMM;;The intercept becomes
158::COMM;;``intercept_scaling * synthetic_feature_weight``.
159::COMM;;.. note::
160::COMM;;The synthetic feature weight is subject to L1 or L2
161::COMM;;regularization as all other features.
162::COMM;;To lessen the effect of regularization on synthetic feature weight
163::COMM;;(and therefore on the intercept) `intercept_scaling` has to be increased.
164::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance, default=None
165::COMM;;Used when ``solver`` == 'sag', 'saga' or 'liblinear' to shuffle the
166::COMM;;data. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
167::COMM;;check_input : bool, default=True
168::COMM;;If False, the input arrays X and y will not be checked.
169::COMM;;max_squared_sum : float, default=None
170::COMM;;Maximum squared sum of X over samples. Used only in SAG solver.
171::COMM;;If None, it will be computed, going through all the samples.
172::COMM;;The value should be precomputed to speed up cross validation.
173::COMM;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
174::COMM;;Array of weights that are assigned to individual samples.
175::COMM;;If not provided, then each sample is given unit weight.
176::COMM;;l1_ratio : float, default=None
177::COMM;;The Elastic-Net mixing parameter, with ``0 <= l1_ratio <= 1``. Only
178::COMM;;used if ``penalty='elasticnet'``. Setting ``l1_ratio=0`` is equivalent
179::COMM;;to using ``penalty='l2'``, while setting ``l1_ratio=1`` is equivalent
180::COMM;;to using ``penalty='l1'``. For ``0 < l1_ratio <1``, the penalty is a
181::COMM;;combination of L1 and L2.
182::COMM;;n_threads : int, default=1
183::COMM;;Number of OpenMP threads to use.
184::COMM;;Returns
185::COMM;;-------
186::COMM;;coefs : ndarray of shape (n_cs, n_classes, n_features + int(fit_intercept)) or \
187::COMM;;(n_cs, n_features + int(fit_intercept))
188::COMM;;List of coefficients for the Logistic Regression model. If fit_intercept is set
189::COMM;;to True, then the last dimension will be n_features + 1, where the last item
190::COMM;;represents the intercept.
191::COMM;;For binary problems the second dimension in n_classes is dropped, i.e. the shape
192::COMM;;will be `(n_cs, n_features + int(fit_intercept))`.
193::COMM;;Cs : ndarray
194::COMM;;Grid of Cs used for cross-validation.
195::COMM;;n_iter : array of shape (n_cs,)
196::COMM;;Actual number of iteration for each C in Cs.
197::COMM;;Notes
198::COMM;;-----
199::COMM;;You might get slightly different results with the solver liblinear than
200::COMM;;with the others since this uses LIBLINEAR which penalizes the intercept.
201::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.19
202::COMM;;The "copy" parameter was removed.
207::COMO;;# Preprocessing.
243::COMO;;# HalfBinomialLoss, used for those solvers, represents y in [0, 1] instead
244::COMO;;# of in [-1, 1].
247::COMO;;# All solvers capable of a multinomial need LabelEncoder, not LabelBinarizer,
248::COMO;;# i.e. y as a 1d-array of integers. LabelEncoder also saves memory
249::COMO;;# compared to LabelBinarizer, especially when n_classes is large.
251::COMO;;# It is important that w0 is F-contiguous.
255::COMO;;# IMPORTANT NOTE:
256::COMO;;# All solvers relying on LinearModelLoss need to scale the penalty with n_samples
257::COMO;;# or the sum of sample weights because the implemented logistic regression
258::COMO;;# objective here is (unfortunately)
259::COMO;;# C * sum(pointwise_loss) + penalty
260::COMO;;# instead of (as LinearModelLoss does)
261::COMO;;# mean(pointwise_loss) + 1/C * penalty
263::COMO;;# This needs to be calculated after sample_weight is multiplied by
264::COMO;;# class_weight. It is even tested that passing class_weight is equivalent to
265::COMO;;# passing sample_weights according to class_weight.
306::COMC;;hess = loss.gradient_hessian_product # hess = [gradient, hessp]
308::COMC;;else: # multinomial
315::COMO;;# scipy.optimize.minimize and newton-cg accept only ravelled parameters,
316::COMO;;# i.e. 1d-arrays. LinearModelLoss expects classes to be contiguous and
317::COMO;;# reconstructs the 2d-array via w0.reshape((n_classes, -1), order="F").
318::COMO;;# As w0 is F-contiguous, ravel(order="F") also avoids a copy.
325::COMC;;hess = loss.gradient_hessian_product # hess = [gradient, hessp]
343::COMC;;"maxls": 50, # default is 20
402::COMO;;# n_iter_i is an array for each class. However, `target` is always encoded
403::COMO;;# in {-1, 1}, so we only take the first element of n_iter_i.
411::COMO;;# alpha is for L2-norm, beta is for L1-norm
418::COMC;;else: # Elastic-Net penalty
454::COMO;;# helper function for LogisticCV

521::COMM;;Decides which solver to use.

524::COMM;;'sag' and 'lbfgs' solvers support only l2 penalties. 'elasticnet' is
525::COMM;;only supported by the 'saga' solver.
526::COMM;;dual : bool

528::COMM;;l2 penalty with liblinear solver. Prefer dual=False when
529::COMM;;n_samples > n_features.

532::COMM;;and `self.fit_intercept` is set to `True`. In this case, `x` becomes
533::COMM;;`[x, self.intercept_scaling]`,

555::COMM;;used if ``penalty='elasticnet'``. Setting ``l1_ratio=0`` is equivalent
556::COMM;;to using ``penalty='l2'``, while setting ``l1_ratio=1`` is equivalent
557::COMM;;to using ``penalty='l1'``. For ``0 < l1_ratio <1``, the penalty is a
558::COMM;;combination of L1 and L2.
559::COMM;;score_params : dict
560::COMM;;Parameters to pass to the `score` method of the underlying scorer.
561::COMM;;Returns
562::COMM;;-------
563::COMM;;coefs : ndarray of shape (n_cs, n_classes, n_features + int(fit_intercept)) or \
564::COMM;;(n_cs, n_features + int(fit_intercept))
565::COMM;;List of coefficients for the Logistic Regression model. If fit_intercept is set
566::COMM;;to True, then the last dimension will be n_features + 1, where the last item
567::COMM;;represents the intercept.
568::COMM;;For binary problems the second dimension in n_classes is dropped, i.e. the shape
569::COMM;;will be `(n_cs, n_features + int(fit_intercept))`.
570::COMM;;Cs : ndarray of shape (n_cs,)
571::COMM;;Grid of Cs used for cross-validation.
572::COMM;;scores : ndarray of shape (n_cs,)
573::COMM;;Scores obtained for each Cs.
574::COMM;;n_iter : ndarray of shape (n_cs,)
575::COMM;;Actual number of iteration for each C in Cs.
586::COMO;;# Note: We pass classes for the whole dataset to avoid inconsistencies, i.e.
587::COMO;;# different number of classes in different folds. This way, if a class is empty
588::COMO;;# in a fold, _logistic_regression_path will initialize it to zero and not change.
610::COMO;;# The score method of Logistic Regression has a classes_ attribute.
630::COMM;;Logistic Regression (aka logit, MaxEnt) classifier.
631::COMM;;This class implements regularized logistic regression using a set of available
632::COMM;;solvers. **Note that regularization is applied by default**. It can handle both
633::COMM;;dense and sparse input `X`. Use C-ordered arrays or CSR matrices containing 64-bit
634::COMM;;floats for optimal performance; any other input format will be converted (and
635::COMM;;copied).
636::COMM;;The solvers 'lbfgs', 'newton-cg', 'newton-cholesky' and 'sag' support only L2
637::COMM;;regularization with primal formulation, or no regularization. The 'liblinear'
638::COMM;;solver supports both L1 and L2 regularization (but not both, i.e. elastic-net),
639::COMM;;with a dual formulation only for the L2 penalty. The Elastic-Net (combination of L1
640::COMM;;and L2) regularization is only supported by the 'saga' solver.
641::COMM;;For :term:`multiclass` problems (whenever `n_classes >= 3`), all solvers except
642::COMM;;'liblinear' optimize the (penalized) multinomial loss. 'liblinear' only handles
643::COMM;;binary classification but can be extended to handle multiclass by using
644::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.multiclass.OneVsRestClassifier`.
645::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <logistic_regression>`.
646::COMM;;Parameters
647::COMM;;----------
648::COMM;;penalty : {'l1', 'l2', 'elasticnet', None}, default='l2'
649::COMM;;Specify the norm of the penalty:
650::COMM;;- `None`: no penalty is added;
651::COMM;;- `'l2'`: add a L2 penalty term and it is the default choice;
652::COMM;;- `'l1'`: add a L1 penalty term;
653::COMM;;- `'elasticnet'`: both L1 and L2 penalty terms are added.
654::COMM;;.. warning::
655::COMM;;Some penalties may not work with some solvers. See the parameter
656::COMM;;`solver` below, to know the compatibility between the penalty and
657::COMM;;solver.
658::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
659::COMM;;l1 penalty with SAGA solver (allowing 'multinomial' + L1)
660::COMM;;dual : bool, default=False
661::COMM;;Dual (constrained) or primal (regularized, see also
662::COMM;;:ref:`this equation <regularized-logistic-loss>`) formulation. Dual formulation
663::COMM;;is only implemented for l2 penalty with liblinear solver. Prefer dual=False when
664::COMM;;n_samples > n_features.
665::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-4
666::COMM;;Tolerance for stopping criteria.
667::COMM;;C : float, default=1.0
668::COMM;;Inverse of regularization strength; must be a positive float.
669::COMM;;Like in support vector machines, smaller values specify stronger
670::COMM;;regularization. For a visual example on the effect of tuning the `C` parameter
671::COMM;;with an L1 penalty, see:
672::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_linear_model_plot_logistic_path.py`.
673::COMM;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
674::COMM;;Specifies if a constant (a.k.a. bias or intercept) should be
675::COMM;;added to the decision function.
676::COMM;;intercept_scaling : float, default=1
677::COMM;;Useful only when the solver `liblinear` is used
678::COMM;;and `self.fit_intercept` is set to `True`. In this case, `x` becomes
679::COMM;;`[x, self.intercept_scaling]`,
680::COMM;;i.e. a "synthetic" feature with constant value equal to
681::COMM;;`intercept_scaling` is appended to the instance vector.
682::COMM;;The intercept becomes
683::COMM;;``intercept_scaling * synthetic_feature_weight``.
684::COMM;;.. note::
685::COMM;;The synthetic feature weight is subject to L1 or L2
686::COMM;;regularization as all other features.
687::COMM;;To lessen the effect of regularization on synthetic feature weight
688::COMM;;(and therefore on the intercept) `intercept_scaling` has to be increased.
689::COMM;;class_weight : dict or 'balanced', default=None
690::COMM;;Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
691::COMM;;If not given, all classes are supposed to have weight one.
692::COMM;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
693::COMM;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
694::COMM;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``.
695::COMM;;Note that these weights will be multiplied with sample_weight (passed
696::COMM;;through the fit method) if sample_weight is specified.
697::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
698::COMM;;*class_weight='balanced'*
699::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance, default=None
700::COMM;;Used when ``solver`` == 'sag', 'saga' or 'liblinear' to shuffle the
701::COMM;;data. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
702::COMM;;solver : {'lbfgs', 'liblinear', 'newton-cg', 'newton-cholesky', 'sag', 'saga'}, \
703::COMM;;default='lbfgs'
704::COMM;;Algorithm to use in the optimization problem. Default is 'lbfgs'.
705::COMM;;To choose a solver, you might want to consider the following aspects:
706::COMM;;- 'lbfgs' is a good default solver because it works reasonably well for a wide
707::COMM;;class of problems.
708::COMM;;- For :term:`multiclass` problems (`n_classes >= 3`), all solvers except
709::COMM;;'liblinear' minimize the full multinomial loss, 'liblinear' will raise an
710::COMM;;error.
711::COMM;;- 'newton-cholesky' is a good choice for
712::COMM;;`n_samples` >> `n_features * n_classes`, especially with one-hot encoded
713::COMM;;categorical features with rare categories. Be aware that the memory usage
714::COMM;;of this solver has a quadratic dependency on `n_features * n_classes`
715::COMM;;because it explicitly computes the full Hessian matrix.
716::COMM;;- For small datasets, 'liblinear' is a good choice, whereas 'sag'
717::COMM;;and 'saga' are faster for large ones;
718::COMM;;- 'liblinear' can only handle binary classification by default. To apply a
719::COMM;;one-versus-rest scheme for the multiclass setting one can wrap it with the
720::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.multiclass.OneVsRestClassifier`.
721::COMM;;.. warning::
722::COMM;;The choice of the algorithm depends on the penalty chosen and on
723::COMM;;(multinomial) multiclass support:
724::COMM;;================= ============================== ======================
725::COMM;;solver penalty multinomial multiclass
726::COMM;;================= ============================== ======================
727::COMM;;'lbfgs' 'l2', None yes
728::COMM;;'liblinear' 'l1', 'l2' no
729::COMM;;'newton-cg' 'l2', None yes
730::COMM;;'newton-cholesky' 'l2', None yes
731::COMM;;'sag' 'l2', None yes
732::COMM;;'saga' 'elasticnet', 'l1', 'l2', None yes
733::COMM;;================= ============================== ======================
734::COMM;;.. note::
735::COMM;;'sag' and 'saga' fast convergence is only guaranteed on features
736::COMM;;with approximately the same scale. You can preprocess the data with
737::COMM;;a scaler from :mod:`sklearn.preprocessing`.
738::COMM;;.. seealso::
739::COMM;;Refer to the :ref:`User Guide <Logistic_regression>` for more
740::COMM;;information regarding :class:`LogisticRegression` and more specifically the
741::COMM;;:ref:`Table <logistic_regression_solvers>`
742::COMM;;summarizing solver/penalty supports.
743::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
744::COMM;;Stochastic Average Gradient (SAG) descent solver. Multinomial support in
745::COMM;;version 0.18.
746::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
747::COMM;;SAGA solver.
748::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
749::COMM;;The default solver changed from 'liblinear' to 'lbfgs' in 0.22.
750::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
751::COMM;;newton-cholesky solver. Multinomial support in version 1.6.
752::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=100
753::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations taken for the solvers to converge.
754::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
755::COMM;;For the liblinear and lbfgs solvers set verbose to any positive
756::COMM;;number for verbosity.
757::COMM;;warm_start : bool, default=False
758::COMM;;When set to True, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit as
759::COMM;;initialization, otherwise, just erase the previous solution.
760::COMM;;Useless for liblinear solver. See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
761::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
762::COMM;;*warm_start* to support *lbfgs*, *newton-cg*, *sag*, *saga* solvers.
763::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
764::COMM;;Does not have any effect.
765::COMM;;.. deprecated:: 1.8
766::COMM;;`n_jobs` is deprecated in version 1.8 and will be removed in 1.10.
767::COMM;;l1_ratio : float, default=None
768::COMM;;The Elastic-Net mixing parameter, with ``0 <= l1_ratio <= 1``. Only
769::COMM;;used if ``penalty='elasticnet'``. Setting ``l1_ratio=0`` is equivalent
770::COMM;;to using ``penalty='l2'``, while setting ``l1_ratio=1`` is equivalent
771::COMM;;to using ``penalty='l1'``. For ``0 < l1_ratio <1``, the penalty is a
772::COMM;;combination of L1 and L2.
773::COMM;;Attributes
774::COMM;;----------
775::COMM;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes, )
776::COMM;;A list of class labels known to the classifier.
777::COMM;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (1, n_features) or (n_classes, n_features)
778::COMM;;Coefficient of the features in the decision function.
779::COMM;;`coef_` is of shape (1, n_features) when the given problem is binary.
780::COMM;;intercept_ : ndarray of shape (1,) or (n_classes,)
781::COMM;;Intercept (a.k.a. bias) added to the decision function.
782::COMM;;If `fit_intercept` is set to False, the intercept is set to zero.
783::COMM;;`intercept_` is of shape (1,) when the given problem is binary.
784::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
785::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
786::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
787::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
788::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
789::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
790::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
791::COMM;;n_iter_ : ndarray of shape (1, )
792::COMM;;Actual number of iterations for all classes.
793::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.20
794::COMM;;In SciPy <= 1.0.0 the number of lbfgs iterations may exceed
795::COMM;;``max_iter``. ``n_iter_`` will now report at most ``max_iter``.
796::COMM;;See Also
797::COMM;;--------

799::COMM;;the parameter ``loss="log_loss"``).

801::COMM;;Notes
802::COMM;;-----
803::COMM;;The underlying C implementation uses a random number generator to
804::COMM;;select features when fitting the model. It is thus not uncommon,
805::COMM;;to have slightly different results for the same input data. If
806::COMM;;that happens, try with a smaller tol parameter.
807::COMM;;Predict output may not match that of standalone liblinear in certain
808::COMM;;cases. See :ref:`differences from liblinear <liblinear_differences>`
809::COMM;;in the narrative documentation.

840::COMM;;For a comparison of the LogisticRegression with other classifiers see:

915::COMM;;Notes

1052::COMM;;Probability estimates.
1053::COMM;;The returned estimates for all classes are ordered by the
1054::COMM;;label of classes.

1077::COMM;;Predict logarithm of probability estimates.
1078::COMM;;The returned estimates for all classes are ordered by the
1079::COMM;;label of classes.
1080::COMM;;Parameters
1081::COMM;;----------
1082::COMM;;X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
1083::COMM;;Vector to be scored, where `n_samples` is the number of samples and
1084::COMM;;`n_features` is the number of features.
1085::COMM;;Returns
1086::COMM;;-------
1087::COMM;;T : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
1088::COMM;;Returns the log-probability of the sample for each class in the
1089::COMM;;model, where classes are ordered as they are in ``self.classes_``.
1100::COMM;;See glossary entry for :term:`cross-validation estimator`.
1101::COMM;;This class implements regularized logistic regression with implicit cross
1102::COMM;;validation for the penalty parameters `C` and `l1_ratio`, see
1103::COMM;;:class:`LogisticRegression`, using a set of available solvers.
1104::COMM;;The solvers 'lbfgs', 'newton-cg', 'newton-cholesky' and 'sag' support only L2
1105::COMM;;regularization with primal formulation. The 'liblinear'
1106::COMM;;solver supports both L1 and L2 regularization (but not both, i.e. elastic-net),
1107::COMM;;with a dual formulation only for the L2 penalty. The Elastic-Net (combination of L1
1108::COMM;;and L2) regularization is only supported by the 'saga' solver.
1109::COMM;;For the grid of `Cs` values and `l1_ratios` values, the best hyperparameter
1110::COMM;;is selected by the cross-validator
1111::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.model_selection.StratifiedKFold`, but it can be changed
1112::COMM;;using the :term:`cv` parameter. All solvers except 'liblinear' can warm-start the
1113::COMM;;coefficients (see :term:`Glossary<warm_start>`).
1114::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <logistic_regression>`.
1115::COMM;;Parameters
1116::COMM;;----------
1117::COMM;;Cs : int or list of floats, default=10
1118::COMM;;Each of the values in Cs describes the inverse of regularization
1119::COMM;;strength. If Cs is as an int, then a grid of Cs values are chosen
1120::COMM;;in a logarithmic scale between 1e-4 and 1e4.
1121::COMM;;Like in support vector machines, smaller values specify stronger
1122::COMM;;regularization.
1123::COMM;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
1124::COMM;;Specifies if a constant (a.k.a. bias or intercept) should be
1125::COMM;;added to the decision function.
1126::COMM;;cv : int or cross-validation generator, default=None
1127::COMM;;The default cross-validation generator used is Stratified K-Folds.
1128::COMM;;If an integer is provided, it specifies the number of folds, `n_folds`, used.
1129::COMM;;See the module :mod:`sklearn.model_selection` module for the
1130::COMM;;list of possible cross-validation objects.
1131::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.22
1132::COMM;;``cv`` default value if None changed from 3-fold to 5-fold.
1133::COMM;;dual : bool, default=False
1134::COMM;;Dual (constrained) or primal (regularized, see also
1135::COMM;;:ref:`this equation <regularized-logistic-loss>`) formulation. Dual formulation
1136::COMM;;is only implemented for l2 penalty with liblinear solver. Prefer dual=False when
1137::COMM;;n_samples > n_features.
1138::COMM;;penalty : {'l1', 'l2', 'elasticnet'}, default='l2'
1139::COMM;;Specify the norm of the penalty:
1140::COMM;;- `'l2'`: add a L2 penalty term (used by default);
1141::COMM;;- `'l1'`: add a L1 penalty term;
1142::COMM;;- `'elasticnet'`: both L1 and L2 penalty terms are added.
1143::COMM;;.. warning::
1144::COMM;;Some penalties may not work with some solvers. See the parameter
1145::COMM;;`solver` below, to know the compatibility between the penalty and
1146::COMM;;solver.
1147::COMM;;scoring : str or callable, default=None
1148::COMM;;The scoring method to use for cross-validation. Options:
1149::COMM;;- str: see :ref:`scoring_string_names` for options.
1150::COMM;;- callable: a scorer callable object (e.g., function) with signature
1151::COMM;;``scorer(estimator, X, y)``. See :ref:`scoring_callable` for details.
1152::COMM;;- `None`: :ref:`accuracy <accuracy_score>` is used.
1153::COMM;;solver : {'lbfgs', 'liblinear', 'newton-cg', 'newton-cholesky', 'sag', 'saga'}, \
1154::COMM;;default='lbfgs'
1155::COMM;;Algorithm to use in the optimization problem. Default is 'lbfgs'.
1156::COMM;;To choose a solver, you might want to consider the following aspects:
1157::COMM;;- 'lbfgs' is a good default solver because it works reasonably well for a wide
1158::COMM;;class of problems.
1159::COMM;;- For :term:`multiclass` problems (`n_classes >= 3`), all solvers except
1160::COMM;;'liblinear' minimize the full multinomial loss, 'liblinear' will raise an
1161::COMM;;error.
1162::COMM;;- 'newton-cholesky' is a good choice for
1163::COMM;;`n_samples` >> `n_features * n_classes`, especially with one-hot encoded
1164::COMM;;categorical features with rare categories. Be aware that the memory usage
1165::COMM;;of this solver has a quadratic dependency on `n_features * n_classes`
1166::COMM;;because it explicitly computes the full Hessian matrix.
1167::COMM;;- For small datasets, 'liblinear' is a good choice, whereas 'sag'
1168::COMM;;and 'saga' are faster for large ones;
1169::COMM;;- 'liblinear' might be slower in :class:`LogisticRegressionCV`
1170::COMM;;because it does not handle warm-starting.
1171::COMM;;- 'liblinear' can only handle binary classification by default. To apply a
1172::COMM;;one-versus-rest scheme for the multiclass setting one can wrap it with the
1173::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.multiclass.OneVsRestClassifier`.
1174::COMM;;.. warning::
1175::COMM;;The choice of the algorithm depends on the penalty chosen and on
1176::COMM;;(multinomial) multiclass support:
1177::COMM;;================= ============================== ======================
1178::COMM;;solver penalty multinomial multiclass
1179::COMM;;================= ============================== ======================
1180::COMM;;'lbfgs' 'l2' yes
1181::COMM;;'liblinear' 'l1', 'l2' no
1182::COMM;;'newton-cg' 'l2' yes
1183::COMM;;'newton-cholesky' 'l2', yes
1184::COMM;;'sag' 'l2', yes
1185::COMM;;'saga' 'elasticnet', 'l1', 'l2' yes
1186::COMM;;================= ============================== ======================
1187::COMM;;.. note::
1188::COMM;;'sag' and 'saga' fast convergence is only guaranteed on features
1189::COMM;;with approximately the same scale. You can preprocess the data with
1190::COMM;;a scaler from :mod:`sklearn.preprocessing`.
1191::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
1192::COMM;;Stochastic Average Gradient (SAG) descent solver. Multinomial support in
1193::COMM;;version 0.18.
1194::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1195::COMM;;SAGA solver.
1196::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
1197::COMM;;newton-cholesky solver. Multinomial support in version 1.6.
1198::COMM;;tol : float, default=1e-4
1199::COMM;;Tolerance for stopping criteria.
1200::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=100
1201::COMM;;Maximum number of iterations of the optimization algorithm.
1202::COMM;;class_weight : dict or 'balanced', default=None
1203::COMM;;Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
1204::COMM;;If not given, all classes are supposed to have weight one.
1205::COMM;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
1206::COMM;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
1207::COMM;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``.
1208::COMM;;Note that these weights will be multiplied with sample_weight (passed
1209::COMM;;through the fit method) if sample_weight is specified.
1210::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
1211::COMM;;class_weight == 'balanced'
1212::COMM;;n_jobs : int, default=None
1213::COMM;;Number of CPU cores used during the cross-validation loop.
1214::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
1215::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
1216::COMM;;for more details.
1217::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
1218::COMM;;For the 'liblinear', 'sag' and 'lbfgs' solvers set verbose to any
1219::COMM;;positive number for verbosity.
1220::COMM;;refit : bool, default=True
1221::COMM;;If set to True, the scores are averaged across all folds, and the
1222::COMM;;coefs and the C that corresponds to the best score is taken, and a
1223::COMM;;final refit is done using these parameters.
1224::COMM;;Otherwise the coefs, intercepts and C that correspond to the
1225::COMM;;best scores across folds are averaged.
1226::COMM;;intercept_scaling : float, default=1
1227::COMM;;Useful only when the solver `liblinear` is used
1228::COMM;;and `self.fit_intercept` is set to `True`. In this case, `x` becomes
1229::COMM;;`[x, self.intercept_scaling]`,
1230::COMM;;i.e. a "synthetic" feature with constant value equal to
1231::COMM;;`intercept_scaling` is appended to the instance vector.
1232::COMM;;The intercept becomes
1233::COMM;;``intercept_scaling * synthetic_feature_weight``.
1234::COMM;;.. note::
1235::COMM;;The synthetic feature weight is subject to L1 or L2
1236::COMM;;regularization as all other features.
1237::COMM;;To lessen the effect of regularization on synthetic feature weight
1238::COMM;;(and therefore on the intercept) `intercept_scaling` has to be increased.
1239::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance, default=None
1240::COMM;;Used when `solver='sag'`, 'saga' or 'liblinear' to shuffle the data.
1241::COMM;;Note that this only applies to the solver and not the cross-validation
1242::COMM;;generator. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
1243::COMM;;l1_ratios : list of float, default=None
1244::COMM;;The list of Elastic-Net mixing parameter, with ``0 <= l1_ratio <= 1``.
1245::COMM;;Only used if ``penalty='elasticnet'``. A value of 0 is equivalent to
1246::COMM;;using ``penalty='l2'``, while 1 is equivalent to using
1247::COMM;;``penalty='l1'``. For ``0 < l1_ratio <1``, the penalty is a combination
1248::COMM;;of L1 and L2.
1249::COMM;;use_legacy_attributes : bool, default=True
1250::COMM;;If True, use legacy values for attributes:
1251::COMM;;- `C_` is an ndarray of shape (n_classes,) with the same value repeated
1252::COMM;;- `l1_ratio_` is an ndarray of shape (n_classes,) with the same value repeated
1253::COMM;;- `coefs_paths_` is a dict with class labels as keys and ndarrays as values
1254::COMM;;- `scores_` is a dict with class labels as keys and ndarrays as values
1255::COMM;;- `n_iter_` is an ndarray of shape (1, n_folds, n_cs) or similar
1256::COMM;;If False, use new values for attributes:
1257::COMM;;- `C_` is a float
1258::COMM;;- `l1_ratio_` is a float
1259::COMM;;- `coefs_paths_` is an ndarray of shape
1260::COMM;;(n_folds, n_l1_ratios, n_cs, n_classes, n_features)
1261::COMM;;For binary problems (n_classes=2), the 2nd last dimension is 1.
1262::COMM;;- `scores_` is an ndarray of shape (n_folds, n_l1_ratios, n_cs)
1263::COMM;;- `n_iter_` is an ndarray of shape (n_folds, n_l1_ratios, n_cs)
1264::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.10
1265::COMM;;The default will change from True to False in version 1.10.
1266::COMM;;.. deprecated:: 1.10
1267::COMM;;`use_legacy_attributes` will be deprecated in version 1.10 and be removed in
1268::COMM;;1.12.
1269::COMM;;Attributes
1270::COMM;;----------
1271::COMM;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes, )
1272::COMM;;A list of class labels known to the classifier.
1273::COMM;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (1, n_features) or (n_classes, n_features)
1274::COMM;;Coefficient of the features in the decision function.
1275::COMM;;`coef_` is of shape (1, n_features) when the given problem
1276::COMM;;is binary.
1277::COMM;;intercept_ : ndarray of shape (1,) or (n_classes,)
1278::COMM;;Intercept (a.k.a. bias) added to the decision function.
1279::COMM;;If `fit_intercept` is set to False, the intercept is set to zero.
1280::COMM;;`intercept_` is of shape (1,) when the problem is binary.
1281::COMM;;Cs_ : ndarray of shape (n_cs)
1282::COMM;;Array of C i.e. inverse of regularization parameter values used
1283::COMM;;for cross-validation.
1284::COMM;;l1_ratios_ : ndarray of shape (n_l1_ratios)
1285::COMM;;Array of l1_ratios used for cross-validation. If no l1_ratio is used
1286::COMM;;(i.e. penalty is not 'elasticnet'), this is set to ``[None]``
1287::COMM;;coefs_paths_ : dict of ndarray of shape (n_folds, n_cs, n_dof) or \
1288::COMM;;(n_folds, n_cs, n_l1_ratios, n_dof)
1289::COMM;;A dict with classes as the keys, and the path of coefficients obtained
1290::COMM;;during cross-validating across each fold (`n_folds`) and then across each Cs
1291::COMM;;(`n_cs`).
1292::COMM;;The size of the coefficients is the number of degrees of freedom (`n_dof`),
1293::COMM;;i.e. without intercept `n_dof=n_features` and with intercept
1294::COMM;;`n_dof=n_features+1`.
1295::COMM;;If `penalty='elasticnet'`, there is an additional dimension for the number of
1296::COMM;;l1_ratio values (`n_l1_ratios`), which gives a shape of
1297::COMM;;``(n_folds, n_cs, n_l1_ratios_, n_dof)``.
1298::COMM;;See also parameter `use_legacy_attributes`.
1299::COMM;;scores_ : dict
1300::COMM;;A dict with classes as the keys, and the values as the
1301::COMM;;grid of scores obtained during cross-validating each fold.
1302::COMM;;The same score is repeated across all classes. Each dict value
1303::COMM;;has shape ``(n_folds, n_cs)`` or ``(n_folds, n_cs, n_l1_ratios)`` if
1304::COMM;;``penalty='elasticnet'``.
1305::COMM;;See also parameter `use_legacy_attributes`.
1306::COMM;;C_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,) or (1,)
1307::COMM;;The value of C that maps to the best score, repeated n_classes times.
1308::COMM;;If refit is set to False, the best C is the average of the
1309::COMM;;C's that correspond to the best score for each fold.
1310::COMM;;`C_` is of shape (1,) when the problem is binary.
1311::COMM;;See also parameter `use_legacy_attributes`.
1312::COMM;;l1_ratio_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,) or (n_classes - 1,)
1313::COMM;;The value of l1_ratio that maps to the best score, repeated n_classes times.
1314::COMM;;If refit is set to False, the best l1_ratio is the average of the
1315::COMM;;l1_ratio's that correspond to the best score for each fold.
1316::COMM;;`l1_ratio_` is of shape (1,) when the problem is binary.
1317::COMM;;See also parameter `use_legacy_attributes`.
1318::COMM;;n_iter_ : ndarray of shape (1, n_folds, n_cs) or (1, n_folds, n_cs, n_l1_ratios)
1319::COMM;;Actual number of iterations for all classes, folds and Cs.
1320::COMM;;If `penalty='elasticnet'`, the shape is `(1, n_folds, n_cs, n_l1_ratios)`.
1321::COMM;;See also parameter `use_legacy_attributes`.
1322::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
1323::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1324::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1325::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1326::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1327::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.

29::COMM;;def _cholesky_omp(X, y, n_nonzero_coefs, tol=None, copy_X=True, return_path=False):
62::COMM;;if copy_X:
63::COMM;;X = X.copy("F")
64::COMM;;else: # even if we are allowed to overwrite, still copy it if bad order
65::COMM;;X = np.asfortranarray(X)
66::COMM;;min_float = np.finfo(X.dtype).eps
67::COMM;;nrm2, swap = linalg.get_blas_funcs(("nrm2", "swap"), (X,))
68::COMM;;(potrs,) = get_lapack_funcs(("potrs",), (X,))
69::COMM;;alpha = np.dot(X.T, y)
70::COMM;;residual = y
71::COMM;;gamma = np.empty(0)
72::COMM;;n_active = 0
73::COMM;;indices = np.arange(X.shape[1]) # keeping track of swapping
74::COMM;;max_features = X.shape[1] if tol is not None else n_nonzero_coefs
75::COMM;;L = np.empty((max_features, max_features), dtype=X.dtype)
76::COMM;;if return_path:
77::COMM;;coefs = np.empty_like(L)
78::COMM;;while True:
79::COMM;;lam = np.argmax(np.abs(np.dot(X.T, residual)))
80::COMM;;if lam < n_active or alpha[lam] ** 2 < min_float:
81::COMM;;# atom already selected or inner product too small
82::COMM;;warnings.warn(premature, RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=2)
83::COMM;;break
84::COMM;;if n_active > 0:
85::COMM;;# Updates the Cholesky decomposition of X' X
86::COMM;;L[n_active, :n_active] = np.dot(X[:, :n_active].T, X[:, lam])
87::COMM;;linalg.solve_triangular(
88::COMM;;L[:n_active, :n_active],
89::COMM;;L[n_active, :n_active],
90::COMM;;trans=0,
91::COMM;;lower=1,
92::COMM;;overwrite_b=True,
93::COMM;;check_finite=False,
94::COMM;;)
95::COMM;;v = nrm2(L[n_active, :n_active]) ** 2
96::COMM;;Lkk = linalg.norm(X[:, lam]) ** 2 - v
97::COMM;;if Lkk <= min_float: # selected atoms are dependent
98::COMM;;warnings.warn(premature, RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=2)
99::COMM;;break
100::COMM;;L[n_active, n_active] = sqrt(Lkk)
101::COMM;;else:
102::COMM;;L[0, 0] = linalg.norm(X[:, lam])
103::COMM;;X.T[n_active], X.T[lam] = swap(X.T[n_active], X.T[lam])
104::COMM;;alpha[n_active], alpha[lam] = alpha[lam], alpha[n_active]
105::COMM;;indices[n_active], indices[lam] = indices[lam], indices[n_active]
106::COMM;;n_active += 1
107::COMM;;# solves LL'x = X'y as a composition of two triangular systems
108::COMM;;gamma, _ = potrs(
109::COMM;;L[:n_active, :n_active], alpha[:n_active], lower=True, overwrite_b=False
110::COMM;;)
111::COMM;;if return_path:
112::COMM;;coefs[:n_active, n_active - 1] = gamma
113::COMM;;residual = y - np.dot(X[:, :n_active], gamma)
114::COMM;;if tol is not None and nrm2(residual) ** 2 <= tol:
115::COMM;;break
116::COMM;;elif n_active == max_features:
117::COMM;;break
118::COMM;;if return_path:
119::COMM;;return gamma, indices[:n_active], coefs[:, :n_active], n_active
120::COMM;;else:
121::COMM;;return gamma, indices[:n_active], n_active
122::COMM;;def _gram_omp(
123::COMM;;Gram,
124::COMM;;Xy,
125::COMM;;n_nonzero_coefs,
126::COMM;;tol_0=None,
127::COMM;;tol=None,
128::COMM;;copy_Gram=True,
129::COMM;;copy_Xy=True,
130::COMM;;return_path=False,
131::COMM;;):
170::COMM;;Gram = Gram.copy("F") if copy_Gram else np.asfortranarray(Gram)
171::COMM;;if copy_Xy or not Xy.flags.writeable:
172::COMM;;Xy = Xy.copy()
173::COMM;;min_float = np.finfo(Gram.dtype).eps
174::COMM;;nrm2, swap = linalg.get_blas_funcs(("nrm2", "swap"), (Gram,))
175::COMM;;(potrs,) = get_lapack_funcs(("potrs",), (Gram,))
176::COMM;;indices = np.arange(len(Gram)) # keeping track of swapping
177::COMM;;alpha = Xy

179::COMM;;delta = 0
180::COMM;;gamma = np.empty(0)
181::COMM;;n_active = 0
182::COMM;;max_features = len(Gram) if tol is not None else n_nonzero_coefs
183::COMM;;L = np.empty((max_features, max_features), dtype=Gram.dtype)
184::COMM;;L[0, 0] = 1.0
185::COMM;;if return_path:
186::COMM;;coefs = np.empty_like(L)
187::COMM;;while True:
188::COMM;;lam = np.argmax(np.abs(alpha))
189::COMM;;if lam < n_active or alpha[lam] ** 2 < min_float:
190::COMM;;# selected same atom twice, or inner product too small
191::COMM;;warnings.warn(premature, RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=3)
192::COMM;;break
193::COMM;;if n_active > 0:
194::COMM;;L[n_active, :n_active] = Gram[lam, :n_active]
195::COMM;;linalg.solve_triangular(
196::COMM;;L[:n_active, :n_active],
197::COMM;;L[n_active, :n_active],
198::COMM;;trans=0,
199::COMM;;lower=1,
200::COMM;;overwrite_b=True,
201::COMM;;check_finite=False,
202::COMM;;)
203::COMM;;v = nrm2(L[n_active, :n_active]) ** 2
204::COMM;;Lkk = Gram[lam, lam] - v
205::COMM;;if Lkk <= min_float: # selected atoms are dependent
206::COMM;;warnings.warn(premature, RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=3)
207::COMM;;break
208::COMM;;L[n_active, n_active] = sqrt(Lkk)
209::COMM;;else:

211::COMM;;Gram[n_active], Gram[lam] = swap(Gram[n_active], Gram[lam])

213::COMM;;indices[n_active], indices[lam] = indices[lam], indices[n_active]
214::COMM;;Xy[n_active], Xy[lam] = Xy[lam], Xy[n_active]
215::COMM;;n_active += 1
216::COMM;;# solves LL'x = X'y as a composition of two triangular systems
217::COMM;;gamma, _ = potrs(
218::COMM;;L[:n_active, :n_active], Xy[:n_active], lower=True, overwrite_b=False
219::COMM;;)
220::COMM;;if return_path:

223::COMM;;alpha = Xy - beta
224::COMM;;if tol is not None:
225::COMM;;tol_curr += delta
226::COMM;;delta = np.inner(gamma, beta[:n_active])
227::COMM;;tol_curr -= delta
228::COMM;;if abs(tol_curr) <= tol:
229::COMM;;break
230::COMM;;elif n_active == max_features:
231::COMM;;break
232::COMM;;if return_path:
233::COMM;;return gamma, indices[:n_active], coefs[:, :n_active], n_active
234::COMM;;else:
235::COMM;;return gamma, indices[:n_active], n_active

25::COMM;;loss="hinge",
26::COMM;;penalty=None,
27::COMM;;learning_rate="pa1", # or "pa2"
28::COMM;;eta0=1.0, # for parameter C
29::COMM;;)
30::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <passive_aggressive>`.
31::COMM;;Parameters
32::COMM;;----------
33::COMM;;C : float, default=1.0
34::COMM;;Aggressiveness parameter for the passive-agressive algorithm, see [1].
35::COMM;;For PA-I it is the maximum step size. For PA-II it regularizes the
36::COMM;;step size (the smaller `C` the more it regularizes).
37::COMM;;As a general rule-of-thumb, `C` should be small when the data is noisy.
38::COMM;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
39::COMM;;Whether the intercept should be estimated or not. If False, the
40::COMM;;data is assumed to be already centered.
41::COMM;;max_iter : int, default=1000
42::COMM;;The maximum number of passes over the training data (aka epochs).
43::COMM;;It only impacts the behavior in the ``fit`` method, and not the
44::COMM;;:meth:`~sklearn.linear_model.PassiveAggressiveClassifier.partial_fit` method.
45::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
46::COMM;;tol : float or None, default=1e-3
47::COMM;;The stopping criterion. If it is not None, the iterations will stop
48::COMM;;when (loss > previous_loss - tol).
49::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
50::COMM;;early_stopping : bool, default=False
51::COMM;;Whether to use early stopping to terminate training when validation
52::COMM;;score is not improving. If set to True, it will automatically set aside
53::COMM;;a stratified fraction of training data as validation and terminate
54::COMM;;training when validation score is not improving by at least `tol` for
55::COMM;;`n_iter_no_change` consecutive epochs.
56::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
57::COMM;;validation_fraction : float, default=0.1
58::COMM;;The proportion of training data to set aside as validation set for
59::COMM;;early stopping. Must be between 0 and 1.
60::COMM;;Only used if early_stopping is True.
61::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
62::COMM;;n_iter_no_change : int, default=5
63::COMM;;Number of iterations with no improvement to wait before early stopping.
64::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.20
65::COMM;;shuffle : bool, default=True
66::COMM;;Whether or not the training data should be shuffled after each epoch.
67::COMM;;verbose : int, default=0
68::COMM;;The verbosity level.
69::COMM;;loss : str, default="hinge"
70::COMM;;The loss function to be used:
71::COMM;;hinge: equivalent to PA-I in the reference paper.
72::COMM;;squared_hinge: equivalent to PA-II in the reference paper.
73::COMM;;n_jobs : int or None, default=None
74::COMM;;The number of CPUs to use to do the OVA (One Versus All, for
75::COMM;;multi-class problems) computation.
76::COMM;;``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
77::COMM;;``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
78::COMM;;for more details.
79::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance, default=None
80::COMM;;Used to shuffle the training data, when ``shuffle`` is set to
81::COMM;;``True``. Pass an int for reproducible output across multiple
82::COMM;;function calls.
83::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
84::COMM;;warm_start : bool, default=False
85::COMM;;When set to True, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit as
86::COMM;;initialization, otherwise, just erase the previous solution.
87::COMM;;See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
88::COMM;;Repeatedly calling fit or partial_fit when warm_start is True can
89::COMM;;result in a different solution than when calling fit a single time
90::COMM;;because of the way the data is shuffled.
91::COMM;;class_weight : dict, {class_label: weight} or "balanced" or None, \
92::COMM;;default=None
93::COMM;;Preset for the class_weight fit parameter.
94::COMM;;Weights associated with classes. If not given, all classes
95::COMM;;are supposed to have weight one.
96::COMM;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
97::COMM;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
98::COMM;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``.
99::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.17
100::COMM;;parameter *class_weight* to automatically weight samples.
101::COMM;;average : bool or int, default=False
102::COMM;;When set to True, computes the averaged SGD weights and stores the
103::COMM;;result in the ``coef_`` attribute. If set to an int greater than 1,
104::COMM;;averaging will begin once the total number of samples seen reaches
105::COMM;;average. So average=10 will begin averaging after seeing 10 samples.
106::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
107::COMM;;parameter *average* to use weights averaging in SGD.
108::COMM;;Attributes
109::COMM;;----------
110::COMM;;coef_ : ndarray of shape (1, n_features) if n_classes == 2 else \
111::COMM;;(n_classes, n_features)
112::COMM;;Weights assigned to the features.
113::COMM;;intercept_ : ndarray of shape (1,) if n_classes == 2 else (n_classes,)
114::COMM;;Constants in decision function.
115::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
116::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
117::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
118::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
119::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
120::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
121::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
122::COMM;;n_iter_ : int
123::COMM;;The actual number of iterations to reach the stopping criterion.
124::COMM;;For multiclass fits, it is the maximum over every binary fit.
125::COMM;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)
126::COMM;;The unique classes labels.
127::COMM;;t_ : int
128::COMM;;Number of weight updates performed during training.
129::COMM;;Same as ``(n_iter_ * n_samples + 1)``.
130::COMM;;See Also
131::COMM;;--------
132::COMM;;SGDClassifier : Incrementally trained logistic regression.
133::COMM;;Perceptron : Linear perceptron classifier.

17::COMM;;The linear :class:`QuantileRegressor` optimizes the pinball loss for a
18::COMM;;desired `quantile` and is robust to outliers.
19::COMM;;This model uses an L1 regularization like
20::COMM;;:class:`~sklearn.linear_model.Lasso`.
21::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <quantile_regression>`.
22::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
23::COMM;;Parameters
24::COMM;;----------
25::COMM;;quantile : float, default=0.5
26::COMM;;The quantile that the model tries to predict. It must be strictly
27::COMM;;between 0 and 1. If 0.5 (default), the model predicts the 50%
28::COMM;;quantile, i.e. the median.
29::COMM;;alpha : float, default=1.0
30::COMM;;Regularization constant that multiplies the L1 penalty term.
31::COMM;;fit_intercept : bool, default=True
32::COMM;;Whether or not to fit the intercept.
33::COMM;;solver : {'highs-ds', 'highs-ipm', 'highs', 'interior-point', \
34::COMM;;'revised simplex'}, default='highs'
35::COMM;;Method used by :func:`scipy.optimize.linprog` to solve the linear
36::COMM;;programming formulation.
37::COMM;;It is recommended to use the highs methods because
38::COMM;;they are the fastest ones. Solvers "highs-ds", "highs-ipm" and "highs"
39::COMM;;support sparse input data and, in fact, always convert to sparse csc.
40::COMM;;From `scipy>=1.11.0`, "interior-point" is not available anymore.
41::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.4
42::COMM;;The default of `solver` changed to `"highs"` in version 1.4.
43::COMM;;solver_options : dict, default=None
44::COMM;;Additional parameters passed to :func:`scipy.optimize.linprog` as
45::COMM;;options. If `None` and if `solver='interior-point'`, then
46::COMM;;`{"lstsq": True}` is passed to :func:`scipy.optimize.linprog` for the
47::COMM;;sake of stability.
48::COMM;;Attributes
49::COMM;;----------
50::COMM;;coef_ : array of shape (n_features,)
51::COMM;;Estimated coefficients for the features.
52::COMM;;intercept_ : float
53::COMM;;The intercept of the model, aka bias term.
54::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
55::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
56::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
57::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
58::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
59::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
60::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
61::COMM;;n_iter_ : int
62::COMM;;The actual number of iterations performed by the solver.
63::COMM;;See Also
64::COMM;;--------
65::COMM;;Lasso : The Lasso is a linear model that estimates sparse coefficients
66::COMM;;with l1 regularization.
67::COMM;;HuberRegressor : Linear regression model that is robust to outliers.
68::COMM;;Examples
69::COMM;;--------
70::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.linear_model import QuantileRegressor
71::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
72::COMM;;>>> n_samples, n_features = 10, 2
73::COMM;;>>> rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
74::COMM;;>>> y = rng.randn(n_samples)
75::COMM;;>>> X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)
76::COMM;;>>> # the two following lines are optional in practice
77::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.utils.fixes import sp_version, parse_version
78::COMM;;>>> reg = QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.8).fit(X, y)
79::COMM;;>>> np.mean(y <= reg.predict(X))
80::COMM;;np.float64(0.8)

121::COMM;;Target values.

126::COMM;;self : object
