519::COMM;;def _prune_tree(self):
524::COMO;;# build pruned tree
531::COMO;;# TODO: the tree shouldn't need this param
539::COMM;;See :ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details on the pruning
540::COMM;;process.
541::COMM;;Parameters
542::COMM;;----------
543::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
544::COMM;;The training input samples. Internally, it will be converted to
545::COMM;;``dtype=np.float32`` and if a sparse matrix is provided
546::COMM;;to a sparse ``csc_matrix``.
547::COMM;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs)
548::COMM;;The target values (class labels) as integers or strings.
549::COMM;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
550::COMM;;Sample weights. If None, then samples are equally weighted. Splits
551::COMM;;that would create child nodes with net zero or negative weight are
552::COMM;;ignored while searching for a split in each node. Splits are also
553::COMM;;ignored if they would result in any single class carrying a
554::COMM;;negative weight in either child node.
555::COMM;;Returns
556::COMM;;-------
557::COMM;;ccp_path : :class:`~sklearn.utils.Bunch`
558::COMM;;Dictionary-like object, with the following attributes.
559::COMM;;ccp_alphas : ndarray
560::COMM;;Effective alphas of subtree during pruning.
561::COMM;;impurities : ndarray
562::COMM;;Sum of the impurities of the subtree leaves for the
563::COMM;;corresponding alpha value in ``ccp_alphas``.
571::COMM;;The importance of a feature is computed as the (normalized) total
572::COMM;;reduction of the criterion brought by that feature.
573::COMM;;It is also known as the Gini importance.
574::COMM;;Warning: impurity-based feature importances can be misleading for
575::COMM;;high cardinality features (many unique values). See
576::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance` as an alternative.
577::COMM;;Returns
578::COMM;;-------
579::COMM;;feature_importances_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
580::COMM;;Normalized total reduction of criteria by feature
581::COMM;;(Gini importance).
589::COMO;;# =============================================================================
590::COMO;;# Public estimators
591::COMO;;# =============================================================================
594::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <tree>`.
595::COMM;;Parameters
596::COMM;;----------
597::COMM;;criterion : {"gini", "entropy", "log_loss"}, default="gini"
598::COMM;;The function to measure the quality of a split. Supported criteria are
599::COMM;;"gini" for the Gini impurity and "log_loss" and "entropy" both for the
600::COMM;;Shannon information gain, see :ref:`tree_mathematical_formulation`.
601::COMM;;splitter : {"best", "random"}, default="best"
602::COMM;;The strategy used to choose the split at each node. Supported
603::COMM;;strategies are "best" to choose the best split and "random" to choose
604::COMM;;the best random split.
605::COMM;;max_depth : int, default=None
606::COMM;;The maximum depth of the tree. If None, then nodes are expanded until
607::COMM;;all leaves are pure or until all leaves contain less than
608::COMM;;min_samples_split samples.
609::COMM;;min_samples_split : int or float, default=2
610::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to split an internal node:
611::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_split` as the minimum number.
612::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_split` is a fraction and
613::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_split * n_samples)` are the minimum
614::COMM;;number of samples for each split.
615::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
616::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
617::COMM;;min_samples_leaf : int or float, default=1
618::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node.
619::COMM;;A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at
620::COMM;;least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and
621::COMM;;right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model,
622::COMM;;especially in regression.
623::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_leaf` as the minimum number.
624::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_leaf` is a fraction and
625::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_leaf * n_samples)` are the minimum
626::COMM;;number of samples for each node.
627::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
628::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
629::COMM;;min_weight_fraction_leaf : float, default=0.0
630::COMM;;The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all
631::COMM;;the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have
632::COMM;;equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.
633::COMM;;max_features : int, float or {"sqrt", "log2"}, default=None
634::COMM;;The number of features to consider when looking for the best split:
635::COMM;;- If int, then consider `max_features` features at each split.
636::COMM;;- If float, then `max_features` is a fraction and
637::COMM;;`max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features are considered at
638::COMM;;each split.
639::COMM;;- If "sqrt", then `max_features=sqrt(n_features)`.
640::COMM;;- If "log2", then `max_features=log2(n_features)`.
641::COMM;;- If None, then `max_features=n_features`.
642::COMM;;.. note::
643::COMM;;The search for a split does not stop until at least one
644::COMM;;valid partition of the node samples is found, even if it requires to
645::COMM;;effectively inspect more than ``max_features`` features.
646::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
647::COMM;;Controls the randomness of the estimator. The features are always
648::COMM;;randomly permuted at each split, even if ``splitter`` is set to
649::COMM;;``"best"``. When ``max_features < n_features``, the algorithm will
650::COMM;;select ``max_features`` at random at each split before finding the best
651::COMM;;split among them. But the best found split may vary across different
652::COMM;;runs, even if ``max_features=n_features``. That is the case, if the
653::COMM;;improvement of the criterion is identical for several splits and one
654::COMM;;split has to be selected at random. To obtain a deterministic behaviour
655::COMM;;during fitting, ``random_state`` has to be fixed to an integer.
656::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
657::COMM;;max_leaf_nodes : int, default=None
658::COMM;;Grow a tree with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion.
659::COMM;;Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity.
660::COMM;;If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.
661::COMM;;min_impurity_decrease : float, default=0.0
662::COMM;;A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity
663::COMM;;greater than or equal to this value.
664::COMM;;The weighted impurity decrease equation is the following::
665::COMM;;N_t / N * (impurity - N_t_R / N_t * right_impurity
666::COMM;;- N_t_L / N_t * left_impurity)
667::COMM;;where ``N`` is the total number of samples, ``N_t`` is the number of
668::COMM;;samples at the current node, ``N_t_L`` is the number of samples in the
669::COMM;;left child, and ``N_t_R`` is the number of samples in the right child.
670::COMM;;``N``, ``N_t``, ``N_t_R`` and ``N_t_L`` all refer to the weighted sum,
671::COMM;;if ``sample_weight`` is passed.
672::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
673::COMM;;class_weight : dict, list of dict or "balanced", default=None
674::COMM;;Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
675::COMM;;If None, all classes are supposed to have weight one. For
676::COMM;;multi-output problems, a list of dicts can be provided in the same
677::COMM;;order as the columns of y.
678::COMM;;Note that for multioutput (including multilabel) weights should be
679::COMM;;defined for each class of every column in its own dict. For example,
680::COMM;;for four-class multilabel classification weights should be
681::COMM;;[{0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1, 1: 5}, {0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1, 1: 1}] instead of
682::COMM;;[{1:1}, {2:5}, {3:1}, {4:1}].
683::COMM;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
684::COMM;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
685::COMM;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``
686::COMM;;For multi-output, the weights of each column of y will be multiplied.
687::COMM;;Note that these weights will be multiplied with sample_weight (passed
688::COMM;;through the fit method) if sample_weight is specified.
689::COMM;;ccp_alpha : non-negative float, default=0.0
690::COMM;;Complexity parameter used for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning. The
691::COMM;;subtree with the largest cost complexity that is smaller than
692::COMM;;``ccp_alpha`` will be chosen. By default, no pruning is performed. See
693::COMM;;:ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details. See
694::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_cost_complexity_pruning.py`
695::COMM;;for an example of such pruning.
696::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
697::COMM;;monotonic_cst : array-like of int of shape (n_features), default=None
698::COMM;;Indicates the monotonicity constraint to enforce on each feature.
699::COMM;;- 1: monotonic increase
700::COMM;;- 0: no constraint
701::COMM;;- -1: monotonic decrease
702::COMM;;If monotonic_cst is None, no constraints are applied.
703::COMM;;Monotonicity constraints are not supported for:
704::COMM;;- multiclass classifications (i.e. when `n_classes > 2`),
705::COMM;;- multioutput classifications (i.e. when `n_outputs_ > 1`),
706::COMM;;- classifications trained on data with missing values.
707::COMM;;The constraints hold over the probability of the positive class.
708::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <monotonic_cst_gbdt>`.
709::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
710::COMM;;Attributes
711::COMM;;----------
712::COMM;;classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,) or list of ndarray
713::COMM;;The classes labels (single output problem),
714::COMM;;or a list of arrays of class labels (multi-output problem).
715::COMM;;feature_importances_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
716::COMM;;The impurity-based feature importances.
717::COMM;;The higher, the more important the feature.
718::COMM;;The importance of a feature is computed as the (normalized)
719::COMM;;total reduction of the criterion brought by that feature. It is also
720::COMM;;known as the Gini importance [4]_.
721::COMM;;Warning: impurity-based feature importances can be misleading for
722::COMM;;high cardinality features (many unique values). See
723::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance` as an alternative.
724::COMM;;max_features_ : int
725::COMM;;The inferred value of max_features.
726::COMM;;n_classes_ : int or list of int
727::COMM;;The number of classes (for single output problems),
728::COMM;;or a list containing the number of classes for each
729::COMM;;output (for multi-output problems).
730::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
731::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
732::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
733::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
734::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
735::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
736::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
737::COMM;;n_outputs_ : int
738::COMM;;The number of outputs when ``fit`` is performed.
739::COMM;;tree_ : Tree instance
740::COMM;;The underlying Tree object. Please refer to
741::COMM;;``help(sklearn.tree._tree.Tree)`` for attributes of Tree object and
742::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_unveil_tree_structure.py`
743::COMM;;for basic usage of these attributes.
744::COMM;;See Also
745::COMM;;--------
746::COMM;;DecisionTreeRegressor : A decision tree regressor.
747::COMM;;Notes
748::COMM;;-----
749::COMM;;The default values for the parameters controlling the size of the trees
750::COMM;;(e.g. ``max_depth``, ``min_samples_leaf``, etc.) lead to fully grown and
751::COMM;;unpruned trees which can potentially be very large on some data sets. To
752::COMM;;reduce memory consumption, the complexity and size of the trees should be
753::COMM;;controlled by setting those parameter values.
754::COMM;;The :meth:`predict` method operates using the :func:`numpy.argmax`
755::COMM;;function on the outputs of :meth:`predict_proba`. This means that in
756::COMM;;case the highest predicted probabilities are tied, the classifier will
757::COMM;;predict the tied class with the lowest index in :term:`classes_`.
758::COMM;;References
759::COMM;;----------
760::COMM;;.. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_tree_learning
761::COMM;;.. [2] L. Breiman, J. Friedman, R. Olshen, and C. Stone, "Classification
762::COMM;;and Regression Trees", Wadsworth, Belmont, CA, 1984.
763::COMM;;.. [3] T. Hastie, R. Tibshirani and J. Friedman. "Elements of Statistical
764::COMM;;Learning", Springer, 2009.
765::COMM;;.. [4] L. Breiman, and A. Cutler, "Random Forests",
766::COMM;;https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~breiman/RandomForests/cc_home.htm
767::COMM;;Examples
768::COMM;;--------
769::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
770::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
771::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
772::COMM;;>>> clf = DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=0)
773::COMM;;>>> iris = load_iris()
774::COMM;;>>> cross_val_score(clf, iris.data, iris.target, cv=10)
775::COMM;;... # doctest: +SKIP
776::COMM;;...
777::COMM;;array([ 1. , 0.93, 0.86, 0.93, 0.93,
778::COMM;;0.93, 0.93, 1. , 0.93, 1. ])
780::COMO;;# "check_input" is used for optimisation and isn't something to be passed
781::COMO;;# around in a pipeline.
824::COMM;;Parameters
825::COMM;;----------
826::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
827::COMM;;The training input samples. Internally, it will be converted to
828::COMM;;``dtype=np.float32`` and if a sparse matrix is provided
829::COMM;;to a sparse ``csc_matrix``.
830::COMM;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs)
831::COMM;;The target values (class labels) as integers or strings.
832::COMM;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
833::COMM;;Sample weights. If None, then samples are equally weighted. Splits
834::COMM;;that would create child nodes with net zero or negative weight are
835::COMM;;ignored while searching for a split in each node. Splits are also
836::COMM;;ignored if they would result in any single class carrying a
837::COMM;;negative weight in either child node.
838::COMM;;check_input : bool, default=True
839::COMM;;Allow to bypass several input checking.
840::COMM;;Don't use this parameter unless you know what you're doing.
841::COMM;;Returns
842::COMM;;-------
843::COMM;;self : DecisionTreeClassifier
844::COMM;;Fitted estimator.
855::COMM;;The predicted class probability is the fraction of samples of the same
856::COMM;;class in a leaf.
857::COMM;;Parameters
858::COMM;;----------
859::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
860::COMM;;The input samples. Internally, it will be converted to
861::COMM;;``dtype=np.float32`` and if a sparse matrix is provided
862::COMM;;to a sparse ``csr_matrix``.
863::COMM;;check_input : bool, default=True
864::COMM;;Allow to bypass several input checking.
865::COMM;;Don't use this parameter unless you know what you're doing.
866::COMM;;Returns
867::COMM;;-------
868::COMM;;proba : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes) or list of n_outputs \
869::COMM;;such arrays if n_outputs > 1
870::COMM;;The class probabilities of the input samples. The order of the
871::COMM;;classes corresponds to that in the attribute :term:`classes_`.
886::COMM;;Parameters
887::COMM;;----------
888::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
889::COMM;;The input samples. Internally, it will be converted to
890::COMM;;``dtype=np.float32`` and if a sparse matrix is provided
891::COMM;;to a sparse ``csr_matrix``.
892::COMM;;Returns
893::COMM;;-------
894::COMM;;proba : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes) or list of n_outputs \
895::COMM;;such arrays if n_outputs > 1
896::COMM;;The class log-probabilities of the input samples. The order of the
897::COMM;;classes corresponds to that in the attribute :term:`classes_`.
908::COMO;;# XXX: nan is only supported for dense arrays, but we set this for
909::COMO;;# common test to pass, specifically: check_estimators_nan_inf
920::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <tree>`.
921::COMM;;Parameters
922::COMM;;----------
923::COMM;;criterion : {"squared_error", "friedman_mse", "absolute_error", \
924::COMM;;"poisson"}, default="squared_error"
925::COMM;;The function to measure the quality of a split. Supported criteria
926::COMM;;are "squared_error" for the mean squared error, which is equal to
927::COMM;;variance reduction as feature selection criterion and minimizes the L2
928::COMM;;loss using the mean of each terminal node, "friedman_mse", which uses
929::COMM;;mean squared error with Friedman's improvement score for potential
930::COMM;;splits, "absolute_error" for the mean absolute error, which minimizes
931::COMM;;the L1 loss using the median of each terminal node, and "poisson" which
932::COMM;;uses reduction in the half mean Poisson deviance to find splits.
933::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.18
934::COMM;;Mean Absolute Error (MAE) criterion.
935::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
936::COMM;;Poisson deviance criterion.
937::COMM;;splitter : {"best", "random"}, default="best"
938::COMM;;The strategy used to choose the split at each node. Supported
939::COMM;;strategies are "best" to choose the best split and "random" to choose
940::COMM;;the best random split.
941::COMM;;max_depth : int, default=None
942::COMM;;The maximum depth of the tree. If None, then nodes are expanded until
943::COMM;;all leaves are pure or until all leaves contain less than
944::COMM;;min_samples_split samples.
945::COMM;;For an example of how ``max_depth`` influences the model, see
946::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_tree_regression.py`.
947::COMM;;min_samples_split : int or float, default=2
948::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to split an internal node:
949::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_split` as the minimum number.
950::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_split` is a fraction and
951::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_split * n_samples)` are the minimum
952::COMM;;number of samples for each split.
953::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
954::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
955::COMM;;min_samples_leaf : int or float, default=1
956::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node.
957::COMM;;A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at
958::COMM;;least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and
959::COMM;;right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model,
960::COMM;;especially in regression.
961::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_leaf` as the minimum number.
962::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_leaf` is a fraction and
963::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_leaf * n_samples)` are the minimum
964::COMM;;number of samples for each node.
965::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
966::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
967::COMM;;min_weight_fraction_leaf : float, default=0.0
968::COMM;;The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all
969::COMM;;the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have
970::COMM;;equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.
971::COMM;;max_features : int, float or {"sqrt", "log2"}, default=None
972::COMM;;The number of features to consider when looking for the best split:
973::COMM;;- If int, then consider `max_features` features at each split.
974::COMM;;- If float, then `max_features` is a fraction and
975::COMM;;`max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features are considered at each
976::COMM;;split.
977::COMM;;- If "sqrt", then `max_features=sqrt(n_features)`.
978::COMM;;- If "log2", then `max_features=log2(n_features)`.
979::COMM;;- If None, then `max_features=n_features`.
980::COMM;;Note: the search for a split does not stop until at least one
981::COMM;;valid partition of the node samples is found, even if it requires to
982::COMM;;effectively inspect more than ``max_features`` features.
983::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
984::COMM;;Controls the randomness of the estimator. The features are always
985::COMM;;randomly permuted at each split, even if ``splitter`` is set to
986::COMM;;``"best"``. When ``max_features < n_features``, the algorithm will
987::COMM;;select ``max_features`` at random at each split before finding the best
988::COMM;;split among them. But the best found split may vary across different
989::COMM;;runs, even if ``max_features=n_features``. That is the case, if the
990::COMM;;improvement of the criterion is identical for several splits and one
991::COMM;;split has to be selected at random. To obtain a deterministic behaviour
992::COMM;;during fitting, ``random_state`` has to be fixed to an integer.
993::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
994::COMM;;max_leaf_nodes : int, default=None
995::COMM;;Grow a tree with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion.
996::COMM;;Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity.
997::COMM;;If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.
998::COMM;;min_impurity_decrease : float, default=0.0
999::COMM;;A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity
1000::COMM;;greater than or equal to this value.
1001::COMM;;The weighted impurity decrease equation is the following::
1002::COMM;;N_t / N * (impurity - N_t_R / N_t * right_impurity
1003::COMM;;- N_t_L / N_t * left_impurity)
1004::COMM;;where ``N`` is the total number of samples, ``N_t`` is the number of
1005::COMM;;samples at the current node, ``N_t_L`` is the number of samples in the
1006::COMM;;left child, and ``N_t_R`` is the number of samples in the right child.
1007::COMM;;``N``, ``N_t``, ``N_t_R`` and ``N_t_L`` all refer to the weighted sum,
1008::COMM;;if ``sample_weight`` is passed.
1009::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1010::COMM;;ccp_alpha : non-negative float, default=0.0
1011::COMM;;Complexity parameter used for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning. The
1012::COMM;;subtree with the largest cost complexity that is smaller than
1013::COMM;;``ccp_alpha`` will be chosen. By default, no pruning is performed. See
1014::COMM;;:ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details. See
1015::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_cost_complexity_pruning.py`
1016::COMM;;for an example of such pruning.
1017::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1018::COMM;;monotonic_cst : array-like of int of shape (n_features), default=None
1019::COMM;;Indicates the monotonicity constraint to enforce on each feature.
1020::COMM;;- 1: monotonic increase
1021::COMM;;- 0: no constraint
1022::COMM;;- -1: monotonic decrease
1023::COMM;;If monotonic_cst is None, no constraints are applied.
1024::COMM;;Monotonicity constraints are not supported for:
1025::COMM;;- multioutput regressions (i.e. when `n_outputs_ > 1`),
1026::COMM;;- regressions trained on data with missing values.
1027::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <monotonic_cst_gbdt>`.
1028::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
1029::COMM;;Attributes
1030::COMM;;----------
1031::COMM;;feature_importances_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
1032::COMM;;The feature importances.
1033::COMM;;The higher, the more important the feature.
1034::COMM;;The importance of a feature is computed as the
1035::COMM;;(normalized) total reduction of the criterion brought
1036::COMM;;by that feature. It is also known as the Gini importance [4]_.
1037::COMM;;Warning: impurity-based feature importances can be misleading for
1038::COMM;;high cardinality features (many unique values). See
1039::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance` as an alternative.
1040::COMM;;max_features_ : int
1041::COMM;;The inferred value of max_features.
1042::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
1043::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1044::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1045::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1046::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1047::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
1048::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1049::COMM;;n_outputs_ : int
1050::COMM;;The number of outputs when ``fit`` is performed.
1051::COMM;;tree_ : Tree instance
1052::COMM;;The underlying Tree object. Please refer to
1053::COMM;;``help(sklearn.tree._tree.Tree)`` for attributes of Tree object and
1054::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_unveil_tree_structure.py`
1055::COMM;;for basic usage of these attributes.
1056::COMM;;See Also
1057::COMM;;--------
1058::COMM;;DecisionTreeClassifier : A decision tree classifier.
1059::COMM;;Notes
1060::COMM;;-----
1061::COMM;;The default values for the parameters controlling the size of the trees
1062::COMM;;(e.g. ``max_depth``, ``min_samples_leaf``, etc.) lead to fully grown and
1063::COMM;;unpruned trees which can potentially be very large on some data sets. To
1064::COMM;;reduce memory consumption, the complexity and size of the trees should be
1065::COMM;;controlled by setting those parameter values.
1066::COMM;;References
1067::COMM;;----------
1068::COMM;;.. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_tree_learning
1069::COMM;;.. [2] L. Breiman, J. Friedman, R. Olshen, and C. Stone, "Classification
1070::COMM;;and Regression Trees", Wadsworth, Belmont, CA, 1984.
1071::COMM;;.. [3] T. Hastie, R. Tibshirani and J. Friedman. "Elements of Statistical
1072::COMM;;Learning", Springer, 2009.
1073::COMM;;.. [4] L. Breiman, and A. Cutler, "Random Forests",
1074::COMM;;https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~breiman/RandomForests/cc_home.htm

1076::COMM;;--------
1077::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import load_diabetes
1078::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
1079::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeRegressor
1080::COMM;;>>> X, y = load_diabetes(return_X_y=True)
1081::COMM;;>>> regressor = DecisionTreeRegressor(random_state=0)
1082::COMM;;>>> cross_val_score(regressor, X, y, cv=10)
1083::COMM;;... # doctest: +SKIP
1084::COMM;;...
1085::COMM;;array([-0.39, -0.46, 0.02, 0.06, -0.50,
1086::COMM;;0.16, 0.11, -0.73, -0.30, -0.00])
1088::COMO;;# "check_input" is used for optimisation and isn't something to be passed
1089::COMO;;# around in a pipeline.
1131::COMM;;Parameters
1132::COMM;;----------
1133::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
1134::COMM;;The training input samples. Internally, it will be converted to
1135::COMM;;``dtype=np.float32`` and if a sparse matrix is provided
1136::COMM;;to a sparse ``csc_matrix``.
1137::COMM;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_outputs)
1138::COMM;;The target values (real numbers). Use ``dtype=np.float64`` and
1139::COMM;;``order='C'`` for maximum efficiency.
1140::COMM;;sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
1141::COMM;;Sample weights. If None, then samples are equally weighted. Splits
1142::COMM;;that would create child nodes with net zero or negative weight are
1143::COMM;;ignored while searching for a split in each node.
1144::COMM;;check_input : bool, default=True
1145::COMM;;Allow to bypass several input checking.
1146::COMM;;Don't use this parameter unless you know what you're doing.
1147::COMM;;Returns
1148::COMM;;-------
1149::COMM;;self : DecisionTreeRegressor
1150::COMM;;Fitted estimator.
1161::COMM;;Parameters
1162::COMM;;----------
1163::COMM;;grid : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_target_features), dtype=np.float32
1164::COMM;;The grid points on which the partial dependence should be
1165::COMM;;evaluated.
1166::COMM;;target_features : ndarray of shape (n_target_features), dtype=np.intp
1167::COMM;;The set of target features for which the partial dependence
1168::COMM;;should be evaluated.
1169::COMM;;Returns
1170::COMM;;-------
1171::COMM;;averaged_predictions : ndarray of shape (n_samples,), dtype=np.float64
1172::COMM;;The value of the partial dependence function on each grid point.
1185::COMO;;# XXX: nan is only supported for dense arrays, but we set this for
1186::COMO;;# common test to pass, specifically: check_estimators_nan_inf
1196::COMM;;Extra-trees differ from classic decision trees in the way they are built.
1197::COMM;;When looking for the best split to separate the samples of a node into two
1198::COMM;;groups, random splits are drawn for each of the `max_features` randomly
1199::COMM;;selected features and the best split among those is chosen. When
1200::COMM;;`max_features` is set 1, this amounts to building a totally random
1201::COMM;;decision tree.
1202::COMM;;Warning: Extra-trees should only be used within ensemble methods.
1203::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <tree>`.
1204::COMM;;Parameters
1205::COMM;;----------
1206::COMM;;criterion : {"gini", "entropy", "log_loss"}, default="gini"
1207::COMM;;The function to measure the quality of a split. Supported criteria are
1208::COMM;;"gini" for the Gini impurity and "log_loss" and "entropy" both for the
1209::COMM;;Shannon information gain, see :ref:`tree_mathematical_formulation`.
1210::COMM;;splitter : {"random", "best"}, default="random"
1211::COMM;;The strategy used to choose the split at each node. Supported
1212::COMM;;strategies are "best" to choose the best split and "random" to choose
1213::COMM;;the best random split.
1214::COMM;;max_depth : int, default=None
1215::COMM;;The maximum depth of the tree. If None, then nodes are expanded until
1216::COMM;;all leaves are pure or until all leaves contain less than
1217::COMM;;min_samples_split samples.
1218::COMM;;min_samples_split : int or float, default=2
1219::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to split an internal node:
1220::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_split` as the minimum number.
1221::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_split` is a fraction and
1222::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_split * n_samples)` are the minimum
1223::COMM;;number of samples for each split.
1224::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1225::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1226::COMM;;min_samples_leaf : int or float, default=1
1227::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node.
1228::COMM;;A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at
1229::COMM;;least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and
1230::COMM;;right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model,
1231::COMM;;especially in regression.
1232::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_leaf` as the minimum number.
1233::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_leaf` is a fraction and
1234::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_leaf * n_samples)` are the minimum
1235::COMM;;number of samples for each node.
1236::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1237::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1238::COMM;;min_weight_fraction_leaf : float, default=0.0
1239::COMM;;The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all
1240::COMM;;the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have
1241::COMM;;equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.
1242::COMM;;max_features : int, float, {"sqrt", "log2"} or None, default="sqrt"
1243::COMM;;The number of features to consider when looking for the best split:
1244::COMM;;- If int, then consider `max_features` features at each split.
1245::COMM;;- If float, then `max_features` is a fraction and
1246::COMM;;`max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features are considered at
1247::COMM;;each split.
1248::COMM;;- If "sqrt", then `max_features=sqrt(n_features)`.
1249::COMM;;- If "log2", then `max_features=log2(n_features)`.
1250::COMM;;- If None, then `max_features=n_features`.
1251::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
1252::COMM;;The default of `max_features` changed from `"auto"` to `"sqrt"`.
1253::COMM;;Note: the search for a split does not stop until at least one
1254::COMM;;valid partition of the node samples is found, even if it requires to
1255::COMM;;effectively inspect more than ``max_features`` features.
1256::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1257::COMM;;Used to pick randomly the `max_features` used at each split.
1258::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
1259::COMM;;max_leaf_nodes : int, default=None
1260::COMM;;Grow a tree with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion.
1261::COMM;;Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity.
1262::COMM;;If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.
1263::COMM;;min_impurity_decrease : float, default=0.0
1264::COMM;;A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity
1265::COMM;;greater than or equal to this value.
1266::COMM;;The weighted impurity decrease equation is the following::
1267::COMM;;N_t / N * (impurity - N_t_R / N_t * right_impurity
1268::COMM;;- N_t_L / N_t * left_impurity)
1269::COMM;;where ``N`` is the total number of samples, ``N_t`` is the number of
1270::COMM;;samples at the current node, ``N_t_L`` is the number of samples in the
1271::COMM;;left child, and ``N_t_R`` is the number of samples in the right child.
1272::COMM;;``N``, ``N_t``, ``N_t_R`` and ``N_t_L`` all refer to the weighted sum,
1273::COMM;;if ``sample_weight`` is passed.
1274::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1275::COMM;;class_weight : dict, list of dict or "balanced", default=None
1276::COMM;;Weights associated with classes in the form ``{class_label: weight}``.
1277::COMM;;If None, all classes are supposed to have weight one. For
1278::COMM;;multi-output problems, a list of dicts can be provided in the same
1279::COMM;;order as the columns of y.
1280::COMM;;Note that for multioutput (including multilabel) weights should be
1281::COMM;;defined for each class of every column in its own dict. For example,
1282::COMM;;for four-class multilabel classification weights should be
1283::COMM;;[{0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1, 1: 5}, {0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1, 1: 1}] instead of
1284::COMM;;[{1:1}, {2:5}, {3:1}, {4:1}].
1285::COMM;;The "balanced" mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust
1286::COMM;;weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data
1287::COMM;;as ``n_samples / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))``
1288::COMM;;For multi-output, the weights of each column of y will be multiplied.
1289::COMM;;Note that these weights will be multiplied with sample_weight (passed
1290::COMM;;through the fit method) if sample_weight is specified.
1291::COMM;;ccp_alpha : non-negative float, default=0.0
1292::COMM;;Complexity parameter used for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning. The
1293::COMM;;subtree with the largest cost complexity that is smaller than
1294::COMM;;``ccp_alpha`` will be chosen. By default, no pruning is performed. See
1295::COMM;;:ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details. See
1296::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_cost_complexity_pruning.py`
1297::COMM;;for an example of such pruning.
1298::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1299::COMM;;monotonic_cst : array-like of int of shape (n_features), default=None
1300::COMM;;Indicates the monotonicity constraint to enforce on each feature.
1301::COMM;;- 1: monotonic increase
1302::COMM;;- 0: no constraint
1303::COMM;;- -1: monotonic decrease
1304::COMM;;If monotonic_cst is None, no constraints are applied.
1305::COMM;;Monotonicity constraints are not supported for:
1306::COMM;;- multiclass classifications (i.e. when `n_classes > 2`),
1307::COMM;;- multioutput classifications (i.e. when `n_outputs_ > 1`),
1308::COMM;;- classifications trained on data with missing values.
1309::COMM;;The constraints hold over the probability of the positive class.
1310::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <monotonic_cst_gbdt>`.
1311::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4

1315::COMM;;The classes labels (single output problem),
1316::COMM;;or a list of arrays of class labels (multi-output problem).
1317::COMM;;max_features_ : int
1318::COMM;;The inferred value of max_features.
1319::COMM;;n_classes_ : int or list of int
1320::COMM;;The number of classes (for single output problems),
1321::COMM;;or a list containing the number of classes for each
1322::COMM;;output (for multi-output problems).
1323::COMM;;feature_importances_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
1324::COMM;;The impurity-based feature importances.
1325::COMM;;The higher, the more important the feature.
1326::COMM;;The importance of a feature is computed as the (normalized)
1327::COMM;;total reduction of the criterion brought by that feature. It is also
1328::COMM;;known as the Gini importance.
1329::COMM;;Warning: impurity-based feature importances can be misleading for
1330::COMM;;high cardinality features (many unique values). See
1331::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance` as an alternative.
1332::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
1333::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1334::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1335::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1336::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1337::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
1338::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1339::COMM;;n_outputs_ : int
1340::COMM;;The number of outputs when ``fit`` is performed.
1341::COMM;;tree_ : Tree instance
1342::COMM;;The underlying Tree object. Please refer to
1343::COMM;;``help(sklearn.tree._tree.Tree)`` for attributes of Tree object and
1344::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_unveil_tree_structure.py`
1345::COMM;;for basic usage of these attributes.
1346::COMM;;See Also
1347::COMM;;--------
1348::COMM;;ExtraTreeRegressor : An extremely randomized tree regressor.
1349::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier : An extra-trees classifier.
1350::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor : An extra-trees regressor.
1351::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier : A random forest classifier.
1352::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestRegressor : A random forest regressor.
1353::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.RandomTreesEmbedding : An ensemble of
1354::COMM;;totally random trees.
1355::COMM;;Notes
1356::COMM;;-----
1357::COMM;;The default values for the parameters controlling the size of the trees
1358::COMM;;(e.g. ``max_depth``, ``min_samples_leaf``, etc.) lead to fully grown and
1359::COMM;;unpruned trees which can potentially be very large on some data sets. To
1360::COMM;;reduce memory consumption, the complexity and size of the trees should be
1361::COMM;;controlled by setting those parameter values.
1362::COMM;;References
1363::COMM;;----------
1364::COMM;;.. [1] P. Geurts, D. Ernst., and L. Wehenkel, "Extremely randomized trees",
1365::COMM;;Machine Learning, 63(1), 3-42, 2006.
1366::COMM;;Examples
1367::COMM;;--------
1368::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
1369::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
1370::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.ensemble import BaggingClassifier
1371::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.tree import ExtraTreeClassifier
1372::COMM;;>>> X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
1373::COMM;;>>> X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
1374::COMM;;... X, y, random_state=0)
1375::COMM;;>>> extra_tree = ExtraTreeClassifier(random_state=0)
1376::COMM;;>>> cls = BaggingClassifier(extra_tree, random_state=0).fit(
1377::COMM;;... X_train, y_train)
1378::COMM;;>>> cls.score(X_test, y_test)
1379::COMM;;0.8947
1415::COMO;;# XXX: nan is only supported for dense arrays, but we set this for the
1416::COMO;;# common test to pass, specifically: check_estimators_nan_inf
1427::COMM;;Extra-trees differ from classic decision trees in the way they are built.
1428::COMM;;When looking for the best split to separate the samples of a node into two
1429::COMM;;groups, random splits are drawn for each of the `max_features` randomly
1430::COMM;;selected features and the best split among those is chosen. When
1431::COMM;;`max_features` is set 1, this amounts to building a totally random
1432::COMM;;decision tree.
1433::COMM;;Warning: Extra-trees should only be used within ensemble methods.
1434::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <tree>`.
1435::COMM;;Parameters
1436::COMM;;----------
1437::COMM;;criterion : {"squared_error", "friedman_mse", "absolute_error", "poisson"}, \
1438::COMM;;default="squared_error"
1439::COMM;;The function to measure the quality of a split. Supported criteria
1440::COMM;;are "squared_error" for the mean squared error, which is equal to
1441::COMM;;variance reduction as feature selection criterion and minimizes the L2
1442::COMM;;loss using the mean of each terminal node, "friedman_mse", which uses
1443::COMM;;mean squared error with Friedman's improvement score for potential
1444::COMM;;splits, "absolute_error" for the mean absolute error, which minimizes
1445::COMM;;the L1 loss using the median of each terminal node, and "poisson" which
1446::COMM;;uses reduction in Poisson deviance to find splits.
1447::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.18
1448::COMM;;Mean Absolute Error (MAE) criterion.
1449::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1450::COMM;;Poisson deviance criterion.
1451::COMM;;splitter : {"random", "best"}, default="random"
1452::COMM;;The strategy used to choose the split at each node. Supported
1453::COMM;;strategies are "best" to choose the best split and "random" to choose
1454::COMM;;the best random split.
1455::COMM;;max_depth : int, default=None
1456::COMM;;The maximum depth of the tree. If None, then nodes are expanded until
1457::COMM;;all leaves are pure or until all leaves contain less than
1458::COMM;;min_samples_split samples.
1459::COMM;;min_samples_split : int or float, default=2
1460::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to split an internal node:
1461::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_split` as the minimum number.
1462::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_split` is a fraction and
1463::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_split * n_samples)` are the minimum
1464::COMM;;number of samples for each split.
1465::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1466::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1467::COMM;;min_samples_leaf : int or float, default=1
1468::COMM;;The minimum number of samples required to be at a leaf node.
1469::COMM;;A split point at any depth will only be considered if it leaves at
1470::COMM;;least ``min_samples_leaf`` training samples in each of the left and
1471::COMM;;right branches. This may have the effect of smoothing the model,
1472::COMM;;especially in regression.
1473::COMM;;- If int, then consider `min_samples_leaf` as the minimum number.
1474::COMM;;- If float, then `min_samples_leaf` is a fraction and
1475::COMM;;`ceil(min_samples_leaf * n_samples)` are the minimum
1476::COMM;;number of samples for each node.
1477::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
1478::COMM;;Added float values for fractions.
1479::COMM;;min_weight_fraction_leaf : float, default=0.0
1480::COMM;;The minimum weighted fraction of the sum total of weights (of all
1481::COMM;;the input samples) required to be at a leaf node. Samples have
1482::COMM;;equal weight when sample_weight is not provided.
1483::COMM;;max_features : int, float, {"sqrt", "log2"} or None, default=1.0
1484::COMM;;The number of features to consider when looking for the best split:
1485::COMM;;- If int, then consider `max_features` features at each split.
1486::COMM;;- If float, then `max_features` is a fraction and
1487::COMM;;`max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_))` features are considered at each
1488::COMM;;split.
1489::COMM;;- If "sqrt", then `max_features=sqrt(n_features)`.
1490::COMM;;- If "log2", then `max_features=log2(n_features)`.
1491::COMM;;- If None, then `max_features=n_features`.
1492::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.1
1493::COMM;;The default of `max_features` changed from `"auto"` to `1.0`.
1494::COMM;;Note: the search for a split does not stop until at least one
1495::COMM;;valid partition of the node samples is found, even if it requires to
1496::COMM;;effectively inspect more than ``max_features`` features.
1497::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default=None
1498::COMM;;Used to pick randomly the `max_features` used at each split.
1499::COMM;;See :term:`Glossary <random_state>` for details.
1500::COMM;;min_impurity_decrease : float, default=0.0
1501::COMM;;A node will be split if this split induces a decrease of the impurity
1502::COMM;;greater than or equal to this value.
1503::COMM;;The weighted impurity decrease equation is the following::
1504::COMM;;N_t / N * (impurity - N_t_R / N_t * right_impurity
1505::COMM;;- N_t_L / N_t * left_impurity)
1506::COMM;;where ``N`` is the total number of samples, ``N_t`` is the number of
1507::COMM;;samples at the current node, ``N_t_L`` is the number of samples in the
1508::COMM;;left child, and ``N_t_R`` is the number of samples in the right child.
1509::COMM;;``N``, ``N_t``, ``N_t_R`` and ``N_t_L`` all refer to the weighted sum,
1510::COMM;;if ``sample_weight`` is passed.
1511::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.19
1512::COMM;;max_leaf_nodes : int, default=None
1513::COMM;;Grow a tree with ``max_leaf_nodes`` in best-first fashion.
1514::COMM;;Best nodes are defined as relative reduction in impurity.
1515::COMM;;If None then unlimited number of leaf nodes.
1516::COMM;;ccp_alpha : non-negative float, default=0.0
1517::COMM;;Complexity parameter used for Minimal Cost-Complexity Pruning. The
1518::COMM;;subtree with the largest cost complexity that is smaller than
1519::COMM;;``ccp_alpha`` will be chosen. By default, no pruning is performed. See
1520::COMM;;:ref:`minimal_cost_complexity_pruning` for details. See
1521::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_cost_complexity_pruning.py`
1522::COMM;;for an example of such pruning.
1523::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.22
1524::COMM;;monotonic_cst : array-like of int of shape (n_features), default=None
1525::COMM;;Indicates the monotonicity constraint to enforce on each feature.
1526::COMM;;- 1: monotonic increase
1527::COMM;;- 0: no constraint
1528::COMM;;- -1: monotonic decrease
1529::COMM;;If monotonic_cst is None, no constraints are applied.
1530::COMM;;Monotonicity constraints are not supported for:
1531::COMM;;- multioutput regressions (i.e. when `n_outputs_ > 1`),
1532::COMM;;- regressions trained on data with missing values.
1533::COMM;;Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <monotonic_cst_gbdt>`.
1534::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.4
1535::COMM;;Attributes
1536::COMM;;----------
1537::COMM;;max_features_ : int
1538::COMM;;The inferred value of max_features.
1539::COMM;;n_features_in_ : int
1540::COMM;;Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.
1541::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.24
1542::COMM;;feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
1543::COMM;;Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
1544::COMM;;has feature names that are all strings.
1545::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.0
1546::COMM;;feature_importances_ : ndarray of shape (n_features,)
1547::COMM;;Return impurity-based feature importances (the higher, the more
1548::COMM;;important the feature).
1549::COMM;;Warning: impurity-based feature importances can be misleading for
1550::COMM;;high cardinality features (many unique values). See
1551::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance` as an alternative.
1552::COMM;;n_outputs_ : int
1553::COMM;;The number of outputs when ``fit`` is performed.
1554::COMM;;tree_ : Tree instance
1555::COMM;;The underlying Tree object. Please refer to
1556::COMM;;``help(sklearn.tree._tree.Tree)`` for attributes of Tree object and
1557::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_tree_plot_unveil_tree_structure.py`
1558::COMM;;for basic usage of these attributes.
1559::COMM;;See Also

1562::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier : An extra-trees classifier.
1563::COMM;;sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor : An extra-trees regressor.
1564::COMM;;Notes
1565::COMM;;-----
1566::COMM;;The default values for the parameters controlling the size of the trees
1567::COMM;;(e.g. ``max_depth``, ``min_samples_leaf``, etc.) lead to fully grown and
1568::COMM;;unpruned trees which can potentially be very large on some data sets. To
1569::COMM;;reduce memory consumption, the complexity and size of the trees should be
1570::COMM;;controlled by setting those parameter values.
1571::COMM;;References
1572::COMM;;----------
1573::COMM;;.. [1] P. Geurts, D. Ernst., and L. Wehenkel, "Extremely randomized trees",

707::COMM;;This function generates a GraphViz representation of the decision tree,
708::COMM;;which is then written into `out_file`. Once exported, graphical renderings

715::COMM;;"Failed, min_impurity_decrease = {0} > {1}".format(
716::COMM;;est.min_impurity_decrease, expected_decrease
717::COMM;;)
718::COMM;;)
719::COMM;;est.fit(X, y)
720::COMM;;for node in range(est.tree_.node_count):
721::COMM;;# If current node is a not leaf node, check if the split was
722::COMM;;# justified w.r.t the min_impurity_decrease

724::COMM;;imp_parent = est.tree_.impurity[node]
725::COMM;;wtd_n_node = est.tree_.weighted_n_node_samples[node]
726::COMM;;left = est.tree_.children_left[node]
727::COMM;;wtd_n_left = est.tree_.weighted_n_node_samples[left]
728::COMM;;imp_left = est.tree_.impurity[left]
729::COMM;;wtd_imp_left = wtd_n_left * imp_left
730::COMM;;right = est.tree_.children_right[node]
731::COMM;;wtd_n_right = est.tree_.weighted_n_node_samples[right]
732::COMM;;imp_right = est.tree_.impurity[right]

734::COMM;;wtd_avg_left_right_imp = wtd_imp_right + wtd_imp_left
735::COMM;;wtd_avg_left_right_imp /= wtd_n_node
736::COMM;;fractional_node_weight = (
737::COMM;;est.tree_.weighted_n_node_samples[node] / X.shape[0]
738::COMM;;)
739::COMM;;actual_decrease = fractional_node_weight * (
740::COMM;;imp_parent - wtd_avg_left_right_imp
741::COMM;;)

1418::COMM;;------------------
1419::COMM;;| X | y | weight |
1420::COMM;;------------------
1421::COMM;;| 3 | 3 | 0.1 |
1422::COMM;;| 5 | 3 | 0.3 |
1423::COMM;;| 8 | 4 | 1.0 |
1424::COMM;;| 3 | 6 | 0.6 |
1425::COMM;;| 5 | 7 | 0.3 |
1426::COMM;;------------------
1427::COMM;;|sum wt:| 2.3 |
1428::COMM;;------------------
1429::COMM;;Because we are dealing with sample weights, we cannot find the median by
1430::COMM;;simply choosing/averaging the centre value(s), instead we consider the
1431::COMM;;median where 50% of the cumulative weight is found (in a y sorted data set)
1432::COMM;;. Therefore with regards to this test data, the cumulative weight is >= 50%
1433::COMM;;when y = 4. Therefore:
1434::COMM;;Median = 4
1435::COMM;;For all the samples, we can get the total error by summing:
1436::COMM;;Absolute(Median - y) * weight
1437::COMM;;I.e., total error = (Absolute(4 - 3) * 0.1)
1438::COMM;;+ (Absolute(4 - 3) * 0.3)
1439::COMM;;+ (Absolute(4 - 4) * 1.0)
1440::COMM;;+ (Absolute(4 - 6) * 0.6)
1441::COMM;;+ (Absolute(4 - 7) * 0.3)
1442::COMM;;= 2.5
1443::COMM;;Impurity = Total error / total weight
1444::COMM;;= 2.5 / 2.3
1445::COMM;;= 1.08695652173913
1446::COMM;;------------------
1447::COMM;;From this root node, the next best split is between X values of 3 and 5.
1448::COMM;;Thus, we have left and right child nodes:
1449::COMM;;LEFT RIGHT
1450::COMM;;------------------ ------------------
1451::COMM;;| X | y | weight | | X | y | weight |
1452::COMM;;------------------ ------------------
1453::COMM;;| 3 | 3 | 0.1 | | 5 | 3 | 0.3 |
1454::COMM;;| 3 | 6 | 0.6 | | 8 | 4 | 1.0 |
1455::COMM;;------------------ | 5 | 7 | 0.3 |
1456::COMM;;|sum wt:| 0.7 | ------------------
1457::COMM;;------------------ |sum wt:| 1.6 |
1458::COMM;;------------------
1459::COMM;;Impurity is found in the same way:
1460::COMM;;Left node Median = 6
1461::COMM;;Total error = (Absolute(6 - 3) * 0.1)
1462::COMM;;+ (Absolute(6 - 6) * 0.6)
1463::COMM;;= 0.3
1464::COMM;;Left Impurity = Total error / total weight
1465::COMM;;= 0.3 / 0.7
1466::COMM;;= 0.428571428571429
1467::COMM;;-------------------
1468::COMM;;Likewise for Right node:
1469::COMM;;Right node Median = 4
1470::COMM;;Total error = (Absolute(4 - 3) * 0.3)
1471::COMM;;+ (Absolute(4 - 4) * 1.0)
1472::COMM;;+ (Absolute(4 - 7) * 0.3)
1473::COMM;;= 1.2
1474::COMM;;Right Impurity = Total error / total weight
1475::COMM;;= 1.2 / 1.6
1476::COMM;;= 0.75
1477::COMM;;------

46::COMM;;----------
47::COMM;;check : callable
48::COMM;;When passed the object with the decorated method, this should return
49::COMM;;a truthy value if the attribute is available, and either return False
50::COMM;;or raise an AttributeError if not available.
51::COMM;;Returns
52::COMM;;-------
53::COMM;;callable

55::COMM;;a truthy value, otherwise the decorated method is unavailable.

126::COMM;;This parameter must be greater than max(indices).
127::COMM;;Returns
128::COMM;;-------
129::COMM;;mask : 1d boolean nd-array
130::COMM;;Boolean array that is True where indices are present, else False.
131::COMM;;Examples
132::COMM;;--------
133::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.utils._mask import indices_to_mask
134::COMM;;>>> indices = [1, 2 , 3, 4]
135::COMM;;>>> indices_to_mask(indices, 5)
136::COMM;;array([False, True, True, True, True])
2::COMM;;Metadata Routing Utility
3::COMM;;In order to better understand the components implemented in this file, one
4::COMM;;needs to understand their relationship to one another.
5::COMM;;The only relevant public API for end users are the ``set_{method}_request`` methods,
6::COMM;;e.g. ``estimator.set_fit_request(sample_weight=True)``. However, third-party
7::COMM;;developers and users who implement custom meta-estimators, need to deal with
8::COMM;;the objects implemented in this file.
9::COMM;;The routing is coordinated by building ``MetadataRequest`` objects
10::COMM;;for objects that consume metadata, and ``MetadataRouter`` objects for objects that
11::COMM;;can route metadata, which are then aligned during a call to `process_routing()`. This
12::COMM;;function returns a Bunch object (dictionary-like) with all the information on the
13::COMM;;consumers and which metadata they had requested and the actual metadata values. A
14::COMM;;routing method (such as `fit` in a meta-estimator) can now provide the metadata to the
15::COMM;;relevant consuming method (such as `fit` in a sub-estimator).
16::COMM;;The ``MetadataRequest`` and ``MetadataRouter`` objects are constructed via a
17::COMM;;``get_metadata_routing`` method, which all scikit-learn estimators provide.
18::COMM;;This method is automatically implemented via ``BaseEstimator`` for all simple
19::COMM;;estimators, but needs a custom implementation for meta-estimators.
20::COMM;;MetadataRequest
21::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
22::COMM;;In non-routing consumers, the simplest case, e.g. ``SVM``, ``get_metadata_routing``
23::COMM;;returns a ``MetadataRequest`` object which is assigned to the consumer's
24::COMM;;`_metadata_request` attribute. It stores which metadata is required by each method of
25::COMM;;the consumer by including one ``MethodMetadataRequest`` per method in ``METHODS``
26::COMM;;(e. g. ``fit``, ``score``, etc).
27::COMM;;Users and developers almost never need to directly add a new ``MethodMetadataRequest``,
28::COMM;;to the consumer's `_metadata_request` attribute, since these are generated
29::COMM;;automatically. This attribute is modified while running `set_{method}_request` methods
30::COMM;;(such as `set_fit_request()`), which adds the request via
31::COMM;;`method_metadata_request.add_request(param=prop, alias=alias)`.
32::COMM;;The ``alias`` in the ``add_request`` method has to be either a string (an alias),
33::COMM;;or one of ``[True (requested), False (unrequested), None (error if passed)]``. There
34::COMM;;are some other special values such as ``UNUSED`` and ``WARN`` which are used
35::COMM;;for purposes such as warning of removing a metadata in a child class, but not
36::COMM;;used by the end users.
37::COMM;;MetadataRouter
38::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
39::COMM;;In routers (such as meta-estimators or multi metric scorers), ``get_metadata_routing``
40::COMM;;returns a ``MetadataRouter`` object. It provides information about which method, from
41::COMM;;the router object, calls which method in a consumer's object, and also, which metadata
42::COMM;;had been requested by the consumer's methods, thus specifying how metadata is to be
43::COMM;;passed. If a sub-estimator is a router as well, their routing information is also stored
44::COMM;;in the meta-estimators router.
45::COMM;;Conceptually, this information looks like:
46::COMM;;```
47::COMM;;{
48::COMM;;"sub_estimator1": (
49::COMM;;mapping=[(caller="fit", callee="transform"), ...],
50::COMM;;router=MetadataRequest(...), # or another MetadataRouter
51::COMM;;),
52::COMM;;...
53::COMM;;}
54::COMM;;```
55::COMM;;The `MetadataRouter` objects are never stored and are always recreated anew whenever
56::COMM;;the object's `get_metadata_routing` method is called.
57::COMM;;An object that is both a router and a consumer, e.g. a meta-estimator which
58::COMM;;consumes ``sample_weight`` and routes ``sample_weight`` to its sub-estimators
59::COMM;;also returns a ``MetadataRouter`` object. Its routing information includes both
60::COMM;;information about what metadata is required by the object itself (added via
61::COMM;;``MetadataRouter.add_self_request``), as well as the routing information for its
62::COMM;;sub-estimators (added via ``MetadataRouter.add``).
63::COMM;;Implementation Details
64::COMM;;~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
65::COMM;;To give the above representation some structure, we use the following objects:
66::COMM;;- ``(caller=..., callee=...)`` is a namedtuple called ``MethodPair``.
67::COMM;;- The list of ``MethodPair`` stored in the ``mapping`` field of a `RouterMappingPair` is
68::COMM;;a ``MethodMapping`` object.
69::COMM;;- ``(mapping=..., router=...)`` is a namedtuple called ``RouterMappingPair``.
70::COMM;;The ``set_{method}_request`` methods are dynamically generated for estimators
71::COMM;;which inherit from ``BaseEstimator``. This is done by attaching instances
72::COMM;;of the ``RequestMethod`` descriptor to classes, which is done in the
73::COMM;;``_MetadataRequester`` class, and ``BaseEstimator`` inherits from this mixin.
74::COMM;;This mixin also implements the ``get_metadata_routing``, which meta-estimators
75::COMM;;need to override, but it works for simple consumers as is.
77::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
78::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
87::COMO;;# Only the following methods are supported in the routing mechanism. Adding new
88::COMO;;# methods at the moment involves monkeypatching this list.
89::COMO;;# Note that if this list is changed or monkeypatched, the corresponding method
90::COMO;;# needs to be added under a TYPE_CHECKING condition like the one done here in
91::COMO;;# _MetadataRequester
104::COMO;;# These methods are a composite of other methods and one cannot set their
105::COMO;;# requests directly. Instead they should be set by setting the requests of the
106::COMO;;# simple methods which make the composite ones.
114::COMM;;This is different than `repr(obj)`, since repr(estimator) can be verbose when
115::COMM;;there are many constructor arguments set by the user.
116::COMM;;This is most suitable for Scorers as it gives a nice representation of what they
117::COMM;;are. This is done by implementing a `_routing_repr` method on the object.
118::COMM;;Since the `owner` object could be the type name (str), we return that string if the
119::COMM;;given `obj` is a string, otherwise we return the object's type name.
120::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.8

167::COMM;;This is used in meta-estimators which have not implemented metadata routing

201::COMO;;# Request values
202::COMO;;# ==============
203::COMO;;# Each request value needs to be one of the following values, or an alias.
204::COMO;;# this is used in `__metadata_request__*` attributes to indicate that a
205::COMO;;# metadata is not present even though it may be present in the
206::COMO;;# corresponding method's signature.
208::COMO;;# this is used whenever a default value is changed, and therefore the user
209::COMO;;# should explicitly set the value, otherwise a warning is shown. An example
210::COMO;;# is when a meta-estimator is only a router, but then becomes also a
211::COMO;;# consumer in a new release.
213::COMO;;# this is the default used in `set_{method}_request` methods to indicate no
214::COMO;;# change requested by the user.
219::COMM;;Values in ``VALID_REQUEST_VALUES`` are not considered aliases in this
220::COMM;;context. Only a string which is a valid identifier is.
221::COMM;;Parameters
222::COMM;;----------
223::COMM;;item : object
224::COMM;;The given item to be checked if it can be an alias for the metadata.
225::COMM;;Returns
226::COMM;;-------
227::COMM;;result : bool
228::COMM;;Whether the given item is a valid alias.
232::COMO;;# item is only an alias if it's a valid identifier
236::COMM;;Parameters
237::COMM;;----------
238::COMM;;item : object
239::COMM;;The given item to be checked.
240::COMM;;Returns
241::COMM;;-------
242::COMM;;result : bool
243::COMM;;Whether the given item is valid.

249::COMO;;# used in simple consumers.

486::COMM;;def __getattr__(self, name):
487::COMM;;# Called when the default attribute access fails with an AttributeError
488::COMM;;# (either __getattribute__() raises an AttributeError because name is
489::COMM;;# not an instance attribute or an attribute in the class tree for self;
490::COMM;;# or __get__() of a name property raises AttributeError). This method
491::COMM;;# should either return the (computed) attribute value or raise an
492::COMM;;# AttributeError exception.

494::COMM;;if name not in COMPOSITE_METHODS:

497::COMM;;)

500::COMM;;mmr = getattr(self, method)
501::COMM;;existing = set(requests.keys())
502::COMM;;upcoming = set(mmr.requests.keys())
503::COMM;;common = existing & upcoming

505::COMM;;if conflicts:

508::COMM;;f" composing the requests for {name}. Metadata with the same name"
509::COMM;;f" for methods {', '.join(COMPOSITE_METHODS[name])} should have the"
510::COMM;;" same request value."
511::COMM;;)

513::COMM;;return MethodMetadataRequest(owner=self.owner, method=name, requests=requests)

586::COMM;;# Metadata Request for Routers
587::COMM;;# ============================
588::COMM;;# This section includes all objects required for MetadataRouter which is used
589::COMM;;# in routers, returned by their ``get_metadata_routing``.
590::COMM;;# `RouterMappingPair` is used to store a (mapping, router) tuple where `mapping` is a
591::COMM;;# `MethodMapping` object and `router` is the output of `get_metadata_routing`.
592::COMM;;# `MetadataRouter` stores a collection of `RouterMappingPair` objects in its
593::COMM;;# `_route_mappings` attribute.
594::COMM;;RouterMappingPair = namedtuple("RouterMappingPair", ["mapping", "router"])
595::COMM;;# `MethodPair` is used to store a single method routing. `MethodMapping` stores a list
596::COMM;;# of `MethodPair` objects in its `_routes` attribute.
597::COMM;;MethodPair = namedtuple("MethodPair", ["caller", "callee"])
598::COMM;;class MethodMapping:
607::COMM;;def __init__(self):
608::COMM;;self._routes = []
609::COMM;;def __iter__(self):
610::COMM;;return iter(self._routes)
611::COMM;;def add(self, *, caller, callee):
624::COMM;;if caller not in METHODS:
625::COMM;;raise ValueError(
626::COMM;;f"Given caller:{caller} is not a valid method. Valid methods are:"
627::COMM;;f" {METHODS}"
628::COMM;;)
629::COMM;;if callee not in METHODS:
630::COMM;;raise ValueError(
631::COMM;;f"Given callee:{callee} is not a valid method. Valid methods are:"
632::COMM;;f" {METHODS}"
633::COMM;;)
634::COMM;;self._routes.append(MethodPair(caller=caller, callee=callee))
635::COMM;;return self

643::COMM;;result = list()

645::COMM;;result.append({"caller": route.caller, "callee": route.callee})
646::COMM;;return result

794::COMM;;if caller == method:

839::COMM;;}

841::COMM;;# conflicts are okay if the passed objects are the same, but it's

849::COMM;;)

852::COMM;;def route_params(self, *, caller, params):
873::COMM;;if self._self_request:

875::COMM;;res = Bunch()

882::COMM;;params=params,

886::COMM;;)

888::COMM;;def validate_metadata(self, *, method, params):

911::COMM;;if extra_keys:

979::COMM;;# Request method
980::COMM;;# ==============
981::COMM;;# This section includes what's needed for the `RequestMethod` descriptor and

983::COMM;;# mixin class.
984::COMM;;# These strings are used to dynamically generate the docstrings for the methods.
1018::COMM;;class RequestMethod:
1043::COMM;;def __init__(self, name, keys, validate_keys=True):

1045::COMM;;self.keys = keys
1046::COMM;;self.validate_keys = validate_keys
1047::COMM;;def __get__(self, instance, owner):
1048::COMM;;# we would want to have a method which accepts only the expected args
1049::COMM;;def func(*args, **kw):
1055::COMM;;if not _routing_enabled():
1056::COMM;;raise RuntimeError(
1057::COMM;;"This method is only available when metadata routing is enabled."
1058::COMM;;" You can enable it using"
1059::COMM;;" sklearn.set_config(enable_metadata_routing=True)."
1060::COMM;;)
1061::COMM;;if self.validate_keys and (set(kw) - set(self.keys)):
1062::COMM;;raise TypeError(
1063::COMM;;f"Unexpected args: {set(kw) - set(self.keys)} in {self.name}. "
1064::COMM;;f"Accepted arguments are: {set(self.keys)}"
1065::COMM;;)
1066::COMM;;# This makes it possible to use the decorated method as an unbound method,
1067::COMM;;# for instance when monkeypatching.
1068::COMM;;# https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/28632
1069::COMM;;if instance is None:
1070::COMM;;_instance = args[0]
1071::COMM;;args = args[1:]
1072::COMM;;else:
1073::COMM;;_instance = instance
1074::COMM;;# Replicating python's behavior when positional args are given other than
1075::COMM;;# `self`, and `self` is only allowed if this method is unbound.
1076::COMM;;if args:
1077::COMM;;raise TypeError(
1078::COMM;;f"set_{self.name}_request() takes 0 positional argument but"
1079::COMM;;f" {len(args)} were given"
1080::COMM;;)
1081::COMM;;requests = _instance._get_metadata_request()

1083::COMM;;for prop, alias in kw.items():
1084::COMM;;if alias is not UNCHANGED:
1085::COMM;;method_metadata_request.add_request(param=prop, alias=alias)
1086::COMM;;_instance._metadata_request = requests
1087::COMM;;return _instance
1088::COMM;;# Now we set the relevant attributes of the function so that it seems
1089::COMM;;# like a normal method to the end user, with known expected arguments.
1090::COMM;;func.__name__ = f"set_{self.name}_request"
1091::COMM;;params = [
1092::COMM;;inspect.Parameter(
1093::COMM;;name="self",
1094::COMM;;kind=inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
1095::COMM;;annotation=owner,
1096::COMM;;)
1097::COMM;;]
1098::COMM;;params.extend(
1099::COMM;;[
1100::COMM;;inspect.Parameter(
1101::COMM;;k,
1102::COMM;;inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY,
1103::COMM;;default=UNCHANGED,
1104::COMM;;annotation=Optional[Union[bool, None, str]],
1105::COMM;;)
1106::COMM;;for k in self.keys
1107::COMM;;]
1108::COMM;;)

1110::COMM;;params,
1111::COMM;;return_annotation=owner,
1112::COMM;;)

1116::COMM;;doc += REQUESTER_DOC_RETURN

1174::COMM;;@classmethod
1175::COMM;;def _get_class_level_metadata_request_values(cls, method: str):
1183::COMM;;# Here we use `isfunction` instead of `ismethod` because calling `getattr`
1184::COMM;;# on a class instead of an instance returns an unbound function.
1185::COMM;;if not hasattr(cls, method) or not inspect.isfunction(getattr(cls, method)):
1186::COMM;;return dict()
1187::COMM;;# ignore the first parameter of the method, which is usually "self"
1188::COMM;;signature_items = list(
1189::COMM;;inspect.signature(getattr(cls, method)).parameters.items()
1190::COMM;;)[1:]
1191::COMM;;params = defaultdict(
1192::COMM;;str,
1193::COMM;;{
1194::COMM;;param_name: None
1195::COMM;;for param_name, param_info in signature_items
1196::COMM;;if param_name not in {"X", "y", "Y", "Xt", "yt"}
1197::COMM;;and param_info.kind
1198::COMM;;not in {param_info.VAR_POSITIONAL, param_info.VAR_KEYWORD}
1199::COMM;;},
1200::COMM;;)
1201::COMM;;# Then overwrite those defaults with the ones provided in
1202::COMM;;# `__metadata_request__{method}` class attributes, which take precedence over
1203::COMM;;# signature sniffing.
1204::COMM;;# need to go through the MRO since this is a classmethod and
1205::COMM;;# ``vars`` doesn't report the parent class attributes. We go through
1206::COMM;;# the reverse of the MRO so that child classes have precedence over
1207::COMM;;# their parents.
1208::COMM;;substr = f"__metadata_request__{method}"
1209::COMM;;for base_class in reversed(inspect.getmro(cls)):
1210::COMM;;# Copy is needed with free-threaded context to avoid
1211::COMM;;# RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration.
1212::COMM;;# copy.deepcopy applied on an instance of base_class adds
1213::COMM;;# __slotnames__ attribute to base_class.
1214::COMM;;base_class_items = vars(base_class).copy().items()
1215::COMM;;for attr, value in base_class_items:
1216::COMM;;# we don't check for equivalence since python prefixes attrs
1217::COMM;;# starting with __ with the `_ClassName`.
1218::COMM;;if substr not in attr:
1219::COMM;;continue
1220::COMM;;for prop, alias in value.items():
1221::COMM;;# Here we add request values specified via those class attributes
1222::COMM;;# to the result dictionary (params). Adding a request which already
1223::COMM;;# exists will override the previous one. Since we go through the
1224::COMM;;# MRO in reverse order, the one specified by the lowest most classes
1225::COMM;;# in the inheritance tree are the ones which take effect.
1226::COMM;;if prop not in params and alias == UNUSED:
1227::COMM;;raise ValueError(
1228::COMM;;f"Trying to remove parameter {prop} with UNUSED which"
1229::COMM;;" doesn't exist."
1230::COMM;;)
1231::COMM;;params[prop] = alias
1232::COMM;;return {param: alias for param, alias in params.items() if alias is not UNUSED}

137::COMM;;This is useful to avoid validating many times the parameters passed by the

139::COMM;;parameters that we pass internally to inner functions that are guaranteed to
140::COMM;;be valid by the test suite.

351::COMM;;f" Got {self.type} instead."

354::COMM;;raise ValueError(

356::COMM;;f"Got {self.closed} instead."

359::COMM;;suffix = "for an interval over the integers."
360::COMM;;if self.left is not None and not isinstance(self.left, Integral):
361::COMM;;raise TypeError(f"Expecting left to be an int {suffix}")
362::COMM;;if self.right is not None and not isinstance(self.right, Integral):
363::COMM;;raise TypeError(f"Expecting right to be an int {suffix}")
364::COMM;;if self.left is None and self.closed in ("left", "both"):
365::COMM;;raise ValueError(
366::COMM;;f"left can't be None when closed == {self.closed} {suffix}"
367::COMM;;)
368::COMM;;if self.right is None and self.closed in ("right", "both"):
369::COMM;;raise ValueError(
370::COMM;;f"right can't be None when closed == {self.closed} {suffix}"
371::COMM;;)
372::COMM;;else:
373::COMM;;if self.left is not None and not isinstance(self.left, Real):
374::COMM;;raise TypeError("Expecting left to be a real number.")
375::COMM;;if self.right is not None and not isinstance(self.right, Real):
376::COMM;;raise TypeError("Expecting right to be a real number.")
377::COMM;;if self.right is not None and self.left is not None and self.right <= self.left:
378::COMM;;raise ValueError(

380::COMM;;f"right={self.right}"
381::COMM;;)

383::COMM;;if not isinstance(val, Integral) and np.isnan(val):
384::COMM;;return False

386::COMM;;right_cmp = operator.gt if self.closed in ("right", "both") else operator.ge
387::COMM;;left = -np.inf if self.left is None else self.left
388::COMM;;right = np.inf if self.right is None else self.right
389::COMM;;if left_cmp(val, left):
390::COMM;;return False
391::COMM;;if right_cmp(val, right):
392::COMM;;return False
393::COMM;;return True

395::COMM;;if not isinstance(val, self.type):
396::COMM;;return False

402::COMM;;right_bound = "inf" if self.right is None else self.right

408::COMM;;right_bound = float(right_bound)

411::COMM;;f"{left_bracket}{left_bound}, {right_bound}{right_bracket}"

90::COMM;;This extends the pprint.PrettyPrinter class, because:
91::COMM;;- we need estimators to be printed with their parameters, e.g.
92::COMM;;Estimator(param1=value1, ...) which is not supported by default.
93::COMM;;- the 'compact' parameter of PrettyPrinter is ignored for dicts, which
94::COMM;;may lead to very long representations that we want to avoid.
95::COMM;;Quick overview of pprint.PrettyPrinter (see also
96::COMM;;https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49565047/pprint-with-hex-numbers):
97::COMM;;- the entry point is the _format() method which calls format() (overridden
98::COMM;;here)
99::COMM;;- format() directly calls _safe_repr() for a first try at rendering the
100::COMM;;object
101::COMM;;- _safe_repr formats the whole object recursively, only calling itself,
102::COMM;;not caring about line length or anything
103::COMM;;- back to _format(), if the output string is too long, _format() then calls
104::COMM;;the appropriate _pprint_TYPE() method (e.g. _pprint_list()) depending on
105::COMM;;the type of the object. This where the line length and the compact
106::COMM;;parameters are taken into account.
107::COMM;;- those _pprint_TYPE() methods will internally use the format() method for
108::COMM;;rendering the nested objects of an object (e.g. the elements of a list)
109::COMM;;In the end, everything has to be implemented twice: in _safe_repr and in
110::COMM;;the custom _pprint_TYPE methods. Unfortunately PrettyPrinter is really not
111::COMM;;straightforward to extend (especially when we want a compact output), so
112::COMM;;the code is a bit convoluted.
113::COMM;;This class overrides:
114::COMM;;- format() to support the changed_only parameter
115::COMM;;- _safe_repr to support printing of estimators (for when they fit on a
116::COMM;;single line)
117::COMM;;- _format_dict_items so that dict are correctly 'compacted'
118::COMM;;- _format_items so that ellipsis is used on long lists and tuples
119::COMM;;When estimators cannot be printed on a single line, the builtin _format()
120::COMM;;will call _pprint_estimator() because it was registered to do so (see
121::COMM;;_dispatch[BaseEstimator.__repr__] = _pprint_estimator).
122::COMM;;both _format_dict_items() and _pprint_estimator() use the
123::COMM;;_format_params_or_dict_items() method that will format parameters and
124::COMM;;key-value pairs respecting the compact parameter. This method needs another
125::COMM;;subroutine _pprint_key_val_tuple() used when a parameter or a key-value
126::COMM;;pair is too long to fit on a single line. This subroutine is called in
127::COMM;;_format() and is registered as well in the _dispatch dict (just like
128::COMM;;_pprint_estimator). We had to create the two classes KeyValTuple and
129::COMM;;KeyValTupleParam for this.

305::COMM;;def _safe_repr(object, context, maxlevels, level, changed_only=False):
308::COMM;;typ = type(object)
309::COMM;;if typ in pprint._builtin_scalars:
310::COMM;;return repr(object), True, False
311::COMM;;r = getattr(typ, "__repr__", None)
312::COMM;;if issubclass(typ, dict) and r is dict.__repr__:
313::COMM;;if not object:
314::COMM;;return "{}", True, False
315::COMM;;objid = id(object)
316::COMM;;if maxlevels and level >= maxlevels:
317::COMM;;return "{...}", False, objid in context
318::COMM;;if objid in context:
319::COMM;;return pprint._recursion(object), False, True
320::COMM;;context[objid] = 1
321::COMM;;readable = True
322::COMM;;recursive = False
323::COMM;;components = []
324::COMM;;append = components.append
325::COMM;;level += 1
326::COMM;;saferepr = _safe_repr
327::COMM;;items = sorted(object.items(), key=pprint._safe_tuple)
328::COMM;;for k, v in items:
329::COMM;;krepr, kreadable, krecur = saferepr(
330::COMM;;k, context, maxlevels, level, changed_only=changed_only
331::COMM;;)
332::COMM;;vrepr, vreadable, vrecur = saferepr(
333::COMM;;v, context, maxlevels, level, changed_only=changed_only
334::COMM;;)
335::COMM;;append("%s: %s" % (krepr, vrepr))
336::COMM;;readable = readable and kreadable and vreadable
337::COMM;;if krecur or vrecur:
338::COMM;;recursive = True
339::COMM;;del context[objid]
340::COMM;;return "{%s}" % ", ".join(components), readable, recursive
341::COMM;;if (issubclass(typ, list) and r is list.__repr__) or (
342::COMM;;issubclass(typ, tuple) and r is tuple.__repr__
343::COMM;;):
344::COMM;;if issubclass(typ, list):
345::COMM;;if not object:
346::COMM;;return "[]", True, False
347::COMM;;format = "[%s]"
348::COMM;;elif len(object) == 1:
349::COMM;;format = "(%s,)"
350::COMM;;else:
351::COMM;;if not object:
352::COMM;;return "()", True, False
353::COMM;;format = "(%s)"
354::COMM;;objid = id(object)
355::COMM;;if maxlevels and level >= maxlevels:
356::COMM;;return format % "...", False, objid in context
357::COMM;;if objid in context:
358::COMM;;return pprint._recursion(object), False, True
359::COMM;;context[objid] = 1
360::COMM;;readable = True
361::COMM;;recursive = False
362::COMM;;components = []
363::COMM;;append = components.append
364::COMM;;level += 1
365::COMM;;for o in object:
366::COMM;;orepr, oreadable, orecur = _safe_repr(
367::COMM;;o, context, maxlevels, level, changed_only=changed_only
368::COMM;;)
369::COMM;;append(orepr)
370::COMM;;if not oreadable:
371::COMM;;readable = False
372::COMM;;if orecur:
373::COMM;;recursive = True
374::COMM;;del context[objid]
375::COMM;;return format % ", ".join(components), readable, recursive
376::COMM;;if issubclass(typ, BaseEstimator):
377::COMM;;objid = id(object)
378::COMM;;if maxlevels and level >= maxlevels:
379::COMM;;return f"{typ.__name__}(...)", False, objid in context
380::COMM;;if objid in context:
381::COMM;;return pprint._recursion(object), False, True
382::COMM;;context[objid] = 1
383::COMM;;readable = True
384::COMM;;recursive = False
385::COMM;;if changed_only:
386::COMM;;params = _changed_params(object)
387::COMM;;else:
388::COMM;;params = object.get_params(deep=False)
389::COMM;;components = []
390::COMM;;append = components.append
391::COMM;;level += 1
392::COMM;;saferepr = _safe_repr
393::COMM;;items = sorted(params.items(), key=pprint._safe_tuple)
394::COMM;;for k, v in items:
395::COMM;;krepr, kreadable, krecur = saferepr(
396::COMM;;k, context, maxlevels, level, changed_only=changed_only
397::COMM;;)
398::COMM;;vrepr, vreadable, vrecur = saferepr(
399::COMM;;v, context, maxlevels, level, changed_only=changed_only
400::COMM;;)
401::COMM;;append("%s=%s" % (krepr.strip("'"), vrepr))
402::COMM;;readable = readable and kreadable and vreadable
403::COMM;;if krecur or vrecur:
404::COMM;;recursive = True
