9::COMM;;This mixin relies on three attributes:
10::COMM;;- `_doc_link_module`: it corresponds to the root module (e.g. `sklearn`). Using this
11::COMM;;mixin, the default value is `sklearn`.
12::COMM;;- `_doc_link_template`: it corresponds to the template used to generate the
13::COMM;;link to the API documentation. Using this mixin, the default value is
14::COMM;;`"https://scikit-learn.org/{version_url}/modules/generated/
15::COMM;;{estimator_module}.{estimator_name}.html"`.
16::COMM;;- `_doc_link_url_param_generator`: it corresponds to a function that generates the
17::COMM;;parameters to be used in the template when the estimator module and name are not
18::COMM;;sufficient.
19::COMM;;The method :meth:`_get_doc_link` generates the link to the API documentation for a
20::COMM;;given estimator.
21::COMM;;This mixin provides all the necessary states for
22::COMM;;:func:`sklearn.utils.estimator_html_repr` to generate a link to the API
23::COMM;;documentation for the estimator HTML diagram.
24::COMM;;Examples
25::COMM;;--------
26::COMM;;If the default values for `_doc_link_module`, `_doc_link_template` are not suitable,
27::COMM;;then you can override them and provide a method to generate the URL parameters:
28::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator
29::COMM;;>>> doc_link_template = "https://address.local/{single_param}.html"
30::COMM;;>>> def url_param_generator(estimator):
31::COMM;;... return {"single_param": estimator.__class__.__name__}
32::COMM;;>>> class MyEstimator(BaseEstimator):
33::COMM;;... # use "builtins" since it is the associated module when declaring
34::COMM;;... # the class in a docstring
35::COMM;;... _doc_link_module = "builtins"
36::COMM;;... _doc_link_template = doc_link_template
37::COMM;;... _doc_link_url_param_generator = url_param_generator
38::COMM;;>>> estimator = MyEstimator()
39::COMM;;>>> estimator._get_doc_link()
40::COMM;;'https://address.local/MyEstimator.html'
41::COMM;;If instead of overriding the attributes inside the class definition, you want to
42::COMM;;override a class instance, you can use `types.MethodType` to bind the method to the
43::COMM;;instance:
44::COMM;;>>> import types
45::COMM;;>>> estimator = BaseEstimator()
46::COMM;;>>> estimator._doc_link_template = doc_link_template
47::COMM;;>>> estimator._doc_link_url_param_generator = types.MethodType(
48::COMM;;... url_param_generator, estimator)
49::COMM;;>>> estimator._get_doc_link()
50::COMM;;'https://address.local/BaseEstimator.html'

12::COMM;;This function process the `y_pred` array in the binary and multi-label cases.

16::COMM;;Parameters
17::COMM;;----------

19::COMM;;Output of `estimator.predict_proba`. The shape depends on the target type:
20::COMM;;- for binary classification, it is a 2d array of shape `(n_samples, 2)`;
21::COMM;;- for multiclass classification, it is a 2d array of shape
22::COMM;;`(n_samples, n_classes)`;
23::COMM;;- for multilabel classification, it is either a list of 2d arrays of shape
24::COMM;;`(n_samples, 2)` (e.g. `RandomForestClassifier` or `KNeighborsClassifier`) or
25::COMM;;an array of shape `(n_samples, n_outputs)` (e.g. `MLPClassifier` or
26::COMM;;`RidgeClassifier`).

28::COMM;;Type of the target.

30::COMM;;Class labels as reported by `estimator.classes_`.
31::COMM;;pos_label : int, float, bool or str
32::COMM;;Only used with binary and multiclass targets.
33::COMM;;Returns

36::COMM;;(n_samples, n_output)

56::COMO;;# array of shape `(n_samples, n_outputs)`
61::COMM;;This function process the `y_pred` array in the binary and multi-label cases.
62::COMM;;In the binary case, it inverts the sign of the score if the positive label
63::COMM;;is not `classes[1]`. In the multi-label case, it stacks the predictions if
64::COMM;;they are not in the "compressed" format `(n_samples, n_outputs)`.
65::COMM;;Parameters
66::COMM;;----------
67::COMM;;y_pred : ndarray
68::COMM;;Output of `estimator.decision_function`. The shape depends on the target type:
69::COMM;;- for binary classification, it is a 1d array of shape `(n_samples,)` where the
70::COMM;;sign is assuming that `classes[1]` is the positive class;
71::COMM;;- for multiclass classification, it is a 2d array of shape
72::COMM;;`(n_samples, n_classes)`;
73::COMM;;- for multilabel classification, it is a 2d array of shape `(n_samples,
74::COMM;;n_outputs)`.
75::COMM;;target_type : {"binary", "multiclass", "multilabel-indicator"}
76::COMM;;Type of the target.
77::COMM;;classes : ndarray of shape (n_classes,) or list of such arrays
78::COMM;;Class labels as reported by `estimator.classes_`.
79::COMM;;pos_label : int, float, bool or str
80::COMM;;Only used with binary and multiclass targets.
81::COMM;;Returns
82::COMM;;-------
83::COMM;;y_pred : ndarray of shape (n_samples,), (n_samples, n_classes) or \
84::COMM;;(n_samples, n_output)
85::COMM;;Compressed predictions format as requested by the metrics.
98::COMM;;The response values are predictions such that it follows the following shape:
99::COMM;;- for binary classification, it is a 1d array of shape `(n_samples,)`;
100::COMM;;- for multiclass classification, it is a 2d array of shape `(n_samples, n_classes)`;
101::COMM;;- for multilabel classification, it is a 2d array of shape `(n_samples, n_outputs)`;
102::COMM;;- for outlier detection, it is a 1d array of shape `(n_samples,)`;
103::COMM;;- for regression, it is a 1d array of shape `(n_samples,)`.
104::COMM;;If `estimator` is a binary classifier, also return the label for the
105::COMM;;effective positive class.
106::COMM;;This utility is used primarily in the displays and the scikit-learn scorers.
107::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.3
108::COMM;;Parameters
109::COMM;;----------
110::COMM;;estimator : estimator instance

114::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)

117::COMM;;"predict"} or list of such str
118::COMM;;Specifies the response method to use get prediction from an estimator

121::COMM;;- if `str`, it corresponds to the name to the method to return;
122::COMM;;- if a list of `str`, it provides the method names in order of
123::COMM;;preference. The method returned corresponds to the first method in

125::COMM;;pos_label : int, float, bool or str, default=None

148::COMM;;This variant introspects the least precise floating point dtype
149::COMM;;in the input argument and automatically sets the relative tolerance
150::COMM;;parameter to 1e-4 float32 and use 1e-7 otherwise (typically float64
151::COMM;;in scikit-learn).
152::COMM;;`atol` is always left to 0. by default. It should be adjusted manually
153::COMM;;to an assertion-specific value in case there are null values expected
154::COMM;;in `desired`.
155::COMM;;The aggregate tolerance is `atol + rtol * abs(desired)`.
156::COMM;;Parameters
157::COMM;;----------
158::COMM;;actual : array_like
159::COMM;;Array obtained.
160::COMM;;desired : array_like
161::COMM;;Array desired.
162::COMM;;rtol : float, optional, default=None
163::COMM;;Relative tolerance.
164::COMM;;If None, it is set based on the provided arrays' dtypes.
165::COMM;;atol : float, optional, default=0.
166::COMM;;Absolute tolerance.
167::COMM;;equal_nan : bool, optional, default=True
168::COMM;;If True, NaNs will compare equal.
169::COMM;;err_msg : str, optional, default=''
170::COMM;;The error message to be printed in case of failure.
171::COMM;;verbose : bool, optional, default=True
172::COMM;;If True, the conflicting values are appended to the error message.
173::COMM;;Raises
174::COMM;;------
175::COMM;;AssertionError
176::COMM;;If actual and desired are not equal up to specified precision.
177::COMM;;See Also
178::COMM;;--------
179::COMM;;numpy.testing.assert_allclose
180::COMM;;Examples
181::COMM;;--------
182::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
183::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.utils._testing import assert_allclose
184::COMM;;>>> x = [1e-5, 1e-3, 1e-1]
185::COMM;;>>> y = np.arccos(np.cos(x))
186::COMM;;>>> assert_allclose(x, y, rtol=1e-5, atol=0)
187::COMM;;>>> a = np.full(shape=10, fill_value=1e-5, dtype=np.float32)
188::COMM;;>>> assert_allclose(a, 1e-5)
207::COMM;;Both x and y need to be either sparse or dense, they
208::COMM;;can't be mixed.
209::COMM;;Parameters
210::COMM;;----------
211::COMM;;x : {array-like, sparse matrix}
212::COMM;;First array to compare.
213::COMM;;y : {array-like, sparse matrix}
214::COMM;;Second array to compare.
215::COMM;;rtol : float, default=1e-07
216::COMM;;relative tolerance; see numpy.allclose.
217::COMM;;atol : float, default=1e-9
218::COMM;;absolute tolerance; see numpy.allclose. Note that the default here is
219::COMM;;more tolerant than the default for numpy.testing.assert_allclose, where
220::COMM;;atol=0.
221::COMM;;err_msg : str, default=''
222::COMM;;Error message to raise.
233::COMO;;# both dense
241::COMM;;Parameters

244::COMM;;The estimator.

246::COMM;;Pseudo random number generator state.

278::COMO;;# Decorator for tests involving both BLAS calls and multiprocessing.
279::COMO;;#
280::COMO;;# Under POSIX (e.g. Linux or OSX), using multiprocessing in conjunction
281::COMO;;# with some implementation of BLAS (or other libraries that manage an
282::COMO;;# internal posix thread pool) can cause a crash or a freeze of the Python
283::COMO;;# process.
284::COMO;;#
285::COMO;;# In practice all known packaged distributions (from Linux distros or
286::COMO;;# Anaconda) of BLAS under Linux seems to be safe. So we this problem seems
287::COMO;;# to only impact OSX users.
288::COMO;;#
289::COMO;;# This wrapper makes it possible to skip tests that can possibly cause
290::COMO;;# this crash under OS X with.
291::COMO;;#
292::COMO;;# Under Python 3.4+ it is possible to use the `forkserver` start method
293::COMO;;# for multiprocessing to avoid this issue. However it can cause pickling
294::COMO;;# errors on interactively defined functions. It therefore not enabled by
295::COMO;;# default.

398::COMM;;def check_docstring_parameters(func, doc=None, ignore=None):
413::COMM;;from numpydoc import docscrape

432::COMM;;# drop self

434::COMM;;param_signature.remove("self")

456::COMM;;param_docs = []

459::COMM;;if not type_definition.strip():

461::COMM;;incorrect += [

464::COMM;;]

475::COMM;;# If one of the docstring's parameters had an error then return that
476::COMM;;# incorrect message

478::COMM;;return incorrect
479::COMM;;# Remove the parameters that should be ignored from list
480::COMM;;param_docs = list(filter(lambda x: x not in ignore, param_docs))

491::COMM;;]

500::COMM;;message += [

502::COMM;;" function signature, first extra item: %s"

541::COMM;;def _get_diff_msg(docstrings_grouped):
547::COMM;;msg_diff = ""
548::COMM;;ref_str = ""
549::COMM;;ref_group = []
550::COMM;;for docstring, group in docstrings_grouped.items():
551::COMM;;if not ref_str and not ref_group:
552::COMM;;ref_str += docstring

554::COMM;;diff = list(
555::COMM;;context_diff(
556::COMM;;ref_str.split(),
557::COMM;;docstring.split(),

559::COMM;;tofile=str(group),
560::COMM;;n=8,
561::COMM;;)

565::COMM;;# Group consecutive 'diff' words to shorten error message
566::COMM;;for start, group in groupby(diff[3:], key=_diff_key):
567::COMM;;if start is None:
568::COMM;;msg_diff += "\n" + "\n".join(group)
569::COMM;;else:

571::COMM;;# Add new lines at end of diff, to separate comparisons

574::COMM;;def _check_consistency_items(

578::COMM;;n_objects,

580::COMM;;ignore_types=tuple(),

607::COMM;;# If item not found in all objects, skip
608::COMM;;if sum([len(objs) for objs in docstrings_grouped.values()]) < n_objects:
609::COMM;;skipped.append(item_name)

620::COMM;;)

622::COMM;;# Skip type checking for items in `ignore_types`
623::COMM;;elif type_or_desc == "type specification" and item_name in ignore_types:

626::COMM;;elif len(docstrings_grouped.keys()) > 1:

633::COMM;;f"between {obj_groups}:"

636::COMM;;raise AssertionError(msg)

763::COMM;;def assert_run_python_script_without_output(source_code, pattern=".+", timeout=60):
778::COMM;;fd, source_file = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix="_src_test_sklearn.py")

788::COMM;;except KeyError:

793::COMM;;if coverage_rc:

796::COMM;;try:

798::COMM;;out = check_output(cmd, **kwargs)
799::COMM;;except CalledProcessError as e:
800::COMM;;raise RuntimeError(
801::COMM;;"script errored with output:\n%s" % e.output.decode("utf-8")
802::COMM;;)
803::COMM;;out = out.decode("utf-8")
804::COMM;;if re.search(pattern, out):
805::COMM;;if pattern == ".+":
806::COMM;;expectation = "Expected no output"
807::COMM;;else:
808::COMM;;expectation = f"The output was not supposed to match {pattern!r}"
809::COMM;;message = f"{expectation}, got the following output instead: {out!r}"
810::COMM;;raise AssertionError(message)
811::COMM;;except TimeoutExpired as e:
812::COMM;;raise RuntimeError(
813::COMM;;"script timeout, output so far:\n%s" % e.output.decode("utf-8")
814::COMM;;)
815::COMM;;finally:
816::COMM;;os.unlink(source_file)
817::COMM;;def _convert_container(
818::COMM;;container,
819::COMM;;constructor_name,
820::COMM;;columns_name=None,
821::COMM;;dtype=None,
822::COMM;;minversion=None,
823::COMM;;categorical_feature_names=None,
824::COMM;;):
849::COMM;;if constructor_name == "list":
850::COMM;;if dtype is None:
851::COMM;;return list(container)
852::COMM;;else:
853::COMM;;return np.asarray(container, dtype=dtype).tolist()
854::COMM;;elif constructor_name == "tuple":
855::COMM;;if dtype is None:
856::COMM;;return tuple(container)
857::COMM;;else:
858::COMM;;return tuple(np.asarray(container, dtype=dtype).tolist())
859::COMM;;elif constructor_name == "array":
860::COMM;;return np.asarray(container, dtype=dtype)
861::COMM;;elif constructor_name in ("pandas", "dataframe"):
862::COMM;;pd = pytest.importorskip("pandas", minversion=minversion)
863::COMM;;result = pd.DataFrame(container, columns=columns_name, dtype=dtype, copy=False)
864::COMM;;if categorical_feature_names is not None:
865::COMM;;for col_name in categorical_feature_names:
866::COMM;;result[col_name] = result[col_name].astype("category")
867::COMM;;return result
868::COMM;;elif constructor_name == "pyarrow":
869::COMM;;pa = pytest.importorskip("pyarrow", minversion=minversion)
870::COMM;;array = np.asarray(container)
871::COMM;;array = array[:, None] if array.ndim == 1 else array
872::COMM;;if columns_name is None:
873::COMM;;columns_name = [f"col{i}" for i in range(array.shape[1])]
874::COMM;;data = {name: array[:, i] for i, name in enumerate(columns_name)}
875::COMM;;result = pa.Table.from_pydict(data)
876::COMM;;if categorical_feature_names is not None:
877::COMM;;for col_idx, col_name in enumerate(result.column_names):
878::COMM;;if col_name in categorical_feature_names:
879::COMM;;result = result.set_column(
880::COMM;;col_idx, col_name, result.column(col_name).dictionary_encode()
881::COMM;;)
882::COMM;;return result
883::COMM;;elif constructor_name == "polars":
884::COMM;;pl = pytest.importorskip("polars", minversion=minversion)
885::COMM;;result = pl.DataFrame(container, schema=columns_name, orient="row")
886::COMM;;if categorical_feature_names is not None:
887::COMM;;for col_name in categorical_feature_names:
888::COMM;;result = result.with_columns(pl.col(col_name).cast(pl.Categorical))
889::COMM;;return result
890::COMM;;elif constructor_name == "series":
891::COMM;;pd = pytest.importorskip("pandas", minversion=minversion)
892::COMM;;return pd.Series(container, dtype=dtype)
893::COMM;;elif constructor_name == "pyarrow_array":
894::COMM;;pa = pytest.importorskip("pyarrow", minversion=minversion)
895::COMM;;return pa.array(container)

4::COMM;;import numpy as np
5::COMM;;from scipy import sparse
6::COMM;;from sklearn.utils._param_validation import StrOptions, validate_params
7::COMM;;from sklearn.utils.validation import _check_sample_weight
8::COMM;;@validate_params(
9::COMM;;{
10::COMM;;"class_weight": [dict, StrOptions({"balanced"}), None],
11::COMM;;"classes": [np.ndarray],
12::COMM;;"y": ["array-like"],
13::COMM;;"sample_weight": ["array-like", None],
14::COMM;;},
15::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
16::COMM;;)
17::COMM;;def compute_class_weight(class_weight, *, classes, y, sample_weight=None):
52::COMM;;# Import error caused by circular imports.
53::COMM;;from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
54::COMM;;if set(y) - set(classes):
55::COMM;;raise ValueError("classes should include all valid labels that can be in y")
56::COMM;;if class_weight is None or len(class_weight) == 0:
57::COMM;;# uniform class weights
58::COMM;;weight = np.ones(classes.shape[0], dtype=np.float64, order="C")
59::COMM;;elif class_weight == "balanced":
60::COMM;;# Find the weight of each class as present in y.
61::COMM;;le = LabelEncoder()
62::COMM;;y_ind = le.fit_transform(y)
63::COMM;;if not all(np.isin(classes, le.classes_)):
64::COMM;;raise ValueError("classes should have valid labels that are in y")
65::COMM;;sample_weight = _check_sample_weight(sample_weight, y)
66::COMM;;weighted_class_counts = np.bincount(y_ind, weights=sample_weight)
67::COMM;;recip_freq = weighted_class_counts.sum() / (
68::COMM;;len(le.classes_) * weighted_class_counts
69::COMM;;)
70::COMM;;weight = recip_freq[le.transform(classes)]
71::COMM;;else:
72::COMM;;# user-defined dictionary
73::COMM;;weight = np.ones(classes.shape[0], dtype=np.float64, order="C")
74::COMM;;unweighted_classes = []
75::COMM;;for i, c in enumerate(classes):
76::COMM;;if c in class_weight:
77::COMM;;weight[i] = class_weight[c]
78::COMM;;else:
79::COMM;;unweighted_classes.append(c)
80::COMM;;n_weighted_classes = len(classes) - len(unweighted_classes)
81::COMM;;if unweighted_classes and n_weighted_classes != len(class_weight):
82::COMM;;unweighted_classes_user_friendly_str = np.array(unweighted_classes).tolist()
83::COMM;;raise ValueError(
84::COMM;;f"The classes, {unweighted_classes_user_friendly_str}, are not in"
85::COMM;;" class_weight"
86::COMM;;)
87::COMM;;return weight
88::COMM;;@validate_params(
89::COMM;;{
90::COMM;;"class_weight": [dict, list, StrOptions({"balanced"}), None],
91::COMM;;"y": ["array-like", "sparse matrix"],
92::COMM;;"indices": ["array-like", None],
93::COMM;;},
94::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
95::COMM;;)
96::COMM;;def compute_sample_weight(class_weight, y, *, indices=None):
133::COMM;;# Ensure y is 2D. Sparse matrices are already 2D.
134::COMM;;if not sparse.issparse(y):
135::COMM;;y = np.atleast_1d(y)
136::COMM;;if y.ndim == 1:
137::COMM;;y = np.reshape(y, (-1, 1))
138::COMM;;n_outputs = y.shape[1]
139::COMM;;if indices is not None and class_weight != "balanced":
140::COMM;;raise ValueError(
141::COMM;;"The only valid class_weight for subsampling is 'balanced'. "
142::COMM;;f"Given {class_weight}."
143::COMM;;)
144::COMM;;elif n_outputs > 1:
145::COMM;;if class_weight is None or isinstance(class_weight, dict):
146::COMM;;raise ValueError(
147::COMM;;"For multi-output, class_weight should be a list of dicts, or the "
148::COMM;;"string 'balanced'."
149::COMM;;)
150::COMM;;elif isinstance(class_weight, list) and len(class_weight) != n_outputs:
151::COMM;;raise ValueError(
152::COMM;;"For multi-output, number of elements in class_weight should match "
153::COMM;;f"number of outputs. Got {len(class_weight)} element(s) while having "
154::COMM;;f"{n_outputs} outputs."
155::COMM;;)
156::COMM;;expanded_class_weight = []
157::COMM;;for k in range(n_outputs):
158::COMM;;if sparse.issparse(y):
159::COMM;;# Ok to densify a single column at a time
160::COMM;;y_full = y[:, [k]].toarray().flatten()
161::COMM;;else:
162::COMM;;y_full = y[:, k]
163::COMM;;classes_full = np.unique(y_full)
164::COMM;;classes_missing = None
165::COMM;;if class_weight == "balanced" or n_outputs == 1:
166::COMM;;class_weight_k = class_weight
167::COMM;;else:
168::COMM;;class_weight_k = class_weight[k]
169::COMM;;if indices is not None:
170::COMM;;# Get class weights for the subsample, covering all classes in
171::COMM;;# case some labels that were present in the original data are
172::COMM;;# missing from the sample.
173::COMM;;y_subsample = y_full[indices]
174::COMM;;classes_subsample = np.unique(y_subsample)
175::COMM;;weight_k = np.take(
176::COMM;;compute_class_weight(
177::COMM;;class_weight_k, classes=classes_subsample, y=y_subsample
178::COMM;;),
179::COMM;;np.searchsorted(classes_subsample, classes_full),
180::COMM;;mode="clip",
181::COMM;;)
182::COMM;;classes_missing = set(classes_full) - set(classes_subsample)
183::COMM;;else:
184::COMM;;weight_k = compute_class_weight(
185::COMM;;class_weight_k, classes=classes_full, y=y_full
186::COMM;;)
187::COMM;;weight_k = weight_k[np.searchsorted(classes_full, y_full)]
188::COMM;;if classes_missing:
189::COMM;;# Make missing classes' weight zero
190::COMM;;weight_k[np.isin(y_full, list(classes_missing))] = 0.0
191::COMM;;expanded_class_weight.append(weight_k)
192::COMM;;expanded_class_weight = np.prod(expanded_class_weight, axis=0, dtype=np.float64)
193::COMM;;return expanded_class_weight

23::COMM;;extra : str, default=''

26::COMO;;# Adapted from https://wiki.python.org/moin/PythonDecoratorLibrary,
27::COMO;;# but with many changes.
32::COMM;;Parameters
33::COMM;;----------
34::COMM;;obj : object
39::COMO;;# Note that this is only triggered properly if the `deprecated`
40::COMO;;# decorator is placed before the `property` decorator, like so:
41::COMO;;#
42::COMO;;# @deprecated(msg)
43::COMO;;# @property
44::COMO;;# def deprecated_attribute_(self):
45::COMO;;# ...
63::COMO;;# Restore the original signature, see PEP 362.
68::COMM;;msg = "Function %s is deprecated" % fun.__name__
69::COMM;;if self.extra:
70::COMM;;msg += "; %s" % self.extra
71::COMM;;@functools.wraps(fun)
72::COMM;;def wrapped(*args, **kwargs):
73::COMM;;warnings.warn(msg, category=FutureWarning)
74::COMM;;return fun(*args, **kwargs)
75::COMM;;# Add a reference to the wrapped function so that we can introspect
76::COMM;;# on function arguments in Python 2 (already works in Python 3)
77::COMM;;wrapped.__wrapped__ = fun
78::COMM;;return wrapped
79::COMM;;def _decorate_property(self, prop):
80::COMM;;msg = self.extra
81::COMM;;@property
82::COMM;;@functools.wraps(prop.fget)
83::COMM;;def wrapped(*args, **kwargs):
84::COMM;;warnings.warn(msg, category=FutureWarning)
85::COMM;;return prop.fget(*args, **kwargs)
86::COMM;;return wrapped

444::COMM;;expected_failed_checks = expected_failed_checks or {}

448::COMM;;return False, "Check is not expected to fail"
449::COMM;;def estimator_checks_generator(

710::COMM;;msg = (
711::COMM;;"Passing a class was deprecated in version 0.23 "

713::COMM;;"Please pass an instance instead."

759::COMM;;}

203::COMM;;def randomized_range_finder(
204::COMM;;A, *, size, n_iter, power_iteration_normalizer="auto", random_state=None
205::COMM;;):
253::COMM;;A = check_array(A, accept_sparse=True)
254::COMM;;return _randomized_range_finder(
255::COMM;;A,
256::COMM;;size=size,
257::COMM;;n_iter=n_iter,
258::COMM;;power_iteration_normalizer=power_iteration_normalizer,
259::COMM;;random_state=random_state,
260::COMM;;)
261::COMM;;def _randomized_range_finder(
262::COMM;;A, *, size, n_iter, power_iteration_normalizer="auto", random_state=None
263::COMM;;):
267::COMO;;# Generating normal random vectors with shape: (A.shape[1], size)
268::COMO;;# XXX: generate random number directly from xp if it's possible
269::COMO;;# one day.
272::COMO;;# Use float32 computation and components if A has a float32 dtype.
274::COMO;;# Move Q to device if needed only after converting to float32 if needed to
275::COMO;;# avoid allocating unnecessary memory on the device.
276::COMO;;# Note: we cannot combine the astype and to_device operations in one go
277::COMO;;# using xp.asarray(..., dtype=dtype, device=device) because downcasting
278::COMO;;# from float64 to float32 in asarray might not always be accepted as only
279::COMO;;# casts following type promotion rules are guarateed to work.
280::COMO;;# https://github.com/data-apis/array-api/issues/647
283::COMO;;# Deal with "auto" mode
288::COMO;;# XXX: https://github.com/data-apis/array-api/issues/627
305::COMO;;# Use scipy.linalg instead of numpy.linalg when not explicitly
306::COMO;;# using the Array API.
314::COMO;;# Perform power iterations with Q to further 'imprint' the top
315::COMO;;# singular vectors of A in Q
319::COMO;;# Sample the range of A using by linear projection of Q
320::COMO;;# Extract an orthonormal basis
350::COMM;;This method solves the fixed-rank approximation problem described in [1]_
351::COMM;;(problem (1.5), p5).
352::COMM;;Refer to
353::COMM;;:ref:`sphx_glr_auto_examples_applications_wikipedia_principal_eigenvector.py`
354::COMM;;for a typical example where the power iteration algorithm is used to rank web pages.
355::COMM;;This algorithm is also known to be used as a building block in Google's PageRank
356::COMM;;algorithm.
357::COMM;;Parameters
358::COMM;;----------
359::COMM;;M : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
360::COMM;;Matrix to decompose.
361::COMM;;n_components : int
362::COMM;;Number of singular values and vectors to extract.
363::COMM;;n_oversamples : int, default=10
364::COMM;;Additional number of random vectors to sample the range of `M` so as
365::COMM;;to ensure proper conditioning. The total number of random vectors
366::COMM;;used to find the range of `M` is `n_components + n_oversamples`. Smaller
367::COMM;;number can improve speed but can negatively impact the quality of
368::COMM;;approximation of singular vectors and singular values. Users might wish
369::COMM;;to increase this parameter up to `2*k - n_components` where k is the
370::COMM;;effective rank, for large matrices, noisy problems, matrices with
371::COMM;;slowly decaying spectrums, or to increase precision accuracy. See [1]_
372::COMM;;(pages 5, 23 and 26).
373::COMM;;n_iter : int or 'auto', default='auto'
374::COMM;;Number of power iterations. It can be used to deal with very noisy
375::COMM;;problems. When 'auto', it is set to 4, unless `n_components` is small
376::COMM;;(< .1 * min(X.shape)) in which case `n_iter` is set to 7.
377::COMM;;This improves precision with few components. Note that in general
378::COMM;;users should rather increase `n_oversamples` before increasing `n_iter`
379::COMM;;as the principle of the randomized method is to avoid usage of these
380::COMM;;more costly power iterations steps. When `n_components` is equal
381::COMM;;or greater to the effective matrix rank and the spectrum does not
382::COMM;;present a slow decay, `n_iter=0` or `1` should even work fine in theory
383::COMM;;(see [1]_ page 9).
384::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
385::COMM;;power_iteration_normalizer : {'auto', 'QR', 'LU', 'none'}, default='auto'
386::COMM;;Whether the power iterations are normalized with step-by-step
387::COMM;;QR factorization (the slowest but most accurate), 'none'
388::COMM;;(the fastest but numerically unstable when `n_iter` is large, e.g.
389::COMM;;typically 5 or larger), or 'LU' factorization (numerically stable
390::COMM;;but can lose slightly in accuracy). The 'auto' mode applies no
391::COMM;;normalization if `n_iter` <= 2 and switches to LU otherwise.
392::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 0.18
393::COMM;;transpose : bool or 'auto', default='auto'
394::COMM;;Whether the algorithm should be applied to M.T instead of M. The
395::COMM;;result should approximately be the same. The 'auto' mode will
396::COMM;;trigger the transposition if M.shape[1] > M.shape[0] since this
397::COMM;;implementation of randomized SVD tend to be a little faster in that
398::COMM;;case.
399::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.18
400::COMM;;flip_sign : bool, default=True
401::COMM;;The output of a singular value decomposition is only unique up to a
402::COMM;;permutation of the signs of the singular vectors. If `flip_sign` is
403::COMM;;set to `True`, the sign ambiguity is resolved by making the largest
404::COMM;;loadings for each component in the left singular vectors positive.
405::COMM;;random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, default='warn'
406::COMM;;The seed of the pseudo random number generator to use when
407::COMM;;shuffling the data, i.e. getting the random vectors to initialize
408::COMM;;the algorithm. Pass an int for reproducible results across multiple
409::COMM;;function calls. See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
410::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.2
411::COMM;;The default value changed from 0 to None.
412::COMM;;svd_lapack_driver : {"gesdd", "gesvd"}, default="gesdd"
413::COMM;;Whether to use the more efficient divide-and-conquer approach
414::COMM;;(`"gesdd"`) or more general rectangular approach (`"gesvd"`) to compute
415::COMM;;the SVD of the matrix B, which is the projection of M into a low
416::COMM;;dimensional subspace, as described in [1]_.
417::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.2
418::COMM;;Returns
419::COMM;;-------
420::COMM;;u : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_components)
421::COMM;;Unitary matrix having left singular vectors with signs flipped as columns.
422::COMM;;s : ndarray of shape (n_components,)
423::COMM;;The singular values, sorted in non-increasing order.
424::COMM;;vh : ndarray of shape (n_components, n_features)
425::COMM;;Unitary matrix having right singular vectors with signs flipped as rows.
426::COMM;;Notes
427::COMM;;-----
428::COMM;;This algorithm finds a (usually very good) approximate truncated
429::COMM;;singular value decomposition using randomization to speed up the
430::COMM;;computations. It is particularly fast on large matrices on which
431::COMM;;you wish to extract only a small number of components. In order to
432::COMM;;obtain further speed up, `n_iter` can be set <=2 (at the cost of
433::COMM;;loss of precision). To increase the precision it is recommended to
434::COMM;;increase `n_oversamples`, up to `2*k-n_components` where k is the
435::COMM;;effective rank. Usually, `n_components` is chosen to be greater than k
436::COMM;;so increasing `n_oversamples` up to `n_components` should be enough.
437::COMM;;References
438::COMM;;----------
439::COMM;;.. [1] :arxiv:`"Finding structure with randomness:
440::COMM;;Stochastic algorithms for constructing approximate matrix decompositions"
441::COMM;;<0909.4061>`
442::COMM;;Halko, et al. (2009)
443::COMM;;.. [2] `"A randomized algorithm for the decomposition of matrices"
444::COMM;;<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.acha.2010.02.003>`_
445::COMM;;Per-Gunnar Martinsson, Vladimir Rokhlin and Mark Tygert (2011)
446::COMM;;.. [3] :arxiv:`"An implementation of a randomized algorithm for principal
447::COMM;;component analysis" <1412.3510>` A. Szlam et al. (2014)
448::COMM;;Examples
449::COMM;;--------
450::COMM;;>>> import numpy as np
451::COMM;;>>> from sklearn.utils.extmath import randomized_svd
452::COMM;;>>> a = np.array([[1, 2, 3, 5],
453::COMM;;... [3, 4, 5, 6],
454::COMM;;... [7, 8, 9, 10]])
455::COMM;;>>> U, s, Vh = randomized_svd(a, n_components=2, random_state=0)
456::COMM;;>>> U.shape, s.shape, Vh.shape
457::COMM;;((3, 2), (2,), (2, 4))
484::COMM;;xp, is_array_api_compliant = get_namespace(M)
485::COMM;;if sparse.issparse(M) and M.format in ("lil", "dok"):
486::COMM;;warnings.warn(
487::COMM;;"Calculating SVD of a {} is expensive. "
488::COMM;;"csr_matrix is more efficient.".format(type(M).__name__),
489::COMM;;sparse.SparseEfficiencyWarning,
490::COMM;;)
491::COMM;;random_state = check_random_state(random_state)
492::COMM;;n_random = n_components + n_oversamples
493::COMM;;n_samples, n_features = M.shape
494::COMM;;if n_iter == "auto":
495::COMM;;# Checks if the number of iterations is explicitly specified
496::COMM;;# Adjust n_iter. 7 was found a good compromise for PCA. See #5299
497::COMM;;n_iter = 7 if n_components < 0.1 * min(M.shape) else 4
498::COMM;;if transpose == "auto":
499::COMM;;transpose = n_samples < n_features
500::COMM;;if transpose:
501::COMM;;# this implementation is a bit faster with smaller shape[1]
502::COMM;;M = M.T
503::COMM;;Q = _randomized_range_finder(
504::COMM;;M,
505::COMM;;size=n_random,
506::COMM;;n_iter=n_iter,
507::COMM;;power_iteration_normalizer=power_iteration_normalizer,
508::COMM;;random_state=random_state,
509::COMM;;)
510::COMM;;# project M to the (k + p) dimensional space using the basis vectors
511::COMM;;B = Q.T @ M
512::COMM;;# compute the SVD on the thin matrix: (k + p) wide
513::COMM;;if is_array_api_compliant:
514::COMM;;Uhat, s, Vt = xp.linalg.svd(B, full_matrices=False)
515::COMM;;else:
516::COMM;;# When array_api_dispatch is disabled, rely on scipy.linalg
517::COMM;;# instead of numpy.linalg to avoid introducing a behavior change w.r.t.
518::COMM;;# previous versions of scikit-learn.
519::COMM;;Uhat, s, Vt = linalg.svd(
520::COMM;;B, full_matrices=False, lapack_driver=svd_lapack_driver
521::COMM;;)
522::COMM;;del B
523::COMM;;U = Q @ Uhat
524::COMM;;if flip_sign:
525::COMM;;if not transpose:
526::COMM;;U, Vt = svd_flip(U, Vt)
527::COMM;;else:
528::COMM;;# In case of transpose u_based_decision=false
529::COMM;;# to actually flip based on u and not v.
530::COMM;;U, Vt = svd_flip(U, Vt, u_based_decision=False)
531::COMM;;if transpose:
532::COMM;;# transpose back the results according to the input convention
533::COMM;;return Vt[:n_components, :].T, s[:n_components], U[:, :n_components].T
534::COMM;;else:
535::COMM;;return U[:, :n_components], s[:n_components], Vt[:n_components, :]
536::COMM;;def _randomized_eigsh(
537::COMM;;M,
538::COMM;;n_components,
539::COMM;;*,
540::COMM;;n_oversamples=10,
541::COMM;;n_iter="auto",
542::COMM;;power_iteration_normalizer="auto",
543::COMM;;selection="module",
544::COMM;;random_state=None,
545::COMM;;):
638::COMM;;if selection == "value": # pragma: no cover
639::COMM;;# to do : an algorithm can be found in the Halko et al reference
640::COMM;;raise NotImplementedError()
641::COMM;;elif selection == "module":
642::COMM;;# Note: no need for deterministic U and Vt (flip_sign=True),
643::COMM;;# as we only use the dot product UVt afterwards
644::COMM;;U, S, Vt = randomized_svd(
645::COMM;;M,
646::COMM;;n_components=n_components,
647::COMM;;n_oversamples=n_oversamples,
648::COMM;;n_iter=n_iter,
649::COMM;;power_iteration_normalizer=power_iteration_normalizer,
650::COMM;;flip_sign=False,
651::COMM;;random_state=random_state,
652::COMM;;)
653::COMM;;eigvecs = U[:, :n_components]
654::COMM;;eigvals = S[:n_components]
655::COMM;;# Conversion of Singular values into Eigenvalues:
656::COMM;;# For any eigenvalue t, the corresponding singular value is |t|.
657::COMM;;# So if there is a negative eigenvalue t, the corresponding singular
658::COMM;;# value will be -t, and the left (U) and right (V) singular vectors
659::COMM;;# will have opposite signs.
660::COMM;;# Fastest way: see <https://stackoverflow.com/a/61974002/7262247>
661::COMM;;diag_VtU = np.einsum("ji,ij->j", Vt[:n_components, :], U[:, :n_components])
662::COMM;;signs = np.sign(diag_VtU)
663::COMM;;eigvals = eigvals * signs
664::COMM;;else: # pragma: no cover
665::COMM;;raise ValueError("Invalid `selection`: %r" % selection)
666::COMM;;return eigvals, eigvecs
667::COMM;;def weighted_mode(a, w, *, axis=0):
699::COMC;;>>> weights = [1, 3, 0.5, 1.5, 1, 2] # deweight the 4's
705::COMM;;if axis is None:
706::COMM;;a = np.ravel(a)
707::COMM;;w = np.ravel(w)
708::COMM;;axis = 0
709::COMM;;else:
710::COMM;;a = np.asarray(a)
711::COMM;;w = np.asarray(w)
712::COMM;;if a.shape != w.shape:
713::COMM;;w = np.full(a.shape, w, dtype=w.dtype)
714::COMM;;scores = np.unique(np.ravel(a)) # get ALL unique values
715::COMM;;testshape = list(a.shape)
716::COMM;;testshape[axis] = 1
717::COMM;;oldmostfreq = np.zeros(testshape)
718::COMM;;oldcounts = np.zeros(testshape)
719::COMM;;for score in scores:
720::COMM;;template = np.zeros(a.shape)
721::COMM;;ind = a == score
722::COMM;;template[ind] = w[ind]
723::COMM;;counts = np.expand_dims(np.sum(template, axis), axis)
724::COMM;;mostfrequent = np.where(counts > oldcounts, score, oldmostfreq)
725::COMM;;oldcounts = np.maximum(counts, oldcounts)
726::COMM;;oldmostfreq = mostfrequent
727::COMM;;return mostfrequent, oldcounts
728::COMM;;def cartesian(arrays, out=None):
766::COMM;;arrays = [np.asarray(x) for x in arrays]
767::COMM;;shape = (len(x) for x in arrays)
768::COMM;;ix = np.indices(shape)
769::COMM;;ix = ix.reshape(len(arrays), -1).T
770::COMM;;if out is None:
771::COMM;;dtype = np.result_type(*arrays) # find the most permissive dtype
772::COMM;;out = np.empty_like(ix, dtype=dtype)
773::COMM;;for n, arr in enumerate(arrays):
774::COMM;;out[:, n] = arrays[n][ix[:, n]]
775::COMM;;return out
776::COMM;;def svd_flip(u, v, u_based_decision=True):
807::COMM;;xp, _ = get_namespace(*[a for a in [u, v] if a is not None])
808::COMM;;if u_based_decision:
809::COMM;;# columns of u, rows of v, or equivalently rows of u.T and v
810::COMM;;max_abs_u_cols = xp.argmax(xp.abs(u.T), axis=1)
811::COMM;;shift = xp.arange(u.T.shape[0], device=device(u))
812::COMM;;indices = max_abs_u_cols + shift * u.T.shape[1]
813::COMM;;signs = xp.sign(xp.take(xp.reshape(u.T, (-1,)), indices, axis=0))
814::COMM;;u *= signs[np.newaxis, :]
815::COMM;;if v is not None:
816::COMM;;v *= signs[:, np.newaxis]
817::COMM;;else:
818::COMM;;# rows of v, columns of u
819::COMM;;max_abs_v_rows = xp.argmax(xp.abs(v), axis=1)
820::COMM;;shift = xp.arange(v.shape[0], device=device(v))
821::COMM;;indices = max_abs_v_rows + shift * v.shape[1]
822::COMM;;signs = xp.sign(xp.take(xp.reshape(v, (-1,)), indices, axis=0))
823::COMM;;if u is not None:
824::COMM;;u *= signs[np.newaxis, :]
825::COMM;;v *= signs[:, np.newaxis]
826::COMM;;return u, v
827::COMM;;def softmax(X, copy=True):
846::COMM;;xp, is_array_api_compliant = get_namespace(X)
847::COMM;;if copy:
848::COMM;;X = xp.asarray(X, copy=True)
849::COMM;;max_prob = xp.reshape(xp.max(X, axis=1), (-1, 1))
850::COMM;;X -= max_prob
851::COMM;;if _is_numpy_namespace(xp):
852::COMM;;# optimization for NumPy arrays
853::COMM;;np.exp(X, out=np.asarray(X))
854::COMM;;else:
855::COMM;;# array_api does not have `out=`
856::COMM;;X = xp.exp(X)
857::COMM;;sum_prob = xp.reshape(xp.sum(X, axis=1), (-1, 1))
858::COMM;;X /= sum_prob
859::COMM;;return X
860::COMM;;def make_nonnegative(X, min_value=0):
877::COMM;;min_ = X.min()
878::COMM;;if min_ < min_value:
879::COMM;;if sparse.issparse(X):
880::COMM;;raise ValueError(
881::COMM;;"Cannot make the data matrix"
882::COMM;;" nonnegative because it is sparse."
883::COMM;;" Adding a value to every entry would"
884::COMM;;" make it no longer sparse."
885::COMM;;)
886::COMM;;X = X + (min_value - min_)
887::COMM;;return X
888::COMM;;# Use at least float64 for the accumulating functions to avoid precision issue
889::COMM;;# see https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/9393. The float64 is also retained
890::COMM;;# as it is in case the float overflows
891::COMM;;def _safe_accumulator_op(op, x, *args, **kwargs):
917::COMM;;xp, _, x_device = get_namespace_and_device(x)
918::COMM;;max_float_dtype = _max_precision_float_dtype(xp, device=x_device)
919::COMM;;if (
920::COMM;;xp.isdtype(x.dtype, "real floating")
921::COMM;;and xp.finfo(x.dtype).bits < xp.finfo(max_float_dtype).bits
922::COMM;;):
923::COMM;;# We need to upcast. Some ops support this natively; others don't.
924::COMM;;target_dtype = _max_precision_float_dtype(xp, device=x_device)
925::COMM;;def convert_dtype(arr):
926::COMM;;return xp.astype(arr, target_dtype, copy=False)
927::COMM;;if "dtype" in inspect.signature(op).parameters:
928::COMM;;return op(x, *args, **kwargs, dtype=target_dtype)
929::COMM;;else:
930::COMM;;# This op doesn't support a dtype kwarg, it seems. Rely on manual
931::COMM;;# type promotion, at the cost of memory allocations.
932::COMM;;# xp.matmul is the most commonly used op that lacks a dtype kwarg at
933::COMM;;# the time of writing.
934::COMM;;x = convert_dtype(x)
935::COMM;;args = [
936::COMM;;(convert_dtype(arg) if hasattr(arg, "dtype") else arg) for arg in args
937::COMM;;]
938::COMM;;return op(x, *args, **kwargs)
939::COMM;;def _incremental_mean_and_var(
940::COMM;;X, last_mean, last_variance, last_sample_count, sample_weight=None
941::COMM;;):
980::COMM;;# old = stats until now
981::COMM;;# new = the current increment
982::COMM;;# updated = the aggregated stats
983::COMM;;xp, _, X_device = get_namespace_and_device(X)
984::COMM;;max_float_dtype = _max_precision_float_dtype(xp, device=X_device)
985::COMM;;# Promoting int -> float is not guaranteed by the array-api, so we cast manually.
986::COMM;;# (Also, last_sample_count may be a python scalar)
987::COMM;;last_sample_count = xp.asarray(
988::COMM;;last_sample_count, dtype=max_float_dtype, device=X_device
989::COMM;;)
990::COMM;;last_sum = last_mean * last_sample_count
991::COMM;;X_nan_mask = xp.isnan(X)
992::COMM;;if xp.any(X_nan_mask):
993::COMM;;sum_op = _nansum
994::COMM;;else:
995::COMM;;sum_op = xp.sum
996::COMM;;if sample_weight is not None:
997::COMM;;# equivalent to np.nansum(X * sample_weight, axis=0)
998::COMM;;# safer because np.float64(X*W) != np.float64(X)*np.float64(W)
999::COMM;;new_sum = _safe_accumulator_op(
1000::COMM;;xp.matmul,
1001::COMM;;sample_weight,
1002::COMM;;xp.where(X_nan_mask, 0, X),
1003::COMM;;)
1004::COMM;;new_sample_count = _safe_accumulator_op(
1005::COMM;;xp.sum,
1006::COMM;;sample_weight[:, None] * xp.astype(~X_nan_mask, sample_weight.dtype),
1007::COMM;;axis=0,
1008::COMM;;)
1009::COMM;;else:
1010::COMM;;new_sum = _safe_accumulator_op(sum_op, X, axis=0)
1011::COMM;;n_samples = X.shape[0]
1012::COMM;;new_sample_count = n_samples - _safe_accumulator_op(
1013::COMM;;sum_op, xp.astype(X_nan_mask, X.dtype), axis=0
1014::COMM;;)
1015::COMM;;updated_sample_count = last_sample_count + new_sample_count
1016::COMM;;updated_mean = (last_sum + new_sum) / updated_sample_count
1017::COMM;;if last_variance is None:
1018::COMM;;updated_variance = None
1019::COMM;;else:
1020::COMM;;T = new_sum / new_sample_count
1021::COMM;;temp = X - T
1022::COMM;;if sample_weight is not None:
1023::COMM;;# equivalent to np.nansum((X-T)**2 * sample_weight, axis=0)
1024::COMM;;# safer because np.float64(X*W) != np.float64(X)*np.float64(W)
1025::COMM;;correction = _safe_accumulator_op(
1026::COMM;;xp.matmul,
1027::COMM;;sample_weight,
1028::COMM;;xp.where(X_nan_mask, 0, temp),
1029::COMM;;)
1030::COMM;;temp **= 2
1031::COMM;;new_unnormalized_variance = _safe_accumulator_op(
1032::COMM;;xp.matmul,
1033::COMM;;sample_weight,
1034::COMM;;xp.where(X_nan_mask, 0, temp),
1035::COMM;;)
1036::COMM;;else:
1037::COMM;;correction = _safe_accumulator_op(sum_op, temp, axis=0)
1038::COMM;;temp **= 2
1039::COMM;;new_unnormalized_variance = _safe_accumulator_op(sum_op, temp, axis=0)
1040::COMM;;# correction term of the corrected 2 pass algorithm.
1041::COMM;;# See "Algorithms for computing the sample variance: analysis
1042::COMM;;# and recommendations", by Chan, Golub, and LeVeque.
1043::COMM;;new_unnormalized_variance -= correction**2 / new_sample_count
1044::COMM;;last_unnormalized_variance = last_variance * last_sample_count
1045::COMM;;# There is no errstate equivalent for warning/error management in array API
1046::COMM;;context_manager = (
1047::COMM;;np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore")
1048::COMM;;if _is_numpy_namespace(xp)
1049::COMM;;else nullcontext()
1050::COMM;;)
1051::COMM;;with context_manager:
1052::COMM;;last_over_new_count = last_sample_count / new_sample_count
1053::COMM;;updated_unnormalized_variance = (
1054::COMM;;last_unnormalized_variance
1055::COMM;;+ new_unnormalized_variance
1056::COMM;;+ last_over_new_count
1057::COMM;;/ updated_sample_count
1058::COMM;;* (last_sum / last_over_new_count - new_sum) ** 2
1059::COMM;;)
1060::COMM;;zeros = last_sample_count == 0
1061::COMM;;updated_unnormalized_variance[zeros] = new_unnormalized_variance[zeros]
1062::COMM;;updated_variance = updated_unnormalized_variance / updated_sample_count
1063::COMM;;return updated_mean, updated_variance, updated_sample_count
1064::COMM;;def _deterministic_vector_sign_flip(u):
1077::COMM;;max_abs_rows = np.argmax(np.abs(u), axis=1)
1078::COMM;;signs = np.sign(u[range(u.shape[0]), max_abs_rows])
1079::COMM;;u *= signs[:, np.newaxis]
1080::COMM;;return u

1188::COMM;;def _approximate_mode(class_counts, n_draws, rng):
1223::COMM;;rng = check_random_state(rng)
1224::COMM;;# this computes a bad approximation to the mode of the
1225::COMM;;# multivariate hypergeometric given by class_counts and n_draws
1226::COMM;;continuous = class_counts / class_counts.sum() * n_draws
1227::COMM;;# floored means we don't overshoot n_samples, but probably undershoot
1228::COMM;;floored = np.floor(continuous)
1229::COMM;;# we add samples according to how much "left over" probability
1230::COMM;;# they had, until we arrive at n_samples
1231::COMM;;need_to_add = int(n_draws - floored.sum())
1232::COMM;;if need_to_add > 0:
1233::COMM;;remainder = continuous - floored
1234::COMM;;values = np.sort(np.unique(remainder))[::-1]
1235::COMM;;# add according to remainder, but break ties
1236::COMM;;# randomly to avoid biases
1237::COMM;;for value in values:
1238::COMM;;(inds,) = np.where(remainder == value)
1239::COMM;;# if we need_to_add less than what's in inds
1240::COMM;;# we draw randomly from them.
1241::COMM;;# if we need to add more, we add them all and
1242::COMM;;# go to the next value
1243::COMM;;add_now = min(len(inds), need_to_add)
1244::COMM;;inds = rng.choice(inds, size=add_now, replace=False)
1245::COMM;;floored[inds] += 1
1246::COMM;;need_to_add -= add_now
1247::COMM;;if need_to_add == 0:
1248::COMM;;break
1249::COMM;;return floored.astype(int)

9::COMM;;# Path and connected component analysis.
10::COMM;;# Code adapted from networkx
11::COMM;;@validate_params(
12::COMM;;{
13::COMM;;"graph": ["array-like", "sparse matrix"],
14::COMM;;"source": [Interval(Integral, 0, None, closed="left")],
15::COMM;;"cutoff": [Interval(Integral, 0, None, closed="left"), None],
16::COMM;;},
17::COMM;;prefer_skip_nested_validation=True,
18::COMM;;)
19::COMM;;def single_source_shortest_path_length(graph, source, *, cutoff=None):
49::COMM;;if sparse.issparse(graph):
50::COMM;;graph = graph.tolil()
51::COMM;;else:
52::COMM;;graph = sparse.lil_matrix(graph)
53::COMM;;seen = {} # level (number of hops) when seen in BFS
54::COMM;;level = 0 # the current level
55::COMM;;next_level = [source] # dict of nodes to check at next level
56::COMM;;while next_level:
57::COMM;;this_level = next_level # advance to next level
58::COMM;;next_level = set() # and start a new list (fringe)
59::COMM;;for v in this_level:
60::COMM;;if v not in seen:
61::COMM;;seen[v] = level # set the level of vertex v
62::COMM;;next_level.update(graph.rows[v])
63::COMM;;if cutoff is not None and cutoff <= level:
64::COMM;;break
65::COMM;;level += 1
66::COMM;;return seen # return all path lengths as dictionary
67::COMM;;def _fix_connected_components(
68::COMM;;X,
69::COMM;;graph,
70::COMM;;n_connected_components,
71::COMM;;component_labels,
72::COMM;;mode="distance",
73::COMM;;metric="euclidean",
74::COMM;;**kwargs,
75::COMM;;):
109::COMM;;if metric == "precomputed" and sparse.issparse(X):
110::COMM;;raise RuntimeError(
111::COMM;;"_fix_connected_components with metric='precomputed' requires the "
112::COMM;;"full distance matrix in X, and does not work with a sparse "
113::COMM;;"neighbors graph."
114::COMM;;)
115::COMM;;for i in range(n_connected_components):
116::COMM;;idx_i = np.flatnonzero(component_labels == i)
117::COMM;;Xi = X[idx_i]
118::COMM;;for j in range(i):
119::COMM;;idx_j = np.flatnonzero(component_labels == j)
120::COMM;;Xj = X[idx_j]
121::COMM;;if metric == "precomputed":
122::COMM;;D = X[np.ix_(idx_i, idx_j)]
123::COMM;;else:
124::COMM;;D = pairwise_distances(Xi, Xj, metric=metric, **kwargs)
125::COMM;;ii, jj = np.unravel_index(D.argmin(axis=None), D.shape)
126::COMM;;if mode == "connectivity":
127::COMM;;graph[idx_i[ii], idx_j[jj]] = 1
128::COMM;;graph[idx_j[jj], idx_i[ii]] = 1
129::COMM;;elif mode == "distance":
130::COMM;;graph[idx_i[ii], idx_j[jj]] = D[ii, jj]
131::COMM;;graph[idx_j[jj], idx_i[ii]] = D[ii, jj]
132::COMM;;else:
133::COMM;;raise ValueError(
134::COMM;;"Unknown mode=%r, should be one of ['connectivity', 'distance']."
135::COMM;;% mode
136::COMM;;)
137::COMM;;return graph

24::COMM;;def _get_params(self, attr, deep=True):
25::COMM;;out = super().get_params(deep=deep)
26::COMM;;if not deep:
27::COMM;;return out
28::COMM;;estimators = getattr(self, attr)
29::COMM;;try:
30::COMM;;out.update(estimators)
31::COMM;;except (TypeError, ValueError):
32::COMM;;# Ignore TypeError for cases where estimators is not a list of
33::COMM;;# (name, estimator) and ignore ValueError when the list is not
34::COMM;;# formatted correctly. This is to prevent errors when calling
35::COMM;;# `set_params`. `BaseEstimator.set_params` calls `get_params` which
36::COMM;;# can error for invalid values for `estimators`.
37::COMM;;return out
38::COMM;;for name, estimator in estimators:
39::COMM;;if hasattr(estimator, "get_params"):
40::COMM;;for key, value in estimator.get_params(deep=True).items():
41::COMM;;out["%s__%s" % (name, key)] = value
42::COMM;;return out
43::COMM;;def _set_params(self, attr, **params):
44::COMM;;# Ensure strict ordering of parameter setting:
45::COMM;;# 1. Replace the entire estimators collection
46::COMM;;if attr in params:
47::COMM;;setattr(self, attr, params.pop(attr))
48::COMM;;# 2. Replace individual estimators by name
49::COMM;;items = getattr(self, attr)
50::COMM;;if isinstance(items, list) and items:
51::COMM;;# Get item names used to identify valid names in params
52::COMM;;# `zip` raises a TypeError when `items` does not contains
53::COMM;;# elements of length 2
54::COMM;;with suppress(TypeError):
55::COMM;;item_names, _ = zip(*items)
56::COMM;;for name in list(params.keys()):
57::COMM;;if "__" not in name and name in item_names:
58::COMM;;self._replace_estimator(attr, name, params.pop(name))
59::COMM;;# 3. Individual estimator parameters and other initialisation arguments
60::COMM;;super().set_params(**params)
61::COMM;;return self
62::COMM;;def _replace_estimator(self, attr, name, new_val):
63::COMM;;# assumes `name` is a valid estimator name
64::COMM;;new_estimators = list(getattr(self, attr))
65::COMM;;for i, (estimator_name, _) in enumerate(new_estimators):
66::COMM;;if estimator_name == name:
67::COMM;;new_estimators[i] = (name, new_val)
68::COMM;;break
69::COMM;;setattr(self, attr, new_estimators)

396::COMM;;def class_distribution(y, sample_weight=None):
413::COMM;;classes = []
414::COMM;;n_classes = []
415::COMM;;class_prior = []
416::COMM;;n_samples, n_outputs = y.shape
417::COMM;;if sample_weight is not None:
418::COMM;;sample_weight = np.asarray(sample_weight)
419::COMM;;if issparse(y):
420::COMM;;y = y.tocsc()
421::COMM;;y_nnz = np.diff(y.indptr)
422::COMM;;for k in range(n_outputs):
423::COMM;;col_nonzero = y.indices[y.indptr[k] : y.indptr[k + 1]]
424::COMM;;# separate sample weights for zero and non-zero elements
425::COMM;;if sample_weight is not None:
426::COMM;;nz_samp_weight = sample_weight[col_nonzero]
427::COMM;;zeros_samp_weight_sum = np.sum(sample_weight) - np.sum(nz_samp_weight)
428::COMM;;else:
429::COMM;;nz_samp_weight = None
430::COMM;;zeros_samp_weight_sum = y.shape[0] - y_nnz[k]
431::COMM;;classes_k, y_k = np.unique(
432::COMM;;y.data[y.indptr[k] : y.indptr[k + 1]], return_inverse=True
433::COMM;;)
434::COMM;;class_prior_k = np.bincount(y_k, weights=nz_samp_weight)
435::COMM;;# An explicit zero was found, combine its weight with the weight
436::COMM;;# of the implicit zeros
437::COMM;;if 0 in classes_k:
438::COMM;;class_prior_k[classes_k == 0] += zeros_samp_weight_sum
439::COMM;;# If there is an implicit zero and it is not in classes and
440::COMM;;# class_prior, make an entry for it
441::COMM;;if 0 not in classes_k and y_nnz[k] < y.shape[0]:
442::COMM;;classes_k = np.insert(classes_k, 0, 0)
443::COMM;;class_prior_k = np.insert(class_prior_k, 0, zeros_samp_weight_sum)
444::COMM;;classes.append(classes_k)
445::COMM;;n_classes.append(classes_k.shape[0])
446::COMM;;class_prior.append(class_prior_k / class_prior_k.sum())
447::COMM;;else:
448::COMM;;for k in range(n_outputs):
449::COMM;;classes_k, y_k = np.unique(y[:, k], return_inverse=True)
450::COMM;;classes.append(classes_k)
451::COMM;;n_classes.append(classes_k.shape[0])
452::COMM;;class_prior_k = np.bincount(y_k, weights=sample_weight)
453::COMM;;class_prior.append(class_prior_k / class_prior_k.sum())
454::COMM;;return (classes, n_classes, class_prior)
455::COMM;;def _ovr_decision_function(predictions, confidences, n_classes):
470::COMM;;n_samples = predictions.shape[0]
471::COMM;;votes = np.zeros((n_samples, n_classes))
472::COMM;;sum_of_confidences = np.zeros((n_samples, n_classes))
473::COMM;;k = 0
474::COMM;;for i in range(n_classes):
475::COMM;;for j in range(i + 1, n_classes):
476::COMM;;sum_of_confidences[:, i] -= confidences[:, k]
477::COMM;;sum_of_confidences[:, j] += confidences[:, k]
478::COMM;;votes[predictions[:, k] == 0, i] += 1
479::COMM;;votes[predictions[:, k] == 1, j] += 1
480::COMM;;k += 1
481::COMM;;# Monotonically transform the sum_of_confidences to (-1/3, 1/3)
482::COMM;;# and add it with votes. The monotonic transformation is
483::COMM;;# f: x -> x / (3 * (|x| + 1)), it uses 1/3 instead of 1/2
484::COMM;;# to ensure that we won't reach the limits and change vote order.
485::COMM;;# The motivation is to use confidence levels as a way to break ties in
486::COMM;;# the votes without switching any decision made based on a difference
487::COMM;;# of 1 vote.
488::COMM;;transformed_confidences = sum_of_confidences / (
489::COMM;;3 * (np.abs(sum_of_confidences) + 1)
490::COMM;;)
491::COMM;;return votes + transformed_confidences
2::COMM;;Our own implementation of the Newton algorithm
3::COMM;;Unlike the scipy.optimize version, this version of the Newton conjugate
4::COMM;;gradient solver uses only one function call to retrieve the
5::COMM;;func value, the gradient value and a callable for the Hessian matvec
6::COMM;;product. If the function call is very expensive (e.g. for logistic
7::COMM;;regression with large design matrix), this approach gives very
8::COMM;;significant speedups.

95::COMM;;Solve iteratively the linear system 'fhess_p . xsupi = fgrad'
96::COMM;;with a conjugate gradient descent.

111::COMM;;Estimated solution.
115::COMC;;ri = np.copy(fgrad) # residual = fgrad - fhess_p @ xsupi
119::COMO;;# We also keep track of |p_i|^2.

134::COMO;;# See https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02924, Algo 1 Capped Conjugate Gradient.

166::COMC;;dri0 = dri1 # update np.dot(ri,ri) for next time.

10::COMM;;def _random_choice_csc(n_samples, classes, class_probability=None, random_state=None):
29::COMM;;data = array.array("i")
30::COMM;;indices = array.array("i")
31::COMM;;indptr = array.array("i", [0])
32::COMM;;for j in range(len(classes)):
33::COMM;;classes[j] = np.asarray(classes[j])
34::COMM;;if classes[j].dtype.kind != "i":
35::COMM;;raise ValueError("class dtype %s is not supported" % classes[j].dtype)
36::COMM;;classes[j] = classes[j].astype(np.int64, copy=False)
37::COMM;;# use uniform distribution if no class_probability is given
38::COMM;;if class_probability is None:
39::COMM;;class_prob_j = np.empty(shape=classes[j].shape[0])
40::COMM;;class_prob_j.fill(1 / classes[j].shape[0])
41::COMM;;else:
42::COMM;;class_prob_j = np.asarray(class_probability[j])
43::COMM;;if not np.isclose(np.sum(class_prob_j), 1.0):
44::COMM;;raise ValueError(
45::COMM;;"Probability array at index {0} does not sum to one".format(j)
46::COMM;;)
47::COMM;;if class_prob_j.shape[0] != classes[j].shape[0]:
48::COMM;;raise ValueError(
49::COMM;;"classes[{0}] (length {1}) and "
50::COMM;;"class_probability[{0}] (length {2}) have "
51::COMM;;"different length.".format(
52::COMM;;j, classes[j].shape[0], class_prob_j.shape[0]
53::COMM;;)
54::COMM;;)
55::COMM;;# If 0 is not present in the classes insert it with a probability 0.0
56::COMM;;if 0 not in classes[j]:
57::COMM;;classes[j] = np.insert(classes[j], 0, 0)
58::COMM;;class_prob_j = np.insert(class_prob_j, 0, 0.0)
59::COMM;;# If there are nonzero classes choose randomly using class_probability
60::COMM;;rng = check_random_state(random_state)
61::COMM;;if classes[j].shape[0] > 1:
62::COMM;;index_class_0 = np.flatnonzero(classes[j] == 0).item()
63::COMM;;p_nonzero = 1 - class_prob_j[index_class_0]
64::COMM;;nnz = int(n_samples * p_nonzero)
65::COMM;;ind_sample = sample_without_replacement(
66::COMM;;n_population=n_samples, n_samples=nnz, random_state=random_state
67::COMM;;)
68::COMM;;indices.extend(ind_sample)
69::COMM;;# Normalize probabilities for the nonzero elements
70::COMM;;classes_j_nonzero = classes[j] != 0
71::COMM;;class_probability_nz = class_prob_j[classes_j_nonzero]
72::COMM;;class_probability_nz_norm = class_probability_nz / np.sum(
73::COMM;;class_probability_nz
74::COMM;;)
75::COMM;;classes_ind = np.searchsorted(
76::COMM;;class_probability_nz_norm.cumsum(), rng.uniform(size=nnz)
77::COMM;;)
78::COMM;;data.extend(classes[j][classes_j_nonzero][classes_ind])
79::COMM;;indptr.append(len(indices))
80::COMM;;return sp.csc_matrix((data, indices, indptr), (n_samples, len(classes)), dtype=int)

1::COMO;;# Authors: The scikit-learn developers
2::COMO;;# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
11::COMM;;Implement an array API compatible (weighted version) of NumPy's 'inverted_cdf'
12::COMM;;method when `average=False` (default) and 'averaged_inverted_cdf' when
13::COMM;;`average=True`.
14::COMM;;For an array ordered by increasing values, when the percentile lies exactly on a
15::COMM;;data point:
16::COMM;;* 'inverted_cdf' takes the exact data point.
17::COMM;;* 'averaged_inverted_cdf' takes the average of the exact data point and the one
18::COMM;;above it (this means it gives the same result as `median` for unit weights).
19::COMM;;E.g., for the array [1, 2, 3, 4] the percentile rank at each data point would
20::COMM;;be [25, 50, 75, 100]. Percentile rank 50 lies on '2'. 'average_inverted_cdf'
21::COMM;;computes the average of '2' and '3', making it 'symmetrical' because if you
22::COMM;;reverse the array, rank 50 would fall on '3'. It also matches 'median'.
23::COMM;;On the other hand, 'inverted_cdf', which does not satisfy the symmetry property,
24::COMM;;would give '2'.
25::COMM;;When the requested percentile lies between two data points, both methods return
26::COMM;;the higher data point.
27::COMM;;E.g., for the array [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] the percentile rank at each data point would
28::COMM;;be [20, 40, 60, 80, 100]. Percentile rank 50, lies between '2' and '3'. Taking the
29::COMM;;higher data point is symmetrical because if you reverse the array, 50 would lie
30::COMM;;between '4' and '3'. Both methods match median in this case.
31::COMM;;If `array` is a 2D array, the `values` are selected along axis 0.
32::COMM;;`NaN` values are ignored by setting their weights to 0. If `array` is 2D, this
33::COMM;;is done in a column-isolated manner: a `NaN` in the second column, does not impact
34::COMM;;the percentile computed for the first column even if `sample_weight` is 1D.
35::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 0.24
36::COMM;;Accepts 2D `array`.
37::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.7
38::COMM;;Supports handling of `NaN` values.
39::COMM;;.. versionchanged:: 1.8
40::COMM;;Supports `average`, which calculates percentile using the
41::COMM;;"averaged_inverted_cdf" method.
42::COMM;;Parameters
43::COMM;;----------
44::COMM;;array : 1D or 2D array
45::COMM;;Values to take the weighted percentile of.
46::COMM;;sample_weight: 1D or 2D array
47::COMM;;Weights for each value in `array`. Must be same shape as `array` or of shape
48::COMM;;`(array.shape[0],)`.
49::COMM;;percentile_rank: scalar or 1D array, default=50
50::COMM;;The probability level(s) of the percentile(s) to compute, in percent. Must be
51::COMM;;between 0 and 100. If a 1D array, computes all percentiles (along each
52::COMM;;axis 0 if `array` is 2D).
53::COMM;;average : bool, default=False
54::COMM;;If `True`, uses the "averaged_inverted_cdf" quantile method, otherwise
55::COMM;;defaults to "inverted_cdf". "averaged_inverted_cdf" is symmetrical with
56::COMM;;unit `sample_weight`, such that the total of `sample_weight` below or equal to
57::COMM;;`_weighted_percentile(percentile_rank)` is the same as the total of
58::COMM;;`sample_weight` above or equal to `_weighted_percentile(100-percentile_rank)`.
59::COMM;;This symmetry is not guaranteed with non-unit weights.
60::COMM;;xp : array_namespace, default=None
61::COMM;;The standard-compatible namespace for `array`. Default: infer.
62::COMM;;Returns
63::COMM;;-------
64::COMM;;percentile : scalar, 1D array, or 2D array
65::COMM;;Weighted percentile at the requested probability level(s).
66::COMM;;If `array` is 1D and `percentile_rank` is scalar, returns a scalar.
67::COMM;;If `array` is 2D and `percentile_rank` is scalar, returns a 1D array
68::COMM;;of shape `(array.shape[1],)`
69::COMM;;If `array` is 1D and `percentile_rank` is 1D, returns a 1D array
70::COMM;;of shape `(percentile_rank.shape[0],)`
71::COMM;;If `array` is 2D and `percentile_rank` is 1D, returns a 2D array
72::COMM;;of shape `(array.shape[1], percentile_rank.shape[0])`
75::COMO;;# `sample_weight` should follow `array` for dtypes

100::COMO;;# NaN values get sorted to end (largest value)
104::COMO;;# Compute the weighted cumulative distribution function (CDF) based on

816::COMM;;raise TypeError("hello how are you")

826::COMM;;raise ValueError()

51::COMM;;def _inner_deprecate_positional_args(f):
52::COMM;;sig = signature(f)
53::COMM;;kwonly_args = []
54::COMM;;all_args = []
55::COMM;;for name, param in sig.parameters.items():
56::COMM;;if param.kind == Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD:
57::COMM;;all_args.append(name)
58::COMM;;elif param.kind == Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY:
59::COMM;;kwonly_args.append(name)
60::COMM;;@wraps(f)
61::COMM;;def inner_f(*args, **kwargs):
62::COMM;;extra_args = len(args) - len(all_args)
63::COMM;;if extra_args <= 0:
64::COMM;;return f(*args, **kwargs)
65::COMM;;# extra_args > 0

1584::COMM;;def _check_psd_eigenvalues(lambdas, enable_warnings=False):
1627::COMC;;>>> _check_psd_eigenvalues([1, 2]) # nominal case
1629::COMC;;>>> _check_psd_eigenvalues([5, 5j]) # significant imag part
1635::COMC;;>>> _check_psd_eigenvalues([5, 5e-5j]) # insignificant imag part
1637::COMC;;>>> _check_psd_eigenvalues([-5, -1]) # all negative
1643::COMC;;>>> _check_psd_eigenvalues([5, -1]) # significant negative
1649::COMC;;>>> _check_psd_eigenvalues([5, -5e-5]) # insignificant negative
1651::COMC;;>>> _check_psd_eigenvalues([5, 4e-12]) # bad conditioning (too small)
1654::COMM;;lambdas = np.array(lambdas)
1655::COMM;;is_double_precision = lambdas.dtype == np.float64
1656::COMM;;# note: the minimum value available is
1657::COMM;;# - single-precision: np.finfo('float32').eps = 1.2e-07
1658::COMM;;# - double-precision: np.finfo('float64').eps = 2.2e-16
1659::COMM;;# the various thresholds used for validation
1660::COMM;;# we may wish to change the value according to precision.
1661::COMM;;significant_imag_ratio = 1e-5
1662::COMM;;significant_neg_ratio = 1e-5 if is_double_precision else 5e-3
1663::COMM;;significant_neg_value = 1e-10 if is_double_precision else 1e-6
1664::COMM;;small_pos_ratio = 1e-12 if is_double_precision else 2e-7
1665::COMM;;# Check that there are no significant imaginary parts
1666::COMM;;if not np.isreal(lambdas).all():
1667::COMM;;max_imag_abs = np.abs(np.imag(lambdas)).max()
1668::COMM;;max_real_abs = np.abs(np.real(lambdas)).max()
1669::COMM;;if max_imag_abs > significant_imag_ratio * max_real_abs:
1670::COMM;;raise ValueError(
1671::COMM;;"There are significant imaginary parts in eigenvalues (%g "
1672::COMM;;"of the maximum real part). Either the matrix is not PSD, or "
1673::COMM;;"there was an issue while computing the eigendecomposition "
1674::COMM;;"of the matrix." % (max_imag_abs / max_real_abs)
1675::COMM;;)
1676::COMM;;# warn about imaginary parts being removed
1677::COMM;;if enable_warnings:
1678::COMM;;warnings.warn(
1679::COMM;;"There are imaginary parts in eigenvalues (%g "
1680::COMM;;"of the maximum real part). Either the matrix is not"
1681::COMM;;" PSD, or there was an issue while computing the "
1682::COMM;;"eigendecomposition of the matrix. Only the real "
1683::COMM;;"parts will be kept." % (max_imag_abs / max_real_abs),
1684::COMM;;PositiveSpectrumWarning,
1685::COMM;;)
1686::COMM;;# Remove all imaginary parts (even if zero)
1687::COMM;;lambdas = np.real(lambdas)
1688::COMM;;# Check that there are no significant negative eigenvalues
1689::COMM;;max_eig = lambdas.max()
1690::COMM;;if max_eig < 0:
1691::COMM;;raise ValueError(
1692::COMM;;"All eigenvalues are negative (maximum is %g). "
1693::COMM;;"Either the matrix is not PSD, or there was an "
1694::COMM;;"issue while computing the eigendecomposition of "
1695::COMM;;"the matrix." % max_eig
1696::COMM;;)
1697::COMM;;else:
1698::COMM;;min_eig = lambdas.min()
1699::COMM;;if (
1700::COMM;;min_eig < -significant_neg_ratio * max_eig
1701::COMM;;and min_eig < -significant_neg_value
1702::COMM;;):
1703::COMM;;raise ValueError(
1704::COMM;;"There are significant negative eigenvalues (%g"
1705::COMM;;" of the maximum positive). Either the matrix is "
1706::COMM;;"not PSD, or there was an issue while computing "
1707::COMM;;"the eigendecomposition of the matrix." % (-min_eig / max_eig)
1708::COMM;;)
1709::COMM;;elif min_eig < 0:
1710::COMM;;# Remove all negative values and warn about it
1711::COMM;;if enable_warnings:
1712::COMM;;warnings.warn(
1713::COMM;;"There are negative eigenvalues (%g of the "
1714::COMM;;"maximum positive). Either the matrix is not "
1715::COMM;;"PSD, or there was an issue while computing the"
1716::COMM;;" eigendecomposition of the matrix. Negative "
1717::COMM;;"eigenvalues will be replaced with 0." % (-min_eig / max_eig),
1718::COMM;;PositiveSpectrumWarning,
1719::COMM;;)
1720::COMM;;lambdas[lambdas < 0] = 0
1721::COMM;;# Check for conditioning (small positive non-zeros)
1722::COMM;;too_small_lambdas = (0 < lambdas) & (lambdas < small_pos_ratio * max_eig)
1723::COMM;;if too_small_lambdas.any():
1724::COMM;;if enable_warnings:
1725::COMM;;warnings.warn(
1726::COMM;;"Badly conditioned PSD matrix spectrum: the largest "
1727::COMM;;"eigenvalue is more than %g times the smallest. "
1728::COMM;;"Small eigenvalues will be replaced with 0."
1729::COMM;;"" % (1 / small_pos_ratio),
1730::COMM;;PositiveSpectrumWarning,
1731::COMM;;)
1732::COMM;;lambdas[too_small_lambdas] = 0
1733::COMM;;return lambdas

2367::COMM;;.. versionadded:: 1.6
2368::COMM;;Parameters
2369::COMM;;----------
2370::COMM;;_estimator : estimator instance
2371::COMM;;The estimator to validate the input for.
2372::COMM;;X : {array-like, sparse matrix, dataframe} of shape \
2373::COMM;;(n_samples, n_features), default='no validation'
2374::COMM;;The input samples.
2375::COMM;;If `'no_validation'`, no validation is performed on `X`. This is
2376::COMM;;useful for meta-estimator which can delegate input validation to
2377::COMM;;their underlying estimator(s). In that case `y` must be passed and
2378::COMM;;the only accepted `check_params` are `multi_output` and
2379::COMM;;`y_numeric`.
2380::COMM;;y : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default='no_validation'
2381::COMM;;The targets.
2382::COMM;;- If `None`, :func:`~sklearn.utils.check_array` is called on `X`. If
2383::COMM;;the estimator's `requires_y` tag is True, then an error will be raised.
2384::COMM;;- If `'no_validation'`, :func:`~sklearn.utils.check_array` is called
2385::COMM;;on `X` and the estimator's `requires_y` tag is ignored. This is a default
2386::COMM;;placeholder and is never meant to be explicitly set. In that case `X` must be
2387::COMM;;passed.
2388::COMM;;- Otherwise, only `y` with `_check_y` or both `X` and `y` are checked with
2389::COMM;;either :func:`~sklearn.utils.check_array` or
2390::COMM;;:func:`~sklearn.utils.check_X_y` depending on `validate_separately`.
2391::COMM;;reset : bool, default=True
2392::COMM;;Whether to reset the `n_features_in_` attribute.
2393::COMM;;If False, the input will be checked for consistency with data
2394::COMM;;provided when reset was last True.
2395::COMM;;.. note::
2396::COMM;;It is recommended to call `reset=True` in `fit` and in the first
2397::COMM;;call to `partial_fit`. All other methods that validate `X`
2398::COMM;;should set `reset=False`.
2399::COMM;;validate_separately : False or tuple of dicts, default=False
2400::COMM;;Only used if `y` is not `None`.
2401::COMM;;If `False`, call :func:`~sklearn.utils.check_X_y`. Else, it must be a tuple of
2402::COMM;;kwargs to be used for calling :func:`~sklearn.utils.check_array` on `X` and `y`
2403::COMM;;respectively.
2404::COMM;;`estimator=self` is automatically added to these dicts to generate
2405::COMM;;more informative error message in case of invalid input data.
2406::COMM;;skip_check_array : bool, default=False
2407::COMM;;If `True`, `X` and `y` are unchanged and only `feature_names_in_` and
2408::COMM;;`n_features_in_` are checked. Otherwise, :func:`~sklearn.utils.check_array`

2415::COMM;;more informative error message in case of invalid input data.

175::COMM;;def _process_queue(self, slot: Slot) -> None:
176::COMM;;if slot.latercall:
177::COMM;;# block processing until slot.latercall is called
178::COMM;;return
179::COMM;;# Delay queue processing if a download_delay is configured
180::COMM;;now = time()
181::COMM;;delay = slot.download_delay()
182::COMM;;if delay:
183::COMM;;penalty = delay - now + slot.lastseen
184::COMM;;if penalty > 0:
185::COMM;;slot.latercall = call_later(penalty, self._latercall, slot)
186::COMM;;return
187::COMM;;# Process enqueued requests if there are free slots to transfer for this slot
188::COMM;;while slot.queue and slot.free_transfer_slots() > 0:
189::COMM;;slot.lastseen = now
190::COMM;;request, queue_dfd = slot.queue.popleft()
191::COMM;;_schedule_coro(self._wait_for_download(slot, request, queue_dfd))
192::COMM;;# prevent burst if inter-request delays were configured
193::COMM;;if delay:
194::COMM;;self._process_queue(slot)
195::COMM;;break
196::COMM;;def _latercall(self, slot: Slot) -> None:
197::COMM;;slot.latercall = None
198::COMM;;self._process_queue(slot)
199::COMM;;async def _download(self, slot: Slot, request: Request) -> Response:
200::COMM;;# The order is very important for the following logic. Do not change!
201::COMM;;slot.transferring.add(request)
202::COMM;;try:
203::COMM;;# 1. Download the response
204::COMM;;response: Response = await maybe_deferred_to_future(
205::COMM;;self.handlers.download_request(request)
206::COMM;;)
207::COMM;;# 2. Notify response_downloaded listeners about the recent download
208::COMM;;# before querying queue for next request
209::COMM;;self.signals.send_catch_log(
210::COMM;;signal=signals.response_downloaded,
211::COMM;;response=response,
212::COMM;;request=request,
213::COMM;;spider=self.crawler.spider,
214::COMM;;)
215::COMM;;return response
216::COMM;;except Exception:
217::COMM;;await _defer_sleep_async()
218::COMM;;raise
219::COMM;;finally:
220::COMM;;# 3. After response arrives, remove the request from transferring
221::COMM;;# state to free up the transferring slot so it can be used by the
222::COMM;;# following requests (perhaps those which came from the downloader
223::COMM;;# middleware itself)
224::COMM;;slot.transferring.remove(request)
225::COMM;;self._process_queue(slot)
226::COMM;;self.signals.send_catch_log(
227::COMM;;signal=signals.request_left_downloader,

2::COMM;;An asynchronous FTP file download handler for scrapy which somehow emulates an http response.
3::COMM;;FTP connection parameters are passed using the request meta field:
4::COMM;;- ftp_user (required)
5::COMM;;- ftp_password (required)
6::COMM;;- ftp_passive (by default, enabled) sets FTP connection passive mode
7::COMM;;- ftp_local_filename
8::COMM;;- If not given, file data will come in the response.body, as a normal scrapy Response,
9::COMM;;which will imply that the entire file will be on memory.
10::COMM;;- if given, file data will be saved in a local file with the given name
11::COMM;;This helps when downloading very big files to avoid memory issues. In addition, for
12::COMM;;convenience the local file name will also be given in the response body.
13::COMM;;The status of the built html response will be, by default
14::COMM;;- 200 in case of success
15::COMM;;- 404 in case specified file was not found in the server (ftp code 550)
16::COMM;;or raise corresponding ftp exception otherwise
17::COMM;;The matching from server ftp command return codes to html response codes is defined in the
18::COMM;;CODE_MAPPING attribute of the handler class. The key 'default' is used for any code
19::COMM;;that is not explicitly present among the map keys. You may need to overwrite this
20::COMM;;mapping if want a different behaviour than default.
21::COMM;;In case of status 200 request, response.headers will come with two keys:
22::COMM;;'Local Filename' - with the value of the local filename if given
23::COMM;;'Size' - with size of the downloaded data

101::COMM;;Requests are stored into priority queues
102::COMM;;(:setting:`SCHEDULER_PRIORITY_QUEUE`) that sort requests by
103::COMM;;:attr:`~scrapy.http.Request.priority`.
104::COMM;;By default, a single, memory-based priority queue is used for all requests.
105::COMM;;When using :setting:`JOBDIR`, a disk-based priority queue is also created,
106::COMM;;and only unserializable requests are stored in the memory-based priority
107::COMM;;queue. For a given priority value, requests in memory take precedence over
108::COMM;;requests in disk.
109::COMM;;Each priority queue stores requests in separate internal queues, one per
110::COMM;;priority value. The memory priority queue uses
111::COMM;;:setting:`SCHEDULER_MEMORY_QUEUE` queues, while the disk priority queue
112::COMM;;uses :setting:`SCHEDULER_DISK_QUEUE` queues. The internal queues determine
113::COMM;;:ref:`request order <request-order>` when requests have the same priority.
114::COMM;;:ref:`Start requests <start-requests>` are stored into separate internal
115::COMM;;queues by default, and :ref:`ordered differently <start-request-order>`.
116::COMM;;Duplicate requests are filtered out with an instance of
117::COMM;;:setting:`DUPEFILTER_CLASS`.
118::COMM;;.. _request-order:
119::COMM;;Request order
120::COMM;;=============
121::COMM;;With default settings, pending requests are stored in a LIFO_ queue
122::COMM;;(:ref:`except for start requests <start-request-order>`). As a result,
123::COMM;;crawling happens in `DFO order`_, which is usually the most convenient
124::COMM;;crawl order. However, you can enforce :ref:`BFO <bfo>` or :ref:`a custom
125::COMM;;order <custom-request-order>` (:ref:`except for the first few requests
126::COMM;;<concurrency-v-order>`).
127::COMM;;.. _LIFO: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type)
128::COMM;;.. _DFO order: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth-first_search
129::COMM;;.. _start-request-order:
130::COMM;;Start request order
131::COMM;;-------------------
132::COMM;;:ref:`Start requests <start-requests>` are sent in the order they are
133::COMM;;yielded from :meth:`~scrapy.Spider.start`, and given the same
134::COMM;;:attr:`~scrapy.http.Request.priority`, other requests take precedence over
135::COMM;;start requests.
136::COMM;;You can set :setting:`SCHEDULER_START_MEMORY_QUEUE` and
137::COMM;;:setting:`SCHEDULER_START_DISK_QUEUE` to ``None`` to handle start requests
138::COMM;;the same as other requests when it comes to order and priority.
139::COMM;;.. _bfo:
140::COMM;;Crawling in BFO order
141::COMM;;---------------------
142::COMM;;If you do want to crawl in `BFO order`_, you can do it by setting the
143::COMM;;following :ref:`settings <topics-settings>`:
144::COMM;;| :setting:`DEPTH_PRIORITY` = ``1``
145::COMM;;| :setting:`SCHEDULER_DISK_QUEUE` = ``"scrapy.squeues.PickleFifoDiskQueue"``
146::COMM;;| :setting:`SCHEDULER_MEMORY_QUEUE` = ``"scrapy.squeues.FifoMemoryQueue"``
147::COMM;;.. _BFO order: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breadth-first_search
148::COMM;;.. _custom-request-order:
149::COMM;;Crawling in a custom order
150::COMM;;--------------------------
151::COMM;;You can manually set :attr:`~scrapy.http.Request.priority` on requests to
152::COMM;;force a specific request order.
153::COMM;;.. _concurrency-v-order:
154::COMM;;Concurrency affects order
155::COMM;;-------------------------
156::COMM;;While pending requests are below the configured values of
157::COMM;;:setting:`CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`, :setting:`CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_DOMAIN`
158::COMM;;or :setting:`CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_IP`, those requests are sent
159::COMM;;concurrently.
160::COMM;;As a result, the first few requests of a crawl may not follow the desired
161::COMM;;order. Lowering those settings to ``1`` enforces the desired order except
162::COMM;;for the very first request, but it significantly slows down the crawl as a
163::COMM;;whole.

215::COMO;;# the result is available immediately if _process_spider_output didn't do downgrading
217::COMO;;# we forbid waiting here because otherwise we would need to return a deferred from
218::COMO;;# _process_spider_exception too, which complicates the architecture
229::COMO;;# This method cannot be made async def, as _process_spider_exception relies on the Deferred result
230::COMO;;# being available immediately which doesn't work when it's a wrapped coroutine.

244::COMO;;# There are three cases for the middleware: def foo, async def foo, def foo + async def foo_async.
245::COMO;;# 1. def foo. Sync iterables are passed as is, async ones are downgraded.
246::COMO;;# 2. async def foo. Sync iterables are upgraded, async ones are passed as is.
