101::COMM;;def _format_cookie(self, cookie: VerboseCookie, request: Request) -> str | None:
106::COMM;;decoded = {}
107::COMM;;flags = set()
108::COMM;;for key in ("name", "value", "path", "domain"):
109::COMM;;value = cookie.get(key)
110::COMM;;if value is None:
111::COMM;;if key in ("name", "value"):
112::COMM;;msg = f"Invalid cookie found in request {request}: {cookie} ('{key}' is missing)"
113::COMM;;logger.warning(msg)
114::COMM;;return None
115::COMM;;continue
116::COMM;;if isinstance(value, (bool, float, int, str)):
117::COMM;;decoded[key] = str(value)
118::COMM;;else:
119::COMM;;assert isinstance(value, bytes)
120::COMM;;try:
121::COMM;;decoded[key] = value.decode("utf8")
122::COMM;;except UnicodeDecodeError:
123::COMM;;logger.warning(
124::COMM;;"Non UTF-8 encoded cookie found in request %s: %s",
125::COMM;;request,
126::COMM;;cookie,
127::COMM;;)
128::COMM;;decoded[key] = value.decode("latin1", errors="replace")
129::COMM;;for flag in ("secure",):
130::COMM;;value = cookie.get(flag, _UNSET)
131::COMM;;if value is _UNSET or not value:
132::COMM;;continue
133::COMM;;flags.add(flag)
134::COMM;;cookie_str = f"{decoded.pop('name')}={decoded.pop('value')}"
135::COMM;;for key, value in decoded.items(): # path, domain
136::COMM;;cookie_str += f"; {key.capitalize()}={value}"
137::COMM;;for flag in flags: # secure
138::COMM;;cookie_str += f"; {flag.capitalize()}"
139::COMM;;return cookie_str
140::COMM;;def _get_request_cookies(
141::COMM;;self, jar: CookieJar, request: Request
142::COMM;;) -> Sequence[Cookie]:

147::COMM;;return []
148::COMM;;cookies: Iterable[VerboseCookie]
149::COMM;;if isinstance(request.cookies, dict):
150::COMM;;cookies = tuple({"name": k, "value": v} for k, v in request.cookies.items())
151::COMM;;else:
152::COMM;;cookies = request.cookies
153::COMM;;for cookie in cookies:
154::COMM;;cookie.setdefault("secure", urlparse_cached(request).scheme == "https")
155::COMM;;formatted = filter(None, (self._format_cookie(c, request) for c in cookies))
156::COMM;;response = Response(request.url, headers={"Set-Cookie": formatted})
157::COMM;;return jar.make_cookies(response, request)

52::COMM;;retry request. It is used to access the :ref:`settings <topics-settings>`
53::COMM;;and :ref:`stats <topics-stats>`, and to provide extra logging context (see
54::COMM;;:func:`logging.debug`).
55::COMM;;*reason* is a string or an :class:`Exception` object that indicates the
56::COMM;;reason why the request needs to be retried. It is used to name retry stats.
57::COMM;;*max_retry_times* is a number that determines the maximum number of times
58::COMM;;that *request* can be retried. If not specified or ``None``, the number is
59::COMM;;read from the :reqmeta:`max_retry_times` meta key of the request. If the
60::COMM;;:reqmeta:`max_retry_times` meta key is not defined or ``None``, the number
61::COMM;;is read from the :setting:`RETRY_TIMES` setting.
62::COMM;;*priority_adjust* is a number that determines how the priority of the new
63::COMM;;request changes in relation to *request*. If not specified, the number is
64::COMM;;read from the :setting:`RETRY_PRIORITY_ADJUST` setting.
65::COMM;;*logger* is the logging.Logger object to be used when logging messages

94::COMM;;# If target delay is bigger than old delay, then use it instead of mean.
95::COMM;;# It works better with problematic sites.

2::COMM;;Item Loader
3::COMM;;See documentation in docs/topics/loaders.rst
14::COMM;;A user-friendly abstraction to populate an :ref:`item <topics-items>` with data
15::COMM;;by applying :ref:`field processors <topics-loaders-processors>` to scraped data.
16::COMM;;When instantiated with a ``selector`` or a ``response`` it supports
17::COMM;;data extraction from web pages using :ref:`selectors <topics-selectors>`.
18::COMM;;:param item: The item instance to populate using subsequent calls to
19::COMM;;:meth:`~ItemLoader.add_xpath`, :meth:`~ItemLoader.add_css`,
20::COMM;;or :meth:`~ItemLoader.add_value`.
21::COMM;;:type item: scrapy.item.Item
22::COMM;;:param selector: The selector to extract data from, when using the
23::COMM;;:meth:`add_xpath`, :meth:`add_css`, :meth:`replace_xpath`, or
24::COMM;;:meth:`replace_css` method.
25::COMM;;:type selector: :class:`~scrapy.Selector` object
26::COMM;;:param response: The response used to construct the selector using the
27::COMM;;:attr:`default_selector_class`, unless the selector argument is given,
28::COMM;;in which case this argument is ignored.
29::COMM;;:type response: :class:`~scrapy.http.Response` object
30::COMM;;If no item is given, one is instantiated automatically using the class in
31::COMM;;:attr:`default_item_class`.
32::COMM;;The item, selector, response and remaining keyword arguments are
33::COMM;;assigned to the Loader context (accessible through the :attr:`context` attribute).
34::COMM;;.. attribute:: item
35::COMM;;The item object being parsed by this Item Loader.
36::COMM;;This is mostly used as a property so, when attempting to override this
37::COMM;;value, you may want to check out :attr:`default_item_class` first.
38::COMM;;.. attribute:: context
39::COMM;;The currently active :ref:`Context <loaders-context>` of this Item Loader.
40::COMM;;.. attribute:: default_item_class
41::COMM;;An :ref:`item <topics-items>` class (or factory), used to instantiate
42::COMM;;items when not given in the ``__init__`` method.
43::COMM;;.. attribute:: default_input_processor
44::COMM;;The default input processor to use for those fields which don't specify
45::COMM;;one.
46::COMM;;.. attribute:: default_output_processor
47::COMM;;The default output processor to use for those fields which don't specify
48::COMM;;one.
49::COMM;;.. attribute:: default_selector_class
50::COMM;;The class used to construct the :attr:`selector` of this
51::COMM;;:class:`ItemLoader`, if only a response is given in the ``__init__`` method.
52::COMM;;If a selector is given in the ``__init__`` method this attribute is ignored.
53::COMM;;This attribute is sometimes overridden in subclasses.
54::COMM;;.. attribute:: selector
55::COMM;;The :class:`~scrapy.Selector` object to extract data from.
56::COMM;;It's either the selector given in the ``__init__`` method or one created from
57::COMM;;the response given in the ``__init__`` method using the
58::COMM;;:attr:`default_selector_class`. This attribute is meant to be
59::COMM;;read-only.

12::COMO;;# typing.Self requires Python 3.11
28::COMM;;All methods must return a dictionary listing the parameters ``level``, ``msg``
29::COMM;;and ``args`` which are going to be used for constructing the log message when
30::COMM;;calling ``logging.log``.
31::COMM;;Dictionary keys for the method outputs:
32::COMM;;* ``level`` is the log level for that action, you can use those from the
33::COMM;;`python logging library <https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html>`_ :
34::COMM;;``logging.DEBUG``, ``logging.INFO``, ``logging.WARNING``, ``logging.ERROR``
35::COMM;;and ``logging.CRITICAL``.
36::COMM;;* ``msg`` should be a string that can contain different formatting placeholders.
37::COMM;;This string, formatted with the provided ``args``, is going to be the long message
38::COMM;;for that action.
39::COMM;;* ``args`` should be a tuple or dict with the formatting placeholders for ``msg``.
40::COMM;;The final log message is computed as ``msg % args``.
41::COMM;;Users can define their own ``LogFormatter`` class if they want to customize how
42::COMM;;each action is logged or if they want to omit it entirely. In order to omit
43::COMM;;logging an action the method must return ``None``.
44::COMM;;Here is an example on how to create a custom log formatter to lower the severity level of
45::COMM;;the log message when an item is dropped from the pipeline::
46::COMM;;class PoliteLogFormatter(logformatter.LogFormatter):
47::COMM;;def dropped(self, item, exception, response, spider):
48::COMM;;return {
49::COMM;;'level': logging.INFO, # lowering the level from logging.WARNING
50::COMM;;'msg': "Dropped: %(exception)s" + os.linesep + "%(item)s",
51::COMM;;'args': {
52::COMM;;'exception': exception,
53::COMM;;'item': item,
54::COMM;;}
55::COMM;;}
61::COMM;;request_flags = f" {request.flags!s}" if request.flags else ""
62::COMM;;response_flags = f" {response.flags!s}" if response.flags else ""
63::COMM;;return {
64::COMM;;"level": logging.DEBUG,
65::COMM;;"msg": CRAWLEDMSG,
66::COMM;;"args": {
67::COMM;;"status": response.status,
68::COMM;;"request": request,
69::COMM;;"request_flags": request_flags,
70::COMM;;"referer": referer_str(request),
71::COMM;;"response_flags": response_flags,
72::COMM;;# backward compatibility with Scrapy logformatter below 1.4 version
73::COMM;;"flags": response_flags,
74::COMM;;},
75::COMM;;}
76::COMM;;def scraped(
77::COMM;;self, item: Any, response: Response | Failure | None, spider: Spider
78::COMM;;) -> LogFormatterResult:
103::COMM;;if (level := getattr(exception, "log_level", None)) is None:
104::COMM;;level = spider.crawler.settings["DEFAULT_DROPITEM_LOG_LEVEL"]
105::COMM;;if isinstance(level, str):
106::COMM;;level = getattr(logging, level)
107::COMM;;return {
108::COMM;;"level": level,
109::COMM;;"msg": DROPPEDMSG,
110::COMM;;"args": {
111::COMM;;"exception": exception,
112::COMM;;"item": item,
113::COMM;;},
114::COMM;;}
115::COMM;;def item_error(
116::COMM;;self,
117::COMM;;item: Any,
118::COMM;;exception: BaseException,

2::COMM;;XPath selectors based on lxml
22::COMM;;The :class:`SelectorList` class is a subclass of the builtin ``list``
23::COMM;;class, which provides a few additional methods.
27::COMM;;An instance of :class:`Selector` is a wrapper over response to select
28::COMM;;certain parts of its content.
29::COMM;;``response`` is an :class:`~scrapy.http.HtmlResponse` or an
30::COMM;;:class:`~scrapy.http.XmlResponse` object that will be used for selecting
31::COMM;;and extracting data.
32::COMM;;``text`` is a unicode string or utf-8 encoded text for cases when a
33::COMM;;``response`` isn't available. Using ``text`` and ``response`` together is
34::COMM;;undefined behavior.
35::COMM;;``type`` defines the selector type, it can be ``"html"``, ``"xml"``, ``"json"``
36::COMM;;or ``None`` (default).
37::COMM;;If ``type`` is ``None``, the selector automatically chooses the best type
38::COMM;;based on ``response`` type (see below), or defaults to ``"html"`` in case it
39::COMM;;is used together with ``text``.
40::COMM;;If ``type`` is ``None`` and a ``response`` is passed, the selector type is
41::COMM;;inferred from the response type as follows:
42::COMM;;* ``"html"`` for :class:`~scrapy.http.HtmlResponse` type
43::COMM;;* ``"xml"`` for :class:`~scrapy.http.XmlResponse` type
44::COMM;;* ``"json"`` for :class:`~scrapy.http.TextResponse` type
45::COMM;;* ``"html"`` for anything else
46::COMM;;Otherwise, if ``type`` is set, the selector type will be forced and no
47::COMM;;detection will occur.

79::COMO;;# Note: this does not follow https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-secure-contexts/#is-url-trustworthy
88::COMM;;https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-no-referrer
89::COMM;;The simplest policy is "no-referrer", which specifies that no referrer information
90::COMM;;is to be sent along with requests made from a particular request client to any origin.
91::COMM;;The header will be omitted entirely.
98::COMM;;https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-no-referrer-when-downgrade
99::COMM;;The "no-referrer-when-downgrade" policy sends a full URL along with requests
100::COMM;;from a TLS-protected environment settings object to a potentially trustworthy URL,
101::COMM;;and requests from clients which are not TLS-protected to any origin.
102::COMM;;Requests from TLS-protected clients to non-potentially trustworthy URLs,
103::COMM;;on the other hand, will contain no referrer information.
104::COMM;;A Referer HTTP header will not be sent.
105::COMM;;This is a user agent's default behavior, if no policy is otherwise specified.
114::COMM;;https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-same-origin
115::COMM;;The "same-origin" policy specifies that a full URL, stripped for use as a referrer,
116::COMM;;is sent as referrer information when making same-origin requests from a particular request client.
117::COMM;;Cross-origin requests, on the other hand, will contain no referrer information.
118::COMM;;A Referer HTTP header will not be sent.
127::COMM;;https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-origin
128::COMM;;The "origin" policy specifies that only the ASCII serialization
129::COMM;;of the origin of the request client is sent as referrer information
130::COMM;;when making both same-origin requests and cross-origin requests
131::COMM;;from a particular request client.
138::COMM;;https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-strict-origin
139::COMM;;The "strict-origin" policy sends the ASCII serialization
140::COMM;;of the origin of the request client when making requests:
141::COMM;;- from a TLS-protected environment settings object to a potentially trustworthy URL, and
142::COMM;;- from non-TLS-protected environment settings objects to any origin.
143::COMM;;Requests from TLS-protected request clients to non- potentially trustworthy URLs,
144::COMM;;on the other hand, will contain no referrer information.
145::COMM;;A Referer HTTP header will not be sent.
157::COMM;;https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-origin-when-cross-origin
158::COMM;;The "origin-when-cross-origin" policy specifies that a full URL,
159::COMM;;stripped for use as a referrer, is sent as referrer information
160::COMM;;when making same-origin requests from a particular request client,
161::COMM;;and only the ASCII serialization of the origin of the request client
162::COMM;;is sent as referrer information when making cross-origin requests
163::COMM;;from a particular request client.
173::COMM;;https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-strict-origin-when-cross-origin
174::COMM;;The "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" policy specifies that a full URL,
175::COMM;;stripped for use as a referrer, is sent as referrer information
176::COMM;;when making same-origin requests from a particular request client,
177::COMM;;and only the ASCII serialization of the origin of the request client
178::COMM;;when making cross-origin requests:
179::COMM;;- from a TLS-protected environment settings object to a potentially trustworthy URL, and
180::COMM;;- from non-TLS-protected environment settings objects to any origin.
181::COMM;;Requests from TLS-protected clients to non- potentially trustworthy URLs,
182::COMM;;on the other hand, will contain no referrer information.
183::COMM;;A Referer HTTP header will not be sent.
198::COMM;;https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-unsafe-url
199::COMM;;The "unsafe-url" policy specifies that a full URL, stripped for use as a referrer,
200::COMM;;is sent along with both cross-origin requests
201::COMM;;and same-origin requests made from a particular request client.
202::COMM;;Note: The policy's name doesn't lie; it is unsafe.
203::COMM;;This policy will leak origins and paths from TLS-protected resources
204::COMM;;to insecure origins.
205::COMM;;Carefully consider the impact of setting such a policy for potentially sensitive documents.

67::COMM;;before attending pending delayed calls, so do not set delay to zero.
74::COMM;;before attending pending delayed calls, so do not set delay to zero.
111::COMM;;callback/errback to next reactor loop
128::COMC;;callable: Callable[Concatenate[_T, _P], _T2], # noqa: A002
133::COMM;;using no more than ``count`` concurrent calls.
134::COMM;;Taken from: https://jcalderone.livejournal.com/24285.html
141::COMM;;for using in Cooperator.coiterate(). As it's only needed for parallel_async(),
142::COMM;;it calls the callable directly in the callback, instead of providing a more
143::COMM;;generic interface.
144::COMM;;On the outside, this class behaves as an iterator that yields Deferreds.
145::COMM;;Each Deferred is fired with the result of the callable which was called on
146::COMM;;the next result from aiterator. It raises StopIteration when aiterator is
147::COMM;;exhausted, as expected.
148::COMM;;Cooperator calls __next__() multiple times and waits on the Deferreds
149::COMM;;returned from it. As async generators (since Python 3.8) don't support
150::COMM;;awaiting on __anext__() several times in parallel, we need to serialize
151::COMM;;this. It's done by storing the Deferreds returned from __next__() and
152::COMM;;firing the oldest one when a result from __anext__() is available.
153::COMM;;The workflow:
154::COMM;;1. When __next__() is called for the first time, it creates a Deferred, stores it
155::COMM;;in self.waiting_deferreds and returns it. It also makes a Deferred that will wait
156::COMM;;for self.aiterator.__anext__() and puts it into self.anext_deferred.
157::COMM;;2. If __next__() is called again before self.anext_deferred fires, more Deferreds
158::COMM;;are added to self.waiting_deferreds.
159::COMM;;3. When self.anext_deferred fires, it either calls _callback() or _errback(). Both
160::COMM;;clear self.anext_deferred.
161::COMM;;3.1. _callback() calls the callable passing the result value that it takes, pops a
162::COMM;;Deferred from self.waiting_deferreds, and if the callable result was a Deferred, it
163::COMM;;chains those Deferreds so that the waiting Deferred will fire when the result
164::COMM;;Deferred does, otherwise it fires it directly. This causes one awaiting task to
165::COMM;;receive a result. If self.waiting_deferreds is still not empty, new __anext__() is
166::COMM;;called and self.anext_deferred is populated.
167::COMM;;3.2. _errback() checks the exception class. If it's StopAsyncIteration it means
168::COMM;;self.aiterator is exhausted and so it sets self.finished and fires all
169::COMM;;self.waiting_deferreds. Other exceptions are propagated.
170::COMM;;4. If __next__() is called after __anext__() was handled, then if self.finished is
171::COMM;;True, it raises StopIteration, otherwise it acts like in step 2, but if
172::COMM;;self.anext_deferred is now empty is also populates it with a new __anext__().
173::COMM;;Note that CooperativeTask ignores the value returned from the Deferred that it waits
174::COMM;;for, so we fire them with None when needed.
175::COMM;;It may be possible to write an async iterator-aware replacement for
176::COMM;;Cooperator/CooperativeTask and use it instead of this adapter to achieve the same
177::COMM;;goal.
194::COMO;;# This gets called when the result from aiterator.__anext__() is available.
195::COMO;;# It calls the callable on it and sends the result to the oldest waiting Deferred
196::COMO;;# (by chaining if the result is a Deferred too or by firing if not).
209::COMO;;# This gets called on any exceptions in aiterator.__anext__().
210::COMO;;# It handles StopAsyncIteration by stopping the iteration and reraises all others.
217::COMO;;# This starts waiting for the next result from aiterator.
218::COMO;;# If aiterator is exhausted, _errback will be called.
222::COMO;;# This puts a new Deferred into self.waiting_deferreds and returns it.
223::COMO;;# It also calls __anext__() if needed.

31::COMM;;Return the request fingerprint.
32::COMM;;The request fingerprint is a hash that uniquely identifies the resource the
33::COMM;;request points to. For example, take the following two urls:
34::COMM;;``http://www.example.com/query?id=111&cat=222``,
35::COMM;;``http://www.example.com/query?cat=222&id=111``.
36::COMM;;Even though those are two different URLs both point to the same resource
37::COMM;;and are equivalent (i.e. they should return the same response).
38::COMM;;Another example are cookies used to store session ids. Suppose the
39::COMM;;following page is only accessible to authenticated users:
40::COMM;;``http://www.example.com/members/offers.html``.
41::COMM;;Lots of sites use a cookie to store the session id, which adds a random
42::COMM;;component to the HTTP Request and thus should be ignored when calculating
43::COMM;;the fingerprint.
44::COMM;;For this reason, request headers are ignored by default when calculating
45::COMM;;the fingerprint. If you want to include specific headers use the
46::COMM;;include_headers argument, which is a list of Request headers to include.
47::COMM;;Also, servers usually ignore fragments in urls when handling requests,
48::COMM;;so they are also ignored by default when calculating the fingerprint.
49::COMM;;If you want to include them, set the keep_fragments argument to True
50::COMM;;(for instance when handling requests with a headless browser).
60::COMO;;# To decode bytes reliably (JSON does not support bytes), regardless of
61::COMO;;# character encoding, we use bytes.hex()

89::COMM;;<scrapy.Request.body>`. It then generates an `SHA1
90::COMM;;<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1>`_ hash.

619::COMM;;request = Request(

622::COMM;;)

624::COMM;;assert response.status == 200

627::COMM;;assert isinstance(response_headers, dict)
628::COMM;;for k, v in request.headers.items():
629::COMM;;k_decoded, v_decoded = str(k, "utf-8"), str(v[0], "utf-8")
630::COMM;;assert k_decoded in response_headers
631::COMM;;assert v_decoded == response_headers[k_decoded]
55::COMO;;# get_all result must be native string
26::COMO;;# Request requires url in the __init__ method
29::COMO;;# url argument must be basestring
50::COMO;;# This test passes by not raising any (ValueError) exception
66::COMO;;# Different ways of setting headers attribute
74::COMO;;# headers must not be unicode
102::COMO;;# encoding affects only query part of URI, not path
103::COMO;;# path part should always be UTF-8 encoded before percent-escaping
111::COMO;;# should be same as above
117::COMO;;# encoding is used for encoding query-string before percent-escaping;
118::COMO;;# path is still UTF-8 encoded before percent-escaping
124::COMO;;# percent-escaping sequences that do not match valid UTF-8 sequences
125::COMO;;# should be kept untouched (just upper-cased perhaps)
126::COMO;;#
127::COMO;;# See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3987#section-3.2
128::COMO;;#
129::COMO;;# "Conversions from URIs to IRIs MUST NOT use any character encoding
130::COMO;;# other than UTF-8 in steps 3 and 4, even if it might be possible to
131::COMO;;# guess from the context that another character encoding than UTF-8 was
132::COMO;;# used in the URI. For example, the URI
133::COMO;;# "http://www.example.org/r%E9sum%E9.html" might with some guessing be
134::COMO;;# interpreted to contain two e-acute characters encoded as iso-8859-1.
135::COMO;;# It must not be converted to an IRI containing these e-acute
136::COMO;;# characters. Otherwise, in the future the IRI will be mapped to
137::COMO;;# "http://www.example.org/r%C3%A9sum%C3%A9.html", which is a different
138::COMO;;# URI from "http://www.example.org/r%E9sum%E9.html".
152::COMC;;assert r2.encoding == "utf-8" # default encoding
165::COMM;;def somecallback():
166::COMM;;pass
167::COMM;;r1 = self.request_class(
168::COMM;;"http://www.example.com",
169::COMM;;flags=["f1", "f2"],
170::COMM;;callback=somecallback,
171::COMM;;errback=somecallback,
172::COMM;;)
173::COMM;;r1.meta["foo"] = "bar"
174::COMM;;r1.cb_kwargs["key"] = "value"
175::COMM;;r2 = r1.copy()
176::COMM;;# make sure copy does not propagate callbacks
177::COMM;;assert r1.callback is somecallback
178::COMM;;assert r1.errback is somecallback
179::COMM;;assert r2.callback is r1.callback
180::COMM;;assert r2.errback is r2.errback
181::COMM;;# make sure flags list is shallow copied
182::COMM;;assert r1.flags is not r2.flags, "flags must be a shallow copy, not identical"
183::COMM;;assert r1.flags == r2.flags
184::COMM;;# make sure cb_kwargs dict is shallow copied
185::COMM;;assert r1.cb_kwargs is not r2.cb_kwargs, (
186::COMM;;"cb_kwargs must be a shallow copy, not identical"
187::COMM;;)
188::COMM;;assert r1.cb_kwargs == r2.cb_kwargs
189::COMM;;# make sure meta dict is shallow copied
190::COMM;;assert r1.meta is not r2.meta, "meta must be a shallow copy, not identical"
191::COMM;;assert r1.meta == r2.meta
192::COMM;;# make sure headers attribute is shallow copied
193::COMM;;assert r1.headers is not r2.headers, (
194::COMM;;"headers must be a shallow copy, not identical"
195::COMM;;)
196::COMM;;assert r1.headers == r2.headers
197::COMM;;assert r1.encoding == r2.encoding
198::COMM;;assert r1.dont_filter == r2.dont_filter
199::COMM;;# Request.body can be identical since it's an immutable object (str)

210::COMM;;hdrs = Headers(r1.headers)
